examples.chinese: 這個案例是典型的標本，可以作為教學參考。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ànlì shì diǎnxíng de biāoběn, kěyǐ zuòwéi jiàoxué cānkǎo.
examples.english: This case is a classic specimen that can serve as a teaching reference.

semanticNote: A mark or label — both physical (marking on a map, package, document) and digital (tagging in apps). 做標記 = make a mark. In tech: tag/label data. The word doubles as both noun and verb.

examples.chinese: 請在重要的地方做標記。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhòngyào de dìfāng zuò biāojì.
examples.english: Please mark the important parts.

examples.chinese: 地圖上用紅色標記標出了危險區域。
examples.pinyin: Dìtú shàng yòng hóngsè biāojì biāochūle wēixiǎn qūyù.
examples.english: Dangerous areas are marked in red on the map.

semanticNote: Title of an article, headline of news, heading of a section. 標題黨 = clickbait artists (literally 'title party' — those who write misleading sensational titles). Modern internet use makes this word ubiquitous.

examples.chinese: 這篇文章的標題很吸引人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de biāotí hěn xīyǐn rén.
examples.english: This article's title is very catchy.

examples.chinese: 新聞的標題有時過於誇大，容易誤導讀者。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén de biāotí yǒushí guòyú kuādà, róngyì wùdǎo dúzhě.
examples.english: News headlines are sometimes exaggerated and can easily mislead readers.

english: to decide by vote; vote on
semanticNote: To put something to a vote — formal/procedural. 舉手表決 (vote by raising hands), 表決通過 (passed by vote). Used in meetings, councils, parliaments. Different from 投票 (cast a vote, individual action) — 表決 is the group decision-making process.

examples.chinese: 委員會將對這個提案進行表決。
examples.pinyin: Wěiyuánhuì jiāng duì zhè ge tí'àn jìnxíng biǎojué.
examples.english: The committee will vote on this proposal.

examples.chinese: 全體成員以舉手表決的方式通過了這項決議。
examples.pinyin: Quántǐ chéngyuán yǐ jǔshǒu biǎojué de fāngshì tōngguòle zhè xiàng juéyì.
examples.english: All members passed the resolution by a show-of-hands vote.

english: to declare one's stance; make one's position known
semanticNote: Particularly common in political and workplace contexts — to publicly state where you stand on an issue. 不肯表態 (refuse to take a position). Carries social weight: refusing to 表態 can be read as cowardly or strategically slick.

examples.chinese: 老闆遲遲不表態。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn chíchí bù biǎotài.
examples.english: The boss is dragging his feet on declaring his position.

examples.chinese: 在敏感議題上，她選擇謹慎表態。
examples.pinyin: Zài mǐngǎn yìtí shàng, tā xuǎnzé jǐnshèn biǎotài.
examples.english: On sensitive issues, she chose to state her position cautiously.

semanticNote: Public commendation — usually formal recognition by an institution. 表彰大會 (commendation meeting), 表彰先進 (commend the outstanding). Stronger and more formal than 表揚 (praise, broader). Often involves certificates, awards, public ceremonies.

examples.chinese: 公司表彰了優秀員工。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī biǎozhāngle yōuxiù yuángōng.
examples.english: The company commended outstanding employees.

examples.chinese: 政府在頒獎典禮上表彰了對社會有貢獻的志工。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zài bānjiǎng diǎnlǐ shàng biǎozhāngle duì shèhuì yǒu gòngxiàn de zhìgōng.
examples.english: The government commended volunteers who contributed to society at the award ceremony.

semanticNote: To hold something in — physically (憋尿 = hold pee, 憋氣 = hold breath) or emotionally (憋著一肚子氣 = bottling up anger). 憋了好久 = held it in for a long time. Earthy, vivid word — implies pressure building up. Also 憋屈 = the feeling of being suppressed/stifled.

examples.chinese: 他憋了一肚子話想說。
examples.pinyin: Tā biēle yí dùzi huà xiǎng shuō.
examples.english: He's been holding back a bellyful of things to say.

examples.chinese: 憋氣太久，她忍不住深吸了一口氣。
examples.pinyin: Biē qì tài jiǔ, tā rěn bù zhù shēn xīle yī kǒu qì.
examples.english: After holding her breath too long, she couldn't help but take a deep breath.

semanticNote: A standalone luxury house — villa, mansion. Implies wealth and detached single-family home (rare and aspirational in dense Chinese cities where most people live in apartments). 海邊別墅 = seaside villa.

examples.chinese: 他在郊區買了一棟別墅。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiāoqū mǎile yí dòng biéshù.
examples.english: He bought a villa in the suburbs.

examples.chinese: 那棟海邊的別墅坐擁無敵海景，令人心曠神怡。
examples.pinyin: Nà dòng hǎibiān de biéshù zuòyōng wúdí hǎijǐng, lìng rén xīnkuàng-shényí.
examples.english: That seaside villa commands a breathtaking ocean view that fills the heart with joy.

semanticNote: Stylishly different — used positively for design, clothing, decor, restaurants. 很別致的小店 (a unique little shop). Compliments that something stands out tastefully (vs. just being weird). Aesthetic word.

examples.chinese: 她的穿著很別致。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chuānzhuó hěn biézhì.
examples.english: Her style of dress is uniquely stylish.

examples.chinese: 這家餐廳的裝潢十分別致，吸引了不少觀光客。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de zhuānghuáng shífēn biézhì, xīyǐnle bù shǎo guāngguāngkè.
examples.english: The restaurant's décor is very distinctive and has attracted many tourists.

semanticNote: A wonderfully Chinese word with several flavors: (1) physically awkward / not fitting right (這姿勢很彆扭 = this posture feels awkward); (2) language that doesn't flow naturally (翻譯得很彆扭 = the translation reads awkwardly); (3) interpersonal tension / sulky / passive-aggressive (鬧彆扭 = act sulky, give the silent treatment, especially between couples or family). The third sense is very vivid in spoken Mandarin.

examples.chinese: 她在跟男朋友鬧彆扭。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gēn nán péngyǒu nào bièniu.
examples.english: She's having a sulky tiff with her boyfriend.

examples.chinese: 這句話聽起來很彆扭，我換個說法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jù huà tīng qǐlái hěn bièniu, wǒ huàn ge shuōfǎ.
examples.english: This sentence sounds awkward — let me rephrase it.

english: on the verge of; close to (a critical point)
semanticNote: To be on the brink of — usually negative outcomes. 瀕臨絕種 (on the verge of extinction), 瀕臨破產 (close to bankruptcy), 瀕臨崩潰 (on the verge of collapse). Formal, weighty word for critical thresholds.

examples.chinese: 這種動物已經瀕臨絕種。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng dòngwù yǐjīng bīnlín juézhǒng.
examples.english: This animal is now on the brink of extinction.

examples.chinese: 公司因資金短缺，已瀕臨倒閉的邊緣。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yīn zījīn duǎnquē, yǐ bīnlín dǎobì de biānyuán.
examples.english: Due to a shortage of funds, the company is on the verge of bankruptcy.

semanticNote: Hail. 下冰雹 = hail is falling. Weather vocabulary. 雹子 alone is the more colloquial form.

examples.chinese: 昨天下了冰雹,把車打凹了。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān xiàle bīngbáo, bǎ chē dǎ āole.
examples.english: It hailed yesterday and dented the car.

examples.chinese: 突如其來的冰雹砸壞了許多農作物。
examples.pinyin: Tūrú-qílái de bīngbáo zá huài le xǔduō nóngzuòwù.
examples.english: The sudden hailstorm damaged many crops.

semanticNote: The third of the ten Heavenly Stems (天干: 甲乙丙丁...). Used in traditional grading (甲乙丙丁 = A B C D), in Chinese astrology, and as 'Party C' / 'Person C' in legal documents alongside 甲 (Party A) and 乙 (Party B). Also 丙級 = grade C.

examples.chinese: 合同分為甲方、乙方、丙方。
examples.pinyin: Hétóng fēnwéi jiǎfāng, yǐfāng, bǐngfāng.
examples.english: The contract distinguishes Party A, Party B, and Party C.

examples.chinese: 這次考試她得了丙等，需要加強練習。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì tā déle bǐng děng, xūyào jiāqiáng liànxí.
examples.english: She got a C grade on this exam and needs more practice.

semanticNote: More formal version of 不是 — 'is not' / 'is by no means.' Used in writing and formal speech to refute or correct a misconception. 並非如此 (it's not like that), 並非偶然 (no coincidence). 並 here adds emphasis. Common in essays, news, and analytical writing.

examples.chinese: 成功並非偶然。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng bìngfēi ǒurán.
examples.english: Success is not a coincidence.

examples.chinese: 這件事並非你想像的那麼簡單。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì bìngfēi nǐ xiǎngxiàng de nàme jiǎndān.
examples.english: This matter is by no means as simple as you imagine.

english: to stand side by side; be juxtaposed
semanticNote: Two or more things placed on equal footing — sports (並列第一 = tied for first), grammar (並列關係 = parallel/coordinate relationship), arrangement (並列在一起 = placed side by side). Implies equal status.

examples.chinese: 兩位選手並列冠軍。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng wèi xuǎnshǒu bìngliè guànjūn.
examples.english: The two contestants tied for the championship.

examples.chinese: 這篇文章有三個並列的論點，結構清晰。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng yǒu sān gè bìngliè de lùndiǎn, jiégòu qīngxī.
examples.english: This essay has three coordinate arguments and a clear structure.

english: to dial; allocate; flip / push aside
semanticNote: Range of physical 'flicking' actions: dial a phone (撥電話 — though increasingly old-school as no one dials anymore), allocate funds (撥款 = allocate funding), push something aside with a finger (撥開頭髮 = push hair aside). Also 撥動心弦 = pluck at the heartstrings.

examples.chinese: 政府撥款支持教育。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ bōkuǎn zhīchí jiàoyù.
examples.english: The government allocated funds to support education.

examples.chinese: 她撥開人群，努力往前走。
examples.pinyin: Tā bōkāi rénqún, nǔlì wǎng qián zǒu.
examples.english: She pushed through the crowd and made her way forward.

semanticNote: Ocean/water waves — concrete and visual. Compare to 波濤 (massive billows, more literary) and 浪 alone (also wave, more colloquial). 波浪線 = wavy line. Standard word for everyday waves on water.

examples.chinese: 海面的波浪很大。
examples.pinyin: Hǎimiàn de bōlàng hěn dà.
examples.english: The waves on the sea are big.

examples.chinese: 風吹過水面，泛起層層波浪。
examples.pinyin: Fēng chuīguò shuǐmiàn, fànqǐ céng céng bōlàng.
examples.english: The wind swept across the water, stirring up layer after layer of waves.

semanticNote: Massive, dramatic waves — literary and powerful. 波濤洶湧 = surging waves (set phrase, used both literally for storms and figuratively for tumultuous events/emotions). Reach for 波濤 when you want emotional grandeur; everyday waves are 波浪.

examples.chinese: 暴風雨中,海上波濤洶湧。
examples.pinyin: Bàofēngyǔ zhōng, hǎi shàng bōtāo xiōngyǒng.
examples.english: In the storm, the sea was raging with huge waves.

examples.chinese: 他在波濤起伏的人生中，始終保持沉著。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bōtāo qǐfú de rénshēng zhōng, shǐzhōng bǎochí chénzhuó.
examples.english: Amid the surging ups and downs of life, he always remained composed.

semanticNote: Marxist-flavored term for economic exploitation — taking surplus labor value from workers. 剝削勞工 (exploit workers). The character 剝 alone (read bāo) means to peel — extending to figurative 'stripping' someone of value. Loaded political word in mainland press; used more loosely in Taiwan / overseas.

examples.chinese: 老闆剝削員工的勞動成果。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn bōxuē yuángōng de láodòng chéngguǒ.
examples.english: The boss exploits the fruits of the workers' labor.

examples.chinese: 歷史上，殖民者對被殖民地的人民進行了嚴酷的剝削。
examples.pinyin: Lìshǐ shàng, zhímínzhě duì bèizhímíndì de rénmín jìnxíngle yánkù de bōxuē.
examples.english: Historically, colonizers subjected the peoples of colonized lands to brutal exploitation.

semanticNote: Literally to scatter seeds for planting. Common metaphor: 播種希望 (sow seeds of hope), 春天播種,秋天收穫 (sow in spring, reap in autumn — also figurative for cause and effect). Agricultural foundation, philosophical extension.

examples.chinese: 農夫春天播種,秋天收成。
examples.pinyin: Nóngfū chūntiān bōzhǒng, qiūtiān shōuchéng.
examples.english: Farmers sow in spring and harvest in autumn.

examples.chinese: 老師的職責不只是教書，也在為學生播種理想的種子。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī de zhízé bù zhǐ shì jiāoshū, yě zài wèi xuéshēng bōzhǒng lǐxiǎng de zhǒngzi.
examples.english: A teacher's responsibility is not just to teach, but also to plant seeds of ideals in students.

semanticNote: Specifically the wife of one's father's older brother — Chinese kinship is precise. 伯父 = father's older brother, 伯母 = his wife. Also commonly used as a polite way to address an older woman roughly your mother's age, even if unrelated (like calling someone 'auntie').

examples.chinese: 伯母,您好!
examples.pinyin: Bómǔ, nín hǎo!
examples.english: Hello, Auntie!

examples.chinese: 過節時，我們全家都去伯母家吃飯。
examples.pinyin: Guòjié shí, wǒmen quánjiā dōu qù bómǔ jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: During holidays, our whole family goes to Auntie's house to eat.

semanticNote: 'Broad and deep' — describes culture, philosophy, knowledge, wisdom that has both wide scope and deep substance. Almost always used to describe Chinese culture itself: 中華文化博大精深. Reverent, often used in formal contexts and cultural pride speech.

examples.chinese: 中華文化博大精深。
examples.pinyin: Zhōnghuá wénhuà bódàjīngshēn.
examples.english: Chinese culture is vast and profound.

examples.chinese: 中醫博大精深，學習起來十分不易。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngyī bódà-jīngshēn, xuéxí qǐlái shífēn bù yì.
examples.english: Traditional Chinese medicine is vast and profound — it is very difficult to master.

semanticNote: A large exhibition or fair — international expos, trade shows, world's fairs. 世界博覽會 = World Expo. 上海世博會 = Shanghai Expo (the famous 2010 one). Formal/event word.

examples.chinese: 上海舉辦了世界博覽會。
examples.pinyin: Shànghǎi jǔbànle Shìjiè bólǎnhuì.
examples.english: Shanghai hosted the World Expo.

examples.chinese: 臺北每年都舉辦國際書展，是亞洲最大的博覽會之一。
examples.pinyin: Táiběi měi nián dōu jǔbàn guójì shūzhǎn, shì Yàzhōu zuìdà de bólǎnhuì zhī yī.
examples.english: Taipei holds an international book fair every year — it's one of Asia's largest expos.

semanticNote: Physical struggle — fighting hand-to-hand with someone, or wrestling against waves, illness, fate. 與命運搏鬥 (struggle against fate). More dramatic than 打架 (fight), heavier than 鬥爭 (struggle, more abstract). Often used metaphorically for life challenges.

examples.chinese: 他與病魔搏鬥了三年。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǔ bìngmó bódòule sān nián.
examples.english: He battled the illness for three years.

examples.chinese: 消防員與烈火搏鬥了數個小時，才將大火撲滅。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán yǔ lièhuǒ bódòule shù gè xiǎoshí, cái jiāng dàhuǒ pūmiè.
examples.english: The firefighters battled the fierce fire for several hours before finally extinguishing it.

semanticNote: Weak in capacity or substance — typically applied to abstract qualities: 意志薄弱 (weak willpower), 基礎薄弱 (weak foundation), 證據薄弱 (weak evidence). Different from 弱 (just 'weak', physical) — 薄弱 implies thinness/insufficiency in something that should be solid.

examples.chinese: 他的數學基礎比較薄弱。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shùxué jīchǔ bǐjiào bóruò.
examples.english: His math foundation is rather weak.

examples.chinese: 這座小鎮的防禦力量相當薄弱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò xiǎozhèn de fángyù lìliàng xiāngdāng bóruò.
examples.english: This small town's defensive forces are quite weak.

semanticNote: To pay back what was lost — money compensation for damage, or making up for time/attention not given (補償你 = make it up to you). Both legal/financial and emotional contexts. Common in insurance, lawsuits, and relationship apologies.

examples.chinese: 公司會補償你的損失。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī huì bǔcháng nǐ de sǔnshī.
examples.english: The company will compensate you for the loss.

examples.chinese: 加班的員工可以申請補償假。
examples.pinyin: Jiābān de yuángōng kěyǐ shēnqǐng bǔcháng jià.
examples.english: Employees who work overtime can apply for compensatory leave.

semanticNote: To fix a mistake or salvage a bad situation before it gets worse. 為時已晚,無法補救 (it's too late, can't be remedied). Carries the sense of damage control. Compare to 修復 (repair, more physical).

examples.chinese: 事情還來得及補救。
examples.pinyin: Shìqíng hái láidejí bǔjiù.
examples.english: There's still time to fix this.

examples.chinese: 出了問題不要逃避，及時補救才是正確的態度。
examples.pinyin: Chūle wèntí bùyào táobì, jíshí bǔjiù cái shì zhèngquè de tàidù.
examples.english: When problems arise, don't avoid them — remedying them promptly is the right attitude.

semanticNote: A subsidy — government, employer, or family financial support. 政府補貼 (government subsidy), 房屋補貼 (housing allowance). Also as verb: to subsidize. Common in policy and HR contexts.

examples.chinese: 政府給農民提供補貼。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ gěi nóngmín tígōng bǔtiē.
examples.english: The government provides subsidies to farmers.

examples.chinese: 公司提供員工交通補貼，減輕通勤費用的負擔。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī tígōng yuángōng jiāotōng bǔtiē, jiǎnqīng tōngqín fèiyòng de fùdān.
examples.english: The company provides a transportation allowance to employees to ease commuting costs.

semanticNote: To catch — animals (捕捉野生動物), criminals, but most beautifully abstract: 捕捉靈感 (capture inspiration), 捕捉瞬間 (capture the moment, common in photography). The metaphorical use is loved by writers.

examples.chinese: 攝影師擅長捕捉精彩瞬間。
examples.pinyin: Shèyǐngshī shàncháng bǔzhuō jīngcǎi shùnjiān.
examples.english: The photographer is skilled at capturing wonderful moments.

examples.chinese: 員警成功捕捉了逃亡多年的嫌疑人。
examples.pinyin: Yuánjǐng chénggōng bǔzhuōle táowáng duō nián de xiányírén.
examples.english: The police successfully captured the suspect who had been on the run for many years.

semanticNote: Breastfeeding. 哺乳期 (lactation period), 哺乳動物 (mammals — literally 'suckling animals'). Medical and biological context.

examples.chinese: 她正在哺乳期。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài bǔrǔqī.
examples.english: She's currently in the breastfeeding period.

examples.chinese: 長頸鹿也是哺乳動物，和人類一樣用乳汁哺育後代。
examples.pinyin: Chángjǐnlù yě shì bǔrǔ dòngwù, hé rénlèi yīyàng yòng rǔzhī bǔyù hòudài.
examples.english: Giraffes are also mammals, nursing their young with milk just like humans.

english: have no alternative; do something reluctantly
semanticNote: 'No choice but to' — used when explaining a reluctant action forced by circumstances. 不得已的選擇 (a forced choice), 萬不得已 (only as a very last resort). Defensive / explanatory tone — implies regret about the necessity.

examples.chinese: 我也是不得已才這麼做的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yě shì bùdéyǐ cái zhème zuò de.
examples.english: I only did this because I had no other choice.

examples.chinese: 他不得已接受了這份薪資很低的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùdéyǐ jiēshòule zhè fèn xīnzī hěn dī de gōngzuò.
examples.english: With no other choice, he accepted this very low-paying job.

english: might as well; there's no harm in
semanticNote: Suggests trying something as a reasonable option — 'might as well,' 'why not,' 'no harm in doing X.' Always followed by a verb phrase: 不妨試試 (might as well give it a try), 不妨直說 (no harm in saying it directly). Slightly softer and more tentative than 可以 (can/may). Has a mildly encouraging tone — the speaker is nudging someone toward an action without pressure. Formal enough to appear in writing but common in spoken Mandarin too.

examples.chinese: 你不妨去問問他，也許他知道。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bùfáng qù wènwen tā, yěxǔ tā zhīdào.
examples.english: Why not go ask him — maybe he knows.

examples.chinese: 這個方法不妨試試，反正沒有損失。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ bùfáng shìshì, fǎnzhèng méiyǒu sǔnshī.
examples.english: Might as well try this method — nothing to lose anyway.

english: you flatter me; I don't deserve such praise
semanticNote: Polite humility phrase — a deflection of praise, like 'oh, you flatter me' or 'I'm not worthy.' Used when complimented or addressed too respectfully. Cultural muscle: Chinese speakers are expected to deflect praise. Particularly common from elders or in formal interactions.

examples.chinese: 您過獎了,不敢當。
examples.pinyin: Nín guòjiǎng le, bùgǎndāng.
examples.english: You praise me too much — I don't deserve it.

examples.chinese: 「您真是多才多藝！」「不敢當，還差得遠呢。」
examples.pinyin: "Nín zhēn shì duōcái-duōyì!" "Bùgǎndāng, hái chà de yuǎn ne."
examples.english: "You are truly multi-talented!" "I don't deserve such praise — I still have a long way to go."

semanticNote: To act without regard for something — usually consequences, others' feelings, or rules. 不顧後果 (regardless of consequences), 不顧一切 (no matter what), 不顧別人感受 (without regard for others' feelings). Often carries criticism — implies recklessness or selfishness.

examples.chinese: 他不顧家人的反對,堅持出國。
examples.pinyin: Tā búgù jiārén de fǎnduì, jiānchí chūguó.
examples.english: He insisted on going abroad despite his family's objections.

examples.chinese: 她不顧風險，毅然辭去了穩定的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā búgù fēngxiǎn, yìrán cíqùle wěndìng de gōngzuò.
examples.english: She disregarded the risks and resolutely quit her stable job.

english: can't help but; can't refrain from
semanticNote: To be unable to hold back a reaction — laughter, tears, a thought. 不禁笑了 (couldn't help laughing), 不禁想起 (can't help but think of). Slightly literary — implies an involuntary, often emotional response. Compare to 忍不住 (couldn't resist, more colloquial).

examples.chinese: 看到那個場景,我不禁掉下了眼淚。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào nà ge chǎngjǐng, wǒ bùjīn diào xiàle yǎnlèi.
examples.english: Seeing that scene, I couldn't help but shed tears.

examples.chinese: 聽到這首兒時的歌，她不禁想起了童年。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhè shǒu érshí de gē, tā bùjīn xiǎngqǐle tóngnián.
examples.english: Hearing this childhood song, she couldn't help but think back to her youth.

semanticNote: Two uses: (1) 'cannot bear' — 不堪重負 (cannot bear the burden), 不堪入目 (unbearable to look at); (2) suffix intensifier — 疲憊不堪 (utterly exhausted), 狼狽不堪 (in a terrible state). The suffix usage is very common and adds 'extremely' to a negative state.

examples.chinese: 工作壓力讓他疲憊不堪。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò yālì ràng tā píbèi bùkān.
examples.english: Work pressure has utterly exhausted him.

examples.chinese: 那場火災之後，建築物已是殘破不堪。
examples.pinyin: Nà chǎng huǒzāi zhīhòu, jiànzhúwù yǐ shì cánpò bùkān.
examples.english: After the fire, the building was left in utterly dilapidated ruins.

semanticNote: Literally 'cannot think or discuss it' — something so extraordinary it defies comprehension. Can express genuine awe (a scientific discovery, a miraculous feat) or incredulous disbelief (something outrageous or absurd). In modern spoken Mandarin, often used hyperbolically and positively — like 'unbelievable!' about a great meal or performance. Less formal than written registers suggest; very common in casual speech. Compare to 難以置信 (hard to believe — more about disbelief than awe).

examples.chinese: 他竟然在三天內跑完了一百公里，真是不可思議。
examples.pinyin: Tā jìngrán zài sān tiān nèi pǎowánle yī bǎi gōnglǐ, zhēn shì bùkěsīyì.
examples.english: He actually ran 100 kilometers in three days — absolutely mind-boggling.

examples.chinese: 宇宙的廣大讓人覺得不可思議。
examples.pinyin: Yǔzhòu de guǎngdà ràng rén juéde bùkěsīyì.
examples.english: The vastness of the universe is simply inconceivable.

english: to live up to (the title); deserve to be called
semanticNote: Used to express genuine admiration — 'truly worthy of being called X.' 不愧是冠軍 (truly worthy of being champion), 不愧為老師 (lives up to being a teacher). Praise-flavored. The 愧 (shame) gets negated — 'no shame in being called this.'

examples.chinese: 他不愧是專業選手。
examples.pinyin: Tā búkuì shì zhuānyè xuǎnshǒu.
examples.english: He truly lives up to being a pro athlete.

examples.chinese: 她不愧是名廚，做出來的每道菜都令人讚嘆。
examples.pinyin: Tā búkuì shì míngchú, zuò chūlái de měi dào cài dōu lìng rén zàntàn.
examples.english: She truly lives up to her reputation as a famous chef — every dish she makes is breathtaking.

semanticNote: Storytelling word: 'who would have thought' / 'unexpectedly.' Used to introduce a plot twist or surprising development. 本來計畫得好好的,不料... (We had planned it all out, but unexpectedly...). Common in narrative, news, anecdotes. Compare to 沒想到 (didn't expect, more colloquial).

examples.chinese: 我們本來要出門,不料下起了大雨。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen běnlái yào chūmén, búliào xiàqǐle dàyǔ.
examples.english: We were going to head out, but unexpectedly it started pouring.

examples.chinese: 他精心準備了演講，不料麥克風卻壞了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngxīn zhǔnbèile yǎnjiǎng, búliào màikèfēng què huài le.
examples.english: He carefully prepared his speech, but to his surprise, the microphone broke down.

semanticNote: 'Unavoidably' / 'inevitably' — usually introducing a feeling or reaction that follows naturally from a situation. 不免擔心 (can't help worrying), 不免有些失望 (inevitably a bit disappointed). Reflective, slightly literary.

examples.chinese: 看到這結果,他不免有些失望。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào zhè jiéguǒ, tā bùmiǎn yǒuxiē shīwàng.
examples.english: Seeing this result, he was inevitably a bit disappointed.

examples.chinese: 初到異鄉，不免感到孤單與不安。
examples.pinyin: Chū dào yìxiāng, bùmiǎn gǎndào gūdān yǔ bù'ān.
examples.english: When first arriving in a foreign land, one inevitably feels lonely and unsettled.

semanticNote: 'Now and then' / 'at frequent intervals.' 不時回頭 (looking back from time to time). Slightly more literary than 經常 (often) or 時不時 (every now and then). Often appears in descriptive narrative writing.

examples.chinese: 她不時看一眼手機。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùshí kàn yì yǎn shǒujī.
examples.english: She glanced at her phone now and then.

examples.chinese: 他不時發出笑聲，顯然心情很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùshí fāchū xiàoshēng, xiǎnrán xīnqíng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He burst out laughing from time to time, clearly in a great mood.

semanticNote: To go to extreme lengths — willing to do or sacrifice anything for a goal. 不惜代價 (whatever the cost), 不惜一切 (regardless of all else), 不惜犧牲 (not sparing the sacrifice). Strong commitment word, can be admiring or critical depending on context.

examples.chinese: 他不惜代價追求夢想。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùxī dàijià zhuīqiú mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: He pursues his dream no matter the cost.

examples.chinese: 她為了孩子的教育，不惜放棄了自己的事業。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile háizi de jiàoyù, bùxī fàngqìle zìjǐ de shìyè.
examples.english: For her children's education, she didn't hesitate to give up her own career.

semanticNote: Two things at the same level — 'neither above nor below the other.' Used for comparison in skill, quality, performance. 兩人實力不相上下 (the two are evenly matched). Common in sports, competition, debate.

examples.chinese: 兩個品牌的品質不相上下。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge pǐnpái de pǐnzhì bùxiāngshàngxià.
examples.english: The two brands' quality is about the same.

examples.chinese: 兩支球隊實力不相上下，比賽一路膠著。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhī qiúduì shílì bùxiāng-shàngxià, bǐsài yīlù jiāozhuó.
examples.english: The two teams were evenly matched, and the game was neck and neck throughout.

semanticNote: Strong colloquial expression of disapproval — 'this is outrageous!' / 'how can you act like this!' 真不像話! is a parental/outraged exclamation when someone has crossed a line. Common in family arguments and indignant complaints. Literally 'not like a [proper] saying' — i.e., beyond reasonable expression.

examples.chinese: 你這樣說真不像話。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng shuō zhēn búxiànghuà.
examples.english: It's outrageous for you to say that.

examples.chinese: 大庭廣眾下大聲吵架，真是不像話。
examples.pinyin: Dàtíng-guǎngzhòng xià dàshēng chǎojià, zhēn shì búxiànghuà.
examples.english: Shouting and arguing loudly in public — how outrageous.

english: to disdain; not even worth a glance
semanticNote: To consider something so beneath you that you won't even look. Strong contempt. 對他不屑一顧 (won't even glance at him in disdain). Powerful and slightly cold — implies the person/thing has been judged unworthy of attention.

examples.chinese: 她對這種小事不屑一顧。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè zhǒng xiǎoshì búxièyígù.
examples.english: She doesn't deign to even glance at such trivial matters.

examples.chinese: 他對批評一向不屑一顧，從不反思自己的問題。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì pīpíng yīxiàng búxiè-yīgù, cóng bù fǎnsī zìjǐ de wèntí.
examples.english: He has always disdained criticism and never reflects on his own problems.

semanticNote: 'Doesn't need to be said to be understood' — used to introduce something obvious. 結果不言而喻 (the result goes without saying). Common in formal writing and analysis to wrap up a point. Slightly more elegant than 顯而易見 (obvious).

examples.chinese: 他的重要性不言而喻。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhòngyàoxìng bùyán'éryù.
examples.english: His importance goes without saying.

examples.chinese: 誠信的重要性不言而喻，卻有太多人忽視它。
examples.pinyin: Chéngxìn de zhòngyàoxìng bùyán'éryù, què yǒu tài duō rén hūshì tā.
examples.english: The importance of integrity goes without saying, yet too many people ignore it.

semanticNote: Same family as 不禁 — describes an involuntary reaction. 不由得笑了 (couldn't help laughing). Slightly more colloquial than 不禁. Implies the response was beyond your control.

examples.chinese: 聽到這消息,她不由得哭了起來。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhè xiāoxī, tā bùyóude kūle qǐlái.
examples.english: Hearing the news, she couldn't help but burst into tears.

examples.chinese: 看到昔日的老照片，她不由得感慨萬千。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào xīrì de lǎo zhàopiàn, tā bùyóude gǎnkǎi-wànqiān.
examples.english: Looking at old photos from the past, she was overcome with a flood of emotions.

english: by any means necessary; stop at nothing; unscrupulous
semanticNote: Strongly negative. Means using whatever methods are available regardless of ethics or legality — 'stop at nothing,' 'by fair means or foul.' Always about someone whose ambition or greed overrides moral constraints. 他為了升職不擇手段 = He'll do anything to get promoted. Not used admiringly; always a criticism. Compare to 不惜一切 (spare no effort — can be neutral/positive) which lacks the moral condemnation.

examples.chinese: 他為了達到目的，可以不擇手段。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile dádào mùdì, kěyǐ bùzéshǒuduàn.
examples.english: To achieve his goals, he'll stop at nothing.

examples.chinese: 這家公司不擇手段地壓低成本，引發員工強烈不滿。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī bùzéshǒuduàn de yā dī chéngběn, yǐnfā yuángōng qiángliè bùmǎn.
examples.english: The company cut costs by any means necessary, sparking fierce employee discontent.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) more than (a number) — 不止一次 (more than once), 不止三十歲 (more than thirty years old); (2) without stopping — 笑個不止 (laughing nonstop), 流血不止 (bleeding non-stop). Context disambiguates which sense applies.

examples.chinese: 我去過那裡不止一次。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qùguò nàlǐ bùzhǐ yí cì.
examples.english: I've been there more than once.

examples.chinese: 他每天工作不止十個小時，幾乎沒有休閒時間。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān gōngzuò bùzhǐ shí gè xiǎoshí, jīhū méiyǒu xiūxián shíjiān.
examples.english: He works more than ten hours every day and has almost no leisure time.

semanticNote: A public notice posted on a board or wall — bulletin-style announcement. 布告欄 = bulletin board. Old-school institutional communication; less common as digital messaging takes over, but still used in schools, offices, government buildings.

examples.chinese: 學校在布告欄貼了通知。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zài bùgàolán tiēle tōngzhī.
examples.english: The school posted a notice on the bulletin board.

examples.chinese: 公司在大廳張貼布告，宣布人事調動。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zài dàtīng zhāngtiē bùgào, xuānbù rénshì diàodòng.
examples.english: The company posted a notice in the lobby announcing personnel transfers.

semanticNote: Spatial or strategic arrangement — chess game (棋局的布局), city layout (城市布局), business strategy (戰略布局). Both physical layouts and abstract positioning. Common in design, urban planning, and strategic discussions.

examples.chinese: 這家店的布局很合理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de bùjú hěn hélǐ.
examples.english: This shop's layout is well-designed.

examples.chinese: 下棋需要精心布局，才能在關鍵時刻取勝。
examples.pinyin: Xià qí xūyào jīngxīn bùjú, cái néng zài guānjiàn shíkè qǔshèng.
examples.english: Playing chess requires careful strategic positioning to win at the critical moment.

semanticNote: To arrange or set up — a room (布置房間 = decorate a room), a task (布置作業 = assign homework), a venue for an event. Common everyday word for organizing physical spaces or assigning tasks. Teachers 布置 homework; party planners 布置 venues.

examples.chinese: 老師布置了很多作業。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bùzhìle hěn duō zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher assigned a lot of homework.

examples.chinese: 她精心布置了婚禮現場，充滿了浪漫氣氛。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngxīn bùzhìle hūnlǐ xiànchǎng, chōngmǎn le làngmàn qìfēn.
examples.english: She carefully decorated the wedding venue, filling it with a romantic atmosphere.

semanticNote: Pace or pacing — physical (a soldier's step) and figurative (跟上時代的步伐 = keep pace with the times, 加快步伐 = quicken the pace). Often used metaphorically about progress, development, or social change. Slightly literary.

examples.chinese: 我們要跟上時代的步伐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào gēnshàng shídài de bùfá.
examples.english: We need to keep pace with the times.

examples.chinese: 他加快步伐，衝上前去接住球。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiākuài bùfá, chōng shàng qián qù jiēzhù qiú.
examples.english: He quickened his pace and rushed forward to catch the ball.

semanticNote: Strategic deployment — military (deploy troops), corporate (deploy resources), tech (deploy software/systems). Implies organized, planned arrangement of assets toward a goal. 戰略部署 = strategic deployment. Top-down, planning-vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 公司部署了新的市場策略。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī bùshǔle xīn de shìchǎng cèlüè.
examples.english: The company deployed a new market strategy.

examples.chinese: 軍隊在邊境附近部署了大量兵力。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì zài biānjìng fùjìn bùshǔle dàliàng bīnglì.
examples.english: The military deployed a large number of troops near the border.

semanticNote: A specific part or area, most often of a body or object. 身體部位 = body part, 受傷部位 = injured area. Medical, anatomical, technical contexts. More precise than 地方 (place, generic).

examples.chinese: 請告訴我哪個部位疼。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosù wǒ nǎ ge bùwèi téng.
examples.english: Please tell me which part hurts.

examples.chinese: 這種按摩主要針對頸肩部位的肌肉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng ànmó zhǔyào zhēnduì jǐngjiān bùwèi de jīròu.
examples.english: This type of massage mainly targets the muscles of the neck and shoulder areas.

semanticNote: Practical talent and capability, especially for getting things done in work or leadership. 有才幹的人 (a competent person). Compare to 才能 (talent, broader/more artistic) and 能力 (ability, neutral). 才幹 specifically connotes practical executive ability.

examples.chinese: 他是個有才幹的領導。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge yǒu cáigàn de lǐngdǎo.
examples.english: He's a competent leader.

examples.chinese: 她的才幹在工作中得到了充分的發揮。
examples.pinyin: Tā de cáigàn zài gōngzuò zhōng dédàole chōngfèn de fāhuī.
examples.english: Her talents were given full play in her work.

semanticNote: Wealth — money, property, but also abstract: 精神財富 (spiritual wealth), 知識是財富 (knowledge is wealth). More dignified and broad than 錢 (money, concrete). Common in finance, philosophy, and inspirational contexts.

examples.chinese: 健康才是真正的財富。
examples.pinyin: Jiànkāng cái shì zhēnzhèng de cáifù.
examples.english: Health is the true wealth.

examples.chinese: 他用了一生積累財富，卻忘了享受生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòngle yīshēng jīlěi cáifù, què wàngle xiǎngshòu shēnghuó.
examples.english: He spent his whole life accumulating wealth, but forgot to enjoy life.

semanticNote: Business/personal finance management. 財務部 (finance department), 財務報表 (financial statements), 財務狀況 (financial situation). Different from 財政 (public/government finance) — 財務 is private/corporate.

examples.chinese: 她在公司負責財務工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī fùzé cáiwù gōngzuò.
examples.english: She handles financial work at the company.

examples.chinese: 公司的財務狀況透明，每季度都公布報告。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī de cáiwù zhuàngkuàng tòumíng, měi jìdù dōu gōngbù bàogào.
examples.english: The company's financial situation is transparent, with reports published every quarter.

semanticNote: Government/public finance — fiscal policy, public budgets. 財政部 = Ministry of Finance, 財政赤字 = fiscal deficit. Sister-word to 財務 — 財政 is government-side, 財務 is business-side. News and economics vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 政府正在調整財政政策。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài tiáozhěng cáizhèng zhèngcè.
examples.english: The government is adjusting fiscal policy.

examples.chinese: 這個國家的財政赤字已超過GDP的百分之三。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de cáizhèng chìzì yǐ chāoguò GDP de bǎifēnzhī sān.
examples.english: This country's fiscal deficit has exceeded three percent of GDP.

semanticNote: A tailor — someone who cuts and sews garments. 裁 (cut) + 縫 (sew). Trade word; less common in modern fast-fashion era but still used.

examples.chinese: 奶奶以前是裁縫。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai yǐqián shì cáifeng.
examples.english: Grandma used to be a tailor.

examples.chinese: 這件洋裝是請裁縫專門量身訂做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yángzhuāng shì qǐng cáifeng zhuānmén liángshēn dìngzuò de.
examples.english: This dress was specially custom-made by a tailor.

semanticNote: Sports referee or, by extension, anyone passing judgment. Both noun (the referee) and verb (to judge/referee). 裁判不公 = unfair officiating — common complaint in sports culture worldwide.

examples.chinese: 裁判判他犯規。
examples.pinyin: Cáipàn pàn tā fànguī.
examples.english: The referee called him for a foul.

examples.chinese: 這次比賽的裁判來自第三方，確保公正性。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài de cáipàn láizì dìsānfāng, quèbǎo gōngzhèngxìng.
examples.english: The referees for this competition come from a third party, ensuring fairness.

semanticNote: Corporate layoffs. 公司裁員 = company laying off staff. Modern, news-flavored word. Common in economic downturns. Distinguished from 解雇 (fire an individual) — 裁員 is structural workforce reduction.

examples.chinese: 公司宣布要裁員百分之十。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xuānbù yào cáiyuán bǎi fēn zhī shí.
examples.english: The company announced 10 percent layoffs.

examples.chinese: 大規模裁員引發了工會的強烈抗議。
examples.pinyin: Dà guīmó cáiyuán yǐnfāle gōnghuì de qiángliè kàngyì.
examples.english: The large-scale layoffs triggered fierce protests from the union.

semanticNote: Procurement — buying for an organization, not personal shopping. 採購部 = procurement department, 政府採購 = government procurement. Business and institutional vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 她負責公司的採購工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā fùzé gōngsī de cǎigòu gōngzuò.
examples.english: She handles the company's procurement.

examples.chinese: 年底大採購前，採購部門要先做好預算規劃。
examples.pinyin: Niándǐ dà cǎigòu qián, cǎigòu bùmén yào xiān zuò hǎo yùsuàn guīhuà.
examples.english: Before the year-end bulk purchase, the procurement department needs to first finalize its budget plan.

semanticNote: To gather — physical things (採集樣本 = collect samples, 採集草藥 = gather herbs) or data (採集信息 = collect information). Scientific/research flavor. Different from 收集 (collect, broader, hobby/general).

examples.chinese: 科學家採集了水樣本進行分析。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā cǎijíle shuǐ yàngběn jìnxíng fēnxī.
examples.english: Scientists collected water samples for analysis.

examples.chinese: 植物學家深入山區採集稀有植物的標本。
examples.pinyin: Zhíwùxuéjiā shēnrù shānqū cǎijí xīyǒu zhíwù de biāoběn.
examples.english: Botanists went deep into the mountains to collect specimens of rare plants.

semanticNote: Specifically to accept and adopt a suggestion, proposal, or opinion. 採納建議 (adopt a suggestion). Implies considered acceptance, not just nodding along. Common in formal/professional contexts.

examples.chinese: 老闆採納了我的建議。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn cǎinàle wǒ de jiànyì.
examples.english: The boss adopted my suggestion.

examples.chinese: 設計師的創意方案最終被採納並付諸實施。
examples.pinyin: Shèjìshī de chuàngyì fāng'àn zuìzhōng bèi cǎinà bìng fùzhū shíshī.
examples.english: The designer's creative plan was ultimately adopted and put into practice.

semanticNote: Lottery ticket. 中彩票 = win the lottery. The 彩 here is the 'colorful prize' sense. Casual/pop-culture vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 他每週買彩票。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu mǎi cǎipiào.
examples.english: He buys lottery tickets every week.

examples.chinese: 她中了彩票，一夜之間成了百萬富翁。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngle cǎipiào, yīyè zhījiān chéngle bǎiwàn fùwēng.
examples.english: She won the lottery and became a millionaire overnight.

english: staff officer; advisor; to give advice
semanticNote: Originally military: a staff officer / strategist. Common verb use: 給我參謀一下 = help me think this through / give me your input. The verb sense is colloquial and warm — asking trusted friends for advice.

examples.chinese: 買房這事兒,你幫我參謀一下。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi fáng zhè shìr, nǐ bāng wǒ cānmóu yíxià.
examples.english: Help me think through this house-buying thing.

examples.chinese: 他在軍中擔任作戰參謀，制定了多項戰術計劃。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jūn zhōng dānrèn zuòzhàn cānmóu, zhìdìngle duō xiàng zhànshù jìhuà.
examples.english: He served as an operations staff officer in the military, formulating multiple tactical plans.

english: to refer to; consult (as a reference)
semanticNote: To use something as reference for one's own work or decision. 參照範例 (refer to the example), 參照標準 (consult the standard). Common in instructions, regulations, professional writing. Implies use as a model, not just looking at.

examples.chinese: 請參照範例完成作業。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng cānzhào fànlì wánchéng zuòyè.
examples.english: Please refer to the example to complete the assignment.

examples.chinese: 新政策的制定參照了多個國家的成功經驗。
examples.pinyin: Xīn zhèngcè de zhìdìng cānzhàole duō gè guójiā de chénggōng jīngyàn.
examples.english: The formulation of the new policy drew on the successful experiences of multiple countries.

semanticNote: Physical disability. 殘疾人 = disabled person (terminology is shifting toward 身心障礙者 in Taiwan as the more respectful current term, but 殘疾 is still standard in mainland and HSK). Sensitive vocabulary — register matters.

examples.chinese: 社會應該關懷殘疾人士。
examples.pinyin: Shèhuì yīnggāi guānhuái cánjí rénshì.
examples.english: Society should care for people with disabilities.

examples.chinese: 他雖然身有殘疾，卻以樂觀的態度面對生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán shēn yǒu cánjí, què yǐ lèguān de tàidù miànduì shēnghuó.
examples.english: Despite having a physical disability, he faces life with an optimistic attitude.

semanticNote: Cruelty in actions or in reality itself. 殘酷的事實 (the cruel truth), 殘酷的戰爭 (brutal war). Often used to describe both human cruelty and the harshness of circumstances/fate. Strong word — heavier than 狠 (ruthless).

examples.chinese: 現實有時很殘酷。
examples.pinyin: Xiànshí yǒushí hěn cánkù.
examples.english: Reality is sometimes very cruel.

examples.chinese: 戰爭是殘酷的，它讓無數無辜的人失去了生命。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng shì cánkù de, tā ràng wúshù wúgū de rén shīqùle shēngmìng.
examples.english: War is brutal — it has taken the lives of countless innocent people.

semanticNote: Residue / lingering remnants — chemicals, traces, memories. 農藥殘留 (pesticide residue), 殘留的記憶 (lingering memories). Often negative or at least neutral-with-concern.

examples.chinese: 這蔬菜上有農藥殘留。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shūcài shàng yǒu nóngyào cánliú.
examples.english: There's pesticide residue on this vegetable.

examples.chinese: 大水退後，地上殘留著一層泥漿。
examples.pinyin: Dàshuǐ tuì hòu, dì shàng cánliúzhe yī céng níjiāng.
examples.english: After the floodwaters receded, a layer of mud remained on the ground.

semanticNote: Cruelty as a moral quality of a person or act. 殘忍的兇手 (cruel murderer). Compare to 殘酷 — 殘忍 emphasizes the cruelty IN the actor/action; 殘酷 can also describe situations or facts.

examples.chinese: 他做了非常殘忍的事。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòle fēicháng cánrěn de shì.
examples.english: He did something extremely cruel.

examples.chinese: 遺棄動物是殘忍的行為，不應被社會容忍。
examples.pinyin: Yíqì dòngwù shì cánrěn de xíngwéi, bù yīng bèi shèhuì róngrěn.
examples.english: Abandoning animals is a cruel act that should not be tolerated by society.

semanticNote: Bright and dazzling — sunshine, smiles, civilizations, futures. 燦爛的笑容 (a brilliant smile), 燦爛的文化 (a brilliant culture), 燦爛的未來 (a glorious future). Warm, celebratory word.

examples.chinese: 她露出燦爛的笑容。
examples.pinyin: Tā lùchū cànlàn de xiàoróng.
examples.english: She showed a brilliant smile.

examples.chinese: 夕陽西下，天邊染上了燦爛的金紅色。
examples.pinyin: Xīyáng xī xià, tiānbiān rǎnshàngle cànlàn de jīn hóng sè.
examples.english: As the sun set in the west, the horizon was painted in brilliant gold and red.

semanticNote: Hasty in a way that suggests inadequate preparation. 倉促決定 (hasty decision), 倉促應對 (hurried response). Slightly negative — implies you should have had more time. Compare to 匆忙 (in a hurry, more neutral about reason).

examples.chinese: 他做了一個倉促的決定。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòle yí ge cāngcù de juédìng.
examples.english: He made a hasty decision.

examples.chinese: 由於時間倉促，報告寫得不夠完善。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyú shíjiān cāngcù, bàogào xiě de bù gòu wánshàn.
examples.english: Due to time pressure, the report was not written thoroughly enough.

semanticNote: A warehouse — for goods, supplies, inventory. Logistics and business vocabulary. 倉庫管理 = warehouse management.

examples.chinese: 商品都存放在倉庫裡。
examples.pinyin: Shāngpǐn dōu cúnfàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
examples.english: All the goods are stored in the warehouse.

examples.chinese: 年末盤點時，工人要清查倉庫裡的所有庫存。
examples.pinyin: Niánmò pándiǎn shí, gōngrén yào qīngchá cāngkù lǐ de suǒyǒu kùcún.
examples.english: At the year-end inventory, workers need to check all stock in the warehouse.

semanticNote: Pale — physically (sick or scared face) or figuratively (蒼白無力 = pale and feeble, often describing weak arguments or unconvincing explanations). 臉色蒼白 = pale-faced. Slightly more vivid than 白 (just white).

examples.chinese: 她的臉色蒼白,看起來很虛弱。
examples.pinyin: Tā de liǎnsè cāngbái, kàn qǐlái hěn xūruò.
examples.english: Her face was pale; she looked very weak.

examples.chinese: 他的辯解蒼白無力，沒有人相信他。
examples.pinyin: Tā de biànjiě cāngbái wúlì, méiyǒu rén xiāngxìn tā.
examples.english: His defense was pale and feeble — no one believed him.

semanticNote: Compartments on aircraft, ships, spacecraft. 頭等艙 (first class), 經濟艙 (economy class), 駕駛艙 (cockpit), 太空艙 (space capsule). Travel and aerospace vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 我訂了商務艙的機票。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìngle shāngwùcāng de jīpiào.
examples.english: I booked a business class ticket.

examples.chinese: 緊急降落時，機艙內的乘客都保持了冷靜。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnjí jiàngluò shí, jīcāng nèi de chéngkè dōu bǎochíle lěngjìng.
examples.english: During the emergency landing, the passengers in the cabin all remained calm.

semanticNote: Hard work specifically motivated by care for others — usually parents toiling for family. 操勞家務 (toil over housework), 為了孩子操勞 (work hard for the kids' sake). Has a tender, slightly sad flavor — implies sacrifice. Common in describing parents and elders.

examples.chinese: 母親一輩子為家庭操勞。
examples.pinyin: Mǔqīn yíbèizi wèi jiātíng cāoláo.
examples.english: Mother toiled her whole life for the family.

examples.chinese: 他日夜操勞，把公司從瀕臨倒閉帶回了正軌。
examples.pinyin: Tā rìyè cāoláo, bǎ gōngsī cóng bīnlín dǎobì dài huíle zhèngguǐ.
examples.english: He toiled day and night, bringing the company back from the brink of bankruptcy.

semanticNote: Repetitive practice or drilling — military exercises (士兵操練), or by extension intensive practice in any skill. Slightly old-fashioned for non-military uses; younger speakers prefer 練習.

examples.chinese: 士兵每天都在操練。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīng měitiān dōu zài cāoliàn.
examples.english: Soldiers drill every day.

examples.chinese: 消防員定期操練，確保緊急情況下能迅速應變。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán dìngqī cāoliàn, quèbǎo jǐnjí qíngkuàng xià néng xùnsù yìngbiàn.
examples.english: Firefighters drill regularly to ensure they can respond swiftly in emergencies.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) operate machinery/controls (操縱機器); (2) manipulate behind the scenes (操縱市場 = manipulate the market, 操縱選舉 = rig elections). The second sense dominates in news contexts and is negative. Compare to 操作 (operate, neutral, no manipulation).

examples.chinese: 他被指控操縱股票市場。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi zhǐkòng cāozòng gǔpiào shìchǎng.
examples.english: He was accused of manipulating the stock market.

examples.chinese: 木偶師靈活地操縱木偶，表演得栩栩如生。
examples.pinyin: Mùǒushī línghuó de cāozòng mùǒu, biǎoyǎn de xǔxǔ-rúshēng.
examples.english: The puppeteer skillfully manipulated the puppet, giving a lifelike performance.

semanticNote: Operate equipment, software, processes. Neutral. 操作系統 (operating system), 操作員 (operator), 簡單易操作 (simple and easy to operate). Standard tech and machinery word.

examples.chinese: 這個機器很容易操作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jīqì hěn róngyì cāozuò.
examples.english: This machine is easy to operate.

examples.chinese: 新版軟體的操作界面更加簡潔直觀。
examples.pinyin: Xīn bǎn ruǎntǐ de cāozuò jièmiàn gèngjiā jiǎnjié zhíguān.
examples.english: The new version of the software's operating interface is cleaner and more intuitive.

semanticNote: Specifically describes mixed, chaotic noise — a crowded restaurant, busy street, packed market. More expressive than 吵 (just 'noisy'). Implies the noise comes from many sources at once.

examples.chinese: 市場裡很嘈雜。
examples.pinyin: Shìchǎng lǐ hěn cáozá.
examples.english: It's very noisy in the market.

examples.chinese: 嘈雜的環境讓她難以集中注意力。
examples.pinyin: Cáozá de huánjìng ràng tā nán yǐ jízhōng zhùyìlì.
examples.english: The noisy environment made it hard for her to concentrate.

semanticNote: A draft document — proposal, legislation, contract — not yet finalized. 法律草案 (draft legislation), 修改草案 (revise the draft). Formal, used in legal/political/business contexts.

examples.chinese: 政府公布了新法律的草案。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ gōngbùle xīn fǎlǜ de cǎo'àn.
examples.english: The government published the draft of the new law.

examples.chinese: 委員會正在審議修憲草案的每一個細節。
examples.pinyin: Wěiyuánhuì zhèngzài shěnyì xiūxiàn cǎo'àn de měi yīgè xìjié.
examples.english: The committee is examining every detail of the constitutional amendment draft.

semanticNote: Done sloppily, without sufficient care or thought. 草率的決定 (a careless decision), 草率了事 (handle perfunctorily). Negative — criticism that someone didn't take it seriously enough. Compare to 倉促 (hasty, lacking time) — 草率 is lacking care.

examples.chinese: 這麼重要的事不能草率決定。
examples.pinyin: Zhème zhòngyào de shì bùnéng cǎoshuài juédìng.
examples.english: You can't decide such an important matter carelessly.

examples.chinese: 他草率地簽了合約，後來才發現其中有不合理的條款。
examples.pinyin: Tā cǎoshuài de qiānle héyuē, hòulái cái fāxiàn qízhōng yǒu bù hélǐ de tiáokuǎn.
examples.english: He hastily signed the contract, only to discover later that it contained unreasonable terms.

semanticNote: The side of something — physical (side view of a face/object) or figurative (an aspect or angle of an issue). 從側面了解 (understand from another angle / find out indirectly). Useful in analysis: 'looking at it from another side.'

examples.chinese: 她的側面很好看。
examples.pinyin: Tā de cèmiàn hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: Her profile is beautiful.

examples.chinese: 我們要從各個側面去了解這個問題。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cóng gège cèmiàn qù liǎojiě zhège wèntí.
examples.english: We need to understand this issue from every angle.

semanticNote: To measure with instruments — distance, temperature, area. More technical than 量 alone. Land surveying, engineering, scientific measurement.

examples.chinese: 工程師正在測量距離。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī zhèngzài cèliáng jùlí.
examples.english: The engineer is measuring the distance.

examples.chinese: 要蓋新建築前，必須先測量土地面積。
examples.pinyin: Yào gài xīn jiànzhú qián, bìxū xiān cèliáng tǔdì miànjī.
examples.english: Before building a new structure, the land area must first be measured.

semanticNote: To plan/orchestrate carefully — events (策劃活動 = plan an event), schemes (策劃陰謀 = plot a conspiracy). Neutral when about events, negative when about schemes. 策劃人 = planner / mastermind. Common in marketing and event vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 她策劃了一場成功的婚禮。
examples.pinyin: Tā cèhuàle yì chǎng chénggōng de hūnlǐ.
examples.english: She planned a successful wedding.

examples.chinese: 這次文化活動由多個單位共同策劃，歷時三個月籌備。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wénhuà huódòng yóu duō gè dānwèi gòngtóng cèhuà, lìshí sān gè yuè chóubèi.
examples.english: This cultural event was jointly planned by multiple organizations and took three months to prepare.

semanticNote: Strategic approach — business, politics, sports, war. 行銷策略 (marketing strategy), 改變策略 (change strategy). Common modern business word. Compare to 戰略 (grand/military strategy, more macro) — 策略 is more practical and tactical.

examples.chinese: 我們需要新的行銷策略。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào xīn de xíngxiāo cèlüè.
examples.english: We need a new marketing strategy.

examples.chinese: 面對競爭對手，公司採取了靈活的應對策略。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì jìngzhēng duìshǒu, gōngsī cǎiqǔle línghuó de yìngduì cèlüè.
examples.english: Facing competitors, the company adopted a flexible response strategy.

semanticNote: Things appearing one after another without end — usually problems, scandals, new ideas, or trends. 問題層出不窮 (problems keep coming up), 新產品層出不窮 (new products keep appearing). Often slightly negative connotation (overwhelming).

examples.chinese: 網路詐騙手法層出不窮。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnglù zhàpiàn shǒufǎ céngchūbùqióng.
examples.english: Online scam techniques keep emerging endlessly.

examples.chinese: 科技創新層出不窮，推動著社會不斷進步。
examples.pinyin: Kējì chuàngxīn céngchū-bùqióng, tuīdòngzhe shèhuì bùduàn jìnbù.
examples.english: Technological innovations keep emerging endlessly, driving continuous social progress.

semanticNote: Levels or layers — physical (layered hair: 有層次的髮型), conceptual (層次分明 = clearly structured), social (社會層次 = social strata). Used in design, education, analysis. 沒有層次 = unstructured/flat (criticism of writing or thinking).

examples.chinese: 他的演講很有層次。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjiǎng hěn yǒu céngcì.
examples.english: His speech is well-structured.

examples.chinese: 這幅畫的色彩層次豐富，給人深刻的視覺感受。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà de sècǎi céngcì fēngfù, gěi rén shēnkè de shìjué gǎnshòu.
examples.english: This painting has rich color layers, giving the viewer a profound visual experience.

semanticNote: Difference between two things — neutral observation. 沒有差別 (no difference), 差別待遇 (different treatment, often discriminatory). Compare to 區別 (distinction, often more about kind) and 差異 (difference, formal).

examples.chinese: 這兩個產品沒什麼差別。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge chǎnpǐn méi shénme chābié.
examples.english: There's not much difference between these two products.

examples.chinese: 城鄉之間的教育差別仍然存在。
examples.pinyin: Chéngxiāng zhījiān de jiàoyù chābié réngrán cúnzài.
examples.english: Educational differences between urban and rural areas still persist.

semanticNote: Electrical wall socket. 插頭 = the plug that goes in. Practical everyday word.

examples.chinese: 這個房間沒有足夠的插座。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge fángjiān méiyǒu zúgòu de chāzuò.
examples.english: This room doesn't have enough outlets.

examples.chinese: 出國旅遊時，記得帶轉接插座。
examples.pinyin: Chūguó lǚyóu shí, jìde dài zhuǎnjiē chāzuò.
examples.english: When traveling abroad, remember to bring a plug adapter.

english: to investigate and seize; uncover and capture
semanticNote: Police/investigation word — to discover and seize through investigation. 查獲毒品 (seize drugs in a bust), 查獲走私 (uncover smuggling). News and law enforcement contexts.

examples.chinese: 警方查獲了大量毒品。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng cháhuòle dàliàng dúpǐn.
examples.english: Police seized a large quantity of drugs.

examples.chinese: 海關在行李中查獲了走私的象牙製品。
examples.pinyin: Hǎiguān zài xínglǐ zhōng cháhuòle zǒusī de xiàngyá zhìpǐn.
examples.english: Customs seized smuggled ivory products in the luggage.

semanticNote: A fork in the road or trail. 岔路 = a fork / branch road. 走岔了 = went the wrong way / took a wrong turn. Also figurative: 把話題岔開 = change the subject (steer the conversation off-topic).

examples.chinese: 前面有個岔路。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn yǒu ge chàlù.
examples.english: There's a fork in the road ahead.

examples.chinese: 別岔開話題，說重點。
examples.pinyin: Bié chà kāi huàtí, shuō zhòngdiǎn.
examples.english: Don't stray from the topic — get to the point.

semanticNote: A literary/Buddhist-origin word for an instant — borrowed from Sanskrit kṣaṇa. Used poetically: 那一剎那 (in that instant). More poetic than 瞬間 (similar meaning) and far more poetic than 一下 (a moment).

examples.chinese: 在那一剎那,我明白了一切。
examples.pinyin: Zài nà yí chànà, wǒ míngbáile yíqiè.
examples.english: In that instant, I understood everything.

examples.chinese: 地震發生的剎那，他立刻躲到桌子下面。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn fāshēng de chànà, tā lìkè duǒ dào zhuōzi xiàmiàn.
examples.english: In the instant the earthquake struck, he immediately ducked under the table.

semanticNote: To be surprised in a 'wait, what?' way — confused-surprise rather than amazed. 感到詫異 (feel astonished). Slightly literary; everyday speech uses 驚訝 or 吃驚 more often.

examples.chinese: 聽到這個消息,大家都很詫異。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhè ge xiāoxī, dàjiā dōu hěn chàyì.
examples.english: Everyone was astonished to hear the news.

examples.chinese: 他詫異地看著她，不敢相信自己的耳朵。
examples.pinyin: Tā chàyì de kànzhe tā, bù gǎn xiāngxìn zìjǐ de ěrduo.
examples.english: He looked at her in astonishment, unable to believe his own ears.

semanticNote: Diesel fuel. 柴油車 = diesel vehicle. Everyday-mechanical vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 這輛卡車用柴油。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng kǎchē yòng cháiyóu.
examples.english: This truck runs on diesel.

examples.chinese: 柴油引擎的燃油效率比汽油引擎高。
examples.pinyin: Cháiyóu yǐnqíng de rányóu xiàolǜ bǐ qìyóu yǐnqíng gāo.
examples.english: Diesel engines are more fuel-efficient than gasoline engines.

english: to support by the arm; mix in
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) physically support someone (esp. elderly) by the arm — 攙著奶奶過馬路 (help grandma across the street); (2) mix in / dilute — 攙水 (mix in water, often deceptively in food/wine). Tender for first sense, deceptive for second.

examples.chinese: 他攙扶著老奶奶上樓。
examples.pinyin: Tā chānfúzhe lǎo nǎinai shàng lóu.
examples.english: He helped the old grandma up the stairs.

examples.chinese: 她受了傷，需要別人攙著才能走路。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòule shāng, xūyào biérén chānzhe cái néng zǒulù.
examples.english: She was injured and needed someone to support her in order to walk.

semanticNote: Specifically food-greedy / craving food. 嘴饞 (mouth-greedy = craving snacks), 看著就饞 (looking at it makes me crave). Cute and self-deprecating in casual conversation. Doesn't carry the moral weight of 貪 (greedy, broad/serious).

examples.chinese: 看到蛋糕,我就饞了。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào dàngāo, wǒ jiù chán le.
examples.english: Just seeing the cake makes me crave it.

examples.chinese: 弟弟饞嘴，總是偷吃零食。
examples.pinyin: Dìdi chánzuǐ, zǒngshì tōu chī língshí.
examples.english: My little brother has a sweet tooth and is always sneaking snacks.

semanticNote: To wind around or be tangled — physical (vines around a tree, cord around something) or figurative (problems that keep entangling you, recurring thoughts). 心結纏繞 = entangled heartknots (poetic). Visual word.

examples.chinese: 藤蔓纏繞在樹上。
examples.pinyin: Téngmàn chánrào zài shù shàng.
examples.english: The vines wind around the tree.

examples.chinese: 電線纏繞在一起，很危險，需要整理一下。
examples.pinyin: Diànxiàn chánrào zài yìqǐ, hěn wēixiǎn, xūyào zhěnglǐ yíxià.
examples.english: The wires are tangled together, which is dangerous and needs to be sorted out.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) an industry/sector — 文化產業 (cultural industry), 旅遊產業 (tourism industry); (2) personal property/estate — 家族產業 (family estate). The 'industry' sense dominates in modern business writing.

examples.chinese: 科技產業發展迅速。
examples.pinyin: Kējì chǎnyè fāzhǎn xùnsù.
examples.english: The tech industry is developing rapidly.

examples.chinese: 文化產業是帶動地方經濟的重要力量。
examples.pinyin: Wénhuà chǎnyè shì dàidòng dìfāng jīngjì de zhòngyào lìliàng.
examples.english: The cultural industry is an important force in driving the local economy.

english: expound; elaborate; set forth (a position or argument)
semanticNote: Formal-register verb for laying out an idea, argument, or position in detail. 闡 means to illuminate or clarify; 述 means to state or narrate — together: systematically explain. Used in academic writing, speeches, policy documents, and formal presentations. 請闡述您的觀點 = Please elaborate on your perspective. More formal and thorough than 說明 (explain) or 解釋 (explain/justify). You wouldn't use 闡述 to explain why you were late for dinner.

examples.chinese: 教授在課堂上詳細闡述了這個理論。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoshòu zài kètáng shàng xiángxì chǎnshùle zhège lǐlùn.
examples.english: The professor expounded on this theory in detail in class.

examples.chinese: 請闡述你對這項政策的看法。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng chǎnshù nǐ duì zhè xiàng zhèngcè de kànfǎ.
examples.english: Please elaborate on your views on this policy.

semanticNote: To tremble — from cold, fear, anger, weakness. 全身顫抖 (whole body trembling). More dramatic than 抖 (shake). Often appears in emotional descriptions.

examples.chinese: 他害怕得渾身顫抖。
examples.pinyin: Tā hàipà de húnshēn chàndǒu.
examples.english: He was so scared his whole body trembled.

examples.chinese: 寒風吹來，她冷得顫抖了起來。
examples.pinyin: Hánfēng chuī lái, tā lěng de chàndǒule qǐlái.
examples.english: When the cold wind blew in, she began to shiver from the cold.

semanticNote: Prosperous and thriving — usually used for nations, eras, families, businesses on a grand scale. 國家昌盛 (the country prospers), 繁榮昌盛 (prosperous and flourishing — set phrase). Formal, often in patriotic and ceremonial contexts.

examples.chinese: 祝願祖國繁榮昌盛。
examples.pinyin: Zhùyuàn zǔguó fánróng chāngshèng.
examples.english: May the motherland prosper and flourish.

examples.chinese: 文化的昌盛需要幾代人的共同努力。
examples.pinyin: Wénhuà de chāngshèng xūyào jǐ dài rén de gòngtóng nǔlì.
examples.english: The flourishing of culture requires the joint effort of several generations.

semanticNote: To try something — a method, an approach, a new experience. Slightly more deliberate than 試試 (give it a try, casual). 大膽嘗試 (boldly try). Common in inspirational and exploratory contexts.

examples.chinese: 我想嘗試新的工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chángshì xīn de gōngzuò.
examples.english: I want to try a new job.

examples.chinese: 失敗了不要緊，重要的是勇於嘗試。
examples.pinyin: Shībài le bùyàojǐn, zhòngyào de shì yǒngyú chángshì.
examples.english: Failure doesn't matter — what's important is having the courage to try.

semanticNote: To repay a debt — financial or moral. 償還貸款 (repay a loan), 償還人情 (repay a favor/kindness). Formal, often legal/financial.

examples.chinese: 他終於償還了所有的債務。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú chánghuánle suǒyǒu de zhàiwù.
examples.english: He finally repaid all his debts.

examples.chinese: 她每月分期償還助學貸款。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi yuè fēnqī chánghuán zhùxué dàikuǎn.
examples.english: She repays her student loan in monthly installments.

semanticNote: The social context or occasion that dictates appropriate behavior. 正式場合 = formal occasion; 公開場合 = public setting; 不合時宜的場合 = an inappropriate occasion. Emphasizes the situational appropriateness angle — what's right for THIS occasion. Different from 場面 (which is about the visual spectacle of a scene) and 情況 (which is about the circumstances of a situation, more neutral). 場合 always carries a 'know how to act here' implication.

examples.chinese: 在正式場合說話要注意禮節。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhèngshì chǎnghé shuōhuà yào zhùyì lǐjié.
examples.english: In formal settings you need to mind your etiquette.

examples.chinese: 他不太懂得看場合說話。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú tài dǒngdé kàn chǎnghé shuōhuà.
examples.english: He doesn't really know how to read the room when he speaks.

semanticNote: The visual impression or spectacle of a scene. 壯觀的場面 (a magnificent spectacle), 感人的場面 (a moving scene), 尷尬的場面 (an awkward scene). Also used figuratively for 'saving face' or maintaining appearances: 撐場面 (maintain a grand appearance/face). Different from 場合 (which is about appropriate context) — 場面 is about what you see and the impression it creates. Common in film, literary, and news contexts.

examples.chinese: 婚禮的場面非常壯觀，賓客多達五百人。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ de chǎngmiàn fēicháng zhuàngguān, bīnkè duō dá wǔ bǎi rén.
examples.english: The wedding was a magnificent spectacle — over five hundred guests.

examples.chinese: 那個感人的場面讓很多人流下了眼淚。
examples.pinyin: Nàge gǎnrén de chǎngmiàn ràng hěn duō rén liúxiàle yǎnlèi.
examples.english: That moving scene brought many people to tears.

semanticNote: A specific place/venue, often categorized by purpose. 公共場所 (public place), 娛樂場所 (entertainment venue), 工作場所 (workplace). More formal than 地方 (place, generic). Common in regulations and signs.

examples.chinese: 請在公共場所保持安靜。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ bǎochí ānjìng.
examples.english: Please keep quiet in public places.

examples.chinese: 圖書館是適合讀書和思考的場所。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn shì shìhé dúshū hé sīkǎo de chǎngsuǒ.
examples.english: A library is a place well-suited for reading and thinking.

english: to open wide; (figurative) open up freely
semanticNote: To open wide — physically (敞開大門 = open the door wide) or figuratively (敞開心扉 = open one's heart, 敞開心懷 = open up emotionally). Welcoming, generous flavor.

examples.chinese: 請敞開心扉,告訴我你的想法。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng chǎngkāi xīnfēi, gàosù wǒ nǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: Please open up and tell me your thoughts.

examples.chinese: 她敞開房門迎接每一位來訪的客人。
examples.pinyin: Tā chǎngkāi fángmén yíngjiē měi yī wèi lái fǎng de kèrén.
examples.english: She threw open the door to welcome every visitor.

semanticNote: Unblocked and flowing freely — traffic (道路暢通 = clear road), communication (信息暢通 = info flows freely). 24小時暢通 = available 24/7 (often for hotlines). Implies smooth, unobstructed function.

examples.chinese: 早上的交通很暢通。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshàng de jiāotōng hěn chàngtōng.
examples.english: Morning traffic was flowing smoothly.

examples.chinese: 確保信息暢通是管理一支大型團隊的關鍵。
examples.pinyin: Quèbǎo xìnxī chàngtōng shì guǎnlǐ yī zhī dàxíng tuánduì de guānjiàn.
examples.english: Ensuring free flow of information is the key to managing a large team.

semanticNote: Selling fast/well — 暢銷書 (bestseller), 暢銷產品 (bestselling product), 暢銷海外 (sells well overseas). Marketing vocabulary. Suggests high demand and broad appeal.

examples.chinese: 這本書是今年的暢銷書。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū shì jīnnián de chàngxiāo shū.
examples.english: This book is this year's bestseller.

examples.chinese: 這款手機一上市就暢銷全球。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī yī shàngshì jiù chàngxiāo quánqiú.
examples.english: This phone model became a global bestseller as soon as it was released.

semanticNote: To advocate for an idea, behavior, or cause — environmental protection, healthy living, equality. 倡導環保 (advocate for environmentalism). Public/social register, common in NGO and government rhetoric.

examples.chinese: 他一直倡導環保生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí chàngdǎo huánbǎo shēnghuó.
examples.english: He has long advocated for an eco-friendly lifestyle.

examples.chinese: 學校積極倡導同學之間互相尊重的文化。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào jījí chàngdǎo tóngxué zhījiān hùxiāng zūnzhòng de wénhuà.
examples.english: The school actively promotes a culture of mutual respect among students.

semanticNote: To propose / initiate (an idea or movement); also the proposal itself. 倡議書 (proposal letter), 一帶一路倡議 (Belt and Road Initiative). Slightly more action-flavored than 建議 (suggestion). Often used for collective initiatives.

examples.chinese: 她倡議大家一起參加義工活動。
examples.pinyin: Tā chàngyì dàjiā yìqǐ cānjiā yìgōng huódòng.
examples.english: She proposed that everyone join the volunteer activity together.

examples.chinese: 這項保護野生動物的倡議得到了各界響應。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng bǎohù yěshēng dòngwù de chàngyì dédàole gèjiè xiǎngyìng.
examples.english: This wildlife protection initiative received responses from all sectors of society.

semanticNote: Paper currency, bills. 一張鈔票 = one bill. Slightly more old-school as digital payments dominate, but still used. 鈔票 emphasizes the physical bills as opposed to digital money.

examples.chinese: 他從錢包裡拿出一張鈔票。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng qiánbāo lǐ ná chū yì zhāng chāopiào.
examples.english: He took a bill out of his wallet.

examples.chinese: 假鈔流通是嚴重的犯罪行為。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎchāo liútōng shì yánzhòng de fànzuì xíngwéi.
examples.english: Circulating counterfeit bills is a serious criminal offense.

semanticNote: To go beyond — exceed expectations (超越期望), surpass a competitor (超越對手), transcend limits (超越極限). Slightly grand/aspirational flavor. Common in motivational and competitive contexts.

examples.chinese: 他超越了所有的對手。
examples.pinyin: Tā chāoyuèle suǒyǒu de duìshǒu.
examples.english: He surpassed all his competitors.

examples.chinese: 藝術的力量在於超越語言的障礙，直達人心。
examples.pinyin: Yìshù de lìliàng zàiyú chāoyuè yǔyán de zhàng'ài, zhí dá rénxīn.
examples.english: The power of art lies in transcending language barriers to reach the heart directly.

semanticNote: Animal lair / criminal hideout. 動物的巢穴 (animal's lair), 罪犯的巢穴 (criminal hideout). The figurative 'criminal hideout' sense is common in news and crime stories.

examples.chinese: 警方搗毀了犯罪集團的巢穴。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dǎohuǐle fànzuì jítuán de cháoxué.
examples.english: Police destroyed the criminal gang's hideout.

examples.chinese: 老鷹築巢於山頂，巢穴外人難以接近。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoyīng zhùcháo yú shāndǐng, cháoxué wàirén nán yǐ jiējìn.
examples.english: Eagles build their nests at mountaintops, their eyries hard for outsiders to reach.

semanticNote: A historical Chinese dynasty — 唐朝 (Tang), 宋朝 (Song), etc. 朝代更替 (dynasties replacing each other). Essential vocabulary for any discussion of Chinese history.

examples.chinese: 中國歷史上有許多朝代。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng yǒu xǔduō cháodài.
examples.english: There were many dynasties in Chinese history.

examples.chinese: 漢朝和唐朝是中國歷史上最輝煌的兩個朝代。
examples.pinyin: Hàncháo hé Tángcháo shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng zuì huīhuáng de liǎng gè cháodài.
examples.english: The Han and Tang Dynasties were the two most glorious dynasties in Chinese history.

english: to mock; ridicule; make fun of
semanticNote: To laugh at someone in a mocking way. Negative — implies cruelty or condescension. 不要嘲笑別人 (don't mock others). Compare to 取笑 (tease, can be playful) — 嘲笑 is meaner.

examples.chinese: 同學們嘲笑他的口音。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen cháoxiào tā de kǒuyīn.
examples.english: His classmates mocked his accent.

examples.chinese: 不應嘲笑別人的失敗，每個人都有努力的過程。
examples.pinyin: Bù yīng cháoxiào biérén de shībài, měi gè rén dōu yǒu nǔlì de guòchéng.
examples.english: One should not mock others' failures — everyone goes through a process of striving.

semanticNote: Trends, currents, social movements. 跟上潮流 (keep up with the trend), 時尚潮流 (fashion trend), 時代潮流 (current of the times). Originally referred to ocean currents — figurative use now dominates.

examples.chinese: 這個年輕人總是走在潮流前面。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge niánqīngrén zǒngshì zǒu zài cháoliú qiánmiàn.
examples.english: This young man is always ahead of the trend.

examples.chinese: 環保意識已成為全球社會的主要潮流之一。
examples.pinyin: Huánbǎo yìshí yǐ chéngwéi quánqiú shèhuì de zhǔyào cháoliú zhī yī.
examples.english: Environmental consciousness has become one of the dominant trends in global society.

semanticNote: Military retreat — withdrawing forces from a position. By extension: companies pulling out of a market, individuals stepping back from a situation. 戰略性撤退 (strategic retreat).

examples.chinese: 軍隊被迫撤退。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì bèipò chètuì.
examples.english: The army was forced to retreat.

examples.chinese: 颱風接近時，島上的居民紛紛撤退到安全地點。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng jiējìn shí, dǎo shàng de jūmín fēnfēn chètuì dào ānquán dìdiǎn.
examples.english: As the typhoon approached, the island's residents evacuated one after another to safe locations.

semanticNote: Officially cancel — orders, decisions, licenses, lawsuits, posts. 撤銷職務 (remove from post), 撤銷指控 (drop charges). Formal, legal/administrative register.

examples.chinese: 法院決定撤銷這項判決。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn juédìng chèxiāo zhè xiàng pànjué.
examples.english: The court decided to overturn this ruling.

examples.chinese: 由於行為不當，他的執照被撤銷了。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyú xíngwéi bùdàng, tā de zhízhào bèi chèxiāo le.
examples.english: Due to improper conduct, his license was revoked.

semanticNote: Chemistry-origin: precipitation/sediment settling out of solution. Figurative use is wonderful: 文化的沉澱 (cultural sediment / accumulated cultural depth), 沉澱下來 (let things settle / let your mind clear). Often used for emotional/intellectual settling.

examples.chinese: 讓思緒沉澱一下,再做決定。
examples.pinyin: Ràng sīxù chéndiàn yíxià, zài zuò juédìng.
examples.english: Let your thoughts settle before making a decision.

examples.chinese: 泥水靜置後，雜質會慢慢沉澱到底部。
examples.pinyin: Níshuǐ jìngzhì hòu, zázhì huì mànmàn chéndiàn dào dǐbù.
examples.english: After muddy water is left to stand, impurities slowly settle to the bottom.

semanticNote: Heavy, suffocating atmosphere — physical (沉悶的天氣 = oppressive weather) or emotional (沉悶的會議 = a stifling meeting, 心情沉悶 = depressed mood). Implies stuffy and unable to breathe — applies to rooms, weather, and moods alike.

examples.chinese: 這場會議氣氛很沉悶。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng huìyì qìfēn hěn chénmèn.
examples.english: The atmosphere of this meeting was oppressive.

examples.chinese: 沉悶的天氣讓人提不起精神來。
examples.pinyin: Chénmèn de tiānqì ràng rén tí bù qǐ jīngshén lái.
examples.english: The oppressive weather makes it hard to feel energetic.

semanticNote: Deep reflective thought — heavier than 思考 (think). Implies stillness, slowness, depth. 陷入沉思 (fall into deep thought). Literary register; conjures images of someone staring out a window thinking about life.

examples.chinese: 他陷入了沉思。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiànrùle chénsī.
examples.english: He fell into deep thought.

examples.chinese: 她沉思片刻，然後給出了一個深刻的回答。
examples.pinyin: Tā chénsī piànkè, ránhòu gěi chū le yīgè shēnkè de huídá.
examples.english: She paused in thought for a moment, then gave a profound answer.

semanticNote: Heavy — physically (沉重的行李 = heavy luggage) or emotionally (心情沉重 = heavy heart, 沉重的責任 = heavy responsibility). The emotional sense dominates in modern usage. Compare to 重 (just heavy, neutral) — 沉重 carries gravity.

examples.chinese: 他懷著沉重的心情離開。
examples.pinyin: Tā huáizhe chénzhòng de xīnqíng líkāi.
examples.english: He left with a heavy heart.

examples.chinese: 他肩上的責任十分沉重，幾乎讓他喘不過氣。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiān shàng de zérèn shífēn chénzhòng, jīhū ràng tā chuǎn bù guòqì.
examples.english: The responsibilities on his shoulders are extremely heavy, almost making it hard to breathe.

semanticNote: Composure under pressure — remaining calm when things are urgent or dangerous. 沈著冷靜 is a common pairing. Often used to praise someone who handled a crisis without panicking: 他非常沈著，沒有慌亂。Differs from 冷靜 (calm/rational — more about clear thinking) in that 沈著 specifically emphasizes physical and emotional steadiness under fire. A 沈著 person is unflappable; 冷靜 describes their reasoning process.

examples.chinese: 面對突發狀況，她非常沈著，迅速做出了正確判斷。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì tūfā zhuàngkuàng, tā fēicháng chénzhuó, xùnsù zuòchūle zhèngquè pànduàn.
examples.english: Faced with the sudden emergency, she stayed completely calm and quickly made the right call.

examples.chinese: 優秀的外科醫生必須沈著冷靜。
examples.pinyin: Yōuxiù de wàikē yīshēng bìxū chénzhuó lěngjìng.
examples.english: An excellent surgeon must be calm and composed.

semanticNote: Old-fashioned and out of date — applied to things or ideas. 陳舊的觀念 (outdated ideas), 陳舊的設備 (old/obsolete equipment). Slightly negative — implies the thing should be updated/replaced.

examples.chinese: 這些設備已經陳舊了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shèbèi yǐjīng chénjiù le.
examples.english: This equipment is already obsolete.

examples.chinese: 他的思想比較陳舊，難以接受新的觀念。
examples.pinyin: Tā de sīxiǎng bǐjiào chénjiù, nányǐ jiēshòu xīn de guānniàn.
examples.english: His thinking is rather old-fashioned, making it hard for him to accept new ideas.

semanticNote: To display items for viewing — in shops, museums, exhibitions. 陳列商品 (display goods), 陳列櫃 (display case). Different from 展覽 (exhibition, more event-focused) — 陳列 is the static arrangement.

examples.chinese: 博物館陳列著珍貴的文物。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn chénlièzhe zhēnguì de wénwù.
examples.english: The museum displays precious cultural artifacts.

examples.chinese: 商場裡的商品被精心陳列，吸引了許多顧客駐足觀看。
examples.pinyin: Shāngchǎng lǐ de shāngpǐn bèi jīngxīn chénliè, xīyǐnle xǔduō gùkè zhùzú guānkàn.
examples.english: The goods in the mall were carefully arranged, attracting many customers to stop and look.

semanticNote: To formally state — in court, official meetings, declarations. 陳述事實 (state the facts), 陳述意見 (state one's opinion). More formal than 說 (say) or 描述 (describe). Legal/official register.

examples.chinese: 證人在法庭上陳述了事實。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngrén zài fǎtíng shàng chénshùle shìshí.
examples.english: The witness stated the facts in court.

examples.chinese: 請就你的立場作出清楚的陳述。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiù nǐ de lìchǎng zuòchū qīngchǔ de chénshù.
examples.english: Please make a clear statement of your position.

english: to set off; serve as a foil
semanticNote: To set something off / make something stand out by contrast. Common in design and writing: 紅花需要綠葉襯托 (red flowers need green leaves to set them off — well-known saying about supporting roles). Aesthetic word.

examples.chinese: 綠色的牆襯托出畫的美。
examples.pinyin: Lǜsè de qiáng chèntuō chū huà de měi.
examples.english: The green wall sets off the beauty of the painting.

examples.chinese: 白色的婚紗更襯托出新娘的氣質。
examples.pinyin: Báisè de hūnshā gèng chèntuō chū xīnniáng de qìzhì.
examples.english: The white wedding dress further accentuates the bride's elegance.

semanticNote: 'Matching the heart, in line with intent' — when something turns out exactly as you hoped. Common in well-wishes: 祝你稱心如意 (wishing you everything you wish for). Positive, often used in greetings and reflections on luck.

examples.chinese: 祝你新的一年稱心如意。
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ xīn de yì nián chènxīnrúyì.
examples.english: Wishing you a new year that fulfills all your wishes.

examples.chinese: 找到稱心如意的工作，不是件容易的事。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎodào chènxīn-rúyì de gōngzuò, bù shì jiàn róngyì de shì.
examples.english: Finding a job that truly satisfies you is not an easy thing.

semanticNote: An official title or designation — honorific, sports champion, professional certification. 獲得冠軍稱號 (earn the champion title). Different from 名稱 (name of something) — 稱號 implies earned/bestowed status.

examples.chinese: 她獲得了世界冠軍的稱號。
examples.pinyin: Tā huòdéle shìjiè guànjūn de chēnghào.
examples.english: She earned the title of world champion.

examples.chinese: 他因長期投入公益而獲得了「社區英雄」的稱號。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn chángqī tóurù gōngyì ér huòdéle "shèqū yīngxióng" de chēnghào.
examples.english: He earned the title of "Community Hero" for his long-term dedication to public welfare.

semanticNote: Cost — manufacturing, production, opportunity. 降低成本 (lower costs), 機會成本 (opportunity cost), 時間成本 (time cost). Business and economics vocabulary, also extends to personal cost-benefit thinking.

examples.chinese: 我們需要降低生產成本。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào jiàngdī shēngchǎn chéngběn.
examples.english: We need to lower production costs.

examples.chinese: 這家公司通過自動化顯著降低了成本。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī tōngguò zìdònghuà xiǎnzhù jiàngdīle chéngběn.
examples.english: This company significantly reduced costs through automation.

english: to close a deal; finalize a transaction
semanticNote: Deal closed, transaction finalized — markets, real estate, sales. 成交價 (closing price), 成交量 (transaction volume). Auction-style 'Sold!' moment. Common in business and stock-market vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 這筆生意終於成交了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ shēngyì zhōngyú chéngjiāo le.
examples.english: This deal finally closed.

examples.chinese: 雙方經過多輪談判，才在最終合約上成交。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng jīngguò duō lún tánpàn, cái zài zuìzhōng héyuē shàng chéngjiāo.
examples.english: After multiple rounds of negotiation, both parties finally closed the deal on the final contract.

semanticNote: 'All day' / 'constantly' — slightly negative or exasperated tone. 成天打遊戲 (gaming all day), 成天抱怨 (complaining all the time). Often used in parental complaints. Compare to 整天 (all day, more neutral).

examples.chinese: 他成天躺在沙發上。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngtiān tǎng zài shāfā shàng.
examples.english: He lies on the couch all day long.

examples.chinese: 她成天抱怨，讓周圍的人都很煩。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngtiān bàoyuàn, ràng zhōuwéi de rén dōu hěn fán.
examples.english: She complains all day long, annoying everyone around her.

semanticNote: Tangible results from effort. 顯著的成效 (notable results), 沒有成效 (no results / ineffective). More formal than 效果 (effect). Common in evaluation contexts: did the policy / strategy / treatment actually work?

examples.chinese: 這個政策初見成效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zhèngcè chū jiàn chéngxiào.
examples.english: This policy is starting to show results.

examples.chinese: 改革措施取得了顯著成效，犯罪率明顯下降。
examples.pinyin: Gǎigé cuòshī qǔdéle xiǎnzhù chéngxiào, fànzuìlǜ míngxiǎn xiàjiàng.
examples.english: The reform measures achieved significant results, with crime rates dropping noticeably.
