semanticNote: Deliberately, on purpose — usually with negative implication of intent to annoy or harm. 你是不是成心的？ (Did you do that on purpose?). Compare to 故意 (intentional, similar) — 成心 is slightly more accusatory, more colloquial.

examples.chinese: 你成心氣我嗎？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chéngxīn qì wǒ ma?
examples.english: Are you trying to make me mad on purpose?

examples.chinese: 他成心說這些刺耳的話，想讓她難堪。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngxīn shuō zhèxiē cì ěr de huà, xiǎng ràng tā nánkān.
examples.english: He deliberately said those harsh words to embarrass her.

semanticNote: Member of a group, family, organization. 家庭成員 (family member), 團隊成員 (team member). Standard formal word. More formal than 會員 (member, often paid/registered).

examples.chinese: 我們團隊有十位成員。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tuánduì yǒu shí wèi chéngyuán.
examples.english: Our team has ten members.

examples.chinese: 這個委員會由五位來自不同領域的成員組成。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wěiyuánhuì yóu wǔ wèi láizì bùtóng lǐngyù de chéngyuán zǔchéng.
examples.english: This committee is made up of five members from different fields.

semanticNote: To display or show (a particular state/condition/appearance). 呈現出新面貌 (present a new look), 數據呈現上升趨勢 (data shows an upward trend). Slightly formal/literary. Common in news, analysis, and design.

examples.chinese: 這個城市呈現出全新的面貌。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge chéngshì chéngxiàn chū quánxīn de miànmào.
examples.english: This city now shows a brand-new face.

examples.chinese: 這位藝術家的作品呈現出濃厚的民間風格。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yìshùjiā de zuòpǐn chéngxiàn chū nónghòu de mínjiān fēnggé.
examples.english: This artist's works display a strong folk style.

semanticNote: Sincere and warm — used for greetings, thanks, condolences. 誠摯的祝福 (sincere blessings), 誠摯地感謝 (sincerely thank). Slightly formal/written. Common in cards, speeches, official letters.

examples.chinese: 我向您致以誠摯的祝賀。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàng nín zhì yǐ chéngzhì de zhùhè.
examples.english: I extend my sincere congratulations to you.

examples.chinese: 他的歉意是誠摯的，大家都感受到了他的誠意。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qiànyì shì chéngzhì de, dàjiā dōu gǎnshòu dàole tā de chéngyì.
examples.english: His apology was heartfelt, and everyone could feel his sincerity.

semanticNote: To take on the responsibility of organizing/handling something — events, contracts, legal matters. 承辦活動 (host/organize an event), 承辦案件 (take on a case). Formal/business context.

examples.chinese: 我們公司承辦了這次大會。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī chéngbànle zhè cì dàhuì.
examples.english: Our company organized this conference.

examples.chinese: 臺灣承辦過多次國際性的體育賽事。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān chéngbàn guò duō cì guójìxìng de tǐyù sàishì.
examples.english: Taiwan has hosted many international sporting events.

semanticNote: To take on a contract — construction, services, projects. 承包商 (contractor). Distinguished from 承辦 — 承包 specifically involves contractual / financial responsibility for the whole job.

examples.chinese: 他承包了這個建築工程。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngbāole zhè ge jiànzhù gōngchéng.
examples.english: He contracted to do this construction project.

examples.chinese: 小包商向大公司承包了這批訂單的生產工作。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo bāoshāng xiàng dà gōngsī chéngbāole zhè pī dìngdān de shēngchǎn gōngzuò.
examples.english: The small contractor took on the production of this batch of orders from the large company.

semanticNote: A formal promise/commitment — heavier than 答應 (agree). Both verb (to promise) and noun (a commitment). 信守承諾 (keep one's promise), 政府的承諾 (government commitments). Carries weight of obligation.

examples.chinese: 他承諾會準時完成。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngnuò huì zhǔnshí wánchéng.
examples.english: He promised to finish on time.

examples.chinese: 公司承諾在三十天內全額退款給不滿意的顧客。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī chéngnuò zài sānshí tiān nèi quán'é tuìkuǎn gěi bù mǎnyì de gùkè.
examples.english: The company promises to give a full refund to unsatisfied customers within thirty days.

semanticNote: Castle — usually European-style. Storybook and tourism vocabulary. Chinese fortified buildings are more often 城 (walled city) or 堡壘 (fortress). 沙堡 = sandcastle.

examples.chinese: 歐洲有許多古老的城堡。
examples.pinyin: Ōuzhōu yǒu xǔduō gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
examples.english: Europe has many ancient castles.

examples.chinese: 他們在英格蘭住了一晚上風景如畫的城堡酒店。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài Yīnggélán zhùle yī wǎnshàng fēngjǐng-rúhuà de chéngbǎo jiǔdiàn.
examples.english: They spent a night at a picturesque castle hotel in England.

english: to ride; multiply; take advantage of
semanticNote: Multi-sense verb: (1) to ride (a vehicle) — 乘車 (take a vehicle), 乘飛機 (take a plane), formal register; (2) math — to multiply (二乘三 = two times three); (3) to take advantage of an opportunity — 乘機 (seize the opportunity), 乘人之危 (take advantage of someone in trouble).

examples.chinese: 他乘飛機去北京。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéng fēijī qù Běijīng.
examples.english: He took a plane to Beijing.

examples.chinese: 四乘以五等於二十。
examples.pinyin: Sì chéng yǐ wǔ děngyú èrshí.
examples.english: Four times five equals twenty.

english: (chéng) to ladle out; contain | (shèng) flourishing; grand
semanticNote: True heteronym: (1) chéng — to ladle/scoop into a container, 盛飯 (serve rice into a bowl), 盛湯 (ladle soup); (2) shèng — flourishing, abundant, grand: 盛大 (grand), 盛開 (in full bloom), 盛行 (prevalent). Same character, two completely different lives.

examples.chinese: 她盛了一碗湯給我。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngle yì wǎn tāng gěi wǒ.
examples.english: She ladled a bowl of soup for me.

examples.chinese: 花園裡的花盛開著。
examples.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ de huā shèngkāi zhe.
examples.english: The flowers in the garden are in full bloom.

semanticNote: Punishment — official or informal. 嚴厲的懲罰 (harsh punishment), 受到懲罰 (be punished). Heavier than 罰 alone. Used in legal, parental, and pedagogical contexts.

examples.chinese: 作弊的學生會受到懲罰。
examples.pinyin: Zuòbì de xuéshēng huì shòudào chéngfá.
examples.english: Students who cheat will be punished.

examples.chinese: 如果違反交通規則，將受到相應的懲罰。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ wéifǎn jiāotōng guīzé, jiāng shòudào xiāngyìng de chéngfá.
examples.english: If you violate traffic rules, you will receive the corresponding penalty.

semanticNote: Originally a chemistry term (clarify a liquid). Modern dominant sense: to clarify a misunderstanding, set the record straight. 澄清謠言 (refute a rumor), 澄清事實 (clarify the facts). Public-statement vocabulary — celebrities and officials 澄清 stuff constantly.

examples.chinese: 他發聲明澄清了傳聞。
examples.pinyin: Tā fā shēngmíng chéngqīngle chuánwén.
examples.english: He issued a statement to clear up the rumors.

examples.chinese: 請務必澄清這個誤會，否則後果難以預料。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng wùbì chéngqīng zhège wùhuì, fǒuzé hòuguǒ nányǐ yùliào.
examples.english: Be sure to clear up this misunderstanding, otherwise the consequences will be hard to predict.

semanticNote: Orange — fruit and color. 橙汁 (orange juice), 橙色 (orange color). In Taiwan, 柳橙 is more common for the fruit; mainland uses 橙子. Fruit names often vary by region.

examples.chinese: 早餐我喜歡喝橙汁。
examples.pinyin: Zǎocān wǒ xǐhuān hē chéngzhī.
examples.english: I like to have orange juice for breakfast.

examples.chinese: 她穿著一件橙色的外套，非常顯眼。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yī jiàn chéngsè de wàitào, fēicháng xiǎnyǎn.
examples.english: She was wearing an orange jacket and stood out very noticeably.

semanticNote: A weighing scale. 體重秤 (bathroom scale), 電子秤 (digital scale). Practical everyday object.

examples.chinese: 請把蘋果放在秤上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ píngguǒ fàng zài chèng shàng.
examples.english: Please put the apples on the scale.

examples.chinese: 市場上賣菜的攤販用秤來計算菜的重量和價格。
examples.pinyin: Shìchǎng shàng mài cài de tānfàn yòng chèng lái jìsuàn cài de zhòngliàng hé jiàgé.
examples.english: Vegetable vendors in the market use a scale to calculate the weight and price of produce.

semanticNote: Literally 'eat bitter' — to endure hardship. Deeply cultural concept: 能吃苦 (able to eat bitter / tough enough to handle hardship) is a high compliment. 吃苦耐勞 (able to endure hardship and labor) is a chengyu of work ethic. Foundational Chinese ethic of suffering as character-building.

examples.chinese: 年輕時應該多吃點苦。
examples.pinyin: Niánqīng shí yīnggāi duō chī diǎn kǔ.
examples.english: When you're young, you should endure more hardship.

examples.chinese: 她從不怕吃苦，再難的事都咬緊牙關撐過去。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng bù pà chīkǔ, zài nán de shì dōu yǎo jǐn yá guān chēng guòqù.
examples.english: She never fears hardship — no matter how difficult things get, she grits her teeth and pushes through.

semanticNote: Effortful — describes work, tasks, or learning that requires strain. 學起來很吃力 (a struggle to learn), 吃力的工作 (demanding work). Compare to 累 (tired, the result) — 吃力 is the quality of being tough to do.

examples.chinese: 這個工作對我來說很吃力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gōngzuò duì wǒ lái shuō hěn chīlì.
examples.english: This job is really demanding for me.

examples.chinese: 他扛著沉重的行李爬樓梯，看起來很吃力。
examples.pinyin: Tā káng zhe chénzhòng de xínglǐ pá lóutī, kàn qǐlái hěn chīlì.
examples.english: He was lugging heavy luggage up the stairs — it looked really strenuous.

semanticNote: Slow in perception, reaction, or thought. 反應遲鈍 (slow to react), 感覺遲鈍 (insensitive). Slightly negative — describes being slow in a way that's a problem. Compare to 笨 (stupid, harsher).

examples.chinese: 他對人情世故有點遲鈍。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì rénqíng shìgù yǒu diǎn chídùn.
examples.english: He's a bit slow at picking up social cues.

examples.chinese: 天冷手腳會遲鈍，要多注意安全。
examples.pinyin: Tiān lěng shǒujiǎo huì chídùn, yào duō zhùyì ānquán.
examples.english: In cold weather, hands and feet can become sluggish — be extra careful.

semanticNote: Slow in pace — economic growth, project progress, response time. 行動遲緩 (slow movement), 進展遲緩 (sluggish progress). Used analytically, often with concern. Compare to 慢 (slow, neutral) — 遲緩 implies slower than expected/desired.

examples.chinese: 政府的反應太遲緩了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ de fǎnyìng tài chíhuǎn le.
examples.english: The government's response was too slow.

examples.chinese: 老人動作遲緩，過馬路需要更多的時間。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén dòngzuò chíhuǎn, guò mǎlù xūyào gèngduō de shíjiān.
examples.english: Elderly people move slowly and need more time to cross the road.

semanticNote: To hesitate — pause due to doubt or indecision. 毫不遲疑 (without hesitation). Slightly more literary than 猶豫 (hesitate). Both work in similar contexts.

examples.chinese: 他毫不遲疑地答應了。
examples.pinyin: Tā háobù chíyí de dāyìng le.
examples.english: He agreed without hesitation.

examples.chinese: 面對那個艱難的決定，她遲疑了很久。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì nà ge jiānnán de juédìng, tā chíyíle hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: Faced with that difficult decision, she hesitated for a long time.

semanticNote: Long-lasting — energy, motivation, effects, relationships. 持久戰 (a long war / drawn-out battle), 持久的友誼 (enduring friendship). Implies endurance through time, not just length.

examples.chinese: 我們需要持久的努力才能成功。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào chíjiǔ de nǔlì cáinéng chénggōng.
examples.english: We need sustained effort to succeed.

examples.chinese: 要保持健康，需要持久的運動習慣，而非一時的熱情。
examples.pinyin: Yào bǎochí jiànkāng, xūyào chíjiǔ de yùndòng xíguàn, ér fēi yīshí de rèqíng.
examples.english: To stay healthy, you need sustained exercise habits, not just a temporary burst of enthusiasm.

semanticNote: The equator. Geography vocabulary. 赤道附近 = near the equator.

examples.chinese: 新加坡靠近赤道,氣候炎熱。
examples.pinyin: Xīnjiāpō kàojìn chìdào, qìhòu yánrè.
examples.english: Singapore is near the equator, with a hot climate.

examples.chinese: 赤道附近的地區常年溫度高，降雨量也豐富。
examples.pinyin: Chìdào fùjìn de dìqū chánnián wēndù gāo, jiàngyǔliàng yě fēngfù.
examples.english: Areas near the equator have high temperatures and abundant rainfall year-round.

semanticNote: Financial deficit — government budget, trade balance. Etymology: 赤 (red) + 字 (writing) — 'red ink,' the color used for losses in old accounting. 財政赤字 = fiscal deficit. Economics and news vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 政府正面臨嚴重的赤字。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèng miànlín yánzhòng de chìzì.
examples.english: The government is facing a serious deficit.

examples.chinese: 連年赤字使得這家公司不得不宣告破產。
examples.pinyin: Lián nián chìzì shǐdé zhè jiā gōngsī bùdébù xuāngào pòchǎn.
examples.english: Years of deficits forced this company to declare bankruptcy.

semanticNote: Both noun (an impulse, urge) and adjective (impulsive). 衝動消費 (impulse buying), 不要衝動 (don't be rash). Often warned against — Chinese culture values measured, deliberate action. 一時衝動 = a moment of impulsiveness.

examples.chinese: 我衝動之下買了這輛車。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chōngdòng zhī xià mǎile zhè liàng chē.
examples.english: I bought this car on impulse.

examples.chinese: 凡事要冷靜思考，不要一時衝動做決定。
examples.pinyin: Fánshì yào lěngjìng sīkǎo, bùyào yīshí chōngdòng zuò juédìng.
examples.english: Think calmly about everything — don't make decisions on a sudden impulse.

semanticNote: Impact — physical (waves crashing) or figurative (cultural shock, economic impact). 文化衝擊 (culture shock), 受到衝擊 (be impacted). Common in news and analysis discussing how events affect society.

examples.chinese: 這個消息對市場帶來巨大衝擊。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiāoxī duì shìchǎng dàilái jùdà chōngjī.
examples.english: This news brought a huge impact on the market.

examples.chinese: 颱風對南部地區農業造成了嚴重的衝擊。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng duì nánbù dìqū nóngyè zàochéngle yánzhòng de chōngjī.
examples.english: The typhoon had a severe impact on agriculture in the southern region.

semanticNote: Conflict — between people, groups, ideas, or scheduling (時間衝突 = scheduling conflict). 武裝衝突 (armed conflict), 利益衝突 (conflict of interest). Common in news, politics, and HR contexts.

examples.chinese: 兩國之間發生了武裝衝突。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhī jiān fāshēngle wǔzhuāng chōngtū.
examples.english: Armed conflict broke out between the two countries.

examples.chinese: 她和老闆之間的個性衝突越來越明顯。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé lǎobǎn zhījiān de gèxìng chōngtū yuèláiyuè míngxiǎn.
examples.english: The clash of personalities between her and her boss was becoming increasingly apparent.

semanticNote: To serve in a role / function as something. 充當翻譯 (act as translator), 充當中介 (serve as middleman). Implies someone or something stepping into a function (often temporarily or unofficially).

examples.chinese: 他在會議中充當翻譯。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huìyì zhōng chōngdāng fānyì.
examples.english: He served as the translator in the meeting.

examples.chinese: 緊急情況下，她只好充當醫生，替傷患進行初步處理。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnjí qíngkuàng xià, tā zhǐhǎo chōngdāng yīshēng, tì shānghuàn jìnxíng chūbù chǔlǐ.
examples.english: In the emergency, she had no choice but to act as a doctor and perform initial treatment on the injured.

semanticNote: Abundant and vigorous — usually applied to energy, vitality, rainfall, emotion. 精力充沛 (full of energy), 雨水充沛 (abundant rainfall). Positive flavor.

examples.chinese: 他每天精力充沛。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān jīnglì chōngpèi.
examples.english: He's full of energy every day.

examples.chinese: 雨季時，山區的水源充沛，不必擔心乾旱。
examples.pinyin: Yǔjì shí, shānqū de shuǐyuán chōngpèi, bù bì dānxīn gānhàn.
examples.english: In the rainy season, water sources in the mountain areas are abundant — no need to worry about drought.

semanticNote: Two main uses: (1) describes a fulfilling, content state of life — 充實的生活 (a fulfilling life), 過得很充實 (live a meaningful life); (2) to enrich/strengthen — 充實知識 (broaden knowledge). Positive emotional word — 'meaningful and full.'

examples.chinese: 我的留學生活很充實。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de liúxué shēnghuó hěn chōngshí.
examples.english: My study-abroad life has been very fulfilling.

examples.chinese: 這門課程內容充實，讓學生獲益良多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè mén kèchéng nèiróng chōngshí, ràng xuéshēng huòyì liángduō.
examples.english: This course's content is substantive and provides great benefit to students.

semanticNote: Sufficient — supplies, time, sleep, light. 陽光充足 (plenty of sunshine), 充足的準備 (adequate preparation). Stronger than 夠 (enough) — implies 'plenty / more than enough.'

examples.chinese: 我們有充足的時間準備。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu chōngzú de shíjiān zhǔnbèi.
examples.english: We have ample time to prepare.

examples.chinese: 只有睡眠充足，才能保持良好的工作狀態。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu shuìmián chōngzú, cái néng bǎochí liánghǎo de gōngzuò zhuàngtài.
examples.english: Only with adequate sleep can you maintain a good state for work.

semanticNote: To overlap — physical (重疊的紙片 = overlapping pieces of paper) or conceptual (職責重疊 = overlapping responsibilities, 時間重疊 = scheduling overlap). Used in design, organization, scheduling.

examples.chinese: 我們兩個的工作有些重疊。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng ge de gōngzuò yǒuxiē chóngdié.
examples.english: Our two jobs overlap a bit.

examples.chinese: 山巒連綿，層層重疊，景色壯觀。
examples.pinyin: Shānluán liánmián, céng céng chóngdié, jǐngsè zhuāngguān.
examples.english: The mountains stretch on and on, layer upon layer — a magnificent sight.

semanticNote: Strong admiration verging on worship — religious worship (崇拜上帝), or fan worship of celebrities, heroes, idols (崇拜明星). Stronger than 喜歡 (like) and 欣賞 (appreciate). 個人崇拜 = cult of personality.

examples.chinese: 她從小就崇拜這位演員。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù chóngbài zhè wèi yǎnyuán.
examples.english: She's idolized this actor since childhood.

examples.chinese: 對神明的崇拜是人類最古老的宗教行為之一。
examples.pinyin: Duì shénmíng de chóngbài shì rénlèi zuì gǔlǎo de zōngjiào xíngwéi zhī yī.
examples.english: Worship of deities is one of humanity's oldest religious practices.

semanticNote: Lofty in moral or aesthetic stature — ideals, character, mountains. 崇高的理想 (lofty ideals), 崇高的精神 (noble spirit). Reverent flavor, often used for things deserving respect.

examples.chinese: 他有著崇高的理想。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒuzhe chónggāo de lǐxiǎng.
examples.english: He has lofty ideals.

examples.chinese: 消防員的奉獻精神讓人感受到人性的崇高。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán de fèngxiàn jīngshén ràng rén gǎnshòu dào rénxìng de chónggāo.
examples.english: The dedication of firefighters allows people to feel the nobility of human nature.

semanticNote: To deeply respect/venerate — typically directed at admirable figures, ancestors, heroes. Stronger than 尊敬 (respect). 受人崇敬 (be revered).

examples.chinese: 他是一位令人崇敬的學者。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi lìng rén chóngjìng de xuézhě.
examples.english: He's a scholar deserving of reverence.

examples.chinese: 她對父親懷有深深的崇敬之情。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì fùqīn huái yǒu shēnshēn de chóngjìng zhīqíng.
examples.english: She holds a deep feeling of reverence for her father.

semanticNote: Densely packed — populations, forests, hair. 人口稠密 (densely populated), 樹木稠密 (thick forest). Slightly more formal than 密 (dense).

examples.chinese: 這個地區人口非常稠密。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dìqū rénkǒu fēicháng chóumì.
examples.english: This area is very densely populated.

examples.chinese: 這座森林植被稠密，陽光幾乎無法穿透。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò sēnlín zhíbèi chóumì, yángguāng jīhū wúfǎ chuāntòu.
examples.english: The vegetation in this forest is so dense that sunlight can barely penetrate.

semanticNote: Preparation for a major event/project — wedding, conference, launch. 籌備婚禮 (planning a wedding), 籌備期 (preparation period). More substantial than 準備 (prepare, generic) — 籌備 implies organizing many moving parts.

examples.chinese: 我們正在籌備年度大會。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhèngzài chóubèi niándù dàhuì.
examples.english: We're preparing for the annual conference.

examples.chinese: 這場婚禮籌備了將近一年，耗資不菲。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng hūnlǐ chóubèile jiāngjìn yī nián, hàozī bùfēi.
examples.english: This wedding took nearly a year to prepare and cost a considerable sum.

semanticNote: Morally ugly/disgusting — applied to behavior, character, social phenomena. 醜惡的行為 (despicable behavior), 醜惡的嘴臉 (ugly true face). Strong moral judgment, more abstract than 醜 alone (ugly in appearance).

examples.chinese: 這部電影揭露了人性的醜惡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiēlùle rénxìng de chǒu'è.
examples.english: This film exposes the ugliness of human nature.

examples.chinese: 他的醜惡行徑最終被媒體曝光。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chǒu'è xíngjìng zuìzhōng bèi méitǐ bàoguāng.
examples.english: His vile conduct was ultimately exposed by the media.

semanticNote: A way out — physical exit or, more commonly, figurative escape from a difficult situation / career path / future prospects. 沒有出路 (no way out), 找出路 (look for a way forward). Common when discussing career, life direction, and societal problems.

examples.chinese: 年輕人需要找到自己的出路。
examples.pinyin: Niánqīngrén xūyào zhǎodào zìjǐ de chūlù.
examples.english: Young people need to find their own way forward.

examples.chinese: 學好一門技術，是在競爭激烈的社會中找出路的好方法。
examples.pinyin: Xuéhǎo yī mén jìshù, shì zài jìngzhēng jīliè de shèhuì zhōng zhǎo chūlù de hǎo fāngfǎ.
examples.english: Mastering a skill is a good way to find prospects in a highly competitive society.

semanticNote: To betray — usually selling out friends/principles for personal gain. Strong negative connotation. 出賣朋友 (sell out a friend). Compare to 背叛 (betray, similar) — 出賣 specifically emphasizes the mercenary motive ('sell').

examples.chinese: 他為了錢出賣了朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile qián chūmàile péngyǒu.
examples.english: He sold out his friend for money.

examples.chinese: 他出賣了公司機密，換取了豐厚的報酬。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūmàile gōngsī jīmì, huànqǔle fēnghòu de bàochou.
examples.english: He sold the company's secrets in exchange for a handsome sum.

semanticNote: Where someone comes from — family background, social origin, professional background. 出身貧寒 (born into a poor family), 名校出身 (graduated from a prestigious school). Common in Chinese discourse where origin still carries weight.

examples.chinese: 他出身名校,前途光明。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūshēn míngxiào, qiántú guāngmíng.
examples.english: He's a graduate of a top school with a bright future.

examples.chinese: 她出身貧困，卻憑藉努力改變了自己的命運。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūshēn pínkùn, què píngjiè nǔlì gǎibiànle zìjǐ de mìngyùn.
examples.english: She came from a poor background but changed her fate through hard work.

english: to be lost in thought; entranced
semanticNote: To be so absorbed your spirit/mind has gone elsewhere. Looking out a window, daydreaming, mesmerized. 看得出神 (so absorbed in watching), 出神地聽 (listening, entranced). Tender, slightly poetic word.

examples.chinese: 她望著窗外出神。
examples.pinyin: Tā wàngzhe chuāngwài chūshén.
examples.english: She gazed out the window, lost in thought.

examples.chinese: 他聽著音樂出神，完全沒注意到有人叫他。
examples.pinyin: Tā tīngzhe yīnyuè chūshén, wánquán méi zhùyì dào yǒurén jiào tā.
examples.english: He was lost in the music, completely unaware that someone was calling his name.

semanticNote: Whether someone has a promising future / will amount to something. 沒出息 (good for nothing — common parental insult), 有出息 (has potential / will go places — high praise). Loaded word in Chinese family talk; typically used to evaluate young people's futures.

examples.chinese: 父母希望孩子有出息。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ xīwàng háizi yǒu chūxi.
examples.english: Parents hope their children will go far in life.

examples.chinese: 他雖然沒念大學，卻靠著努力和才幹做出了一番出息。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán méi niàn dàxué, què kàozhe nǔlì hé cáigàn zuò chūle yī fān chūxi.
examples.english: Though he never went to college, he made a name for himself through hard work and talent.

semanticNote: Initial / preliminary stage of something. 初步成果 (initial results), 初步了解 (a preliminary understanding). Common in research, planning, agreements (initial agreement before final).

examples.chinese: 我們達成了初步的協議。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dáchéngle chūbù de xiéyì.
examples.english: We've reached a preliminary agreement.

examples.chinese: 科學家對這種疾病的研究還處於初步階段。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā duì zhè zhǒng jíbìng de yánjiū hái chǔyú chūbù jiēduàn.
examples.english: Scientists' research on this disease is still in its preliminary stage.

semanticNote: Multi-purpose: (1) to remove/eliminate — 除草 (weed); (2) divide (math) — 除以 (divided by); (3) preposition 'besides/except' — 除了...以外. The third use is most common in everyday speech.

examples.chinese: 除了他,沒人知道。
examples.pinyin: Chúle tā, méi rén zhīdào.
examples.english: Apart from him, no one knows.

examples.chinese: 二十除以四等於五。
examples.pinyin: Èrshí chú yǐ sì děngyú wǔ.
examples.english: Twenty divided by four equals five.

semanticNote: Official disciplinary action — workplace, school, party. 受到處分 (receive a punishment), 行政處分 (administrative discipline). Different from 懲罰 (punishment, broader/heavier) — 處分 is institutional/procedural.

examples.chinese: 他因違規而受到處分。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn wéiguī ér shòudào chǔfèn.
examples.english: He received disciplinary action for the violation.

examples.chinese: 公司對多次遲到的員工給予了書面處分。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī duì duō cì chídào de yuángōng gěiyǔle shūmiàn chǔfèn.
examples.english: The company issued a written disciplinary notice to employees who were repeatedly late.

semanticNote: The circumstances someone finds themselves in — almost always tinged with difficulty or disadvantage. 處境艱難 (in a difficult situation), 處境尷尬 (in an awkward position). Unlike 情況 (which is neutral — just 'situation/conditions'), 處境 implies the person is affected by and somewhat trapped in these circumstances. You'd use 處境 to express sympathy: 他現在的處境很不好 (his current situation is quite bad). Not used for positive situations.

components.meaning: to be in; to deal with; place

examples.chinese: 她現在的處境讓我們很擔心。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiànzài de chǔjìng ràng wǒmen hěn dānxīn.
examples.english: Her current situation has us very worried.

examples.chinese: 在戰亂中，難民的處境非常艱苦。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhànluàn zhōng, nànmín de chǔjìng fēicháng jiānkǔ.
examples.english: During the conflict, the refugees were in extremely dire circumstances.

semanticNote: To handle / take care of / dispose of — issues, situations, criminals, property. 妥善處置 (properly handle). Slightly more formal than 處理 (handle). Used in administrative, legal, and emergency contexts.

examples.chinese: 危機已經得到妥善處置。
examples.pinyin: Wéijī yǐjīng dédào tuǒshàn chǔzhì.
examples.english: The crisis has been properly handled.

examples.chinese: 廢棄物必須依照法規妥善處置，不得任意丟棄。
examples.pinyin: Fèiqìwù bìxū yīzhào fǎguī tuǒshàn chǔzhì, bùdé rènyì diūqì.
examples.english: Waste must be properly disposed of in accordance with regulations and cannot be discarded arbitrarily.

semanticNote: Strategic reserves — food, energy, foreign currency, talent. 外匯儲備 (foreign currency reserves), 戰略儲備 (strategic reserves), 人才儲備 (talent pipeline). Implies forward-thinking accumulation for future needs.

examples.chinese: 國家需要充足的能源儲備。
examples.pinyin: Guójiā xūyào chōngzú de néngyuán chǔbèi.
examples.english: The country needs ample energy reserves.

examples.chinese: 這個家庭在地震後立刻補充了緊急儲備物資。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiātíng zài dìzhèn hòu lìkè bǔchōngle jǐnjí chǔbèi wùzī.
examples.english: After the earthquake, this family immediately replenished their emergency stockpile.

semanticNote: To store — physical goods, energy, data. 儲存食物 (store food), 儲存資料 (store data). The Taiwan IT term for 'save' (file/document) — though Tim's locked decision is to keep 保存 for 'save' in general contexts.

examples.chinese: 請把資料儲存到雲端。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zīliào chǔcún dào yúnduān.
examples.english: Please save the data to the cloud.

examples.chinese: 松鼠會在秋天儲存食物，以備過冬之需。
examples.pinyin: Sōngshǔ huì zài qiūtiān chǔcún shíwù, yǐbèi guòdōng zhī xū.
examples.english: Squirrels store food in autumn to prepare for the winter ahead.

semanticNote: Savings — money set aside for the future. 儲蓄帳戶 (savings account), 儲蓄習慣 (savings habit). Personal finance vocabulary. Slightly more formal than 存錢 (save money, casual).

examples.chinese: 他每個月都會儲蓄一部分薪水。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge yuè dōu huì chǔxù yí bùfèn xīnshuǐ.
examples.english: He saves part of his salary every month.

examples.chinese: 從小培養儲蓄的習慣，長大後才不會有財務問題。
examples.pinyin: Cóngxiǎo péiyǎng chǔxù de xíguàn, zhǎngdà hòu cái bù huì yǒu cáiwù wèntí.
examples.english: Cultivating the habit of saving money from a young age prevents financial problems in adulthood.

semanticNote: To cross a line / violate something held sacred — laws (觸犯法律), taboos (觸犯禁忌), authority. Implies the act crossed a definite boundary, not just being annoying.

examples.chinese: 他的行為觸犯了法律。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xíngwéi chùfànle fǎlǜ.
examples.english: His behavior violated the law.

examples.chinese: 任何人都不得觸犯他人的合法權益。
examples.pinyin: Rènhé rén dōu bùdé chùfàn tārén de héfǎ quányì.
examples.english: No one may infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of others.

semanticNote: Like a river that never stops flowing — used for endless streams of traffic, people, customers. 人潮川流不息 (an endless stream of people). Vivid and common in descriptive writing.

examples.chinese: 假日的觀光景點人潮川流不息。
examples.pinyin: Jiàrì de guānguāng jǐngdiǎn réncháo chuānliúbùxī.
examples.english: The tourist spot has an endless stream of visitors during holidays.

examples.chinese: 大城市的街頭車輛川流不息，從未停歇。
examples.pinyin: Dà chéngshì de jiētóu chēliàng chuānliú-bùxī, cóng wèi tíngxiē.
examples.english: On the streets of big cities, vehicles flow in an endless stream without stopping.

english: to pass through; cut across; (fiction) time-travel
semanticNote: To traverse / cut through — physical (穿越森林 = cross through the forest) or temporal. Modern pop-culture sense: 穿越劇 = time-travel drama (a huge genre in Chinese TV/web fiction). 穿越時空 = travel across time and space.

examples.chinese: 這部小說講的是穿越古代的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō jiǎng de shì chuānyuè gǔdài de gùshì.
examples.english: This novel tells a story of time-travel to ancient times.

examples.chinese: 高鐵穿越重重山嶺，連結了臺灣的南北兩端。
examples.pinyin: Gāotiě chuānyuè chóngchóng shānlǐng, liánjié le Táiwān de nánběi liǎng duān.
examples.english: The high-speed rail passes through layer after layer of mountains, linking the north and south ends of Taiwan.

semanticNote: To pass on a message, instruction, or sentiment from one party to another. 傳達指示 (convey instructions), 傳達情感 (convey emotion). Implies acting as a conduit. Common in workplace, diplomacy, art.

examples.chinese: 請把這個信息傳達給其他人。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè ge xìnxī chuándá gěi qítā rén.
examples.english: Please convey this information to the others.

examples.chinese: 總統的聲明透過電視傳達給全國民眾。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng de shēngmíng tòuguò diànshì chuándá gěi quánguó mínzhòng.
examples.english: The president's statement was conveyed to the entire nation through television.

semanticNote: Paper flyer for advertising or promotion. 發傳單 = hand out flyers. Old-school marketing word — still common in restaurants, political campaigns, religious outreach.

examples.chinese: 店員在街上發傳單。
examples.pinyin: Diànyuán zài jiē shàng fā chuándān.
examples.english: The shop assistant is handing out flyers on the street.

examples.chinese: 選舉期間，各候選人的支持者到處發傳單拉票。
examples.pinyin: Xuǎnjǔ qījiān, gè hòuxuǎnrén de zhīchírén dàochù fā chuándān lāpiào.
examples.english: During the election, supporters of various candidates handed out flyers everywhere to solicit votes.

semanticNote: To pass on knowledge or a skill — typically from teacher to student, master to apprentice, generation to generation. 傳授經驗 (pass on experience), 傳授武功 (transmit martial arts skills). Carries a sense of lineage.

examples.chinese: 老師把知識傳授給學生。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ zhīshì chuánshòu gěi xuéshēng.
examples.english: The teacher passes knowledge on to students.

examples.chinese: 師傅把數十年的廚藝傳授給了徒弟。
examples.pinyin: Shīfù bǎ shùshí nián de chúyì chuánshòu gěile túdì.
examples.english: The master chef passed on decades of culinary skills to his apprentice.

semanticNote: Maritime/shipping vocabulary — ships and boats as a category. More formal than 船 (boat/ship). 船舶業 = shipping industry. Industry and policy register.

examples.chinese: 這個港口可以停靠各種船舶。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gǎngkǒu kěyǐ tíngkào gè zhǒng chuánbó.
examples.english: This port can dock various kinds of vessels.

examples.chinese: 遠洋漁船是一種特殊的船舶，能在深海作業。
examples.pinyin: Yuǎnyáng yúchuán shì yī zhǒng tèshū de chuánbó, néng zài shēnhǎi zuòyè.
examples.english: Ocean-going fishing boats are a special type of vessel able to operate in the deep sea.

semanticNote: Heavy breathing — from exertion, illness, or panic. Also figurative: 讓我喘口氣 (let me catch my breath / give me a break) — used metaphorically for needing a pause from stress.

examples.chinese: 跑完步後他喘著氣。
examples.pinyin: Pǎo wán bù hòu tā chuǎnzhe qì.
examples.english: After running he was panting.

examples.chinese: 她在最後一段路衝刺，跑到終點時幾乎喘不過氣。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zuìhòu yī duàn lù chōngcì, pǎo dào zhōngdiǎn shí jīhū chuǎn bù guòqì.
examples.english: She sprinted in the final stretch, arriving at the finish line barely able to breathe.

english: to string together; (measure) string of; bunch
semanticNote: Multi-purpose: (1) measure word for bundles/strings of things — 一串葡萄 (a bunch of grapes), 一串鑰匙 (a string of keys); (2) verb — string together (串起來), conspire (串通); (3) Taiwanese street food — 串燒 (kebabs).

examples.chinese: 他買了一串葡萄。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎile yí chuàn pútáo.
examples.english: He bought a bunch of grapes.

examples.chinese: 幾個孩子把錯誤的情節串在一起，說出了一個荒誕的故事。
examples.pinyin: Jǐ gè háizi bǎ cuòwù de qíngjié chuàn zài yìqǐ, shuō chūle yīgè huāngdàn de gùshì.
examples.english: A few children strung together a series of wrong plot points and told an absurd story.

semanticNote: Bed sheet. 換床單 = change the sheets. Household vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 我每週換一次床單。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi zhōu huàn yí cì chuángdān.
examples.english: I change the sheets once a week.

examples.chinese: 她選了一套淡藍色的床單，讓臥室看起來更清爽。
examples.pinyin: Tā xuǎnle yī tào dàn lánsè de chuángdān, ràng wòshì kàn qǐlái gèng qīngshuǎng.
examples.english: She chose a set of light blue sheets, making the bedroom look fresher.

semanticNote: To found / establish — companies, schools, organizations, theories. 創立公司 (found a company). Compare to 成立 (establish, similar but more procedural). 創立 emphasizes original creation.

examples.chinese: 他在三十歲時創立了這家公司。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài sānshí suì shí chuànglìle zhè jiā gōngsī.
examples.english: He founded this company when he was thirty.

examples.chinese: 這家慈善機構由一群熱心市民共同創立，已服務社區三十年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā císhàn jīgòu yóu yī qún rèxīn shìmín gòngtóng chuànglì, yǐ fúwù shèqū sānshí nián.
examples.english: This charitable organization was jointly founded by dedicated citizens and has served the community for thirty years.

semanticNote: Innovation — buzzword in modern Chinese business and policy. 創新精神 (spirit of innovation), 不斷創新 (continuously innovate). Common in tech, startup, education contexts.

examples.chinese: 這家公司一直在創新。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yìzhí zài chuàngxīn.
examples.english: This company is constantly innovating.

examples.chinese: 臺灣在半導體領域的技術創新，在全球名列前茅。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān zài bàndǎotǐ lǐngyù de jìshù chuàngxīn, zài quánqiú míngliè-qiánmáo.
examples.english: Taiwan's technological innovations in the semiconductor field rank among the world's best.

semanticNote: To start a business / venture. Massive cultural buzzword in Chinese-speaking world over the last 15 years. 創業者 (entrepreneur), 創業精神 (entrepreneurial spirit). Aspirational.

examples.chinese: 他大學畢業就決定創業。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè jiù juédìng chuàngyè.
examples.english: He decided to start his own business right after college.

examples.chinese: 政府設立了創業輔導基金，幫助年輕人實現創業夢想。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ shèlìle chuàngyè fǔdǎo jījīn, bāngzhù niánqīngrén shíxiàn chuàngyè mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: The government established a startup mentorship fund to help young people realize their entrepreneurial dreams.

semanticNote: Specifically creative/artistic creation — writing, music, art. 文學創作 (literary creation), 創作靈感 (creative inspiration). Distinguished from 創造 (create, broader, including non-artistic). 創作 is the artist's word.

examples.chinese: 她創作了很多動人的歌曲。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuàngzuòle hěn duō dòngrén de gēqǔ.
examples.english: She has created many moving songs.

examples.chinese: 這位作家以親身經歷為素材，創作出令人動容的長篇小說。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā yǐ qīnshēn jīnglì wéi sùcái, chuàngzuò chū lìng rén dòngróng de chángpiān xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: This author drew on personal experience to create a deeply moving novel.

semanticNote: Literally 'blow the cow' — to brag, exaggerate one's accomplishments. Casual and slightly humorous. 別吹牛了 (stop bragging). The Taiwan-mainland regional twist: 吹牛 in some Northern dialects also means 'to chat / shoot the breeze.'

examples.chinese: 他特別愛吹牛。
examples.pinyin: Tā tèbié ài chuīniú.
examples.english: He really loves to brag.

examples.chinese: 他說他能一口氣爬完百岳，純粹是在吹牛。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō tā néng yī kǒuqì pá wán bǎiyuè, chúncuì shì zài chuīniú.
examples.english: He claims he can climb all of Taiwan's Hundred Peaks in one go — that's pure bragging.

semanticNote: To excessively praise someone — usually with negative undertone of insincerity or sycophancy. 互相吹捧 (mutually flatter). Compare to 讚美 (praise, sincere) — 吹捧 implies overdone, often manipulative praise.

examples.chinese: 我不喜歡這種互相吹捧的場合。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuān zhè zhǒng hùxiāng chuīpěng de chǎnghé.
examples.english: I don't like these mutual-flattery occasions.

examples.chinese: 媒體對這部電影的吹捧程度，讓觀眾大感失望。
examples.pinyin: Méitǐ duì zhè bù diànyǐng de chuīpěng chéngdù, ràng guānzhòng dà gǎn shīwàng.
examples.english: The media's excessive praise for this film left audiences greatly disappointed.

semanticNote: Smoke rising from kitchen chimneys — evocative rural/nostalgic image of village life. 炊煙裊裊 (smoke curling upward, set phrase, very poetic). Literary, often appears in poems and rural memoir writing.

examples.chinese: 傍晚時分,村莊升起了炊煙。
examples.pinyin: Bàngwǎn shífèn, cūnzhuāng shēngqǐle chuīyān.
examples.english: At dusk, smoke from cooking fires rose from the village.

examples.chinese: 遠遠望去，山腰上幾縷炊煙，說明那裡有人居住。
examples.pinyin: Yuǎnyuǎn wàng qù, shānyāo shàng jǐ lǚ chuīyān, shuōmíng nàlǐ yǒu rén jūzhù.
examples.english: Looking from afar, a few wisps of cooking smoke rose from the hillside, indicating that people lived there.

semanticNote: Vertical / perpendicular — geometry, architecture, fashion (垂直線條 = vertical lines). Pair with 水平 (horizontal). 垂直整合 (vertical integration) is a business term.

examples.chinese: 這條線和那條線是垂直的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiàn hé nà tiáo xiàn shì chuízhí de.
examples.english: This line is perpendicular to that line.

examples.chinese: 這棟大樓的外牆是完全垂直的，工程師的水準令人讚嘆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng dàlóu de wàiqiáng shì wánquán chuízhí de, gōngchéngshī de shuǐzhǔn lìng rén zàntàn.
examples.english: The exterior wall of this building is perfectly vertical — the engineer's skill level is admirable.

semanticNote: Hammer — both noun and verb. 鐵錘 = iron hammer. As verb: 錘煉 (to temper / forge / refine through hardship — figurative use is powerful). Tool and metaphor.

examples.chinese: 他用錘子釘釘子。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng chuízi dīng dīngzi.
examples.english: He uses a hammer to drive in nails.

examples.chinese: 煉鐵師傅揮舞著大錘，一下一下地鍛造鐵器。
examples.pinyin: Liàn tiě shīfù huīwǔzhe dà chuí, yī xià yī xià de duànzào tiěqì.
examples.english: The blacksmith swung the heavy hammer, forging iron tools one blow at a time.

english: purely; absolutely; sheer; pure (without anything mixed in)
semanticNote: Both an adjective (pure, unadulterated) and an adverb (purely, simply). As an adjective: 純粹的好奇心 (pure curiosity), 純粹的中文 (pure Mandarin). As an adverb: 我純粹是好奇 (I'm purely curious), 這純粹是誤會 (this is purely a misunderstanding). The adverbial use is very common in speech and emphasizes that there's no other motive or element involved. Often used to deflect suspicion or clarify intent.

examples.chinese: 我純粹是好奇，沒有其他意思。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chúncuì shì hàoqí, méiyǒu qítā yìsi.
examples.english: I'm purely curious — no other meaning.

examples.chinese: 他對音樂有一種純粹的熱愛。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì yīnyuè yǒu yī zhǒng chúncuì de rè'ài.
examples.english: He has a pure, uncomplicated love for music.

semanticNote: Pure — describes hearts, souls, love, friendships. 純潔的友誼 (pure friendship), 心靈純潔 (a pure heart/soul). Idealistic, often used about youth or untainted ideals.

examples.chinese: 孩子的心靈是最純潔的。
examples.pinyin: Háizi de xīnlíng shì zuì chúnjié de.
examples.english: Children's hearts are the purest.

examples.chinese: 他們的友誼純潔，從未因為利益而改變。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de yǒuyì chúnjié, cóng wèi yīnwèi lìyì ér gǎibiàn.
examples.english: Their friendship is pure, never changed by self-interest.

semanticNote: Charity — institutional or personal. 慈善機構 (charitable organization), 慈善活動 (charity event). 做慈善 = do charity work. Common in news about wealthy individuals and NGOs.

examples.chinese: 她常常參加慈善活動。
examples.pinyin: Tā chángcháng cānjiā císhàn huódòng.
examples.english: She often participates in charity events.

examples.chinese: 企業家捐款成立了一個慈善基金會，專門資助弱勢學生。
examples.pinyin: Qǐyèjiā juānkuǎn chénglìle yīgè císhàn jījīnhuì, zhuānmén zīzhù ruòshì xuéshēng.
examples.english: The entrepreneur donated to establish a charitable foundation to fund disadvantaged students.

semanticNote: Specifically describes the kindly demeanor of older people — grandmothers, elderly neighbors. 慈祥的笑容 (a kind, grandmotherly smile), 慈祥的老人 (a kindly old person). Reserved for elders; not used for kids or peers.

examples.chinese: 奶奶總是露出慈祥的笑容。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zǒngshì lùchū cíxiáng de xiàoróng.
examples.english: Grandma always has a kindly smile.

examples.chinese: 那位慈祥的老神父在村裡服務了幾十年，深受居民愛戴。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi cíxiáng de lǎo shénfù zài cūn lǐ fúwùle jǐshí nián, shēnshòu jūmín àidài.
examples.english: That kindly old priest served in the village for decades, deeply loved by the residents.

semanticNote: Cassette tape — magnetic tape for audio/video. Increasingly nostalgic vocabulary as digital replaces it. Still in HSK because of generational continuity.

examples.chinese: 我家還有一些舊的磁帶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā hái yǒu yìxiē jiù de cídài.
examples.english: My family still has some old cassette tapes.

examples.chinese: 數位時代到來前，音樂主要靠磁帶傳播。
examples.pinyin: Shùwèi shídài dàolái qián, yīnyuè zhǔyào kào cídài chuánbō.
examples.english: Before the digital age arrived, music was mainly spread through cassette tapes.

english: male and female (animals); winners and losers
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) biology — male (雄) and female (雌) animals; (2) idiomatic — 一決雌雄 (decide the winner once and for all, literally 'decide the male and female'), used in dramatic competitive contexts. Note: for humans, the words are 男女 not 雌雄.

examples.chinese: 我們明天比賽,一決雌雄!
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān bǐsài, yì jué cíxióng!
examples.english: We compete tomorrow — let's settle this once and for all!

examples.chinese: 科學家透過基因分析來判斷動物的雌雄。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā tòuguò jīyīn fēnxī lái pànduàn dòngwù de cíxióng.
examples.english: Scientists use genetic analysis to determine the sex of animals.

semanticNote: Defective product — failed quality control. 次品打折 (defective items at a discount). Common in manufacturing and outlet shopping.

examples.chinese: 這些都是次品,賣得便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōu shì cìpǐn, mài de piányí.
examples.english: These are all defective items, sold cheap.

examples.chinese: 消費者保護法規定，購買到次品時，消費者有權要求退換。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofèizhě bǎohùfǎ guīdìng, gòumǎi dào cìpǐn shí, xiāofèizhě yǒu quán yāoqiú tuìhuàn.
examples.english: Consumer protection law stipulates that when a defective product is purchased, the consumer has the right to request a return or replacement.

semanticNote: The order/sequence of things. 按照次序 (in order), 次序顛倒 (out of order). Compare to 順序 (sequence, very similar). Common in instructions and lists.

examples.chinese: 請按照次序排隊。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào cìxù páiduì.
examples.english: Please line up in order.

examples.chinese: 編寫程式要講究邏輯次序，否則程式無法正常運行。
examples.pinyin: Biānxiě chéngshì yào jiǎngjiū luójí cìxù, fǒuzé chéngshì wúfǎ zhèngcháng yùnxíng.
examples.english: Writing a program requires attention to logical sequence; otherwise, the program cannot run properly.

semanticNote: To attend to / serve someone — usually with implicit hierarchy (servants attending masters, kids attending elderly parents). Can be neutral (caring for) or sarcastic in colloquial use: 我可伺候不起 (I can't afford to wait on this princess/diva).

examples.chinese: 她在家裡伺候生病的父親。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiā lǐ cìhou shēngbìng de fùqīn.
examples.english: She cares for her sick father at home.

examples.chinese: 舊時，富貴人家都雇有傭人專門伺候主人。
examples.pinyin: Jiùshí, fùguì rénjiā dōu gù yǒu yōngrén zhuānmén cìhou zhǔrén.
examples.english: In the old days, wealthy families all hired servants specifically to wait on their masters.

semanticNote: To pierce / stab — physical (刺破 = pierce through) and figurative (刺傷 = wound emotionally, 刺痛 = sting). As noun: thorn, splinter. Sharp, vivid word. 刺青 = tattoo. 諷刺 = satirize (figurative pricking).

examples.chinese: 他的話刺傷了我的心。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà cìshāngle wǒ de xīn.
examples.english: His words pierced my heart.

examples.chinese: 玫瑰雖然美麗，但莖上的刺很容易刺破皮膚。
examples.pinyin: Méiguī suīrán měilì, dàn jīng shàng de cì hěn róngyì cì pò pífū.
examples.english: Though roses are beautiful, the thorns on their stems can easily prick the skin.

semanticNote: An unhurried, easy composure — the sense of moving through something difficult or demanding without being rushed or flustered. 從容不迫 (completely unhurried) is a common chengyu expansion. 他從容地回答了所有問題 (he answered all the questions with ease). The key nuance: it's not just being calm internally, it's also the outward unhurried manner. More elegant and literary than 輕鬆 (relaxed/easy) — 從容 is composed grace under pressure, not casual ease.

examples.chinese: 她從容地走上舞台，完全不緊張。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngróng de zǒu shàng wǔtái, wánquán bù jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: She walked onto the stage with perfect composure — not nervous at all.

examples.chinese: 面對困難，他總是從容不迫。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì kùnnán, tā zǒng shì cóngróng bùpò.
examples.english: Faced with difficulties, he's always completely unhurried.

semanticNote: A cluster — of plants, things growing together. 草叢 (grass thicket), 花叢 (flower bed/cluster). Also a measure word for clusters: 一叢竹子 (a clump of bamboo).

examples.chinese: 花叢中有很多蝴蝶。
examples.pinyin: Huācóng zhōng yǒu hěn duō húdié.
examples.english: There are many butterflies among the flowers.

examples.chinese: 他在草叢裡發現了一隻受傷的小鳥。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài cǎocóng lǐ fāxiànle yī zhī shòushāng de xiǎoniǎo.
examples.english: He found an injured little bird in the bushes.

english: to make do; manage with what's available
semanticNote: Beautiful colloquial word: 'make do' / 'good enough' / 'gather together haphazardly.' 湊合著用吧 (just make do with it), 湊合過日子 (get by). Slightly resigned tone — implies the situation isn't ideal but workable. Quintessentially Chinese pragmatism.

examples.chinese: 沒有椅子,你坐這裡湊合一下吧。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu yǐzi, nǐ zuò zhèlǐ còuhe yíxià ba.
examples.english: No chair available — just make do sitting here.

examples.chinese: 旅途中找不到餐廳，我們只好買個便當湊合著吃。
examples.pinyin: Lǚtú zhōng zhǎo bù dào cāntīng, wǒmen zhǐhǎo mǎi ge biàndāng còuhe zhe chī.
examples.english: During the trip we couldn't find a restaurant, so we had to buy a bento box and make do.

semanticNote: Rough or crude in manner — speech, behavior. 說話粗魯 (speak rudely), 粗魯的舉動 (rude behavior). Compare to 沒禮貌 (impolite, kid-friendly framing) — 粗魯 implies a more visceral lack of refinement.

examples.chinese: 他的言行很粗魯。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yánxíng hěn cūlǔ.
examples.english: His words and actions are very rude.

examples.chinese: 那個陌生人說話粗魯，毫不顧及旁人的感受。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge mòshēngrén shuōhuà cūlǔ, háo bù gùjí pángrén de gǎnshòu.
examples.english: That stranger spoke very rudely, showing no consideration for others' feelings.

semanticNote: To flee in a panicked, scurrying way — 鼠竄 (scurry like a rat). Also: 竄改 (tamper with text/data, change deceptively). Carries a sneaky/desperate flavor.

examples.chinese: 小偷一見警察就四處逃竄。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu yí jiàn jǐngchá jiù sìchù táocuàn.
examples.english: The thief scurried in all directions when he saw the police.

examples.chinese: 老鼠在廚房裡亂竄，嚇到了房裡的人。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshǔ zài chúfáng lǐ luàn cuàn, xià dào le fáng lǐ de rén.
examples.english: The rat scurried around wildly in the kitchen, frightening everyone in the room.

semanticNote: To severely damage / ravage / brutalize — applied to bodies (摧殘身心 = damage body and mind), forests, environment, freedoms. Strong word implying systematic destruction.

examples.chinese: 長期熬夜會摧殘身體。
examples.pinyin: Chángqī áoyè huì cuīcán shēntǐ.
examples.english: Long-term sleep deprivation will ravage your body.

examples.chinese: 戰爭摧殘了這座城市，留下了無數廢墟。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng cuīcánle zhè zuò chéngshì, liú xià le wúshù fèixū.
examples.english: The war devastated this city, leaving behind countless ruins.

semanticNote: Fragile — emotionally (脆弱的心 = fragile heart), physically (脆弱的關係 = fragile relationship), structurally (脆弱的生態系統 = fragile ecosystem). Slightly more poignant than 弱 (weak).

examples.chinese: 她最近心情很脆弱。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn xīnqíng hěn cuìruò.
examples.english: She's been emotionally fragile lately.

examples.chinese: 玻璃製品比較脆弱，搬運時要特別小心。
examples.pinyin: Bōlí zhìpǐn bǐjiào cuìruò, bānyùn shí yào tèbié xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: Glass items are relatively fragile — be especially careful when handling them.

semanticNote: To rub between hands or fingers — 搓手 (rub hands together, often for warmth or anticipation), 搓澡 (scrub yourself in the bath, very Chinese-style), 搓湯圓 (roll glutinous rice balls). Tactile, hands-on word.

examples.chinese: 她搓了搓凍僵的手。
examples.pinyin: Tā cuōle cuō dòng jiāng de shǒu.
examples.english: She rubbed her frozen hands together.

examples.chinese: 媽媽搓著一小球麵糰，準備包湯圓。
examples.pinyin: Māma cuōzhe yī xiǎo qiú miàntuán, zhǔnbèi bāo tāngyuán.
examples.english: Mom rolled a small ball of dough, getting ready to make tang yuan.

semanticNote: Formal consultation/negotiation — diplomatic talks, business deals, official discussions. 進行磋商 (engage in consultation). Heavier and more formal than 商量 (discuss). News and diplomacy register.

examples.chinese: 兩國正在磋商貿易協議。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhèngzài cuōshāng màoyì xiéyì.
examples.english: The two countries are negotiating a trade agreement.

examples.chinese: 管理層與工會經過長時間磋商，才達成薪資協議。
examples.pinyin: Guǎnlǐcéng yǔ gōnghuì jīngguò cháng shíjiān cuōshāng, cái dáchéng xīnzī xiéyì.
examples.english: Management and the union reached a wage agreement only after lengthy negotiations.

semanticNote: A setback — in career, study, life. 遭遇挫折 (encounter a setback), 抗挫折能力 (resilience, literally 'ability to resist setbacks'). Common in motivational and self-help contexts. The Chinese culture has invested deeply in 'setback education' as a concept.

examples.chinese: 人生難免會遇到挫折。
examples.pinyin: Rénshēng nánmiǎn huì yùdào cuòzhé.
examples.english: It's inevitable to face setbacks in life.

examples.chinese: 他在挫折中成長，變得更加堅韌。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài cuòzhé zhōng chéngzhǎng, biànde gèngjiā jiānrèn.
examples.english: He grew stronger through setbacks, becoming more resilient.

semanticNote: Multi-purpose action verb: (1) take public transport — 搭公車 (take the bus, 搭飛機 = take a plane — common in Taiwan); (2) build by joining pieces — 搭橋 (build a bridge), 搭帳篷 (pitch a tent); (3) hang/drape — 搭在椅子上 (drape over the chair). Very productive verb.

examples.chinese: 我每天搭捷運上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dā jiéyùn shàngbān.
examples.english: I take the metro to work every day.

examples.chinese: 工人們正在搭舞台，準備迎接週末的演唱會。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài dā wǔtái, zhǔnbèi yíngjiē zhōumò de yǎnchànghuì.
examples.english: Workers are setting up the stage in preparation for the weekend concert.

semanticNote: A working partner — police partner, comedy duo, business partner. 老搭檔 (old partner — long-term teammate, warm flavor). Implies ongoing collaboration, not just one-time partnership.

examples.chinese: 我們是工作上的好搭檔。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì gōngzuò shàng de hǎo dādàng.
examples.english: We're great work partners.

examples.chinese: 這對相聲演員是多年的搭檔，配合默契十足。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì xiàngshēng yǎnyuán shì duō nián de dādàng, pèihé mòqì shífú.
examples.english: These two crosstalk comedians have been partners for many years, with seamless coordination.

semanticNote: To pair things together — clothes (服裝搭配 = outfit coordination), food (酒和菜的搭配 = wine pairing), colors. Style and design vocabulary. Very common in fashion and home decor talk.

examples.chinese: 她很會搭配衣服。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì dāpèi yīfu.
examples.english: She's great at coordinating outfits.

examples.chinese: 飲食要均衡，注意食材的搭配。
examples.pinyin: Yǐnshí yào jūnhéng, zhùyì shícái de dāpèi.
examples.english: Diet should be balanced, with attention to how ingredients are paired.

semanticNote: To reach / achieve — most commonly with agreements, consensus, goals. 達成協議 (reach an agreement), 達成共識 (reach consensus), 達成目標 (achieve a goal). Business and diplomatic register.

examples.chinese: 雙方達成了合作協議。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng dáchéngle hézuò xiéyì.
examples.english: The two sides reached a cooperation agreement.

examples.chinese: 經過多次協商，他們終於達成了共識。
examples.pinyin: Jīngguò duō cì xiéshāng, tāmen zhōngyú dáchéngle gòngshí.
examples.english: After multiple consultations, they finally reached a consensus.

semanticNote: Two contexts: (1) academic — defend a thesis (論文答辯 = thesis defense); (2) legal — respond to accusations in court. Both involve formal verbal defense. 答辯會 = defense session.

examples.chinese: 她下週要進行論文答辯。
examples.pinyin: Tā xià zhōu yào jìnxíng lùnwén dábiàn.
examples.english: She's defending her thesis next week.

examples.chinese: 答辯委員會的問題很刁鑽，她還是一一化解了。
examples.pinyin: Dábiàn wěiyuánhuì de wèntí hěn diāozuān, tā háishì yī yī huàjiěle.
examples.english: The thesis committee's questions were very tricky, but she managed to address them one by one.

semanticNote: Formal response — to a request, inquiry, or letter. 給予答覆 (give a reply). More formal than 回答 (answer, general) or 回應 (respond). Common in business correspondence and official communications.

examples.chinese: 我們會盡快給您答覆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huì jǐnkuài gěi nín dáfù.
examples.english: We'll give you a reply as soon as possible.

examples.chinese: 他的電子郵件已送出，正在等待對方的答覆。
examples.pinyin: Tā de diànzǐ yóujiàn yǐ sòngchū, zhèngzài děngdài duìfāng de dáfù.
examples.english: His email has been sent, and he's waiting for the other party's reply.

english: to pack up; (restaurant) take leftovers home
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) restaurant — take leftovers in a doggy bag (剩菜打包 = pack up the leftovers — common and unembarrassed in Chinese culture); (2) bundle items (also software/data: pack up a release).

examples.chinese: 剩下的菜我打包帶走。
examples.pinyin: Shèngxià de cài wǒ dǎbāo dàizǒu.
examples.english: I'll pack up the leftovers and take them home.

examples.chinese: 搬家前他把所有書籍都打包好，裝進了紙箱。
examples.pinyin: Bānjiā qián tā bǎ suǒyǒu shūjí dōu dǎbāo hǎo, zhuāng jìnle zhǐxiāng.
examples.english: Before moving, he packed all his books and put them into cardboard boxes.

semanticNote: Colloquial way to say 'sue / go to court.' 跟人打官司 = sue someone. More casual than 提起訴訟 (file a lawsuit, formal). Often used dismissively or with reluctance ('we don't want it to get to that').

examples.chinese: 他們為了財產打官司。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen wèile cáichǎn dǎguānsi.
examples.english: They went to court over the property.

examples.chinese: 公司因違約被合作廠商告上法院，不得不打官司。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yīn wéiyuē bèi hézuò chǎngshāng gào shàng fǎyuàn, bùdébù dǎguānsi.
examples.english: The company was sued by a partner for breach of contract and had no choice but to go to court.

english: to strike; blow; deal a blow
semanticNote: Both physical and emotional blow. 沉重的打擊 (a heavy blow), 受到打擊 (be struck a blow). Also: 打擊犯罪 (crack down on crime), 打擊毒品 (war on drugs). Strong word, often in news contexts.

examples.chinese: 這個消息對他是巨大的打擊。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiāoxī duì tā shì jùdà de dǎjī.
examples.english: This news was a huge blow to him.

examples.chinese: 執法單位積極打擊網路詐騙行為。
examples.pinyin: Zhífǎ dānwèi jījí dǎjī wǎnglù zhàpiàn xíngwéi.
examples.english: Law enforcement agencies are actively cracking down on online fraud.

semanticNote: Physical fight — usually fistfight, brawl. Children, drunks, neighbors. Common everyday word. Compare to 打仗 (war/battle, large-scale) and 打鬥 (fight, more dramatic).

examples.chinese: 兩個小孩在學校打架。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge xiǎohái zài xuéxiào dǎjià.
examples.english: Two kids got into a fight at school.

examples.chinese: 雙方球迷在場外打架，警方出動了大批人員維持秩序。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng qiúmí zài chǎngwài dǎjià, jǐngfāng chūdòngle dà pī rényuán wéichí zhìxù.
examples.english: Fans from both sides got into a fight outside the venue, and police deployed large numbers to maintain order.

english: to size up; look over carefully
semanticNote: To carefully examine someone with your eyes — assessing them. 上下打量 (look someone up and down). Slightly intrusive feel, often noticed: 他打量了我半天 (he sized me up for a long time).

examples.chinese: 他上下打量了我一番。
examples.pinyin: Tā shàngxià dǎliangle wǒ yì fān.
examples.english: He looked me up and down.

examples.chinese: 她打量了一眼店裡的擺設，心想這家店裝潢不錯。
examples.pinyin: Tā dǎliàngle yīyǎn diàn lǐ de bǎishè, xīn xiǎng zhè jiā diàn zhuānghuáng bùcuò.
examples.english: She glanced around at the store's décor, thinking to herself that it was nicely decorated.

semanticNote: To hunt animals. 去山上打獵 (go hunting in the mountains). Increasingly historical/rural vocabulary in modern China and Taiwan. Common in stories, ethnic minority contexts, period dramas.

examples.chinese: 古人經常上山打獵。
examples.pinyin: Gǔrén jīngcháng shàng shān dǎliè.
examples.english: Ancient people often went hunting in the mountains.

examples.chinese: 在臺灣，原住民族的傳統祭儀中有打獵的習俗。
examples.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, yuánzhùmínzú de chuántǒng jìyí zhōng yǒu dǎliè de xísú.
examples.english: In Taiwan, hunting is a custom in the traditional ceremonies of indigenous peoples.

english: to fight a war; go into battle
semanticNote: Wage war / fight battles. Military scale. 打勝仗 (win the battle). Common in war-related discussions and historical references. Also figurative: 打硬仗 (fight a tough battle, in business or work contexts).

examples.chinese: 沒有人想打仗。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén xiǎng dǎzhàng.
examples.english: Nobody wants to go to war.

examples.chinese: 歷史上，人們為了爭奪資源而打仗，造成了無數悲劇。
examples.pinyin: Lìshǐ shàng, rénmen wèile zhēngduó zīyuán ér dǎzhàng, zàochéngle wúshù bēijù.
examples.english: Throughout history, people have gone to war to compete for resources, causing countless tragedies.

english: at the worst; no big deal
semanticNote: 'Worst case' / 'no big deal' — used to dismiss a worry. 大不了我辭職 (worst case I quit). Casual, often defiant tone. Implies acceptance of the worst outcome.

examples.chinese: 大不了我們重新開始。
examples.pinyin: Dàbuliǎo wǒmen chóngxīn kāishǐ.
examples.english: Worst case, we just start over.

examples.chinese: 大不了被拒絕，也沒什麼好怕的，試試看。
examples.pinyin: Dàbuliǎo bèi jùjué, yě méi shénme hǎo pà de, shì shì kàn.
examples.english: At worst you'll be rejected — nothing to fear, just give it a try.

semanticNote: High-ranking minister in an imperial court. Historical/literary — Chinese emperors had 大臣, kings of Britain still have ministers translated this way. Period-drama and history vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 皇帝召見了大臣們。
examples.pinyin: Huángdì zhàojiànle dàchénmen.
examples.english: The emperor summoned his ministers.

examples.chinese: 這位大臣忠心耿耿，從不結黨營私。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi dàchén zhōngxīn-gěnggěng, cóng bù jiédǎng-yíngsī.
examples.english: This minister was utterly loyal and never formed cliques for personal gain.

semanticNote: 'Everyone' / 'all of us' — colloquial and warm. Heavily Northern/Mainland flavored, especially the 兒 (er) ending. Tim's 'gang/group' word. In Taiwan, 大家 dominates.

examples.chinese: 大夥兒一起努力!
examples.pinyin: Dàhuǒr yìqǐ nǔlì!
examples.english: Let's all work hard together!

examples.chinese: 大夥兒齊心協力，把這件事辦得很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Dàhuǒr qíxīn-xiélì, bǎ zhè jiàn shì bàn de hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: Everyone pulled together and handled this matter beautifully.

semanticNote: 'Without restraint' — usually for negative actions: 大肆破壞 (wantonly destroy), 大肆批評 (heap criticism on), 大肆宣傳 (heavy-handed propaganda). Critical tone — implies excess and lack of limit.

examples.chinese: 媒體大肆報導這件事。
examples.pinyin: Méitǐ dàsì bàodǎo zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: The media reported on this matter excessively.

examples.chinese: 不法商人大肆偽造品牌商品，侵害了消費者的權益。
examples.pinyin: Bùfǎ shāngrén dàsì wèizào pǐnpái shāngpǐn, qīnhài le xiāofèizhě de quányì.
examples.english: Illegal merchants wantonly counterfeited branded goods, infringing on consumers' rights.

semanticNote: 'Broadly speaking' / 'overall.' 大體上 (overall), 大體相同 (broadly the same). Common in summarizing and analytical contexts. Compare to 大致 (approximately, similar).

examples.chinese: 情況大體上是這樣的。
examples.pinyin: Qíngkuàng dàtǐ shàng shì zhèyàng de.
examples.english: The situation is generally like this.

examples.chinese: 他大體上同意這個方案，但細節上有幾點需要調整。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàtǐ shàng tóngyì zhège fāng'àn, dàn xìjié shàng yǒu jǐ diǎn xūyào tiáozhěng.
examples.english: He generally agreed to this plan, but there were a few details that needed adjustment.

semanticNote: Tonal heteronym: (1) dàyì — gist/main idea (文章的大意 = the main point of the article); (2) dàyi (neutral tone) — careless, off-guard (一時大意 = a momentary lapse, 別大意 = don't let your guard down). Tone disambiguates.

examples.chinese: 請告訴我這篇文章的大意。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosù wǒ zhè piān wénzhāng de dàyì.
examples.english: Please tell me the main idea of this article.

examples.chinese: 考試時不要大意。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì shí búyào dàyi.
examples.english: Don't be careless during the exam.

semanticNote: 'Approximately' / 'broadly.' 大致相同 (roughly the same), 大致了解 (have a general understanding). Common in estimates and overviews. Sister-adverb to 大體.

examples.chinese: 我大致了解了情況。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dàzhì liǎojiěle qíngkuàng.
examples.english: I have a general understanding of the situation.

examples.chinese: 兩者大致相同，但仔細比較還是能發現微小差異。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhě dàzhì xiāngtóng, dàn zǐxì bǐjiào háishì néng fāxiàn wēixiǎo chāyì.
examples.english: The two are roughly the same, but careful comparison still reveals subtle differences.

semanticNote: News-vocabulary word for criminals — robbers, thugs, criminals caught in news stories. 歹徒被捕 (the criminals were arrested). Slightly old-fashioned/dramatic — common in headlines.

examples.chinese: 警方很快抓住了歹徒。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng hěn kuài zhuāzhùle dǎitú.
examples.english: The police quickly caught the criminals.

examples.chinese: 歹徒持刀搶劫便利商店，卻被店員機智地拖延了時間，直到警方趕到。
examples.pinyin: Dǎitú chí dāo qiǎngjié biànlì shāngdiàn, què bèi diànyuán jīzhì de tuōyán le shíjiān, zhídào jǐngfāng gǎndào.
examples.english: The criminal robbed a convenience store at knifepoint but was cleverly stalled by the clerk until police arrived.

semanticNote: The price you pay — usually figurative. 付出代價 (pay the price), 沉重的代價 (heavy cost), 不惜任何代價 (whatever it costs). Used for moral, emotional, or strategic costs, not literal prices.

examples.chinese: 自由是要付出代價的。
examples.pinyin: Zìyóu shì yào fùchū dàijià de.
examples.english: Freedom comes at a price.

examples.chinese: 為了成功，他付出了極大的代價，犧牲了健康與家庭生活。
examples.pinyin: Wèile chénggōng, tā fùchūle jí dà de dàijià, xīshēngle jiànkāng yǔ jiātíng shēnghuó.
examples.english: In pursuit of success, he paid a great price, sacrificing his health and family life.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) acting in someone's role temporarily — 代理董事長 (acting chairman), 代理總統 (acting president); (2) acting on someone's behalf — 代理商 (sales agent), 法律代理人 (legal representative). Business and legal contexts.

examples.chinese: 她暫時代理經理的職務。
examples.pinyin: Tā zànshí dàilǐ jīnglǐ de zhíwù.
examples.english: She's temporarily acting in the manager role.

examples.chinese: 這家貿易公司是那個歐洲品牌在臺灣的獨家代理商。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā màoyì gōngsī shì nà ge Ōuzhōu pǐnpái zài Táiwān de dújiā dàilǐshāng.
examples.english: This trading company is the exclusive agent for that European brand in Taiwan.

semanticNote: To lead a group — physically (帶領遊客 = lead tourists) or organizationally (帶領團隊 = lead a team). Implies guiding others by example or direction. Common in leadership and tour-guiding contexts.

examples.chinese: 他帶領團隊取得了成功。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàilǐng tuánduì qǔdéle chénggōng.
examples.english: He led the team to success.

examples.chinese: 導遊帶領遊客欣賞了國立故宮博物院的珍貴文物。
examples.pinyin: Dǎoyóu dàilǐng yóukè xīnshǎngle Guólì Gùgōng Bówùyuàn de zhēnguì wénwù.
examples.english: The tour guide led visitors to appreciate the precious cultural artifacts at the National Palace Museum.

semanticNote: To give cold/indifferent treatment to someone (especially a guest). Often used in apologetic phrasing: 招待不周,怠慢了 (sorry for the inadequate hospitality). Hospitality-culture vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 招待不周,怠慢了各位。
examples.pinyin: Zhāodài bù zhōu, dàimànle gèwèi.
examples.english: Forgive my poor hospitality.

examples.chinese: 服務生怠慢了那桌顧客，老闆立刻道歉並補送一道菜。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùshēng dàimànle nà zhuō gùkè, lǎobǎn lìkè dàoqiàn bìng bǔ sòng yī dào cài.
examples.english: The waiter was negligent with those customers, so the boss immediately apologized and sent an extra dish.

semanticNote: Formal arrest — by law enforcement. 逮捕令 (arrest warrant). News and legal vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 警方逮捕了嫌疑犯。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔle xiányífàn.
examples.english: Police arrested the suspect.

examples.chinese: 國際刑警組織協助各國逮捕跨境罪犯。
examples.pinyin: Guójì Xíngjǐng Zǔzhī xiézhù gè guó dàibǔ kuàjìng zuìfàn.
examples.english: Interpol assists countries in arresting cross-border criminals.

semanticNote: To formally guarantee — usually financial (loan guarantee) or for someone's character/conduct (vouch for them). 擔保人 (guarantor). Compare to 保證 (guarantee, broader/everyday).

examples.chinese: 我可以為他擔保。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèi tā dānbǎo.
examples.english: I can vouch for him.

examples.chinese: 他用自己的房子作抵押，為這筆貸款擔保。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng zìjǐ de fángzi zuò dǐyā, wèi zhè bǐ dàikuǎn dānbǎo.
examples.english: He used his house as collateral to guarantee this loan.

semanticNote: Lacking courage in the moment — afraid to speak up, take action, take risks. 膽怯的眼神 (timid look). Compare to 膽小 (timid, more colloquial) and 懦弱 (cowardly, harsher and more characterological).

examples.chinese: 他在陌生人面前很膽怯。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài mòshēngrén miànqián hěn dǎnqiè.
examples.english: He's very timid around strangers.

examples.chinese: 第一次上台表演時，她感到十分膽怯。
examples.pinyin: Dì yī cì shàngtái biǎoyǎn shí, tā gǎndào shífēn dǎnqiè.
examples.english: When performing on stage for the first time, she felt extremely timid.

semanticNote: Formal birthday — used for important historical figures (孫中山誕辰 = Sun Yat-sen's birthday) or in highly respectful contexts. For everyday birthdays, use 生日.

examples.chinese: 今年是這位偉人誕辰一百周年。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián shì zhè wèi wěirén dànchén yìbǎi zhōunián.
examples.english: This year is the 100th anniversary of this great figure's birth.

examples.chinese: 今天是父親的七十誕辰，全家人聚在一起慶祝。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì fùqīn de qīshí dànchén, quánjiārén jù zài yìqǐ qìngzhù.
examples.english: Today is Father's seventieth birthday, and the whole family gathered to celebrate.

english: to be born; come into being
semanticNote: Formal/literary birth — usually used for great figures, ideas, organizations, eras (一個新時代誕生了 = a new era was born). For everyday people being born, use 出生.

examples.chinese: 這個品牌誕生於1995年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge pǐnpái dànshēng yú yī jiǔ jiǔ wǔ nián.
examples.english: This brand was born in 1995.

examples.chinese: 隨著科技的進步，許多新的產業模式正在誕生。
examples.pinyin: Suízhe kējì de jìnbù, xǔduō xīn de chǎnyè móshì zhèngzài dànshēng.
examples.english: With advances in technology, many new business models are coming into being.

semanticNote: Off-season for business, travel, agriculture. Pair with 旺季 (peak season). Tourism, hospitality, retail vocabulary. 淡季打折 = off-season discounts.

examples.chinese: 冬天是這家飯店的淡季。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān shì zhè jiā fàndiàn de dànjì.
examples.english: Winter is this hotel's off-season.

examples.chinese: 淡季時房價通常比旺季便宜許多，適合旅遊預算有限的旅客。
examples.pinyin: Dànjì shí fángjià tōngcháng bǐ wàngjì piányí xǔduō, shìhé lǚyóu yùsuàn yǒuxiàn de lǚkè.
examples.english: Room rates in the off-season are usually much cheaper than peak season, ideal for budget-conscious travelers.

semanticNote: Freshwater — pair with 鹹水 (saltwater). 淡水魚 (freshwater fish). Geography and ecology vocabulary. Also a famous district in northern Taiwan: 淡水 (Tamsui).

examples.chinese: 地球上的淡水資源很有限。
examples.pinyin: Dìqiú shàng de dànshuǐ zīyuán hěn yǒuxiàn.
examples.english: Earth's freshwater resources are very limited.

examples.chinese: 淡水鱸魚是臺灣常見的養殖魚類之一。
examples.pinyin: Dànshuǐ lúyú shì Táiwān cháng jiàn de yǎngzhí yúlèi zhī yī.
examples.english: Freshwater bass is one of the common farmed fish species in Taiwan.

semanticNote: Protein (nutrition/biology). Literally 'egg-white substance.' Health, fitness, and dietary vocabulary. 高蛋白 = high-protein.

examples.chinese: 運動後要補充蛋白質。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng hòu yào bǔchōng dànbáizhì.
examples.english: After exercise you need to replenish protein.

examples.chinese: 豆腐是優質植物性蛋白質的重要來源。
examples.pinyin: Dòufu shì yōuzhì zhíwùxìng dànbáizhì de zhòngyào láiyuán.
examples.english: Tofu is an important source of high-quality plant-based protein.

english: on the spot; at the scene
semanticNote: Immediately, in the moment, at the scene. 當場拒絕 (refuse on the spot), 當場死亡 (died at the scene). Implies immediacy and the same physical location.

examples.chinese: 他當場就答應了。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngchǎng jiù dāyìng le.
examples.english: He agreed on the spot.

examples.chinese: 小偷被當場抓住，無法抵賴。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu bèi dāngchǎng zhuāzhù, wúfǎ dǐlài.
examples.english: The thief was caught red-handed and had no way to deny it.

semanticNote: Refers to a past time when a decision was made — often with retrospective regret or reflection. 當初我為什麼會... (back then, why did I ever...). Carries a wistful/nostalgic flavor.

examples.chinese: 早知道是這樣,當初就不該答應。
examples.pinyin: Zǎo zhīdào shì zhèyàng, dāngchū jiù bù gāi dāyìng.
examples.english: If I'd known it would be like this, I shouldn't have agreed back then.

examples.chinese: 他後悔當初沒有把握那個工作機會。
examples.pinyin: Tā hòuhuǐ dāngchū méiyǒu bǎwò nà ge gōngzuò jīhuì.
examples.english: He regrets not having seized that job opportunity back then.

semanticNote: Contemporary era — used for art (當代藝術), literature, society, music. Distinguished from 現代 (modern, broader 1900-present) — 當代 specifically means living-now contemporary.

examples.chinese: 她是當代著名的作家。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì dāngdài zhùmíng de zuòjiā.
examples.english: She's a famous contemporary writer.

examples.chinese: 當代藝術打破了許多傳統的創作框架，引發廣泛討論。
examples.pinyin: Dāngdài yìshù dǎpòle xǔduō chuántǒng de chuàngzuò kuāngjià, yǐnfā guǎngfàn tǎolùn.
examples.english: Contemporary art has broken many traditional creative frameworks, sparking widespread discussion.

semanticNote: Face to face — when contrasting with messages, gossip, or behind-the-back action. 當面說 (say to my face), 當面道歉 (apologize in person). Direct, sometimes confrontational flavor.

examples.chinese: 有意見當面說。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu yìjiàn dāngmiàn shuō.
examples.english: If you have an opinion, say it to my face.

examples.chinese: 她決定當面向他道歉，而不是發簡訊。
examples.pinyin: Tā juédìng dāngmiàn xiàng tā dàoqiàn, ér bù shì fā jiǎnxùn.
examples.english: She decided to apologize to him in person rather than by text message.

semanticNote: Current state of affairs — typically used in formal/analytical contexts. 當前形勢 (current situation), 當前的問題 (the present issue). Common in news and analysis. More formal than 現在 (now).

examples.chinese: 當前的經濟形勢比較嚴峻。
examples.pinyin: Dāngqián de jīngjì xíngshì bǐjiào yánjùn.
examples.english: The current economic situation is quite serious.

examples.chinese: 解決氣候變遷是當前人類面臨的最重大課題之一。
examples.pinyin: Jiějué qìhòu biànqiān shì dāngqián rénlèi miànlín de zuì zhòngdà kètí zhī yī.
examples.english: Addressing climate change is one of the most pressing issues facing humanity today.

english: the persons involved; parties to (a case)
semanticNote: The actual people involved in an event, dispute, or legal case. 你不是當事人 (you weren't involved). Common in legal contexts (parties to a contract/case) and in 'mind your own business' contexts.

examples.chinese: 當事人都沒說話,你別插嘴。
examples.pinyin: Dāngshìrén dōu méi shuōhuà, nǐ bié chāzuǐ.
examples.english: The people involved aren't even talking — don't butt in.

examples.chinese: 法院要求當事人在指定日期出庭。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn yāoqiú dāngshìrén zài zhǐdìng rìqī chūtíng.
examples.english: The court required the parties involved to appear on the designated date.

semanticNote: 'The most urgent thing right now.' Used to focus attention on the highest priority. 當務之急是解決問題 (the priority right now is solving the problem). Common in management and policy contexts.

examples.chinese: 當務之急是穩定市場。
examples.pinyin: Dāngwùzhījí shì wěndìng shìchǎng.
examples.english: The top priority is stabilizing the market.

examples.chinese: 災後重建是當務之急，政府立即投入大量資源。
examples.pinyin: Zāi hòu chóngjiàn shì dāngwùzhījí, zhèngfǔ lìjí tóurù dàliàng zīyuán.
examples.english: Post-disaster reconstruction is the top priority; the government immediately mobilized large resources.

semanticNote: To be elected to a position via voting. 當選總統 (be elected president), 高票當選 (elected by a wide margin). News and politics vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 他當選了新一任的市長。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngxuǎnle xīn yí rèn de shìzhǎng.
examples.english: He was elected the new mayor.

examples.chinese: 她以高票當選學生會主席。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐ gāo piào dāngxuǎn xuéshēnghuì zhǔxí.
examples.english: She was elected student council president by a large margin.

semanticNote: Political party. 共產黨 (Communist Party), 民進黨 (DPP — Democratic Progressive Party in Taiwan), 國民黨 (KMT). Also: 黨員 (party member), 入黨 (join the party). Politically heavy word in Chinese-speaking world.

examples.chinese: 他加入了這個政黨。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiārùle zhè ge zhèngdǎng.
examples.english: He joined this political party.

examples.chinese: 兩黨之間的協商破裂，導致政府停擺。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng dǎng zhījiān de xiéshāng pòliè, dǎozhì zhèngfǔ tíngbǎi.
examples.english: Negotiations between the two parties collapsed, causing a government shutdown.

semanticNote: A file or record — both physical archives and digital files. 個人檔案 (personal file), 電子檔案 (electronic file). In Taiwan, the standard everyday word for computer file (whereas mainland often uses 文件). Tim's locked decision: 文件 stays as the broader 'document' word.

examples.chinese: 請把檔案存到電腦裡。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ dàng'àn cún dào diànnǎo lǐ.
examples.english: Please save the file to the computer.

examples.chinese: 國家檔案局保存著大量珍貴的歷史文獻。
examples.pinyin: Guójiā dàng'ànjú bǎocúnzhe dàliàng zhēnguì de lìshǐ wénxiàn.
examples.english: The National Archives preserves a large number of precious historical documents.

semanticNote: Quality grade or tier — products, restaurants, hotels, levels of taste. 高檔次 (high-end), 提升檔次 (raise the level/class). Status-aware word in commerce.

examples.chinese: 這家餐廳檔次很高。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng dàngcì hěn gāo.
examples.english: This restaurant is very high-end.

examples.chinese: 換了新裝潢之後，這家店整體檔次提升了不少。
examples.pinyin: Huànle xīn zhuānghuáng zhīhòu, zhè jiā diàn zhěngtǐ dàngcì tíshēngle bù shǎo.
examples.english: After the renovation, the overall class of this store improved significantly.

semanticNote: Guided missile. 導彈試射 (missile test launch), 彈道導彈 (ballistic missile). Military and news vocabulary. Also pronounced 飛彈 (fēidàn) in Taiwan, which is the more common term there.

examples.chinese: 這個國家研發了新型導彈。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge guójiā yánfāle xīnxíng dǎodàn.
examples.english: This country has developed a new type of missile.

examples.chinese: 反導彈系統能夠攔截來襲的彈道導彈。
examples.pinyin: Fǎn dǎodàn xìtǒng nénggòu lánjié láixí de dàndào dǎodàn.
examples.english: An anti-missile system can intercept incoming ballistic missiles.

semanticNote: Navigation — GPS, ships, aircraft. Modern dominant use: GPS in cars and phones (打開導航 = open the navigation). Tech vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 開車最好用導航。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē zuìhǎo yòng dǎoháng.
examples.english: It's best to use GPS when driving.

examples.chinese: 古代船員利用星象進行海上導航。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài chuányuán lìyòng xīngxiàng jìnxíng hǎishàng dǎoháng.
examples.english: Ancient sailors used celestial observations for maritime navigation.

semanticNote: To direct/orient toward — strategy, behavior, society. 結果導向 (results-oriented), 用戶導向 (user-oriented), 政策導向 (policy direction). Modern business and policy vocabulary; the 'X-oriented' suffix is everywhere now.

examples.chinese: 我們公司是用戶導向的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī shì yònghù dǎoxiàng de.
examples.english: Our company is user-oriented.

examples.chinese: 教育應以培養批判性思維為導向。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoyù yīng yǐ péiyǎng pīpànxìng sīwéi wéi dǎoxiàng.
examples.english: Education should be oriented toward cultivating critical thinking.

english: to make trouble; cause a disturbance
semanticNote: To deliberately disrupt — kids acting up in class, troublemakers in a meeting, hecklers. 別搗亂 (stop making trouble). Familiar from parental and teacherly vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 小孩在教室搗亂。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái zài jiàoshì dǎoluàn.
examples.english: The kid is making trouble in the classroom.

examples.chinese: 他故意搗亂會議秩序，被工作人員請出會場。
examples.pinyin: Tā gùyì dǎoluàn huìyì zhìxù, bèi gōngzuòrényuán qǐng chū huìchǎng.
examples.english: He deliberately disrupted the meeting order and was escorted out by staff.

semanticNote: Business failure / closure — store, company, factory. 公司倒閉了 (the company went bankrupt). Different from 破產 (personal bankruptcy, broader). 倒閉 specifically applies to a business that shut down.

examples.chinese: 那家百年老店終於倒閉了。
examples.pinyin: Nà jiā bǎinián lǎodiàn zhōngyú dǎobì le.
examples.english: That century-old store finally closed down.

examples.chinese: 金融危機期間，許多中小企業相繼倒閉。
examples.pinyin: Jīnróng wēijī qījiān, xǔduō zhōngxiǎo qǐyè xiāngjì dǎobì.
examples.english: During the financial crisis, many small and medium enterprises went bankrupt one after another.

semanticNote: Formal/legal term for theft. 盜竊罪 (theft as a crime), 盜竊案 (theft case). More formal than 偷 (steal, everyday) — used in court and news. 數據盜竊 = data theft (modern context).

examples.chinese: 警方破獲了一起盜竊案。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng pòhuòle yì qǐ dàoqiè àn.
examples.english: The police cracked a theft case.

examples.chinese: 他因盜竊罪被判處三年有期徒刑。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn dàoqiè zuì bèi pànchǔ sān nián yǒuqī túxíng.
examples.english: He was sentenced to three years in prison for theft.

semanticNote: Unhusked rice — the grain on the stalk or in storage. 稻穀豐收 (a bountiful rice harvest). Compare to 米 (uncooked rice grains, market-ready) and 飯 (cooked rice). Agricultural word.

examples.chinese: 今年的稻穀大豐收。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de dàogǔ dà fēngshōu.
examples.english: This year's rice harvest is bountiful.

examples.chinese: 農民們正在田裡收割稻穀，忙得不可開交。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmínmen zhèngzài tián lǐ shōugē dàogǔ, máng de bùkě-kāijiāo.
examples.english: The farmers were harvesting rice in the fields, overwhelmingly busy.

english: the gains don't outweigh the losses (idiom)
semanticNote: Net loss when you weigh costs vs. benefits. Used to caution against decisions where the price is too high. 這樣做太得不償失了 (it's not worth it). Common in advice and analytical contexts.

examples.chinese: 為了省小錢花了大時間,得不償失。
examples.pinyin: Wèile shěng xiǎo qián huāle dà shíjiān, débùchángshī.
examples.english: Spending big time to save small money — not worth it.

examples.chinese: 為了追求短期利潤而忽視產品品質，長期來看得不償失。
examples.pinyin: Wèile zhuīqiú duǎnqī lìrùn ér hūshì chǎnpǐn pǐnzhì, chángqī lái kàn débùchángshī.
examples.english: Pursuing short-term profits at the expense of product quality is ultimately not worth it in the long run.

semanticNote: Capable and dependable — usually applied to subordinates, assistants, helpers. 得力助手 (capable assistant — common compliment), 得力幹將 (an effective achiever). High praise in workplace contexts.

examples.chinese: 她是老闆的得力助手。
