components.meaning: to plan; delineate; draw a line

examples.chinese: 政府將這片土地劃分為農業用地和住宅用地。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiāng zhè piàn tǔdì huàfēn wéi nóngyè yòngdì hé zhùzhái yòngdì.
examples.english: The government divided this land into agricultural land and residential land.

examples.chinese: 這道河流自然地劃分了兩個行政區。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào héliú zìrán de huàfēnle liǎng ge xíngzhèngqū.
examples.english: This river naturally demarcates two administrative districts.

english: draw legs on a snake; ruin something by adding the superfluous
semanticNote: From a classic fable: competitors raced to draw a snake; one finished first but then started adding legs, allowing a slower competitor to win. Means to ruin a perfectly good thing by adding unnecessary elements. 你說的已經夠清楚了，再解釋就是畫蛇添足 (what you said was already clear — any more explanation is adding legs to a snake). A criticism of over-elaboration or unnecessary additions.

examples.chinese: 這篇文章結構完整，再加一段就是畫蛇添足了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng jiégòu wánzhěng, zài jiā yī duàn jiù shì huàshétiānzú le.
examples.english: This essay has a complete structure — adding another paragraph would be adding legs to a snake.

examples.chinese: 他的設計已經很好了，修改反而畫蛇添足。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shèjì yǐjīng hěn hǎo le, xiūgǎi fǎn'ér huàshétiānzú.
examples.english: His design is already excellent — making changes would only ruin it.

semanticNote: Technically: any tube or device that carries voice — microphone, phone handset, megaphone. In modern usage: primarily microphone (often interchangeable with 麥克風 mic — the loanword). 拿起話筒 (pick up the receiver/mic), 對著話筒說話 (speak into the microphone). 麥克風 is more common for stage/recording mics; 話筒 can still refer to the phone handset in older or formal usage.

examples.chinese: 主持人拿起話筒，宣布晚會正式開始。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔchírén ná qǐ huàtǒng, xuānbù wǎnhuì zhèngshì kāishǐ.
examples.english: The host picked up the microphone and announced the evening event officially open.

examples.chinese: 她緊張地對著話筒清了清嗓子。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǐnzhāng de duìzhe huàtǒng qīngle qīng sǎngzi.
examples.english: Nervously, she cleared her throat into the microphone.

semanticNote: Joyful happiness — lively and festive rather than quiet contentment. 歡樂的氣氛 (a joyful atmosphere), 充滿歡樂 (full of joy), 歡樂時光 (happy times). More exuberant than 幸福 (happiness as contentment/bliss) and 快樂 (happy — general and versatile). 歡樂 suggests a shared, celebratory, animated joy — parties, festivals, family gatherings all have 歡樂.

examples.chinese: 春節期間，到處都洋溢著歡樂的氣氛。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié qījiān, dàochù dōu yángyìzhe huānlè de qìfēn.
examples.english: During Chinese New Year, there's a joyful atmosphere everywhere.

examples.chinese: 孩子們在公園裡玩耍，充滿歡樂。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài gōngyuán lǐ wánshuǎ, chōngmǎn huānlè.
examples.english: The children played in the park, full of joy.

english: restore; return to original state; (chemistry) reduce
semanticNote: To bring something back to its original state — 還原真相 (restore the truth), 還原現場 (reconstruct the scene), 還原歷史 (restore/reconstruct history). In chemistry: reduction (the opposite of oxidation). Forensic and investigative use is common: 還原事件經過 (reconstruct the sequence of events). Also used in cooking/nutrition: 還原奶 (reconstituted milk — dried milk with water added back).

examples.chinese: 警方試圖還原案發當天的現場情況。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng shìtú huányuán ànfā dāngtiān de xiànchǎng qíngkuàng.
examples.english: Police tried to reconstruct the situation at the crime scene on the day of the incident.

examples.chinese: 這款修復液聲稱能還原受損的頭髮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn xiūfù yè shēngchēng néng huányuán shòusǔn de tóufa.
examples.english: This repair serum claims to restore damaged hair to its original state.

english: link; ring; segment; part of a chain
semanticNote: A link in a chain — a component stage in a process or system. 關鍵環節 (key link/stage), 薄弱環節 (weak link), 各個環節 (every stage/link). The image is of chain links — each 環節 connects to others and the whole breaks if one fails. Common in business process, supply chain, and systems analysis. Different from 步驟 (step — implies a sequence you follow) — 環節 emphasizes the interconnectedness.

examples.chinese: 食品安全需要控制好每一個生產環節。
examples.pinyin: Shípǐn ānquán xūyào kòngzhì hǎo měi yī ge shēngchǎn huánjié.
examples.english: Food safety requires controlling every link in the production chain.

examples.chinese: 客服是整個服務流程中最重要的環節之一。
examples.pinyin: Kèfú shì zhěng ge fúwù liúchéng zhōng zuì zhòngyào de huánjié zhī yī.
examples.english: Customer service is one of the most important links in the entire service process.

semanticNote: To reduce tension or soften a situation — 緩和局勢 (ease tensions), 緩和氣氛 (lighten the atmosphere), 關係緩和 (relations have eased). Both verb and adjective. In diplomacy: 中美關係有所緩和 (China-US relations have eased somewhat). Also for physical/medical: 症狀緩和 (symptoms have moderated). Implies things are still tense but less so — a reduction, not a resolution.

examples.chinese: 雙方做出讓步，緊張局勢略有緩和。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng zuòchū ràngbù, jǐnzhāng júshì lüè yǒu huǎnhé.
examples.english: Both sides made concessions and the tense situation eased slightly.

examples.chinese: 他開了個玩笑，讓尷尬的氣氛緩和了一些。
examples.pinyin: Tā kāile ge wánxiào, ràng gāngà de qìfēn huǎnhéle yīxiē.
examples.english: He cracked a joke and lightened the awkward atmosphere a little.

semanticNote: A medical patient — someone suffering from an illness. 癌症患者 (cancer patient), 患者的需求 (the needs of patients). More clinical than 病人 (sick person — everyday word) — 患者 is the formal/written term used in medical records, news reports, and academic writing. 患 means to suffer from an illness; 者 = person. In Taiwan hospital contexts, official signage and announcements use 患者 over 病人.

examples.chinese: 醫院為長期患者提供了特別的照護計畫。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn wèi chángqī huànzhě tígōngle tèbié de zhàohù jìhuà.
examples.english: The hospital provided a special care plan for long-term patients.

examples.chinese: 這種藥物在初期患者身上效果顯著。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yàowù zài chūqī huànzhě shēnshàng xiàoguǒ xiǎnzhù.
examples.english: This medication shows significant effects in patients in the early stages.

semanticNote: Desolate — abandoned, empty, and lonely. 荒涼的原野 (a desolate plain), 荒涼的小鎮 (a bleak ghost town). Combines physical barrenness (荒 = wasteland) with an emotional bleakness (涼 = cold/cool). More evocative and melancholy than just 荒廢 (abandoned/in disuse). A 荒涼 landscape makes you feel the loneliness. Common in literary descriptions and travel writing about remote or uninhabited places.

examples.chinese: 地震後，這個小村莊變得荒涼，人去樓空。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn hòu, zhège xiǎo cūnzhuāng biàn de huāngliáng, rén qù lóu kōng.
examples.english: After the earthquake, this small village became desolate — completely deserted.

examples.chinese: 夕陽下，荒涼的沙漠顯得格外孤寂。
examples.pinyin: Xīyáng xià, huāngliáng de shāmò xiǎn de géwài gūjì.
examples.english: Under the setting sun, the desolate desert looked especially lonely.

semanticNote: Something logically or morally absurd — beyond reason or decency. 荒謬的理由 (a preposterous reason), 荒謬至極 (utterly absurd), 荒謬的現象 (an absurd phenomenon). Stronger than 可笑 (laughable) and more formal than 扯淡 (bullshit — vulgar). Also a philosophical/literary term: 荒謬主義 (absurdism — Camus etc.). In everyday Mandarin, 荒謬 is mid-register — emphatic but not vulgar.

examples.chinese: 他給出的理由荒謬至極，根本站不住腳。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi chū de lǐyóu huāngmiù zhì jí, gēnběn zhàn bú zhù jiǎo.
examples.english: The reason he gave was utterly preposterous — completely without merit.

examples.chinese: 這個規定太荒謬了，誰想得出來的？
examples.pinyin: Zhège guīdìng tài huāngmiù le, shuí xiǎng de chūlái de?
examples.english: This rule is absurd — who came up with it?

semanticNote: Absurd or outrageous — similar to 荒謬 but slightly more colloquial and can also describe behavior (wild, dissolute, reckless). 這個主意太荒唐了 (this idea is outrageous), 荒唐的行為 (outrageous behavior). Also implies moral recklessness: 他年輕時做過很多荒唐事 (he did a lot of wild/foolish things when he was young). 荒唐 is often used with a shake of the head.

examples.chinese: 他說的話太荒唐了，在場所有人都不相信。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà tài huāngtang le, zàichǎng suǒyǒu rén dōu bù xiāngxìn.
examples.english: What he said was so outrageous that nobody present believed it.

examples.chinese: 年輕時犯的那些荒唐錯誤讓他後悔不已。
examples.pinyin: Niánqīng shí fàn de nàxiē huāngtang cuòwù ràng tā hòuhuǐ bùyǐ.
examples.english: The wild mistakes he made in his youth fill him with endless regret.

semanticNote: Emperor — the supreme ruler of imperial China. 中國歷史上有多少個皇帝？ Common in historical discussion. Colloquial extension: 他在家裡是皇帝 (he acts like an emperor at home — spoiled/pampered). Also: 皇帝不急，急死太監 (a proverb — 'the emperor's not worried, but it's killing the eunuchs' = don't stress more than the person in charge). 天皇 = Japanese emperor (different term).

examples.chinese: 乾隆皇帝是清朝在位最久的皇帝之一。
examples.pinyin: Qiánlóng huángdì shì Qīngcháo zàiwèi zuì jiǔ de huángdì zhī yī.
examples.english: Emperor Qianlong is one of the longest-reigning emperors of the Qing dynasty.

examples.chinese: 他在家被寵得像個小皇帝。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiā bèi chǒng de xiàng ge xiǎo huángdì.
examples.english: He's been spoiled at home like a little emperor.

semanticNote: The emperor's principal wife — empress. 武則天是中國歷史上唯一的女皇帝 (Wu Zetian is the only female emperor in Chinese history — distinct from 皇后 which is a consort title). Used historically and colloquially as a term for a dominant or exceptional woman. Taiwan's brand 皇后 appears in various product names. Note: not to be confused with 女王 (queen who rules in her own right, as in modern monarchies).

examples.chinese: 她在劇中扮演一位深宮裡的皇後。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jù zhōng bànyǎn yī wèi shēngōng lǐ de huánghòu.
examples.english: She plays an empress living deep in the imperial palace in the drama.

examples.chinese: 武則天從皇後晉升為中國唯一的女皇帝。
examples.pinyin: Wǔ Zétiān cóng huánghòu jìnshēng wéi Zhōngguó wéiyī de nǚ huángdì.
examples.english: Wu Zetian rose from empress consort to become China's only female emperor.

semanticNote: The period just after sunset — dusk, twilight. 黃昏時分 (at dusk), 夕陽黃昏 (twilight sunset). Has a literary and slightly melancholy tone. Commonly used in poetry and song lyrics. 黃昏戀 (twilight romance — romance between elderly people; lit. 'dusk love') is a common term for late-life relationships. The word 黃昏 is more literary than 傍晚 (evening — the everyday word for this time period).

examples.chinese: 黃昏時，他們坐在海邊看著夕陽慢慢沉入海面。
examples.pinyin: Huánghūn shí, tāmen zuò zài hǎibiān kànzhe xīyáng màn màn chén rù hǎimiàn.
examples.english: At dusk, they sat by the sea watching the sun slowly sink into the horizon.

examples.chinese: 黃昏的光線讓這座城市顯得格外迷人。
examples.pinyin: Huánghūn de guāngxiàn ràng zhè zuò chéngshì xiǎnde géwài mírén.
examples.english: The twilight light makes this city look especially enchanting.

english: suddenly see the light; have a sudden realization
semanticNote: The sudden flash of understanding — 'aha moment.' 恍 means dazed or suddenly; 然 = in that manner; 大悟 = great awakening. Used when something that was confusing suddenly clicks into place. 他聽完解釋後恍然大悟 (after hearing the explanation, he suddenly understood). The English equivalent is 'the penny dropped' or 'it finally clicked.' Positive and satisfying feeling — not just any realization, but a big one.

examples.chinese: 聽到這個解釋，我才恍然大悟，原來問題出在這裡。
examples.pinyin: Tīng dào zhège jiěshì, wǒ cái huǎngrándàwù, yuánlái wèntí chū zài zhèlǐ.
examples.english: Hearing this explanation, I finally had my aha moment — so that's where the problem was.

examples.chinese: 他思考了很久，終於恍然大悟，找到了解決方案。
examples.pinyin: Tā sīkǎole hěn jiǔ, zhōngyú huǎngrándàwù, zhǎodàole jiějué fāng'àn.
examples.english: He thought about it for a long time and finally had a flash of insight — finding the solution.

semanticNote: To sway or shake — 搖晃 (rock/sway — the common compound), 晃眼 (dazzle the eyes), 晃動 (shake/rock). Heteronym: 晃 huǎng (third tone) = to flash/dazzle, to shake quickly; 晃 huàng (fourth tone) = to sway slowly. In common usage 搖晃 (second + fourth tone) is how most people use the concept. 別晃了 = stop swaying/shaking.

examples.chinese: 地震時，吊燈不停地晃動。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn shí, diàodēng bù tíng de huàngdòng.
examples.english: During the earthquake, the hanging lights kept swaying.

examples.chinese: 他喝醉了，走路搖搖晃晃的。
examples.pinyin: Tā hēzuì le, zǒulù yáoyao huànghuàng de.
examples.english: He was drunk and walking in a swaying, staggering way.

semanticNote: To spend money lavishly and wastefully — 揮霍無度 (spend without restraint), 揮霍金錢 (squander money). Always negative; implies irresponsible excess. 他把遺產全部揮霍一空 (he squandered the entire inheritance). More emphatic than 浪費 (waste — can be mild) — 揮霍 suggests a reckless, almost ostentatious spending. Common in cautionary tales about wealth and responsibility.

components.meaning: to wave; to wield; to scatter

examples.chinese: 他年輕時揮霍無度，把家產敗光了。
examples.pinyin: Tā niánqīng shí huīhuò wúdù, bǎ jiāchǎn bài guāng le.
examples.english: In his youth he spent without restraint and squandered the family fortune.

examples.chinese: 不要揮霍父母辛苦賺來的錢。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào huīhuò fùmǔ xīnkǔ zhuànlái de qián.
examples.english: Don't squander the money your parents worked hard to earn.

semanticNote: Glorious and brilliant — 輝煌的成就 (brilliant achievements), 輝煌的歷史 (glorious history), 前途輝煌 (a brilliant future). Both literally bright and figuratively glorious. 輝 = radiance/glow; 煌 = brilliant light. Often applied to civilizations, sports careers, and achievements — things that shine brightly in their field. 創造輝煌 (create glory/achieve brilliance) is a common motivational phrase.

examples.chinese: 中華文明有著幾千年輝煌的歷史。
examples.pinyin: Zhōnghuá wénmíng yǒuzhe jǐ qiān nián huīhuáng de lìshǐ.
examples.english: Chinese civilization has thousands of years of glorious history.

examples.chinese: 她在體壇的輝煌歲月讓人難以忘懷。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tǐtán de huīhuáng suìyuè ràng rén nányǐ wànghuái.
examples.english: Her brilliant years in the sports world are unforgettable.

semanticNote: What you get back or give back — 投資回報 (return on investment), 感恩回報 (repay with gratitude), 社會回報 (social return). Can be financial (ROI) or relational (repaying kindness). 回饋社會 and 回報社會 are both common for 'giving back to society.' 以德回報 (repay with virtue). More specific and transactional in feel than 報答 (to repay — more about gratitude for personal kindness).

examples.chinese: 他希望能以實際行動回報父母多年來的付出。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīwàng néng yǐ shíjì xíngdòng huíbào fùmǔ duōnián lái de fùchū.
examples.english: He hopes to repay his parents' years of sacrifice through concrete actions.

examples.chinese: 這項投資的回報相當可觀。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng tóuzī de huíbào xiāngdāng kěguān.
examples.english: The return on this investment is quite impressive.

semanticNote: To deliberately avoid or sidestep — a difficult question, a person, a responsibility. 回避問題 (dodge a question), 回避衝突 (avoid conflict), 依法回避 (legally recuse oneself — as a judge with a conflict of interest). The legal usage (recusal) is important: 法官應回避 (the judge should recuse). More intentional than 避免 (avoid — preventive) and more formal than 躲避 (flee/duck — more physical).

examples.chinese: 記者問到敏感問題時，他選擇回避。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě wèn dào mǐngǎn wèntí shí, tā xuǎnzé huíbì.
examples.english: When the reporter asked sensitive questions, he chose to dodge them.

examples.chinese: 有利益衝突的法官必須主動回避。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu lìyì chōngtū de fǎguān bìxū zhǔdòng huíbì.
examples.english: A judge with a conflict of interest must proactively recuse themselves.

semanticNote: Looking back at the past — 回顧歷史 (review history), 回顧過去一年 (look back at the past year), 年度回顧 (year in review). More reflective and systematic than 回想 (recall — just thinking back, more personal) or 回憶 (reminisce — emotional memory). 回顧 implies a structured review, often with the purpose of learning or summarizing. Very common in year-end summaries, academic reviews, and speeches.

components.meaning: to look back; consider; attend to

examples.chinese: 在演講的結尾，她回顧了自己十年的創業歷程。
examples.pinyin: Zài yǎnjiǎng de jiéwěi, tā huígùle zìjǐ shí nián de chuàngyè lìchéng.
examples.english: At the end of her speech, she reviewed her ten-year entrepreneurial journey.

examples.chinese: 年底回顧是很好的自我反省機會。
examples.pinyin: Niándǐ huígù shì hěn hǎo de zìwǒ fǎnxǐng jīhuì.
examples.english: A year-end review is a great opportunity for self-reflection.

semanticNote: To collect for reuse — recycling in the environmental sense (回收廢紙 = recycle waste paper, 資源回收 = resource recycling) or recovering assets (回收成本 = recoup costs, 回收舊書 = buy back used books). In Taiwan, 資源回收 is a major civic program with separate bins everywhere. 回收率 = recycling rate. Can also mean financial recovery: 投資回收期 (payback period).

examples.chinese: 台灣的資源回收率在全球名列前茅。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de zīyuán huíshōu lǜ zài quánqiú míngliè qiánmáo.
examples.english: Taiwan's resource recycling rate ranks among the highest in the world.

examples.chinese: 請把用過的電池投入回收桶。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yòngguò de diànchí tóurù huíshōu tǒng.
examples.english: Please put used batteries in the recycling bin.

english: remorse; regret deeply; feel bitter regret
semanticNote: Deep, bitter regret — stronger than 後悔 (regret — general). 悔恨 combines 悔 (regret one's actions) with 恨 (hate/bitter feeling) — you don't just regret it, you feel a bitter ache about it. 悔恨交加 (overwhelmed with remorse and bitterness). Often applied to serious moral failures or irreversible mistakes. Literary and somewhat formal compared to the everyday 後悔.

examples.chinese: 他為自己年輕時的錯誤深感悔恨。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi zìjǐ niánqīng shí de cuòwù shēn gǎn huǐhèn.
examples.english: He feels deep remorse for the mistakes he made in his youth.

examples.chinese: 她悔恨地說：「早知道就不那樣做了。」
examples.pinyin: Tā huǐhèn de shuō: 「Zǎo zhīdào jiù bú nàyàng zuò le.」
examples.english: She said bitterly, 'If only I had known, I never would have done that.'

semanticNote: Total destruction — 毀滅性的打擊 (a devastating blow), 走向毀滅 (head toward destruction), 自我毀滅 (self-destruction). The most extreme word for destruction in Mandarin — implies total, irreversible annihilation. Different from 破壞 (damage/destroy — not necessarily total) and 摧毀 (crush/destroy — similar intensity but 毀滅 implies more finality). Common in existential, historical, and dramatic contexts.

examples.chinese: 戰爭毀滅了整座城市。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng huǐmièle zhěng zuò chéngshì.
examples.english: The war destroyed the entire city.

examples.chinese: 吸毒會毀滅一個人的前途和人生。
examples.pinyin: Xīdú huì huǐmiè yī ge rén de qiántú hé rénshēng.
examples.english: Drug use destroys a person's future and life.

english: report (to superiors); give a briefing; debrief
semanticNote: To report back to a superior — 向上級彙報 (report to superiors), 工作彙報 (work report/briefing). The 彙 character means to compile or pool — 彙報 implies gathering information and presenting it upward in a hierarchy. More formal and hierarchical than 報告 (report — can go in any direction) — 彙報 specifically implies reporting UP in an organization. Very common in corporate and government contexts.

examples.chinese: 下屬每週都要向部門主管彙報工作進度。
examples.pinyin: Xìashǔ měi zhōu dōu yào xiàng bùmén zhǔguǎn huìbào gōngzuò jìndù.
examples.english: Subordinates must report their work progress to the department manager every week.

examples.chinese: 她把調查結果彙報給了總經理。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ diàochá jiéguǒ huìbàogěile zǒngjīnglǐ.
examples.english: She reported the investigation findings to the general manager.

semanticNote: A formal meeting between high-level officials or dignitaries — 兩國領導人會晤 (the leaders of the two countries met), 雙邊會晤 (bilateral meeting). Exclusively formal/diplomatic register — you'd never use 會晤 for a casual coffee catch-up. In Taiwan news, very common for describing cross-strait or international diplomatic contacts. Compare to 見面 (meet — casual), 開會 (hold a meeting — general), 峰會 (summit).

components.meaning: to meet; have an interview with

examples.chinese: 兩國外長在日內瓦舉行了正式會晤。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó wàizhǎng zài Rìnèiwǎ jǔxíngle zhèngshì huìwù.
examples.english: The foreign ministers of the two countries held a formal meeting in Geneva.

examples.chinese: 這次會晤被視為改善雙邊關係的重要一步。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huìwù bèi shìwéi gǎishàn shuāngbiān guānxì de zhòngyào yī bù.
examples.english: This meeting was seen as an important step in improving bilateral relations.

semanticNote: A bribe or the act of bribing — 行賄 (offer a bribe), 受賄 (accept a bribe), 賄賂官員 (bribe officials). Both noun (the bribe itself) and verb (to bribe). Anti-corruption discourse in Taiwan frequently uses these terms. 收賄罪 = accepting bribes (criminal charge). 賄賂 is a serious crime — the term carries full legal weight. Compare to 回扣 (kickback — a more business-specific form of bribery).

examples.chinese: 這名官員因涉嫌收受賄賂被逮捕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè míng guānyuán yīn shèxián shōushòu huìlù bèi dàibǔ.
examples.english: This official was arrested on suspicion of accepting bribes.

examples.chinese: 賄賂是嚴重的腐敗行為，必須依法懲處。
examples.pinyin: Huìlù shì yánzhòng de fǔbài xíngwéi, bìxū yīfǎ chéngchǔ.
examples.english: Bribery is a serious act of corruption that must be punished in accordance with the law.

semanticNote: Being in a coma or losing consciousness. 陷入昏迷 (fall into a coma), 昏迷不醒 (unconscious and unresponsive), 從昏迷中甦醒 (regain consciousness from a coma). Medical and emergency contexts. Different from 暈倒 (faint/collapse — usually brief) — 昏迷 implies a deeper, more sustained loss of consciousness. 昏迷指數 (Glasgow Coma Scale — the medical scoring system).

examples.chinese: 車禍後，他昏迷了三天才甦醒。
examples.pinyin: Chēhuò hòu, tā hūnmíle sān tiān cái sūxǐng.
examples.english: After the car accident, he was in a coma for three days before regaining consciousness.

examples.chinese: 患者目前仍處於昏迷狀態，情況危急。
examples.pinyin: Huànzhě mùqián réng chǔyú hūnmí zhuàngtài, qíngkuàng wéijí.
examples.english: The patient is still in a coma — the situation is critical.

semanticNote: Food containing meat or the five pungent vegetables forbidden to Buddhists (葷食 = meat/non-veg food). 吃葷 (eat meat), 葷食 (meat dishes), 素食 vs 葷食 (vegetarian vs non-vegetarian). Also colloquially: 葷段子 (dirty/off-color jokes — lit. 'meaty jokes'). In Buddhist contexts, 葷 includes garlic, onion, chives, etc. as 'pungent vegetables.' Common in restaurant ordering: 您要葷的還是素的？ (Meat or vegetarian?)

examples.chinese: 她信佛，所以不吃葷，只吃素。
examples.pinyin: Tā xìn Fó, suǒyǐ bù chī hūn, zhǐ chī sù.
examples.english: She's Buddhist, so she doesn't eat meat — only vegetarian food.

examples.chinese: 這個笑話有點葷，不太適合在正式場合說。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiàohuà yǒudiǎn hūn, bú tài shìhé zài zhèngshì chǎnghé shuō.
examples.english: This joke is a bit off-color — not really appropriate for a formal occasion.

english: whole body; all over; from head to foot
semanticNote: The whole body — 渾身是勁 (full of energy all over), 渾身疼痛 (aching all over), 渾身發抖 (trembling all over). Used with physical sensations and states that cover the entire body. 渾 suggests complete/total — every part. Always implies totality. Similar to 全身 but 渾身 is more colloquial and vivid, often used in emotional or physical extremity descriptions.

examples.chinese: 一聽到那個消息，她渾身發冷。
examples.pinyin: Yī tīng dào nàge xiāoxi, tā húnshēn fā lěng.
examples.english: The moment she heard the news, she felt cold all over.

examples.chinese: 他下班回來，渾身是汗，非常疲憊。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàbān huílái, húnshēn shì hàn, fēicháng píbèi.
examples.english: He came home from work drenched in sweat all over, completely exhausted.

semanticNote: To mix or blend things together — 混合材料 (mix materials), 混合雙打 (mixed doubles in tennis), 混合動力 (hybrid power — as in hybrid electric vehicles). More neutral and technical than 摻雜 (mix in — with a sense of contaminating or adulterating). 混合經濟 (mixed economy), 混合飲料 (mixed drink/cocktail). The word 混 alone can suggest confusion or muddling, but 混合 itself is neutral.

examples.chinese: 將兩種顏料混合可以調出新的顏色。
examples.pinyin: Jiāng liǎng zhǒng yánjìào hùnhé kěyǐ tiáo chū xīn de yánsè.
examples.english: Mixing two paints together can produce a new color.

examples.chinese: 這款車採用混合動力系統，兼顧動力與省油。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn chē cǎiyòng hùnhé dòonglì xìtǒng, jiāngù dòonglì yǔ shěngyóu.
examples.english: This car uses a hybrid power system, balancing performance and fuel efficiency.

semanticNote: Chaotic disorder — 社會混亂 (social chaos), 交通混亂 (traffic chaos), 思緒混亂 (confused thoughts). Can describe a physical situation (a chaotic scene) or a mental state (confused thinking). More intense than 亂 (messy/disorderly — general) — 混亂 implies things have broken down systematically. 造成混亂 (cause chaos), 陷入混亂 (fall into chaos). Common in news about crises, disasters, and political instability.

examples.chinese: 停電後，整個辦公室陷入一片混亂。
examples.pinyin: Tíngdiàn hòu, zhěng ge bàngōngshì xiànrù yīpiàn hùnluàn.
examples.english: After the power outage, the entire office fell into chaos.

examples.chinese: 她的情緒很混亂，不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qíngxù hěn hùnluàn, bù zhīdào gāi zěnme bàn.
examples.english: Her emotions are in chaos — she doesn't know what to do.

semanticNote: To confuse or blur the distinction between things — 混淆視聽 (confuse public perception; muddy the waters), 混淆是非 (blur the line between right and wrong), 不要混淆兩個概念 (don't confuse these two concepts). More deliberate than 混亂 (chaos) — 混淆 implies an intentional or problematic blurring of lines. 混淆視聽 is a fixed phrase meaning to deliberately mislead or confuse people.

examples.chinese: 他故意混淆視聽，讓人搞不清楚真相。
examples.pinyin: Tā gùyì hùnxiáo shìtīng, ràng rén gǎo bù qīngchǔ zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: He deliberately muddied the waters so people couldn't figure out the truth.

examples.chinese: 這兩個詞義相近，容易被混淆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge cí yì xiāng jìn, róngyì bèi hùnxiáo.
examples.english: These two words have similar meanings and are easy to confuse.

semanticNote: Murky and turbid — 混濁的河水 (murky river water), 空氣混濁 (polluted/murky air). Physically describes liquid or air that is dirty and unclear. Figuratively: 混濁的世道 (a corrupt/murky world — literary). The physical sense is most common. In environmental reporting about water quality: 河水混濁 is a clear sign of pollution. Different from 骯髒 (dirty — general filth) — 混濁 specifically implies turbidity/cloudiness.

examples.chinese: 暴雨後，溪水變得十分混濁。
examples.pinyin: Bàoyǔ hòu, xīshuǐ biàn de shífēn hùnzhuó.
examples.english: After the heavy rain, the stream became very murky.

examples.chinese: 工廠排放的廢水讓附近河流混濁不堪。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng páifàng de fèishuǐ ràng fùjìn héliú hùnzhuó bùkān.
examples.english: Wastewater discharged by the factory left nearby rivers hopelessly turbid.

english: serve someone right; they deserve it
semanticNote: Expressing that someone brought misfortune on themselves — 'serves you right,' 'you had it coming.' 活該！誰讓你不聽勸 (Serves you right! Who told you not to listen to advice). Direct and blunt — essentially gloating about deserved consequences. Common in casual speech; not appropriate in formal situations. Can be said sympathetically (活該，真可惜) — no wait, it's always a bit judgmental. A distinctly colloquial Chinese expression with no polite equivalent.

examples.chinese: 你不好好準備，考砸了活該！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù hǎohǎo zhǔnbèi, kǎo zá le huógāi!
examples.english: You didn't prepare properly — serves you right for bombing the exam!

examples.chinese: 他平時那麼壞，現在沒人理他，活該。
examples.pinyin: Tā píngshí nàme huài, xiànzài méi rén lǐ tā, huógāi.
examples.english: He's always been terrible — now nobody wants anything to do with him. Serves him right.

semanticNote: The energy and vitality of a living thing or organization — 充滿活力 (full of vitality), 年輕有活力 (young and energetic), 城市活力 (urban dynamism). Applied to people, organizations, economies, and cities. More specifically about dynamic energy than 精力 (energy/stamina — personal physical energy) or 力量 (strength/power). An 有活力 person is lively and dynamic; an 有活力 economy is growing and innovative.

examples.chinese: 這座城市充滿了年輕人的活力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì chōngmǎnle niánqīngrén de huólì.
examples.english: This city is full of youthful vitality.

examples.chinese: 早晨運動讓她整天都充滿活力。
examples.pinyin: Zǎochén yùndòng ràng tā zhěng tiān dōu chōngmǎn huólì.
examples.english: Morning exercise keeps her energized all day.

semanticNote: A rocket — both literal (space rockets, military missiles) and figurative (rocket-like speed). 火箭升空 (rocket launch), 火箭速度 (rocket speed). In modern usage, 火箭 also appears in colloquial hyperbole: 像火箭一樣快 (fast as a rocket), 薪水像坐火箭 (salary shooting up like a rocket). Also: 火箭筒 (rocket launcher/bazooka). The Houston Rockets 休士頓火箭 brought this word to basketball contexts.

examples.chinese: 太空船搭載火箭成功發射升空。
examples.pinyin: Tàikōngchuán dāzài huǒjiàn chénggōng fāshè shēngkōng.
examples.english: The spacecraft successfully launched into the sky aboard the rocket.

examples.chinese: 這家公司的股價像火箭一樣一飛沖天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de gǔjià xiàng huǒjiàn yīyàng yīfēichōngtiān.
examples.english: This company's stock price shot up like a rocket.

semanticNote: A flame or blaze — more visual and vivid than 火 (fire — general). 熊熊火焰 (roaring flames), 火焰噴射器 (flamethrower), 燭火焰 (candle flame). Used in both literal descriptions and metaphors: 熱情的火焰 (the flame of passion), 希望的火焰 (the flame of hope). Literary and visual; you'd see 火焰 in description-heavy writing, while everyday talk about fire uses 火.

examples.chinese: 蠟燭燃燒著微弱的火焰，在黑暗中閃爍。
examples.pinyin: Làzhú ránshāozhe wēiruò de huǒyàn, zài hēi'àn zhōng shǎnshuò.
examples.english: The candle burned with a faint flame, flickering in the dark.

examples.chinese: 消防員冒著熊熊火焰衝進建築物救人。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán màozhe xióngxióng huǒyàn chōng jìn jiànzhúwù jiù rén.
examples.english: Firefighters rushed into the building through roaring flames to save people.

semanticNote: Gunpowder — one of the four great Chinese inventions (四大發明). 黑色火藥 (black powder), 火藥味 (the smell of gunpowder — figuratively: the atmosphere is getting tense/explosive). 火藥味十足 = the situation is extremely tense and about to explode. 火藥桶 (powder keg — a metaphor for a volatile situation ready to blow). The figurative uses are as common as the historical/technical sense.

examples.chinese: 火藥是中國古代四大發明之一。
examples.pinyin: Huǒyào shì Zhōngguó gǔdài sì dà fāmíng zhī yī.
examples.english: Gunpowder is one of the four great inventions of ancient China.

examples.chinese: 雙方爭論越來越激烈，現場火藥味十足。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng zhēnglùn yuè lái yuè jīliè, xiànchǎng huǒyào wèi shízú.
examples.english: The argument between the two sides grew increasingly fierce — the atmosphere was explosive.

semanticNote: Currency in the economic/formal sense — 法定貨幣 (legal tender), 外國貨幣 (foreign currency), 數字貨幣 (digital currency), 貨幣政策 (monetary policy). More technical than 錢 (money — everyday) or 現金 (cash). 貨幣 is the term for currency as an economic institution. Common in finance, economics, and news. Taiwan dollar: 新台幣 (NTD).

examples.chinese: 各國貨幣匯率受到國際市場的影響。
examples.pinyin: Gè guó huòbì huìlǜ shòudào guójì shìchǎng de yǐngxiǎng.
examples.english: Exchange rates of currencies from various countries are affected by international markets.

examples.chinese: 數字貨幣的發展正在改變全球金融體系。
examples.pinyin: Shùzì huòbì de fāzhǎn zhèngzài gǎibiàn quánqiú jīnróng tǐxì.
examples.english: The development of digital currencies is transforming the global financial system.

semanticNote: To mock or sneer at someone — laughing at them with contempt or derision. 被人譏笑 (be mocked by others), 不怕被人譏笑 (not afraid of being ridiculed). More contemptuous than 嘲笑 (laugh at/mock — similar meaning, slightly softer). 譏 specifically means 'to jeer' or 'criticize sarcastically' — 譏笑 is therefore pointed and mean-spirited. Common in narratives about bullying, social mockery, and prejudice.

examples.chinese: 他的夢想曾被許多人譏笑，但他最終成功了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mèngxiǎng céng bèi xǔduō rén jīxiào, dàn tā zuìzhōng chénggōng le.
examples.english: His dream was once mocked by many people, but he ultimately succeeded.

examples.chinese: 即使被人譏笑，她也堅持走自己的路。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ bèi rén jīxiào, tā yě jiānchí zǒu zìjǐ de lù.
examples.english: Even when mocked by others, she persisted in walking her own path.

semanticNote: Hunger and starvation — more serious than 餓 (hungry — everyday). 飢餓 implies significant food deprivation, from serious hunger to famine-level starvation. 挨飢餓 (go hungry), 飢餓感 (feeling of hunger), 消除飢餓 (eliminate hunger). Used in humanitarian, historical, and literary contexts. Marketing note: 飢餓行銷 (hunger marketing = artificial scarcity marketing — creating demand through limited supply) is a common business term in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 世界上仍有數億人口飽受飢餓之苦。
examples.pinyin: Shìjiè shàng réng yǒu shù yì rénkǒu bǎoshòu jī'è zhī kǔ.
examples.english: Hundreds of millions of people in the world still suffer from hunger.

examples.chinese: 這個品牌採用飢餓行銷，讓產品供不應求。
examples.pinyin: Zhège pǐnpái cǎiyòng jī'è xíngxiāo, ràng chǎnpǐn gōng bù yìng qiú.
examples.english: This brand uses hunger marketing to create more demand than supply.

semanticNote: Flexible and adaptable — able to respond to changing situations. 機動性 (flexibility/mobility), 機動部隊 (mobile unit/rapid response team), 機動時間 (flexible/buffer time). In planning, 機動 means keeping something in reserve for unexpected needs. Military: motorized/mechanized units. In scheduling: 我保留了一些機動時間 (I've kept some buffer time). The key idea: not fixed, able to adapt.

examples.chinese: 警方派出機動隊伍，隨時準備應對突發狀況。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng pàichū jīdòng duìwǔ, suíshí zhǔnbèi yìngduì tūfā zhuàngkuàng.
examples.english: Police deployed a mobile unit, ready to respond to emergencies at any time.

examples.chinese: 計畫要保留一些機動空間，以防萬一。
examples.pinyin: Jìhuà yào bǎoliú yīxiē jīdòng kōngjiān, yǐfáng wànyī.
examples.english: The plan should reserve some flexible space, just in case.

semanticNote: An organization or institution — government agencies, NGOs, financial institutions, research bodies. 政府機構 (government agency), 金融機構 (financial institution), 非營利機構 (non-profit organization). Also the physical structure of a mechanism. More formal than 組織 (organization — broad) and 單位 (work unit — Chinese-specific bureaucratic term). In Taiwan, 機構 appears in formal names of bodies, hospitals, and research institutes.

examples.chinese: 這家慈善機構專門幫助弱勢兒童。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā císhàn jīgòu zhuānmén bāngzhù ruòshì értóng.
examples.english: This charitable organization specializes in helping disadvantaged children.

examples.chinese: 她在一家國際金融機構擔任分析師。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī jiā guójì jīnróng jīgòu dānrèn fēnxīshī.
examples.english: She works as an analyst at an international financial institution.

semanticNote: Quick-witted and mentally sharp — 這孩子真機靈 (this child is really sharp/clever). More about practical cleverness and quick reactions than book smarts. A 機靈 person reads situations quickly and responds smartly. Also: 打個機靈 (shudder with a sudden chill — a different meaning: a sudden physical tremor, often from fear or cold). The 'clever' sense is the HSK-relevant one.

examples.chinese: 這個孩子非常機靈，一學就會。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi fēicháng jīling, yī xué jiù huì.
examples.english: This child is very sharp — learns things the first time they're shown.

examples.chinese: 她機靈地察覺到老闆今天心情不好，趕快閉嘴。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīling de chájué dào lǎobǎn jīntiān xīnqíng bù hǎo, gǎnkuài bìzuǐ.
examples.english: She quickly sensed that the boss was in a bad mood today and wisely kept quiet.

semanticNote: Classified or secret — 機密文件 (classified documents), 國家機密 (state secrets), 洩露機密 (leak classified information). The government/military level of secrecy — more serious than 秘密 (secret — general, personal). 機密 implies formal classification; unauthorized disclosure is a criminal offense. 最高機密 = top secret. Used in espionage, government, and military contexts.

examples.chinese: 這份文件列為最高機密，不得外洩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn lièwéi zuìgāo jīmì, bùdé wài xiè.
examples.english: This document is classified top secret and may not be disclosed.

examples.chinese: 他因洩露國家機密而被判入獄。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn xiè lù guójiā jīmì ér bèi pàn rùyù.
examples.english: He was sentenced to prison for leaking state secrets.

semanticNote: Machinery (noun) or mechanical/rigid (adjective). 機械工程 (mechanical engineering), 機械設備 (machinery/equipment). As adjective: 機械式的思維 (mechanical/rigid thinking) — following rules without flexibility or thought. The figurative 'mechanical' sense (inflexible, by-the-book) is important: 他處理事情太機械了 (he handles things too mechanically/rigidly). Often contrasted with 靈活 (flexible).

examples.chinese: 工廠引進了大量先進機械，大幅提升了產能。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng yǐnjìnle dàliàng xiānjìn jīxiè, dàfú tíshēngle chǎnnéng.
examples.english: The factory introduced large amounts of advanced machinery, greatly boosting production capacity.

examples.chinese: 學習不能太機械，要懂得靈活運用。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí bù néng tài jīxiè, yào dǒngde línghuó yùnyòng.
examples.english: You can't learn too mechanically — you need to know how to apply things flexibly.

semanticNote: A fortuitous opportunity — one that arrives somewhat by luck or circumstance. 把握機遇 (seize the opportunity), 千載難逢的機遇 (a once-in-a-millennium opportunity). More literary than 機會 (opportunity — the everyday word). 機遇 implies the opportunity came to you; 機會 is more neutral about source. 機遇與挑戰 (opportunities and challenges) is a very common paired phrase in business and policy writing.

examples.chinese: 這次危機中也蘊含著難得的發展機遇。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wéijī zhōng yě yùnhánzhe nándé de fāzhǎn jīyù.
examples.english: Within this crisis lie rare opportunities for development.

examples.chinese: 要有把握機遇的眼光和勇氣。
examples.pinyin: Yào yǒu bǎwò jīyù de yǎnguāng hé yǒngqì.
examples.english: You need the vision and courage to seize opportunities when they arise.

semanticNote: The cleverness to handle difficult situations well — wit and resourcefulness under pressure. 機智的回答 (a witty comeback), 機智地化解了危機 (cleverly defused the crisis). Different from 機靈 (sharp/alert — more about quick perception) and 聰明 (intelligent — general). 機智 implies situational cleverness — finding the right response in the moment. Common in praise of people who handle tricky social or professional situations well.

examples.chinese: 她機智地回答了那個刁鑽的問題，全場鼓掌。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīzhì de huídále nàge diāozuān de wèntí, quánchǎng gǔzhǎng.
examples.english: She gave a witty answer to that tricky question and the whole room applauded.

examples.chinese: 談判時需要機智，才能在僵局中找到突破口。
examples.pinyin: Tánpàn shí xūyào jīzhì, cái néng zài jiāngjú zhōng zhǎodào túpòkǒu.
examples.english: Negotiation requires resourcefulness to find a breakthrough in a deadlock.

semanticNote: A base of operations — military base (軍事基地), research base (研究基地), production base (生產基地), launch base (發射基地). Also transliterated: 蓋達基地 (Al-Qaeda — '基地' is the Arabic word for 'base'). The word is neutral — it describes where operations are centered from. Taiwan's Jiufen (九份) is sometimes described as a 文化基地 for its artistic community.

examples.chinese: 這座城市是台灣半導體產業的重要基地。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì shì Táiwān bàndǎotǐ chǎnyè de zhòngyào jīdì.
examples.english: This city is an important base for Taiwan's semiconductor industry.

examples.chinese: 軍隊已撤回基地，等候進一步指令。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì yǐ chè huí jīdì, děnghòu jìnyī bù zhǐlìng.
examples.english: The troops have withdrawn to base, awaiting further orders.

semanticNote: A fund — financial pool for a specific purpose. 共同基金 (mutual fund), 慈善基金 (charitable fund), 基金會 (foundation — like 台積電基金會), 投資基金 (investment fund), 退休基金 (pension fund). Very common in Taiwan's financial and philanthropic landscape. 買基金 = invest in a fund. Different from 資金 (capital/funds — general money for operations) — 基金 is specifically a structured, purpose-designated fund.

examples.chinese: 她每個月固定購買基金，作為長期投資。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge yuè gùdìng gòumǎi jījīn, zuòwéi chángqī tóuzī.
examples.english: She regularly buys funds every month as a long-term investment.

examples.chinese: 這個慈善基金會每年資助數百名清寒學生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège císhàn jījīnhuì měi nián zīzhù shù bǎi míng qīnghán xuéshēng.
examples.english: This charitable foundation sponsors hundreds of low-income students every year.

semanticNote: Gene — the biological unit of heredity. 基因工程 (genetic engineering), 基因改造 (GMO — genetically modified), 基因檢測 (genetic testing), 基因突變 (genetic mutation). Also used metaphorically: 創新已經成為這家公司的基因 (innovation has become this company's DNA). Very common in biotech, medical, and food safety discourse in Taiwan. 基改食品 (GMO food) is a hot topic in Taiwan consumer culture.

examples.chinese: 科學家發現了與這種疾病相關的基因。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā fāxiànle yǔ zhè zhǒng jíbìng xiāngguān de jīyīn.
examples.english: Scientists discovered the gene associated with this disease.

examples.chinese: 台灣消費者對基改食品普遍持審慎態度。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān xiāofèizhě duì jī gǎi shípǐn pǔbiàn chí shěnshèn tàidù.
examples.english: Taiwanese consumers are generally cautious about GMO food products.

semanticNote: To arouse or trigger a strong response — 激發熱情 (arouse enthusiasm), 激發潛能 (unlock potential), 激發靈感 (spark inspiration). The key idea is that something dormant or potential is activated. Different from 激勵 (encourage/motivate — about sustained motivation) and 鼓勵 (encourage — general). 激發 implies a spark that sets something off. Common in educational, creative, and leadership contexts.

examples.chinese: 這位老師善於激發學生的學習興趣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī shànyú jīfā xuéshēng de xuéxí xìngqù.
examples.english: This teacher is skilled at sparking students' interest in learning.

examples.chinese: 旅行激發了她創作的靈感。
examples.pinyin: Lǚxíng jīfāle tā chuàngzuò de línggǎn.
examples.english: Travel sparked her creative inspiration.

semanticNote: To motivate and spur someone on — 激勵員工 (motivate employees), 激勵人心的演講 (an inspiring speech), 激勵機制 (incentive mechanism). Both verb and noun. Different from 激發 (to spark/trigger — activating something dormant) — 激勵 is more about sustained encouragement and drive. In business HR: 員工激勵 (employee motivation) is a key management concept. Also: 自我激勵 (self-motivation).

examples.chinese: 他的演講激勵了在場所有人，讓大家重新燃起鬥志。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjiǎng jīlìle zàichǎng suǒyǒu rén, ràng dàjiā chóngxīn rán qǐ dòuzhì.
examples.english: His speech inspired everyone present, reigniting their fighting spirit.

examples.chinese: 好的薪酬制度能有效激勵員工的積極性。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo de xīnchóu zhìdù néng yǒuxiào jīlì yuángōng de jījíxìng.
examples.english: A good compensation system can effectively motivate employee initiative.

semanticNote: Intense passion or fervor — 充滿激情 (full of passion), 激情燃燒 (passion burning). Can refer to romantic passion (激情的吻 = a passionate kiss) or emotional intensity about a cause (對工作充滿激情 = passionate about work). Note: 激情犯罪 (crime of passion — a legal concept). In Taiwan's youth culture, 激情 often implies romantic/sexual passion specifically; context matters. Compare to 熱情 (warm enthusiasm — gentler and safer for general use).

examples.chinese: 她對舞蹈充滿激情，每天練習好幾個小時。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì wǔdǎo chōngmǎn jīqíng, měitiān liànxí hǎo jǐ ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: She's passionate about dance and practices for hours every day.

examples.chinese: 那場演唱會充滿激情，觀眾全程沸騰。
examples.pinyin: Nà chǎng yǎnchànghuì chōngmǎn jīqíng, guānzhòng quánchéng fèiténg.
examples.english: That concert was full of electric passion — the audience was fired up the whole time.

english: as early as possible; at the earliest opportunity
semanticNote: Do something early, before it's too late — 及早發現 (detect early), 及早治療 (treat early), 及早準備 (prepare in advance). Always paired with a verb. Emphasizes the importance of not waiting — acting early to avoid problems. Common in health, legal, and practical advice contexts. 及早 = 趁早 (the more colloquial synonym: 你趁早走吧 = get out of here while you can).

examples.chinese: 癌症及早發現、及早治療，存活率大幅提高。
examples.pinyin: Áizhèng jízǎo fāxiàn, jízǎo zhìliáo, cúnhuólǜ dàfú tígāo.
examples.english: With early detection and early treatment of cancer, survival rates increase significantly.

examples.chinese: 如果有法律問題，最好及早諮詢律師。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ yǒu fǎlǜ wèntí, zuì hǎo jízǎo zīxún lǜshī.
examples.english: If you have legal issues, it's best to consult a lawyer as early as possible.

semanticNote: Lucky and auspicious — 吉祥如意 (may good fortune be with you — a common blessing), 吉祥物 (mascot — lit. 'auspicious creature'), 吉祥話 (auspicious/lucky words — the polite well-wishes exchanged at New Year). Deeply embedded in Chinese festival culture: red envelopes, lucky numbers, auspicious animals all carry 吉祥 symbolism. Used on gifts, New Year greetings, and celebratory occasions.

examples.chinese: 龍在中國文化中是吉祥的象徵。
examples.pinyin: Lóng zài Zhōngguó wénhuà zhōng shì jíxiáng de xiàngzhēng.
examples.english: The dragon is a symbol of good fortune in Chinese culture.

examples.chinese: 新年快樂，吉祥如意！
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián kuàilè, jíxiáng rúyì!
examples.english: Happy New Year — may good fortune be with you!

semanticNote: Rank or level within a hierarchy — 高級別 (high-level), 省級別 (provincial level), 軍事級別 (military rank), 職稱級別 (professional title rank). Used for people, governments, events, and products. In Taiwan workplace culture, 級別 matters for salary bands and seniority. Also used for natural disasters (颱風級別 = typhoon grade) and product quality (酒店星級 vs 品質級別).

examples.chinese: 這次峰會是國家級別的重要外交活動。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì fēnghuì shì guójiā jíbié de zhòngyào wàijiāo huódòng.
examples.english: This summit is a national-level important diplomatic event.

examples.chinese: 他的職位級別比我高兩個等級。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhíwèi jíbié bǐ wǒ gāo liǎng ge děngjí.
examples.english: His position is two levels higher than mine.

semanticNote: The extreme end of a spectrum — 走極端 (go to extremes), 極端天氣 (extreme weather), 極端主義 (extremism), 極端分子 (extremist). As adjective: 極端的情緒 (extreme emotions). The word 極端 always implies too far — it's negative or neutral-to-negative. Used in political discourse (極端民族主義 = extreme nationalism), climate discussion, and psychological description.

examples.chinese: 凡事不要走極端，應保持理性中立。
examples.pinyin: Fánshì bú yào zǒu jíduān, yīng bǎochí lǐxìng zhōnglì.
examples.english: Don't go to extremes in anything — maintain rational, balanced thinking.

examples.chinese: 極端天氣事件近年來日益頻繁。
examples.pinyin: Jíduān tiānqì shìjiàn jìnnián lái rìyì pínfán.
examples.english: Extreme weather events have become increasingly frequent in recent years.

semanticNote: The outer boundary — physical, mathematical, or figurative. 挑戰極限 (challenge limits), 超越極限 (exceed limits), 到達極限 (reach one's limit). In physics/math: a limit value. In sports and life: the absolute boundary of what's possible. 極限運動 (extreme sports). 我已經到極限了 (I've reached my limit) expresses exhaustion or inability to continue.

examples.chinese: 馬拉松運動員不斷挑戰自己的體能極限。
examples.pinyin: Mǎlāsōng yùndòng yuán bùduàn tiǎozhàn zìjǐ de tǐnéng jíxiàn.
examples.english: Marathon runners constantly challenge their physical limits.

examples.chinese: 他已經超負荷工作，快到極限了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng chāo fùhè gōngzuò, kuài dào jíxiàn le.
examples.english: He's been overworked and is nearly at his limit.

english: even if; even though; even so
semanticNote: Concessive conjunction — 'even if' or 'even though.' 即便如此 (even so), 即便下雨我也要去 (even if it rains, I'll still go). More formal than 就算 and 即使 (both meaning 'even if'). 即便、即使、就算 are essentially synonyms in this meaning, with 即便 being slightly more literary. Always introduces the less expected condition that doesn't change the conclusion.

examples.chinese: 即便困難重重，她也沒有放棄。
examples.pinyin: Jíbiàn kùnnán chóngchóng, tā yě méiyǒu fàngqì.
examples.english: Even though the difficulties were enormous, she never gave up.

examples.chinese: 即便你不同意，這個決定也已經做出了。
examples.pinyin: Jíbiàn nǐ bù tóngyì, zhège juédìng yě yǐjīng zuòchū le.
examples.english: Even if you disagree, this decision has already been made.

english: about to; soon; on the verge of
semanticNote: Something that will happen very soon — 即將開幕 (about to open), 即將到來 (coming soon), 即將畢業 (about to graduate). More formal than 快要 (about to — everyday spoken) and 馬上 (right away — emphasizes immediacy). 即將 appears in news headlines, formal announcements, and written language. 即將來臨的颱風 (the approaching typhoon) — news register.

examples.chinese: 新任總統即將在下週宣誓就職。
examples.pinyin: Xīn rèn zǒngtǒng jíjiāng zài xià zhōu xuānshì jiùzhí.
examples.english: The new president is about to be sworn in next week.

examples.chinese: 即將到來的春節讓人充滿期待。
examples.pinyin: Jíjiāng dào lái de Chūnjié ràng rén chōngmǎn qīdài.
examples.english: The approaching Chinese New Year has everyone filled with anticipation.

english: eager for quick success and immediate gain; short-sighted
semanticNote: Prioritizing immediate results and profit over long-term thinking. A criticism of impatience and short-termism. 這家公司急功近利，只顧眼前利益 (this company is short-sighted, only caring about immediate gains). Common in business criticism, educational philosophy discussions, and policy debates. The person or organization sacrifices quality, integrity, or long-term sustainability for quick wins.

examples.chinese: 教育不能急功近利，要重視學生的長遠發展。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoyù bù néng jígōngjìnlì, yào zhòngshì xuéshēng de chángyuǎn fāzhǎn.
examples.english: Education can't be short-sighted — it must prioritize students' long-term development.

examples.chinese: 這種急功近利的做法雖然短期有效，卻留下了嚴重隱患。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jígōngjìnlì de zuòfǎ suīrán duǎnqī yǒuxiào, què liúxiàle yánzhòng yǐnhuàn.
examples.english: This short-sighted approach may work in the short term, but leaves serious hidden problems.

semanticNote: Rapid and dramatic change — 急劇下降 (a sharp drop), 急劇上升 (a sharp rise), 急劇惡化 (rapid deterioration). Always describes fast, significant change — often negative or at least alarming. More dramatic than 迅速 (quick — general speed) — 急劇 implies the change is both fast AND large in magnitude. Common in data reporting, economic analysis, and news about worsening situations.

examples.chinese: 氣溫急劇下降，民眾要注意保暖。
examples.pinyin: Qìwēn jíjù xiàjiàng, mínzhòng yào zhùyì bǎonuǎn.
examples.english: Temperatures are dropping sharply — people should take care to keep warm.

examples.chinese: 疫情期間，觀光業的收入急劇萎縮。
examples.pinyin: Yìqíng qījiān, guānguāngyè de shōurù jíjù wēisuō.
examples.english: During the pandemic, the tourism industry's revenue contracted sharply.

semanticNote: An eager, pressing urgency — 急切的眼神 (eager eyes), 急切地盼望 (eagerly await), 急切的需求 (urgent need). Can describe a person's emotional eagerness or an urgent external demand. The feeling of being unable to wait — wanting something right now. Different from 緊急 (emergency — about objective urgency) — 急切 is more about the person's emotional state of impatience or eagerness.

examples.chinese: 她急切地等待著考試結果。
examples.pinyin: Tā jíqiè de děngdàizhe kǎoshì jiéguǒ.
examples.english: She eagerly awaited the exam results.

examples.chinese: 他急切地想見到久別的家人。
examples.pinyin: Tā jíqiè de xiǎng jiàndào jiǔbié de jiārén.
examples.english: He urgently wanted to see his family whom he hadn't seen in a long time.

english: too eager for success; rush to get results
semanticNote: Impatience for results that leads to rushing and mistakes. 欲速則不達 (haste makes waste) is the complementary wisdom. 做事不能急于求成，要腳踏實地 (in doing things you can't rush for results — you have to be steady and grounded). Common in advice to students, entrepreneurs, and anyone being criticized for cutting corners. A very Chinese cultural value: patience and thoroughness over speed.

examples.chinese: 學語言急于求成反而容易打擊信心。
examples.pinyin: Xué yǔyán jíyúqiúchéng fǎn'ér róngyì dǎjī xìnxīn.
examples.english: Being too eager for results when learning a language can actually undermine your confidence.

examples.chinese: 創業不能急于求成，要穩扎穩打。
examples.pinyin: Chuàngyè bù néng jíyúqiúchéng, yào wěnzhā wěndǎ.
examples.english: Entrepreneurship can't be rushed — you have to be steady and methodical.

semanticNote: An irritable, easily agitated temperament. 脾氣急躁 (a hot-tempered nature), 急躁的情緒 (impatient mood). Different from 急于求成 (impatient for results) — 急躁 is more about emotional irritability and quick-to-anger behavior. 他一遇到問題就急躁起來 (he gets irritable the moment a problem arises). The antidote in Chinese wisdom: 冷靜 (calm) and 耐心 (patience).

examples.chinese: 他的個性急躁，常常衝動行事後悔不已。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gèxìng jízào, chángcháng chōngdòng xíngshì hòuhuǐ bùyǐ.
examples.english: He has an impetuous personality — often acts impulsively and deeply regrets it.

examples.chinese: 遇到困難時，最忌急躁，要冷靜思考。
examples.pinyin: Yù dào kùnnán shí, zuì jì jízào, yào lěngjìng sīkǎo.
examples.english: When facing difficulties, the worst thing is to be impetuous — you must think calmly.

semanticNote: Disease and illness in general — 預防疾病 (prevent disease), 傳染性疾病 (infectious disease), 慢性疾病 (chronic disease). More formal and medical than 病 (sick/illness — everyday). 疾 originally meant sudden serious illness; 病 means illness broadly — together they cover all illness. 罕見疾病 (rare disease), 職業疾病 (occupational disease). Common in medical and public health contexts.

examples.chinese: 良好的生活習慣有助於預防許多疾病。
examples.pinyin: Liánghǎo de shēnghuó xíguàn yǒuzhù yú yùfáng xǔduō jíbìng.
examples.english: Good lifestyle habits help prevent many diseases.

examples.chinese: 這種疾病主要透過飛沫傳播。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jíbìng zhǔyào tòuguò fēimò chuánbō.
examples.english: This disease is mainly transmitted through droplets.

semanticNote: A large group with shared interests — corporate conglomerate (企業集團 = business group), political bloc (政治集團), military alliance (軍事集團). Common in Taiwan corporate naming: 台塑集團 (Formosa Plastics Group), 鴻海集團 (Foxconn Group). Also used for criminal organizations (犯罪集團 = criminal syndicate). The word implies organized collective power — more structured than 群體 (group of people) or 組織 (organization).

examples.chinese: 這家企業集團旗下擁有超過三十家子公司。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā qǐyè jítuán qíxià yōngyǒu chāoguò sānshí jiā zǐgōngsī.
examples.english: This business conglomerate has over thirty subsidiaries.

examples.chinese: 警方搗毀了一個跨國詐騙集團。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dǎohuǐle yí ge kuàguó zhàpiàn jítuán.
examples.english: Police dismantled a transnational fraud syndicate.

english: jealous; envy; to be jealous of
semanticNote: Jealousy and envy — 嫉妒心 (jealousy/envy), 令人嫉妒 (enviable), 嫉妒別人的成就 (be jealous of others' achievements). Both jealousy (wanting what someone else has) and envy (resenting someone for having it). Chinese makes less of a distinction between the two than English does. 嫉 means to resent others' advantages; 妒 means to be jealous. Together: the classic green-eyed feeling.

examples.chinese: 她嫉妒同事得到了提升，心裡很不是滋味。
examples.pinyin: Tā jídù tóngshì dédàole tíshēng, xīnlǐ hěn bú shì zīwèi.
examples.english: She was jealous that her colleague got promoted — it didn't sit well with her.

examples.chinese: 他的嫉妒心讓他看不了別人過得比他好。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jídùxīn ràng tā kàn bùliǎo biérén guò de bǐ tā hǎo.
examples.english: His jealousy won't let him bear to see others doing better than him.

english: place of origin; native place; ancestral home
semanticNote: One's ancestral or registered place of origin — not necessarily where you were born or grew up. On official Taiwanese forms: 籍貫 means the birthplace of your father (or grandfather before 1945). Historically important in Chinese bureaucracy. 籍貫：台北 (place of origin: Taipei). In modern casual contexts, it can just mean 'where are you from originally?' — 你的籍貫是哪裡？

components.meaning: to pass through; string of cash; native place

examples.chinese: 他的籍貫是廣東，但出生在台北。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jíguàn shì Guǎngdōng, dàn chūshēng zài Táiběi.
examples.english: His ancestral home is Guangdong, but he was born in Taipei.

examples.chinese: 填寫申請表時，需要填入籍貫資料。
examples.pinyin: Tiánxiě shēnqǐng biǎo shí, xūyào tiánrù jíguàn zīliào.
examples.english: When filling out the application form, you need to fill in your place of origin.

semanticNote: Formal/literary 'to give' — 給予支持 (provide support), 給予鼓勵 (offer encouragement), 給予機會 (grant an opportunity). Much more formal than 給 (give — everyday) and implies the giver has authority or the gift has weight. Common in official communications, requests, and formal statements. 請給予協助 (please provide assistance). In Taiwan official writing: 敬請給予指教 (please offer your guidance — polite request for advice).

examples.chinese: 感謝大家給予我這個機會。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè dàjiā gěiyǔ wǒ zhège jīhuì.
examples.english: Thank you all for giving me this opportunity.

examples.chinese: 政府決定給予受災戶適當的補償。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ juédìng gěiyǔ shòuzāi hù shìdàng de bǔcháng.
examples.english: The government decided to provide appropriate compensation to disaster-affected households.

english: haggle; nitpick; take offense; mind (minor things)
semanticNote: To fuss over or take offense at small things — 不要太計較 (don't be too petty about it), 斤斤計較 (be penny-pinching / obsessively petty — the most common compound), 我不跟你計較 (I won't hold it against you / I won't make a fuss). Usually appears in negative constructions advising against being petty. The person who 計較 too much over small things is seen as lacking magnanimity.

examples.chinese: 朋友之間不要為小事斤斤計較。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou zhījiān bú yào wèi xiǎoshì jīnjīn jìjiào.
examples.english: Among friends, don't be petty over trivial things.

examples.chinese: 算了，我不跟你計較這件事了。
examples.pinyin: Suàn le, wǒ bù gēn nǐ jìjiào zhè jiàn shì le.
examples.english: Forget it — I won't make an issue of this with you.

semanticNote: One's memory capacity — the ability to remember things. 記性好 (good memory), 記性差 (poor memory), 記性不好 (bad at remembering). Purely colloquial — you wouldn't use 記性 in formal writing (use 記憶力 instead). Very common in everyday speech: 你記性真好！(You have such a good memory!). Different from 記憶 (memory as content — what you remember) — 記性 is about the capacity itself.

examples.chinese: 她記性很好，幾乎不會忘記任何事情。
examples.pinyin: Tā jìxing hěn hǎo, jīhū bú huì wàngjì rènhé shìqíng.
examples.english: She has an excellent memory — she almost never forgets anything.

examples.chinese: 最近太累了，記性好像變差了。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn tài lèi le, jìxing hǎoxiàng biàn chà le.
examples.english: I've been so tired lately — my memory seems to be getting worse.

semanticNote: To record in writing — especially historical records. 歷史記載 (historical records), 有記載以來 (since records began), 據史書記載 (according to historical records). More formal and historical than 記錄 (record — general, including audio/video). 記載 implies a written document or chronicle. Common in history writing: 根據史料記載... (according to documented historical materials...).

examples.chinese: 根據歷史記載，這座城市已有兩千年的歷史。
examples.pinyin: Gēnjù lìshǐ jìzǎi, zhè zuò chéngshì yǐ yǒu liǎng qiān nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: According to historical records, this city has a history of two thousand years.

examples.chinese: 這場地震是有記載以來最嚴重的一次。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dìzhèn shì yǒu jìzǎi yǐlái zuì yánzhòng de yīcì.
examples.english: This earthquake is the most severe since records began.

semanticNote: Meeting minutes or a written summary of key points. 會議紀要 (meeting minutes), 整理紀要 (compile a summary). More formal than 筆記 (notes — personal). 紀要 is the official record that captures decisions and key discussions. In Taiwan corporate and government settings, 會議紀要 is a standard output of formal meetings. Similar to 備忘錄 (memo) but 紀要 specifically summarizes meetings.

examples.chinese: 會議結束後，秘書整理了一份詳細的紀要。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì jiéshù hòu, mìshū zhěnglǐle yī fèn xiángxì de jìyào.
examples.english: After the meeting ended, the secretary compiled a detailed set of minutes.

examples.chinese: 請在七日內簽回會議紀要以確認內容。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài qī rì nèi qiān huí huìyì jìyào yǐ quèrèn nèiróng.
examples.english: Please sign and return the meeting minutes within seven days to confirm the contents.

semanticNote: A skill or technique — the practical know-how for doing something well. 說話技巧 (communication skills/speaking technique), 寫作技巧 (writing skills), 談判技巧 (negotiation skills). More specific than 技術 (technology/skill — broader) — 技巧 focuses on the artful or clever execution aspect. 有技巧地 = skillfully. Common in educational and self-improvement contexts. 技巧性 (technical/skillful).

examples.chinese: 演講需要許多技巧，包括語調、節奏和表情。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnjiǎng xūyào xǔduō jìqiǎo, bāokuò yǔdiào, jiézòu hé biǎoqíng.
examples.english: Public speaking requires many skills, including intonation, rhythm, and expression.

examples.chinese: 學習游泳最重要的是掌握正確的技巧。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí yóuyǒng zuì zhòngyào de shì zhǎngwò zhèngquè de jìqiǎo.
examples.english: The most important thing in learning to swim is mastering the correct technique.

english: taboo; avoid as taboo; forbidden; a thing to be avoided
semanticNote: A cultural or personal taboo — something that must be avoided. 這是大忌諱 (this is a major taboo), 忌諱說不吉利的話 (avoid saying inauspicious things), 過年的忌諱 (New Year taboos). Taiwan has rich cultural taboos: avoid saying 死 (die) during New Year, don't give clocks as gifts (送鐘 sounds like 送終 = see someone to their death), no umbrellas (傘 sounds like 散 = scatter/break up). 忌諱 is the word for all these forbidden things.

components.meaning: to avoid; to taboo; to conceal

examples.chinese: 台灣文化中，送鐘是一大忌諱，因為諧音不吉利。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān wénhuà zhōng, sòng zhōng shì yī dà jìhuì, yīnwèi xiéyīn bù jílì.
examples.english: In Taiwanese culture, giving clocks is a major taboo because the phrase 'giving a clock' sounds like 'attending a funeral.'

examples.chinese: 在這家公司，直接批評老闆是大家心照不宣的忌諱。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhè jiā gōngsī, zhíjiē pīpíng lǎobǎn shì dàjiā xīnzhào bùxuān de jìhuì.
examples.english: In this company, directly criticizing the boss is an unspoken taboo everyone understands.

english: quarter (of a year); a three-month period
semanticNote: A financial or calendar quarter — 第一季度 (Q1), 季度報告 (quarterly report), 季度業績 (quarterly performance). Very common in business and financial reporting. 上季度 (last quarter), 本季度 (this quarter). 季 alone means season (春/夏/秋/冬季 = spring/summer/fall/winter), so 季度 is literally 'season period' — the three-month unit matching Earth's seasons.

components.meaning: season; quarter; end of a period

examples.chinese: 公司每季度召開一次業績檢討會議。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī měi jìdù zhàokāi yīcì yèjī jiǎntǎo huìyì.
examples.english: The company holds a quarterly performance review meeting.

examples.chinese: 第三季度的營業額比去年同期增長了二十%。
examples.pinyin: Dì sān jìdù de yíngyè é bǐ qùnián tóngqī zēngzhǎngle èrshí %.
examples.english: Q3 revenue increased 20% compared to the same period last year.

semanticNote: Third place — the bronze position in a competition. 冠軍 (first/gold), 亞軍 (second/silver), 季軍 (third/bronze). Used in sports, competitions, talent shows, and rankings. 獲得季軍 (win third place), 季軍得主 (third-place winner). The 季 here relates to 'fourth season' in an archaic sense (lowest of the seasons), though in modern use it simply means 'third in ranking.'

examples.chinese: 她在這次全國歌唱比賽中獲得季軍。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhè cì quánguó gēchàng bǐsài zhōng huòdé jìjūn.
examples.english: She won third place in this national singing competition.

examples.chinese: 台灣隊在這次錦標賽中取得了季軍的佳績。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān duì zài zhè cì jǐnbiāosài zhōng qǔdéle jìjūn de jiājì.
examples.english: The Taiwan team achieved third place in this championship — a fine result.

english: sign; indication; signal (that something is happening)
semanticNote: Signs or indications that something is occurring — 跡象顯示 (signs indicate), 有跡象表明 (there are signs suggesting), 沒有跡象 (no sign of). Different from 徵兆 (omen/sign — more about warning signs) and 信號 (signal — more technical/mechanical). 跡象 is the evidence-based reading of clues — detectives look for 跡象, doctors read 跡象 of disease, economists read 跡象 of recovery.

examples.chinese: 根據種種跡象，他可能知道真相。
examples.pinyin: Gēnjù zhǒngzhǒng jìxiàng, tā kěnéng zhīdào zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: Based on all the signs, he probably knows the truth.

examples.chinese: 經濟已出現復甦的跡象。
examples.pinyin: Jīngjì yǐ chūxiàn fùsū de jìxiàng.
examples.english: Signs of economic recovery have already appeared.

semanticNote: To inherit or carry on — property (繼承遺產 = inherit an estate), position (繼承王位 = succeed to the throne), tradition (繼承傳統 = carry on traditions), culture (繼承文化遺產 = inherit cultural heritage). Broader than the English 'inherit' — 繼承 applies to material assets, roles, and immaterial legacies. 繼承人 = heir/successor.

examples.chinese: 他繼承了父親的事業，將公司發展得更大。
examples.pinyin: Tā jìchéngle fùqīn de shìyè, jiāng gōngsī fāzhǎn de gèng dà.
examples.english: He inherited his father's business and grew the company even larger.

examples.chinese: 傳統藝術需要有人繼承，才不會失傳。
examples.pinyin: Chuántǒng yìshù xūyào yǒurén jìchéng, cái bú huì shīchuán.
examples.english: Traditional arts need someone to carry them on, or they'll be lost.

english: entrust; place one's hopes in; find solace in
semanticNote: To place something (emotionally significant) in another's keeping — hopes, emotions, dreams. 寄托希望 (pin one's hopes on), 寄托哀思 (find an outlet for grief — common at memorial ceremonies: 寄托哀思 = express condolences), 精神寄托 (a spiritual anchor / something one finds meaning in). Also literally: entrust someone's care to another. The emotional and spiritual use is most common.

examples.chinese: 父母把所有的希望都寄托在孩子身上。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ bǎ suǒyǒu de xīwàng dōu jìtuō zài háizi shēnshàng.
examples.english: The parents place all their hopes on their child.

examples.chinese: 音樂是她情感的寄托，讓她在失落時找到安慰。
examples.pinyin: Yīnyuè shì tā qínggǎn de jìtuō, ràng tā zài shīluò shí zhǎodào ānwèi.
examples.english: Music is her emotional anchor — it brings her comfort in moments of loss.

semanticNote: Deep, profound quiet — 寂靜的夜晚 (a silent night), 萬籟俱寂 (absolute silence — the ultimate expression of 寂靜). More literary and complete than 安靜 (quiet — everyday: 請保持安靜 = please be quiet). 寂靜 describes a state of silence that has settled in — an atmosphere of quietude, not just the absence of noise. Common in literary descriptions of night, nature, and atmosphere.

examples.chinese: 深夜的街道一片寂靜，只有風聲。
examples.pinyin: Shēnyè de jiēdào yīpiàn jìjìng, zhǐyǒu fēng shēng.
examples.english: The streets in the dead of night were completely silent — only the sound of wind.

examples.chinese: 圖書館裡保持著一種莊嚴的寂靜。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ bǎochízhe yī zhǒng zhuāngyán de jìjìng.
examples.english: The library maintained a kind of solemn silence.

english: process; manufacture; machining; to work on
semanticNote: To process raw materials into finished products — 食品加工 (food processing), 加工廠 (processing plant), 精密加工 (precision machining). Also used figuratively: 這個故事是加工過的 (this story has been embellished/processed). Taiwan is famous for its 代工加工 (OEM/contract manufacturing) industry — 台灣的加工出口區 (Taiwan's export processing zones) were key to its economic development.

examples.chinese: 這家工廠專門從事金屬零件的精密加工。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng zhuānmén cóngshì jīnshǔ língjiàn de jīngmì jiāgōng.
examples.english: This factory specializes in precision machining of metal parts.

examples.chinese: 加工食品方便但營養成分通常不及新鮮食材。
examples.pinyin: Jiāgōng shípǐn fāngbiàn dàn yíngyǎng chéngfèn tōngcháng bùjí xīnxiān shícái.
examples.english: Processed foods are convenient but usually have fewer nutrients than fresh ingredients.

semanticNote: To worsen or intensify — 加劇矛盾 (intensify contradictions), 加劇病情 (aggravate the illness), 氣候變遷加劇 (climate change worsens). Always describes something getting worse or more severe. Common in news: 貧富差距加劇 (the wealth gap is widening), 衝突加劇 (conflict is escalating). The antonym would be 緩和 (ease/alleviate).

examples.chinese: 若不採取行動，氣候危機只會進一步加劇。
examples.pinyin: Ruò bù cǎiqǔ xíngdòng, qìhòu wéijī zhǐ huì jìnyī bù jiājù.
examples.english: Without action, the climate crisis will only continue to worsen.

examples.chinese: 雙方的誤解加劇了彼此的矛盾。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng de wùjiě jiājùle bǐcǐ de máodùn.
examples.english: The mutual misunderstanding intensified the conflict between the two sides.

english: mix together; intersperse; have mixed in
semanticNote: Having dissimilar things mixed in together — 夾雜著笑聲和哭聲 (interspersed with laughter and crying), 方言中夾雜英文 (mixing English words into the dialect). Always implies the mixing of things that are somewhat incongruent. Common in describing speech patterns (夾雜外來語 = mix in loanwords), emotions (悲喜夾雜 = mixed emotions), or physical contents (食物中夾雜異物 = foreign objects mixed into food).

examples.chinese: 她說話時常常夾雜一些台語，聽起來很有趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà shí chángcháng jiāzá yīxiē Táiyǔ, tīng qǐlái hěn yǒuqù.
examples.english: When she speaks she often mixes in some Taiwanese — it sounds very interesting.

examples.chinese: 人群中夾雜著幾聲噓聲，讓演講者十分尷尬。
examples.pinyin: Rénqún zhōng jiāzázhe jǐ shēng xūshēng, ràng yǎnjiǎngzhě shífēn gāngà.
examples.english: A few boos mixed into the crowd, making the speaker extremely embarrassed.

semanticNote: Fine dishes and delicacies — 美酒佳肴 (fine wine and gourmet food — the classic pairing phrase), 山珍海味佳肴 (delicacies from mountain and sea). Formal and literary; you'd see this in restaurant menus written in elegant script, banquet invitations, and travel writing about food. Not everyday language — in casual speech you'd say 好吃的菜 or 美食. 佳 = excellent; 肴 = cooked meat dishes.

examples.chinese: 宴席上擺滿了各式各樣的佳肴，讓人食指大動。
examples.pinyin: Yànxí shàng bǎi mǎnle gèshì gèyàng de jiāyáo, ràng rén shí zhǐ dà dòng.
examples.english: The banquet table was filled with all kinds of delicacies that made everyone's mouth water.

examples.chinese: 美酒佳肴，賓主盡歡。
examples.pinyin: Měijiǔ jiāyáo, bīnzhǔ jìn huān.
examples.english: Fine wine and excellent food — guests and host all enjoyed themselves to the fullest.

semanticNote: The ordinary stuff of daily family life — 家常便飯 (a simple everyday meal; fig. commonplace occurrence), 家常菜 (home-style cooking — the stuff mom makes, not restaurant food), 聊家常 (chitchat about daily life). In cooking: 家常豆腐 (home-style tofu — a classic Chinese dish). 家常便飯 figuratively: 這種事是家常便飯 = this kind of thing is a regular/ordinary occurrence.

examples.chinese: 她最拿手的就是家常菜，每道都讓人回味無窮。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì náshǒu de jiùshì jiācháng cài, měi dào dōu ràng rén huíwèi wúqióng.
examples.english: What she does best is home-style cooking — every dish leaves you wanting more.

examples.chinese: 遲到對他來說已經是家常便飯了。
examples.pinyin: Chídào duì tā lái shuō yǐjīng shì jiācháng biànfàn le.
examples.english: Being late is already a commonplace occurrence for him.

semanticNote: Colloquial and versatile: (1) a person — 這傢伙 (this guy), 好傢伙！(What a character!/Wow!); (2) a tool or weapon — 傢伙事兒 (tools of the trade). The 'guy/fellow' sense is most common in Taiwan. Can be neutral or slightly contemptuous depending on tone. 好傢伙 (with admiration: 'what a guy!' or surprise: 'holy cow!'). Note: 傢伙 is also how children refer to parents/authority figures in some dialects.

examples.chinese: 這傢伙每次都遲到，真讓人受不了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiāhuo měi cì dōu chídào, zhēn ràng rén shòu bù liǎo.
examples.english: This guy is late every single time — it's really unbearable.

examples.chinese: 好傢伙，這一桌菜得花多少錢啊？
examples.pinyin: Hǎo jiāhuo, zhè yī zhuō cài děi huā duōshǎo qián a?
examples.english: Whoa, how much must this whole table of food have cost?

english: family member; dependent; next of kin
semanticNote: Family members — especially in formal/official contexts. 家屬探視 (family visits — to hospital patients or prisoners), 通知家屬 (notify next of kin), 隨軍家屬 (military dependents). Used when referring to relatives in an official capacity. Different from 家人 (family members — warm and personal) — 家屬 is bureaucratic/formal. Common in hospitals, prisons, disaster notifications, and government documents.

examples.chinese: 意外發生後，醫院立刻通知了傷亡者家屬。
examples.pinyin: Yìwài fāshēng hòu, yīyuàn lìkè tōngzhīle shāngwáng zhě jiāshǔ.
examples.english: After the accident occurred, the hospital immediately notified the families of casualties.

examples.chinese: 家屬可在下午兩點到四點之間探視病患。
examples.pinyin: Jiāshǔ kě zài xiàwǔ liǎng diǎn dào sì diǎn zhījiān tànshì bìnghuàn.
examples.english: Family members may visit patients between 2pm and 4pm.

english: household name; known to every family; widely known
semanticNote: Known to every household — a true household name. 家喻戶曉的人物 (a household-name figure), 這首歌家喻戶曉 (this song is known to everyone). 喻 = understand; 曉 = know/dawn — every family understands and knows it. Stronger than 著名 (famous) or 知名 (well-known) — implies saturation-level fame across all demographics. Often used for folk heroes, classic songs, or ubiquitous brands.

examples.chinese: 《望春風》是台灣家喻戶曉的民謠。
examples.pinyin: 《Wàng Chūn Fēng》 shì Táiwān jiāyùhùxiǎo de mínyáo.
examples.english: 'Looking Forward to Spring Breeze' is a folk song known to every household in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 他是個家喻戶曉的明星，走到哪裡都有人認出他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge jiāyùhùxiǎo de míngxīng, zǒu dào nǎlǐ dōu yǒu rén rènchū tā.
examples.english: He's a household-name celebrity — wherever he goes, someone recognizes him.

semanticNote: The very tip or point of something — literally (針尖端 = tip of a needle) or figuratively (尖端科技 = cutting-edge technology, 尖端人才 = top-tier talent). The figurative use — 'at the leading edge' — is very common in business and tech discourse. 尖端武器 = advanced weaponry. Taiwan's semiconductor industry is often described as 尖端科技 (high-tech / cutting-edge technology).

examples.chinese: 台灣在半導體領域擁有尖端技術。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān zài bàndǎotǐ lǐngyù yōngyǒu jiānduān jìshù.
examples.english: Taiwan possesses cutting-edge technology in the semiconductor field.

examples.chinese: 研究人員站在這一科學領域的尖端。
examples.pinyin: Yánjiū rényuán zhàn zài zhè yī kēxué lǐngyù de jiānduān.
examples.english: The researchers are at the forefront of this scientific field.

semanticNote: Sharp and penetrating — 尖銳的聲音 (a sharp/piercing sound), 尖銳的批評 (incisive criticism), 尖銳的矛盾 (acute/sharp contradictions). The physical sense (sharp/pointed) feeds the figurative sense (penetrating/incisive). A 尖銳的問題 (sharp question) cuts right to the heart of the matter. Often used to praise insightful analysis or criticism that gets to the point. Also describes conflicts: 矛盾尖銳化 (contradictions becoming acute).

examples.chinese: 她提出了幾個尖銳的問題，讓在場所有人都沉默了。
examples.pinyin: Tā tíchūle jǐ ge jiānruì de wèntí, ràng zàichǎng suǒyǒu rén dōu chénmò le.
examples.english: She raised a few incisive questions that left everyone present speechless.

examples.chinese: 雙方矛盾日趨尖銳，協商空間越來越小。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng máodùn rìqū jiānruì, xiéshāng kōngjiān yuè lái yuè xiǎo.
examples.english: The contradictions between the two sides are becoming increasingly acute, leaving less and less room for negotiation.

semanticNote: Unwavering firmness — in beliefs, commitments, or determination. 堅定的信念 (firm belief), 立場堅定 (an unwavering stance), 堅定地走下去 (persist firmly). Also as a verb: 堅定了我的決心 (strengthened my resolve). The key is that pressure and difficulty don't change the position. 堅定 = 不動搖 (unshakeable). More about mental resolve than physical strength (that would be 堅強).

examples.chinese: 無論面對多大的壓力，她都堅定地堅持自己的原則。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn miànduì duō dà de yāli, tā dōu jiāndìng de jiānchí zìjǐ de yuánzé.
examples.english: No matter how much pressure she faced, she firmly upheld her principles.

examples.chinese: 這次挫折反而堅定了他繼續奮鬥的決心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì cuòzhé fǎn'ér jiāndìngle tā jìxù fèndòu de juéxīn.
examples.english: This setback actually strengthened his resolve to keep fighting.

semanticNote: Physically solid and durable — 堅固的建築 (a sturdy building), 堅固的材料 (durable materials), 城牆堅固 (the city walls are solid). Different from 堅定 (firmly resolute — mental/emotional) — 堅固 is about physical solidity and durability. Also used for structures like fortifications: 堅固的防線 (a solid defensive line). Compare to 牢固 (firm and secure — similar, but often about attachments being secure).

examples.chinese: 這棟建築採用堅固的鋼筋混凝土結構。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dòng jiànzhú cǎiyòng jiāngù de gāngjīn hùnníngtǔ jiégòu.
examples.english: This building uses a sturdy reinforced concrete structure.

examples.chinese: 古城的城牆非常堅固，歷經千年仍屹立不倒。
examples.pinyin: Gǔchéng de chéngqiáng fēicháng jiāngù, lìjīng qiānnián réng yìlì bú dǎo.
examples.english: The ancient city's walls are extremely solid — still standing after a thousand years.

semanticNote: Tough and resilient — hard to break and able to endure. 堅韌不拔 (tenacious and persevering — lit. can't be uprooted; a common chengyu form). 堅韌的精神 (a tough, resilient spirit), 堅韌的性格 (a tenacious character). Different from 堅強 (strong and brave — about courage) and 堅定 (resolute — about unwavering commitment). 堅韌 specifically emphasizes being BOTH hard AND flexible — like bamboo: it bends but doesn't break.

examples.chinese: 她以堅韌不拔的毅力克服了病魔。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐ jiānrèn bù bá de yìlì kèfúle bìngmó.
examples.english: She overcame her illness with tenacious, unyielding perseverance.

examples.chinese: 竹子象徵著堅韌不屈的精神。
examples.pinyin: Zhúzi xiàngzhēngzhe jiānrèn bùqū de jīngshén.
examples.english: Bamboo symbolizes a tough, unyielding spirit.

semanticNote: Solid and substantial — both physically and figuratively. 堅實的基礎 (a solid foundation), 堅實的肌肉 (solid muscles), 堅實的論據 (well-founded arguments). Implies density and quality — not hollow or superficial. Different from 堅固 (sturdy/durable — more about withstanding force) — 堅實 implies substance and thoroughness. Common in academic, business, and physical description contexts.

examples.chinese: 打好堅實的語言基礎，學什麼都更快。
examples.pinyin: Dǎ hǎo jiānshí de yǔyán jīchǔ, xué shénme dōu gèng kuài.
examples.english: Build a solid language foundation and you'll learn anything more quickly.

examples.chinese: 他的論文建立在堅實的數據和研究之上。
examples.pinyin: Tā de lùnwén jiànlì zài jiānshí de shùjù hé yánjiū zhī shàng.
examples.english: His thesis is built on solid data and research.

semanticNote: Physically hard and rigid — 堅硬的岩石 (hard rock), 堅硬的外殼 (a hard shell), 堅硬的金屬 (rigid metal). Purely physical sense of hardness; no figurative use like 堅定 or 堅韌. Opposite: 柔軟 (soft/flexible). Common in geology, materials science, and physical description. 質地堅硬 (hard in texture) is a useful compound for describing materials.

examples.chinese: 鑽石是自然界中最堅硬的物質之一。
examples.pinyin: Zuànshí shì zìrán jiè zhōng zuì jiānyìng de wùzhì zhī yī.
examples.english: Diamond is one of the hardest substances in nature.

examples.chinese: 這塊木頭質地堅硬，很難用普通鋸子切割。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài mùtou zhìdì jiānyìng, hěn nán yòng pǔtōng jùzi qiēgē.
examples.english: This piece of wood is extremely hard — difficult to cut with an ordinary saw.

semanticNote: Difficult and trying — 艱難的處境 (difficult circumstances), 艱難的選擇 (a hard choice), 艱難時期 (trying times). More weighty and literary than 困難 (difficult — everyday). 艱 implies hardship and suffering; 難 implies difficulty. 艱難 = both hard to do AND painful to endure. Common in historical and biographical narratives: 艱難的歲月 (difficult years), 艱難的創業歷程 (an arduous entrepreneurial journey).

examples.chinese: 創業初期，他度過了一段非常艱難的時期。
examples.pinyin: Chuàngyè chūqī, tā dùguòle yī duàn fēicháng jiānnán de shíqī.
examples.english: In the early days of the business, he went through an extremely difficult period.

examples.chinese: 面對艱難的選擇，她沉默了很久。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì jiānnán de xuǎnzé, tā chénmòle hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: Faced with the difficult choice, she was silent for a long time.

semanticNote: Oversight and supervision — 監督工作 (supervise work), 政府監督 (government oversight), 接受監督 (be subject to oversight). Both the act and the system of overseeing. Key in democratic governance: 立法監督行政 (legislative oversight of the executive). In business: 監督機制 (oversight mechanism), 財務監督 (financial supervision). More authoritative than 觀察 (observe) — 監督 implies the authority to ensure compliance.

examples.chinese: 政府有責任接受人民的監督。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ yǒu zérèn jiēshòu rénmín de jiāndū.
examples.english: The government has a responsibility to be subject to the people's oversight.

examples.chinese: 他負責監督整個工程的進度。
examples.pinyin: Tā fùzé jiāndū zhěng ge gōngchéng de jìndù.
