examples.english: He's responsible for overseeing the progress of the entire project.

english: keep under surveillance; monitor; watch closely
semanticNote: To surveil or closely watch someone or something — 監視犯罪嫌疑人 (surveil a criminal suspect), 監視攝影機 (surveillance camera), 被監視 (be under surveillance). More intensive and often more adversarial than 監督 (oversight — which can be collaborative). 監視 implies you're watching for wrongdoing or security threats. 監視國 (surveillance state) is a political concern frequently discussed in Taiwan's civil society.

components.meaning: to watch; to look; to see

examples.chinese: 警方對嫌疑人實施了全天候監視。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng duì xiányírén shíshīle quán tiānhòu jiānshì.
examples.english: Police placed the suspect under round-the-clock surveillance.

examples.chinese: 街道上安裝的監視攝影機有助於提升治安。
examples.pinyin: Jiēdào shàng ānzhuāng de jiānshì shèyǐngjī yǒuzhù yú tíshēng zhì'ān.
examples.english: The surveillance cameras installed on the streets help improve public security.

semanticNote: Prison — formal term. 關進監獄 (put in prison), 出獄 (be released from prison), 在監獄服刑 (serve a sentence in prison). More formal than 牢 (cell/cage — poetic/historical) or 大牢 (big prison — colloquial). 監獄改革 (prison reform), 監獄人口 (prison population). Taiwan note: 法務部矯正署 manages Taiwan's prisons. Metaphorical: 像坐牢 (like being in prison — very restricted).

examples.chinese: 他因詐欺罪被判入獄三年。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn zhàqī zuì bèi pàn rùyù sān nián.
examples.english: He was sentenced to three years in prison for fraud.

examples.chinese: 許多國家正在推動監獄系統改革。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō guójiā zhèngzài tuīdòng jiānyù xìtǒng gǎigé.
examples.english: Many countries are pushing for prison system reform.

semanticNote: To pan-fry or shallow-fry — the technique of cooking in a small amount of oil in a flat pan. 煎蛋 (fried egg), 煎魚 (pan-fried fish), 煎餃 (pan-fried dumplings = pot stickers). Common cooking verb in Taiwan. Distinct from 炸 (deep-fry — submerged in oil) and 炒 (stir-fry — high heat, constant stirring). 煎 is lower heat, more oil on the surface, for things you want nicely browned.

examples.chinese: 她用平底鍋煎了兩個荷包蛋當早餐。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng píngdǐguō jiānle liǎng ge hépāodàn dāng zǎocān.
examples.english: She pan-fried two sunny-side-up eggs for breakfast.

examples.chinese: 把豆腐兩面都煎至金黃，口感會更好。
examples.pinyin: Bǎ dòufu liǎng miàn dōu jiān zhì jīnhuáng, kǒugǎn huì gèng hǎo.
examples.english: Pan-fry the tofu until both sides are golden — the texture will be much better.

semanticNote: To pick or select from a group — 揀菜 (pick over vegetables, removing bad parts), 揀好的挑 (pick the good ones), 挑三揀四 (be picky/choosy — can't decide; lit. 'choose three, pick four'). The Taiwan usage is warm and practical: 揀菜 in the kitchen is a grandmother sitting at the table picking through vegetables. 挑三揀四 describes someone excessively fussy.

examples.chinese: 奶奶坐在院子裡揀豆子，邊揀邊和鄰居聊天。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zuò zài yuànzi lǐ jiǎn dòuzi, biān jiǎn biān hé línjū liáotiān.
examples.english: Grandma sat in the courtyard sorting beans, chatting with the neighbors as she worked.

examples.chinese: 你別挑三揀四了，這些都差不多。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié tiāo sān jiǎn sì le, zhèxiē dōu chàbuduō.
examples.english: Stop being so picky — they're all pretty much the same.

english: self-criticism; examine; review; reflect on mistakes
semanticNote: To examine and reflect on mistakes — 做檢討 (conduct a self-criticism / review), 檢討制度 (examine the system for flaws), 深刻檢討 (thorough self-examination). Has an organizational/institutional sense: after a failure, a team 做檢討 to identify what went wrong. In Taiwan corporate culture, the post-event 檢討會 (review meeting) is standard. Also personal: 我需要好好檢討自己 (I need to seriously reflect on myself).

examples.chinese: 這次活動出了很多問題，我們需要認真檢討。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huódòng chūle hěn duō wèntí, wǒmen xūyào rènzhēn jiǎntǎo.
examples.english: This event had a lot of problems — we need to seriously review what went wrong.

examples.chinese: 政府對這起事故進行了深入的檢討和反省。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ duì zhè qǐ shìgù jìnxíngle shēnrù de jiǎntǎo hé fǎnxǐng.
examples.english: The government conducted a thorough review and reflection on this incident.

semanticNote: To test or inspect for quality, correctness, or truth — 檢驗產品 (inspect products), 接受歷史的檢驗 (stand the test of history), 檢驗假設 (test a hypothesis). Both technical (lab testing, quality control) and figurative (standing the test of time, verifying claims). 檢驗結果 (test results). More rigorous than 檢查 (check/inspect — can be casual) — 檢驗 implies formal verification.

examples.chinese: 出口產品必須通過嚴格的品質檢驗。
examples.pinyin: Chūkǒu chǎnpǐn bìxū tōngguò yángé de pǐnzhí jiǎnyàn.
examples.english: Export products must pass strict quality inspection.

examples.chinese: 是否正確，最終要靠實踐來檢驗。
examples.pinyin: Shìfǒu zhèngquè, zuìzhōng yào kào shíjiàn lái jiǎnyàn.
examples.english: Whether something is correct ultimately has to be verified through practice.

english: cut the ribbon (at an opening ceremony)
semanticNote: The ribbon-cutting ceremony — 舉行剪彩典禮 (hold a ribbon-cutting ceremony), 貴賓剪彩 (VIP cuts the ribbon). 彩 = colored ribbon/streamer. The ceremony marks the official opening of a building, event, or enterprise. Common in Taiwan business and government contexts. Note: you CAN say 剪綵 (綵 = colored silk) — same meaning, 綵 is the more classical character.

examples.chinese: 新的購物中心今天舉行開幕剪彩典禮。
examples.pinyin: Xīn de gòuwù zhōngxīn jīntiān jǔxíng kāimù jiǎncǎi diǎnlǐ.
examples.english: The new shopping center held its grand opening ribbon-cutting ceremony today.

examples.chinese: 市長親自為新橋剪彩，宣告通車。
examples.pinyin: Shìzhǎng qīnzì wèi xīn qiáo jiǎncǎi, xuāngào tōngchē.
examples.english: The mayor personally cut the ribbon for the new bridge, officially opening it to traffic.

semanticNote: To make simpler or more streamlined — 簡化流程 (streamline procedures), 簡化手續 (simplify formalities), 簡化字 (simplified characters — 簡體字). The most famous use is 漢字簡化 (Chinese character simplification — the 1950s-60s PRC reform that created 簡體字). In Taiwan, 簡化 has a neutral-to-positive administrative sense (reducing bureaucratic steps) while 簡體字 is what mainland China uses (Taiwan uses traditional characters 繁體字).

examples.chinese: 政府計畫簡化申請流程，讓民眾辦事更便利。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jìhuà jiǎnhuà shēnqǐng liúchéng, ràng mínzhòng bànshì gèng biànlì.
examples.english: The government plans to streamline application procedures to make things more convenient for the public.

examples.chinese: 台灣使用繁體字，中國大陸使用簡化後的簡體字。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān shǐyòng fántǐzì, Zhōngguó dàlù shǐyòng jiǎnhuà hòu de jiǎntǐzì.
examples.english: Taiwan uses traditional characters; mainland China uses the simplified characters produced by the simplification reform.

semanticNote: Plain and poorly-equipped — 簡陋的住所 (a shabby dwelling), 設備簡陋 (primitive/inadequate equipment), 條件簡陋 (crude conditions). Describes physical places or equipment that are basic to the point of being insufficient. Not necessarily dirty — just bare and inadequate. 孔子曾住在簡陋的環境中仍勤奮治學 (Confucius studied diligently even in primitive conditions — a classic virtue story).

examples.chinese: 他早年住在一間簡陋的小屋裡，卻從未放棄學習。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǎonián zhù zài yī jiān jiǎnlòu de xiǎo wū lǐ, què cóng wèi fàngqì xuéxí.
examples.english: In his early years he lived in a crude little room but never gave up studying.

examples.chinese: 山區的學校設備簡陋，急需改善。
examples.pinyin: Shānqū de xuéxiào shèbèi jiǎnlòu, jí xū gǎishàn.
examples.english: Mountain area schools have inadequate equipment and urgently need improvement.

semanticNote: Simplified Chinese characters — the script used in mainland China, Singapore, and Malaysia, introduced in the PRC in the 1950s-60s to increase literacy. Contrast with 繁體字 (traditional characters — used in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau). In Taiwan, 簡體字 are recognizable to many but not taught in schools. Many characters are the same; others differ significantly (e.g. 愛 vs 爱, 龍 vs 龙). This is a politically and culturally sensitive topic between Taiwan and the PRC.

examples.chinese: 台灣使用繁體字，而中國大陸使用簡體字。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān shǐyòng fántǐzì, ér Zhōngguó dàlù shǐyòng jiǎntǐzì.
examples.english: Taiwan uses traditional characters while mainland China uses simplified characters.

examples.chinese: 學習中文時，選擇繁體字還是簡體字，取決於你的目標市場。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí Zhōngwén shí, xuǎnzé fántǐzì háishi jiǎntǐzì, qǔjué yú nǐ de mùbiāo shìchǎng.
examples.english: When learning Chinese, whether to learn traditional or simplified characters depends on your target market.

semanticNote: Brief and to the point — 簡要地說 (to put it briefly), 簡要介紹 (brief introduction), 請簡要回答 (please answer concisely). Different from 簡單 (simple — about complexity level) — 簡要 is about communication style: hitting the key points without excess. A 簡要 explanation is efficient and focused. Common in academic and professional contexts as a writing/speaking standard.

examples.chinese: 請簡要說明你的計畫，不超過五分鐘。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiǎnyào shuōmíng nǐ de jìhuà, bù chāoguò wǔ fēnzhōng.
examples.english: Please give a brief explanation of your plan — no more than five minutes.

examples.chinese: 她的報告簡要清晰，重點突出，讓人印象深刻。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bàogào jiǎnyào qīngxī, zhòngdiǎn tūchū, ràng rén yìnxiàng shēnkè.
examples.english: Her report was concise and clear, with the key points standing out — very impressive.

english: experienced and knowledgeable; well-traveled and well-read
semanticNote: Having seen a lot and knowing a lot — the wisdom that comes from broad experience. 她走南闖北，見多識廣 (she's traveled widely and seen a great deal). Always complimentary. The assumption: exposure to diverse people, places, and situations makes you more insightful and less easily rattled. Contrast with 井底之蛙 (a frog in a well — narrow-minded from limited experience).

examples.chinese: 他走遍世界各地，見多識廣，說話很有見地。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒubiàn shìjiè gèdì, jiànduōshíguǎng, shuōhuà hěn yǒu jiàndì.
examples.english: He's traveled all over the world — experienced and knowledgeable, everything he says is insightful.

examples.chinese: 多出去走走，見多識廣，對人生很有幫助。
examples.pinyin: Duō chūqù zǒuzǒu, jiànduōshíguǎng, duì rénshēng hěn yǒu bāngzhù.
examples.english: Getting out more and broadening your experience is very beneficial for life.

semanticNote: One's view or understanding — 獨到的見解 (unique/insightful perspective), 請分享你的見解 (please share your views), 見解深刻 (deep insight). More intellectual and considered than 意見 (opinion — which can be casual: 你有什麼意見？= what do you think?). 見解 implies a thoughtful, developed perspective. 有見解的人 = a person with insight. Common in academic, intellectual, and professional discourse.

examples.chinese: 他對這個問題有獨到的見解，值得參考。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège wèntí yǒu dúdào de jiànjiě, zhídé cānkǎo.
examples.english: He has unique insights on this issue that are worth considering.

examples.chinese: 請就這個議題分享你的見解。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiù zhège yìtí fēnxiǎng nǐ de jiànjiě.
examples.english: Please share your views on this topic.

english: knowledge from experience; what one has seen and heard
semanticNote: Knowledge gained through direct experience — things you've seen and heard firsthand. 增廣見聞 (broaden one's horizons — the most common phrase), 見聞廣博 (broadly experienced). 增廣見聞 is a very common goal stated for travel, reading, and study. Different from 知識 (academic knowledge) — 見聞 is experiential, firsthand. A journal of travels might be called 旅行見聞錄.

examples.chinese: 多旅行可以增廣見聞，開拓視野。
examples.pinyin: Duō lǚxíng kěyǐ zēngguǎng jiànwén, kāituò shìyě.
examples.english: Traveling more broadens your experience and expands your horizons.

examples.chinese: 她把旅行中的所見所聞寫成了一本書。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ lǚxíng zhōng de suǒ jiàn suǒ wén xiě chéngle yī běn shū.
examples.english: She wrote a book about everything she saw and heard during her travels.

english: act heroically in a just cause; bravely do what is right
semanticNote: Seeing what is right and bravely acting on it — the courage to intervene when you witness injustice. 見義勇為的英雄 (a hero who acted bravely for justice). This is a highly praised virtue in Chinese culture. There's also a modern ironic dimension: in mainland China, bystanders sometimes hesitate to help accident victims for fear of being falsely blamed — 見義勇為 has become a social issue there. In Taiwan: generally still unambiguously admired.

examples.chinese: 他見義勇為，挺身而出幫助了被搶劫的老人。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiànyìyǒngwéi, tǐngshēn ér chū bāngzhùle bèi qiǎngjié de lǎorén.
examples.english: He acted bravely and stepped forward to help the elderly person who was being robbed.

examples.chinese: 社會需要更多見義勇為的人，才能變得更美好。
examples.pinyin: Shèhuì xūyào gèng duō jiànyìyǒngwéi de rén, cái néng biàn de gèng měihǎo.
examples.english: Society needs more people who bravely do what's right for it to become better.

semanticNote: A spy or intelligence agent. 間諜活動 (espionage), 雙面間諜 (double agent), 工業間諜 (industrial espionage). Common in political, military, and thriller contexts. Taiwan, given its geopolitical situation, features news about 間諜 activities relatively frequently. Also used in games and movies: 間諜電影 (spy films). 間 here = 'between/in the gaps' — a spy works in the gaps, hidden between sides.

examples.chinese: 這名間諜在敵方潛伏了五年才被識破。
examples.pinyin: Zhè míng jiàndié zài dífāng qiánfúle wǔ nián cái bèi shípò.
examples.english: This spy was embedded with the enemy for five years before being exposed.

examples.chinese: 他最喜歡看各種間諜電影。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuān kàn gèzhǒng jiàndié diànyǐng.
examples.english: He loves watching all kinds of spy movies.

english: interval; gap; space; be separated by
semanticNote: A space or interval between things — 間隔兩年 (separated by two years), 間隔五公分 (spaced 5 centimeters apart), 定期間隔 (at regular intervals). Both physical distance and time gaps. Common in schedules (服藥間隔 = dosing interval), spacing (座位間隔 = seat spacing), and history (兩次戰爭間隔了二十年). 間隔 focuses on the gap between things, not the things themselves.

examples.chinese: 這種藥每次服用的間隔不能少於四小時。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào měi cì fúyòng de jiàngé bù néng shǎo yú sì xiǎoshí.
examples.english: The dosing interval for this medicine must be at least four hours.

examples.chinese: 兩棟建築之間的間隔太小，採光很差。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng dòng jiànzhú zhījiān de jiàngé tài xiǎo, cǎiguāng hěn chà.
examples.english: The gap between the two buildings is too small — the lighting is terrible.

semanticNote: Indirect — as opposed to 直接 (direct). 間接影響 (indirect influence), 間接溝通 (indirect communication), 間接稅 (indirect tax). In Chinese communication culture, 間接 is often the default — saying things through hints, metaphors, or intermediaries to avoid confrontation. 間接表達不滿 (express dissatisfaction indirectly). Also in logic and law: 間接證據 (circumstantial evidence).

examples.chinese: 她間接地暗示他應該早點回家。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiànjiē de ànshì tā yīnggāi zǎodiǎn huíjiā.
examples.english: She indirectly hinted that he should come home earlier.

examples.chinese: 汙染雖然是間接原因，但仍不可忽視。
examples.pinyin: Wūrǎn suīrán shì jiànjiē yuányīn, dàn réng bùkě hūshì.
examples.english: Although pollution is an indirect cause, it still cannot be overlooked.

semanticNote: A double-edged straight sword — the traditional Chinese 劍 (jian) is a two-edged blade, distinct from 刀 (dāo = single-edged saber/knife). 練劍 (practice sword technique), 太極劍 (tai chi sword form), 劍客 (swordsman). Classical cultural associations: refined and scholar-warrior aesthetic. Also 劍橋 (Cambridge — transliteration: 劍 jiàn + 橋 = bridge). A famous word pairing: 劍拔弩張 (swords drawn and crossbows ready — tension is about to explode).

examples.chinese: 他從小學習劍術，動作瀟灑飄逸。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo xuéxí jiànshù, dòngzuò xiāosǎ piāoyì.
examples.english: He studied sword technique from a young age — his movements are graceful and flowing.

examples.chinese: 兩人之間的關係已到了劍拔弩張的地步。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng rén zhījiān de guānxì yǐ dào le jiànbá nǔzhāng de dìbù.
examples.english: The relationship between the two has reached the point where the tension is about to explode.

semanticNote: Complete and sound — free from defects or gaps. 健全的制度 (a sound system), 法制健全 (sound rule of law), 心智健全 (mentally sound). As a verb: 健全機制 (improve/perfect the mechanism), 健全法規 (strengthen regulations). Common in governance and institutional language: 健全民主制度 (perfect/strengthen the democratic system). The sense is of completeness — all parts present and functioning properly.

examples.chinese: 台灣擁有相對健全的民主制度。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān yōngyǒu xiāngduì jiànquán de mínzhǔ zhìdù.
examples.english: Taiwan has a relatively sound democratic system.

examples.chinese: 政府致力於健全社會保障制度。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhìlì yú jiànquán shèhuì bǎozhàng zhìdù.
examples.english: The government is committed to perfecting the social security system.

semanticNote: Naval vessels — warships collectively. 艦艇 covers both 艦 (large warships like destroyers and frigates) and 艇 (smaller vessels like patrol boats and submarines). 海軍艦艇 (naval vessels), 艦艇巡邏 (warship patrol). Relevant to Taiwan in the context of the Taiwan Strait and cross-strait military dynamics. Common in military news reports.

examples.chinese: 海軍派遣艦艇在附近海域巡邏。
examples.pinyin: Hǎijūn pàiqiǎn jiàntǐng zài fùjìn hǎiyù xúnluó.
examples.english: The navy dispatched warships to patrol the nearby waters.

examples.chinese: 台灣海峽的艦艇動態備受國際關注。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān Hǎixiá de jiàntǐng dòongtài bèi shòu guójì guānzhù.
examples.english: Naval vessel movements in the Taiwan Strait are closely watched internationally.

semanticNote: To trample or tread on — physically (踐踏草皮 = trample the lawn) or figuratively (踐踏人權 = trample on human rights, 踐踏尊嚴 = trample on dignity). The figurative sense is very common and important. 踐踏 implies deliberate or contemptuous disregard — not just accidentally stepping on something, but crushing it. Strong word for rights violations and dehumanizing treatment.

examples.chinese: 請勿踐踏草皮，保護公共環境。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng wù jiàntà cǎopí, bǎohù gōnggòng huánjìng.
examples.english: Please do not trample the lawn — protect the public environment.

examples.chinese: 任何踐踏基本人權的行為都不可接受。
examples.pinyin: Rènhé jiàntà jīběn rénquán de xíngwéi dōu bùkě jiēshòu.
examples.english: Any act that tramples on basic human rights is unacceptable.

semanticNote: Liquid splashing or spattering — 水花四濺 (water splashing everywhere), 血濺牆壁 (blood spattering on the wall), 泥水濺到衣服上 (muddy water splashing onto clothes). Very visual and onomatopoeic in feel. Common in descriptive writing about rain, water, blood, and any forceful liquid impact. 四濺 (splashing in all directions) is a common collocation.

examples.chinese: 汽車快速駛過，水花濺了他一身。
examples.pinyin: Qìchē kuàisù shǐguò, shuǐhuā jiànle tā yīshēn.
examples.english: A car sped past and splashed him from head to toe.

examples.chinese: 她在廚房炒菜，油濺到手，被燙了一下。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài chúfáng chǎocài, yóu jiàn dào shǒu, bèi tàngle yīxià.
examples.english: While stir-frying in the kitchen, hot oil splashed onto her hand and burned her.

semanticNote: To identify and distinguish between things — especially distinguishing authentic from fake, or telling apart similar things. 鑒別真偽 (distinguish genuine from fake), 鑒別古董 (authenticate antiques), 鑒別人才 (identify talent). Implies expert discernment — 鑒 means mirror/appraise; to 鑒別 is to hold something up to scrutiny. Common in art authentication, wine tasting, talent assessment, and quality control.

examples.chinese: 他有鑒別古玩真偽的獨特能力。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu jiànbié gǔwán zhēnwěi de dútè nénglì.
examples.english: He has a unique ability to authenticate antiques and distinguish genuine from fake.

examples.chinese: 資訊爆炸的時代，鑒別資訊真偽非常重要。
examples.pinyin: Zīxùn bàozhà de shídài, jiànbié zīxùn zhēnwěi fēicháng zhòngyào.
examples.english: In an era of information overload, the ability to distinguish true information from false is very important.

english: appraise; evaluate; authenticate; make a determination
semanticNote: Expert appraisal or evaluation — 鑒定文物 (appraise cultural relics), 司法鑒定 (forensic examination), 體能鑒定 (physical fitness evaluation). More formal and authoritative than 鑒別 — 鑒定 produces an official determination or conclusion, while 鑒別 is the act of discerning. 鑒定書 = appraisal certificate. Common in legal, medical, cultural relic, and professional evaluation contexts.

examples.chinese: 這件文物需要送去專家處進行鑒定。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn wénwù xūyào sòng qù zhuānjiā chù jìnxíng jiàndìng.
examples.english: This artifact needs to be sent to experts for appraisal.

examples.chinese: 法院委託進行司法鑒定以確定案發原因。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn wěituō jìnxíng sīfǎ jiàndìng yǐ quèdìng ànfā yuányīn.
examples.english: The court commissioned a forensic examination to determine the cause of the incident.

english: in light of; in view of; given that
semanticNote: Formal conjunction meaning 'given that' or 'in view of the fact that.' 鑒于以上情況... (In light of the above situation...), 鑒于此... (Given this...). Almost exclusively written/formal — you'd never say 鑒于 in casual conversation. Common in official letters, legal documents, and formal reports. Used to cite a reason or basis for an action or decision that follows. Equivalent to 由於、考慮到 in more colloquial register.

components.meaning: take as a mirror; in light of

examples.chinese: 鑒于目前的疫情形勢，活動暫時取消。
examples.pinyin: Jiànyú mùqián de yìqíng xíngshì, huódòng zànshí qǔxiāo.
examples.english: In view of the current pandemic situation, the event is temporarily cancelled.

examples.chinese: 鑒于您的優秀表現，公司決定給予晉升。
examples.pinyin: Jiànyú nín de yōuxiù biǎoxiàn, gōngsī juédìng jǐyǔ jìnshēng.
examples.english: In light of your excellent performance, the company has decided to promote you.

semanticNote: Just under or close to a quantity — 將近一百人 (nearly a hundred people), 將近午夜 (close to midnight). Always used before a number or time — the quantity hasn't quite been reached. Similar to 將近 vs 差不多 (approximately — more casual and about general similarity). 將近 = just short of X; 超過 = more than X. Common in news, reports, and factual descriptions.

examples.chinese: 這項工程歷時將近三年才完工。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng gōngchéng lìshí jiāngjìn sān nián cái wángōng.
examples.english: This project took nearly three years to complete.

examples.chinese: 音樂會的觀眾將近三千人。
examples.pinyin: Yīnyuèhuì de guānzhòng jiāngjìn sān qiān rén.
examples.english: The concert audience was close to three thousand people.

english: make do with; put up with; accept reluctantly
semanticNote: To make do with something imperfect — 就將就吧 (just make do with it), 將就著用 (make do with this for now). Always implies settling for less than ideal. In Taiwan: 隨便將就 (just accept whatever, don't fuss). The cultural dimension: 將就 vs insisting on quality — knowing when to 將就 is practical; being too demanding (挑剔) is difficult. 你就將就吃點吧 = just eat something, don't be picky.

examples.chinese: 酒店沒有空房了，就將就住這間吧。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn méiyǒu kōngfáng le, jiù jiāngjiu zhù zhè jiān ba.
examples.english: There are no other rooms in the hotel — just make do with this one.

examples.chinese: 時間緊，先將就吃個三明治，以後再說。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān jǐn, xiān jiāngjiu chī ge sānmíngzhì, yǐhòu zài shuō.
examples.english: We're short on time — just make do with a sandwich for now, we can figure the rest out later.

semanticNote: A military general — 大將軍 (general), 將軍級別 (general officer rank). Also the chess move 'check' in Chinese chess (象棋): 將軍！ (Check!). Figurative: 將人一軍 = put someone in a difficult position / challenge them (from the chess move). 你這是在將我一軍嗎？= are you trying to put me on the spot? This extended sense is very colloquial.

examples.chinese: 他在二十年前晉升為將軍，是部隊裡最年輕的。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài èrshí nián qián jìnshēng wéi jiāngjūn, shì bùduì lǐ zuì niánqīng de.
examples.english: He was promoted to general twenty years ago — the youngest in the military.

examples.chinese: 他這番話擺明了是要將我一軍。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhè fān huà bǎimíngle shì yào jiāng wǒ yī jūn.
examples.english: What he said was clearly meant to put me on the spot.

semanticNote: Stiff and rigid — physically (肌肉僵硬 = stiff muscles, 屍體僵硬 = rigor mortis) or behaviorally (態度僵硬 = a rigid/inflexible attitude). The physical sense (body stiffness from cold, tension, or death) is the core meaning. The behavioral sense (inflexible thinking or manner) extends from it. 表情僵硬 (stiff/frozen expression) — common in describing someone who's uncomfortable or performing poorly in social situations.

examples.chinese: 在外面站了太久，他的手腳都僵硬了。
examples.pinyin: Zài wàimiàn zhànle tài jiǔ, tā de shǒujiǎo dōu jiāngyìng le.
examples.english: Having stood outside too long, his hands and feet went stiff.

examples.chinese: 第一次上台，她因緊張而表情僵硬。
examples.pinyin: Dì yī cì shàngtái, tā yīn jǐnzhāng ér biǎoqíng jiāngyìng.
examples.english: Taking the stage for the first time, her expression was stiff from nerves.

semanticNote: A reward given as encouragement or recognition — 獎勵優秀員工 (reward outstanding employees), 獎勵機制 (incentive system), 物質獎勵 (material reward). Both verb (to reward) and noun (the reward/incentive). The key sense is positive reinforcement — rewarding good behavior to encourage more. Different from 獎賞 (reward/prize — can be more about compensation after merit) — 獎勵 emphasizes the motivational purpose.

examples.chinese: 公司用年終獎金獎勵表現優異的員工。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yòng niánzhōng jiǎngjīn jiǎnglì biǎoxiàn yōuyì de yuángōng.
examples.english: The company uses year-end bonuses to reward employees with excellent performance.

examples.chinese: 學校設立了多種獎勵機制來激勵學生努力學習。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào shèlìle duō zhǒng jiǎnglì jīzhì lái jīlì xuéshēng nǔlì xuéxí.
examples.english: The school established various reward systems to motivate students to study hard.

semanticNote: A reward or prize — especially for meritorious deeds or outstanding work. 給予獎賞 (bestow a reward), 豐厚的獎賞 (a generous reward). More formal and slightly grander than 獎勵 (which emphasizes encouraging future behavior) — 獎賞 feels more like recognizing and compensating past merit. Historical resonance: 皇帝獎賞功臣 (the emperor rewarded loyal ministers). Common in traditional and formal contexts.

examples.chinese: 他立下大功，受到了豐厚的獎賞。
examples.pinyin: Tā lì xià dà gōng, shòudàole fēnghòu de jiǎngshǎng.
examples.english: He rendered great service and received a generous reward.

examples.chinese: 公司用旅遊機會作為獎賞最佳員工的方式。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yòng lǚyóu jīhuì zuòwéi jiǎngshǎng zuìjiā yuángōng de fāngshì.
examples.english: The company uses travel opportunities as a way to reward top employees.

semanticNote: An oar or paddle — used to propel a boat. 划槳 (row/paddle), 船槳 (oar). Common in dragon boat racing contexts: 划龍舟的槳 (dragon boat paddle). Taiwan's dragon boat festival (端午節) makes 槳 seasonally relevant. Also: 螺旋槳 (propeller — lit. 'spiral oar'). A simple, concrete word; most interesting in its compounds and figurative extensions.

examples.chinese: 選手們齊心划槳，龍舟在水面上快速前進。
examples.pinyin: Xuǎnshǒumen qíxīn huá jiǎng, lóngzhōu zài shuǐmiàn shàng kuàisù qiánjìn.
examples.english: The athletes paddled in unison and the dragon boat sped across the water.

examples.chinese: 他輕輕地撥動船槳，在平靜的湖面上漂行。
examples.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng de bōdòng chuán jiǎng, zài píngjìng de húmiàn shàng piāo xíng.
examples.english: He gently moved the oar, drifting across the calm lake surface.

semanticNote: To arrive or descend — of something grand, divine, or significant. 黑暗降臨 (darkness descends), 新年降臨 (the New Year arrives), 災難降臨 (disaster befalls). Has a literary and slightly elevated tone — you wouldn't say 降臨 about a friend arriving for coffee. Used for the arrival of seasons, divine figures, catastrophes, or momentous events. 救世主降臨 (the savior descends).

examples.chinese: 夜幕降臨，城市漸漸亮起了燈火。
examples.pinyin: Yèmù jiànglín, chéngshì jiànjiàn liàng qǐle dēnghuǒ.
examples.english: As night descended, the city gradually lit up with lights.

examples.chinese: 幸福不會自動降臨，需要用心去創造。
examples.pinyin: Xìngfú bú huì zìdòng jiànglín, xūyào yòng xīn qù chuàngzào.
examples.english: Happiness doesn't arrive on its own — you have to put your heart into creating it.

semanticNote: Things crossing or intersecting — 道路交叉 (roads intersecting), 交叉點 (intersection/crossroads), 交叉感染 (cross-infection), 學科交叉 (interdisciplinary overlap). Both physical (roads, lines crossing) and abstract (interests overlapping, disciplines intersecting). 交叉路口 = intersection/crossroads. Common in biology, traffic, and academic interdisciplinary discussions.

examples.chinese: 這兩條線在中間交叉，形成一個X形。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng tiáo xiàn zài zhōngjiān jiāochā, xíngchéng yī ge X xíng.
examples.english: These two lines intersect in the middle, forming an X shape.

examples.chinese: 這項研究橫跨多個學科，具有高度交叉性。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng yánjiū héngkuà duō ge xuékē, jùyǒu gāodù jiāochā xìng.
examples.english: This research spans multiple disciplines and has a high degree of interdisciplinary overlap.

english: explain; account for; hand over; confess
semanticNote: Several uses: (1) explain or account for — 交代清楚 (explain clearly); (2) hand something over / brief someone — 把任務交代下去 (hand down the task); (3) confess — 把事情全部交代了 (confessed everything). The confess sense is key in legal/interrogation contexts. Also written 交待. Taiwan use: 你得跟大家交代一下 = you owe everyone an explanation.

examples.chinese: 出發前，他把工作都交代給同事。
examples.pinyin: Chūfā qián, tā bǎ gōngzuò dōu jiāodài gěi tóngshì.
examples.english: Before leaving, he handed over all the work to his colleagues.

examples.chinese: 警方要求嫌疑人交代作案經過。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng yāoqiú xiányírén jiāodài zuò'àn jīngguò.
examples.english: Police demanded that the suspect account for how the crime was committed.

english: negotiate; take up a matter with; deal with through discussion
semanticNote: Negotiating or taking up a matter with another party — 與對方交涉 (negotiate with the other side), 外交交涉 (diplomatic negotiations). More formal and confrontational than 商量 (discuss — collaborative). 交涉 implies a dispute that needs to be worked out between parties with conflicting interests. 多次交涉未果 (repeated negotiations yielded no result) is a common news phrase.

examples.chinese: 公司就賠償問題與對方多次交涉。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī jiù péicháng wèntí yǔ duìfāng duō cì jiāoshè.
examples.english: The company negotiated repeatedly with the other party on the compensation issue.

examples.chinese: 外交官奉命就此事向對方政府提出交涉。
examples.pinyin: Wàijiāoguān fèng mìng jiù cǐ shì xiàng duìfāng zhèngfǔ tíchū jiāoshè.
examples.english: The diplomat was ordered to raise this matter with the opposing government.

semanticNote: A business transaction or deal — 進行交易 (conduct a transaction), 股票交易 (stock trading), 交易所 (exchange — as in stock exchange). Common in finance and commerce. Also figurative: 政治交易 (political deal). Taiwan's financial market: 台灣證券交易所 (Taiwan Stock Exchange). The key feature of 交易 is mutual exchange — something given for something received.

examples.chinese: 這次房屋交易順利完成，買賣雙方都很滿意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì fángwū jiāoyì shùnlì wánchéng, mǎimài shuāngfāng dōu hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: The real estate transaction was completed smoothly — both buyer and seller were satisfied.

examples.chinese: 網路購物讓交易變得更加便捷。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnglù gòuwù ràng jiāoyì biàn de gèngjiā biànjié.
examples.english: Online shopping has made transactions much more convenient.

semanticNote: Overly delicate, pampered, or fussy — unable to handle hardship. 別那麼嬌氣 (don't be so fussy), 嬌氣的孩子 (a pampered child). Always slightly negative — a criticism of someone who needs to toughen up. Can also describe plants that need delicate care. In Taiwan parenting discourse, raising children who are too 嬌氣 is seen as a problem.

examples.chinese: 別那麼嬌氣，只是下個小雨而已。
examples.pinyin: Bié nàme jiāoqì, zhǐshì xià ge xiǎo yǔ ér yǐ.
examples.english: Don't be so fussy — it's just a little rain.

examples.chinese: 現在的孩子太嬌氣了，吃不了一點苦。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài de háizi tài jiāoqì le, chī bù liǎo yīdiǎn kǔ.
examples.english: Kids nowadays are too pampered — they can't handle even the slightest hardship.

english: focus; focal point; center of attention
semanticNote: The focal point — in optics (where light rays converge) and figuratively (what attention converges on). 輿論焦點 (focus of public opinion), 成為焦點 (become the center of attention), 爭議的焦點 (the crux of the dispute). Taiwan media: 焦點新聞 (focus news segment). 焦 = scorched — the point where concentrated light burns.

examples.chinese: 這個議題已成為各界討論的焦點。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yìtí yǐ chénwéi gèjiè tǎolùn de jiāodiǎn.
examples.english: This issue has become the focal point of discussion across all sectors.

examples.chinese: 她一出現就成為全場的焦點。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī chūxiàn jiù chénwéi quánchǎng de jiāodiǎn.
examples.english: The moment she appeared, she became the center of everyone's attention.

semanticNote: Anxious and impatient worry — 焦急地等待 (wait anxiously), 焦急的眼神 (anxious eyes). More about the physical agitation of worry than deep psychological anxiety (that's 焦慮). 焦急 is the acute, in-the-moment feeling when you're worried something bad is happening or time is running out. 他急得焦急萬分 (he was overwhelmed with anxious worry). Often paired with 不安 (uneasy): 焦急不安.

examples.chinese: 孩子遲遲沒回家，媽媽焦急地在門口等著。
examples.pinyin: Háizi chíchí méi huíjiā, māma jiāojí de zài ménkǒu děngzhe.
examples.english: The child was long overdue home — mom waited anxiously at the door.

examples.chinese: 他焦急地翻找著手機，卻找不到。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiāojí de fān zhǎozhe shǒujī, què zhǎo bú dào.
examples.english: He anxiously rummaged around for his phone but couldn't find it.

semanticNote: A corner or nook — physical (房間的角落 = corner of the room) or metaphorical (世界的每個角落 = every corner of the world). 躲在角落裡 (hide in a corner) connotes shyness or isolation. 每個角落 (every corner/nook and cranny) is very common. A 角落 人物 is a peripheral figure — someone on the margins. The word combines 角 (angle/corner) + 落 (fall/settle).

examples.chinese: 她把書桌擺在房間的角落，安靜地讀書。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shūzhuō bǎi zài fángjiān de jiǎoluò, ānjìng de dúshū.
examples.english: She placed her desk in the corner of the room and read quietly.

examples.chinese: 這首歌的旋律傳遍了世界的每個角落。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de xuánlǜ chuánbiànle shìjiè de měi ge jiǎoluò.
examples.english: This song's melody has spread to every corner of the world.

english: lucky by fluke; by a stroke of luck; to count on luck
semanticNote: Getting lucky in a way you didn't deserve or couldn't count on — 僥幸逃過 (escaped by sheer luck), 抱有僥幸心理 (harbor the wishful thinking that luck will save you). Always implies you shouldn't rely on this luck — it was a narrow escape or unearned good fortune. 抱著僥幸心理 is a warning phrase: don't count on luck; plan properly. More negative-tinged than simply 幸運 (lucky — neutral).

examples.chinese: 這次他僥幸通過了考試，但其實完全沒準備。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì tā jiǎoxìng tōngguòle kǎoshì, dàn qíshí wánquán méi zhǔnbèi.
examples.english: He squeaked through the exam this time by sheer luck — but he hadn't prepared at all.

examples.chinese: 做事不能抱著僥幸心理，要認真準備。
examples.pinyin: Zuòshì bù néng bàozhe jiǎoxìng xīnlǐ, yào rènzhēn zhǔnbèi.
examples.english: You can't count on luck in what you do — you need to prepare seriously.

semanticNote: Stirring or mixing — 攪拌均勻 (stir evenly), 攪拌機 (blender/mixer), 攪拌棒 (stirring stick). Common cooking and baking term: 把材料攪拌在一起 (mix the ingredients together). Unlike 混合 (mix — combine together), 攪拌 specifically means the physical action of stirring with a tool or motion. Common in recipe instructions throughout Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 將奶油和麵粉攪拌均勻後，加入雞蛋。
examples.pinyin: Jiāng nǎiyóu hé miànfěn jiǎobàn jūnyún hòu, jiā rù jīdàn.
examples.english: After stirring the butter and flour evenly, add the eggs.

examples.chinese: 咖啡加了糖之後，記得攪拌一下。
examples.pinyin: Kāfēi jiāle táng zhīhòu, jìde jiǎobàn yīxià.
examples.english: After adding sugar to your coffee, remember to give it a stir.

semanticNote: Formally paying fees or taxes to an authority — 繳納稅款 (pay taxes), 繳納罰款 (pay a fine), 繳納會費 (pay membership dues). The 繳 implies an obligatory payment submitted upward to an institution. More formal than 繳 alone or 付 (pay — general). In Taiwan: 繳稅 (pay taxes), 繳費 (pay fees) are everyday administrative terms. 繳不出錢 = can't afford to pay.

examples.chinese: 每年五月是台灣個人所得稅的繳納期。
examples.pinyin: Měi nián wǔ yuè shì Táiwān gèrén suǒdéshuì de jiǎonà qī.
examples.english: May of each year is Taiwan's individual income tax payment period.

examples.chinese: 違規停車必須在期限內繳納罰款。
examples.pinyin: Wéiguī tíngchē bìxū zài qīxiàn nèi jiǎonà fákuǎn.
examples.english: Illegal parking fines must be paid within the deadline.

english: compete; have a contest; measure strength against
semanticNote: A direct contest or competition — 進行較量 (have a contest), 智力較量 (battle of wits), 一較高下 (compete to see who's better — related phrase). More combative than 競爭 (compete — market/general) — 較量 implies direct head-to-head confrontation to determine superiority. Common in sports, chess, intellectual debates, and military/political rivalries.

examples.chinese: 兩隊在決賽中展開了激烈的較量。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng duì zài juésài zhōng zhǎnkāile jīliè de jiàoliàng.
examples.english: The two teams engaged in an intense contest in the final.

examples.chinese: 這場談判是兩方智慧和意志的較量。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng tánpàn shì liǎng fāng zhìhuì hé yìzhì de jiàoliàng.
examples.english: This negotiation is a contest of wits and willpower between the two sides.

semanticNote: The manners and character formed through upbringing and education — 有教養 (well-bred, mannerly), 沒有教養 (ill-bred, rude). A holistic concept combining moral character, social graces, and cultural refinement instilled from childhood. In Taiwan: 他很有教養 = he has good manners / is well brought up. More about character formation than academic learning (that's 教育). 家教 (home tutor, or family upbringing) overlaps significantly.

examples.chinese: 她從小接受良好的教養，說話做事都很得體。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo jiēshòu liánghǎo de jiàoyǎng, shuōhuà zuòshì dōu hěn détǐ.
examples.english: She received a good upbringing from childhood — everything she says and does is appropriate.

examples.chinese: 在公共場所大聲喧嘩是沒有教養的行為。
examples.pinyin: Zài gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ dàshēng xuānhuá shì méiyǒu jiàoyǎng de xíngwéi.
examples.english: Making loud noise in public places is ill-mannered behavior.

semanticNote: A social stratum or class — 社會階層 (social strata), 中產階層 (middle class), 不同階層的人 (people from different social strata). More specific than 階級 (class — Marxist sense, more about power/production relations) — 階層 is about the layered structure of society without necessarily implying class conflict. Common in sociology, demographic analysis, and marketing (消費者階層 = consumer segments).

examples.chinese: 台灣的中產階層是消費市場的主要驅動力。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de zhōngchǎn jiēcéng shì xiāofèi shìchǎng de zhǔyào qūdòng lì.
examples.english: Taiwan's middle class is the main driving force of the consumer market.

examples.chinese: 這項政策對不同社會階層的影響各有不同。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè duì bùtóng shèhuì jiēcéng de yǐngxiǎng gè yǒu bùtóng.
examples.english: This policy affects different social strata in different ways.

english: all; each and every; without exception
semanticNote: Classical/literary 'all' or 'every' — 皆大歡喜 (everyone is happy — a chengyu), 四海之內皆兄弟 (within the four seas, all are brothers — Confucian saying), 比比皆是 (found everywhere). More literary than 都 (all — everyday spoken). Almost exclusively written or in set phrases. Seeing 皆 in modern Mandarin outside of idioms or formal writing is unusual — it signals a deliberately literary register.

examples.chinese: 這部電影結局皆大歡喜，觀眾都很滿意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiéjú jiē dà huānxǐ, guānzhòng dōu hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: The film had a happy ending for everyone — the audience was very satisfied.

examples.chinese: 這種情況比比皆是，並不罕見。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng qíngkuàng bǐbǐ jiē shì, bìng bù hǎnjiàn.
examples.english: This kind of situation can be found everywhere — it's not at all rare.

english: in succession; one after another; repeatedly
semanticNote: One after another in quick succession — 接連失敗 (fail again and again), 接連幾天 (several days in a row), 接連不斷 (unending/continuous). Emphasizes continuity and repetition — things happening without a meaningful break. Different from 陸續 (gradually/one by one — more spread out) and 相繼 (in succession — similar, slightly more formal). 接連 often implies things happening faster than expected.

components.meaning: link; connect; in a row; even

examples.chinese: 他接連三次面試失敗，士氣大受打擊。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiēlián sān cì miànshì shībài, shìqì dà shòu dǎjī.
examples.english: He failed three job interviews in a row — his morale took a big hit.

examples.chinese: 最近接連下了好幾天的大雨。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn jiēlián xiàle hǎo jǐ tiān de dàyǔ.
examples.english: It's been raining heavily for several days in a row recently.

english: expose; unmask; bring wrongdoing to light
semanticNote: To expose wrongdoing or deception — 揭露醜聞 (expose a scandal), 揭露腐敗 (expose corruption). Has a strong investigative/accusatory flavor — journalists, whistleblowers, and investigators 揭露. The sense is always that something was deliberately hidden and is now being forced into the open. Different from 揭示 (reveal — analytical, bringing hidden truths to understanding without the adversarial sense).

examples.chinese: 記者歷時兩年調查，終於揭露了這起腐敗案。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě lìshí liǎng nián diàochá, zhōngyú jiēlùle zhè qǐ fǔbài àn.
examples.english: After two years of investigation, the journalist finally exposed this corruption case.

examples.chinese: 吹哨者冒著危險揭露了公司的違法行為。
examples.pinyin: Chuī shào zhě màozhe wéixiǎn jiēlùle gōngsī de wéifǎ xíngwéi.
examples.english: The whistleblower risked their safety to expose the company's illegal activities.

semanticNote: Practicing moderation and self-restraint — 飲食要節制 (eat and drink in moderation), 節制消費 (moderate consumption), 缺乏節制 (lacking restraint). The classical virtue of temperance — not going to extremes. 節 = regulate; 制 = control. Common in health, ethics, and self-discipline contexts. A 有節制的人 knows when to stop. Confucian resonance: moderation in all things is virtuous.

examples.chinese: 飲酒要節制，過量飲酒對身體有害。
examples.pinyin: Yǐnjiǔ yào jiézhì, guòliàng yǐnjiǔ duì shēntǐ yǒuhài.
examples.english: Drink in moderation — excessive drinking is harmful to your health.

examples.chinese: 他在花錢方面很有節制，從不亂花。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huāqián fāngmiàn hěn yǒu jiézhì, cóng bù luàn huā.
examples.english: He's very restrained when it comes to spending money — never spends carelessly.

semanticNote: Rhythm and tempo — in music (節奏感 = sense of rhythm) and life (生活節奏 = pace/rhythm of life, 工作節奏 = work pace). One of the most versatile words: 城市節奏 (city pace), 掌握節奏 (control the pace/rhythm), 跟上節奏 (keep up with the pace). Taiwan has a reputation for a more relaxed 生活節奏 compared to mainland China cities. 節奏 also appears in internet slang: 帶節奏 = stir things up / set the narrative.

components.meaning: play music; present to ruler; achieve

examples.chinese: 台北的生活節奏比想像中輕鬆。
examples.pinyin: Táiběi de shēnghuó jiézòu bǐ xiǎngxiàng zhōng qīngsōng.
examples.english: Taipei's pace of life is more relaxed than you'd imagine.

examples.chinese: 她天生有節奏感，學跳舞很快。
examples.pinyin: Tā tiānshēng yǒu jiézòu gǎn, xué tiàowǔ hěn kuài.
examples.english: She has a natural sense of rhythm — she picked up dancing very quickly.

semanticNote: Outstanding and remarkable — 傑出的成就 (outstanding achievement), 傑出人才 (exceptional talent), 傑出貢獻 (remarkable contribution). Always highly positive. More emphatic than 優秀 (excellent — the everyday standard) — 傑出 implies standing clearly above the rest. Often used in awards, tributes, and formal recognition: 傑出校友 (distinguished alumnus). 傑 alone means 'outstanding person' — a hero or exceptional individual.

examples.chinese: 她是這個世代最傑出的科學家之一。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhège shìdài zuì jiéchū de kēxuéjiā zhī yī.
examples.english: She is one of the most outstanding scientists of this generation.

examples.chinese: 頒獎典禮表揚了各領域的傑出人士。
examples.pinyin: Bānjiǎng diǎnlǐ biǎoyángle gè lǐngyù de jiéchū rénshì.
examples.english: The awards ceremony honored outstanding individuals in various fields.

semanticNote: A crystal (literal) or the beautiful product of concentrated effort/wisdom (figurative). 鹽的結晶 (salt crystal), 智慧的結晶 (crystallization of wisdom), 心血的結晶 (the fruit of one's heart and blood — a labor of love). The figurative sense is very common: this achievement is the 結晶 of years of work. 孩子是愛情的結晶 (a child is the crystallization of love) — a somewhat poetic way to describe a child.

examples.chinese: 這部小說是她二十年心血的結晶。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō shì tā èrshí nián xīnxuè de jiéjīng.
examples.english: This novel is the crystallization of twenty years of her heart and soul.

examples.chinese: 在顯微鏡下，鹽的結晶美得令人驚嘆。
examples.pinyin: Zài xiǎnwēijìng xià, yán de jiéjīng měi de lìng rén jīngtàn.
examples.english: Under the microscope, salt crystals are breathtakingly beautiful.

semanticNote: The final outcome or ending — of a story, event, or situation. 悲劇結局 (tragic ending), 圓滿結局 (happy ending), 事件的結局 (the outcome of the event). More narrative and final than 結果 (result — which can be intermediate). 結局 implies the story is over and the final state has been determined. Very common in film/drama criticism: 這部劇的結局讓人意想不到 (the drama's ending was completely unexpected).

examples.chinese: 這部電影的結局出人意料，讓觀眾大感驚訝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéjú chūrén yìliào, ràng guānzhòng dà gǎn jīngyà.
examples.english: The film's ending was completely unexpected — the audience was stunned.

examples.chinese: 他希望這段關係能有一個圓滿的結局。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīwàng zhè duàn guānxì néng yǒu yī ge yuánmǎn de jiéjú.
examples.english: He hopes this relationship will have a happy ending.

english: settle accounts; close out; final settlement
semanticNote: Settling accounts or closing out a financial transaction — 月末結算 (end-of-month settlement), 結算帳單 (settle the bill), 年度結算 (annual accounting close). Common in finance, business, and restaurant contexts. In restaurants: 結帳 is the everyday word for paying the bill; 結算 is more formal/business. Also used for final tallying: 選票結算 (tabulating votes).

examples.chinese: 月底時，會計部門負責所有帳款的結算工作。
examples.pinyin: Yuèdǐ shí, kuàijì bùmén fùzé suǒyǒu zhàngkuǎn de jiésuàn gōngzuò.
examples.english: At month's end, the accounting department handles the settlement of all accounts.

examples.chinese: 比賽結束後，裁判組開始進行最終結算。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jiéshù hòu, cáipàn zǔ kāishǐ jìnxíng zuìzhōng jiésuàn.
examples.english: After the competition ended, the referee panel began the final tally.

semanticNote: A cut-off point — 報名截止日期 (registration deadline), 截止日為本月底 (the deadline is end of month). Common in applications, registrations, and official announcements. 截止 focuses on the point where something ends/closes — you cannot submit after this point. 截止日期 (deadline) is one of the most useful compounds to know.

examples.chinese: 報名截止日期為本月二十日，請盡快報名。
examples.pinyin: Bàomíng jiézhǐ rìqī wéi běn yuè èrshí rì, qǐng jǐnkuài bàomíng.
examples.english: The registration deadline is the 20th of this month — please register as soon as possible.

examples.chinese: 截止目前，已有超過一千人報名參加。
examples.pinyin: Jiézhǐ mùqián, yǐ yǒu chāoguò yīqiān rén bàomíng cānjiā.
examples.english: As of now, over a thousand people have already registered.

english: up until; as of; by (a specified time)
semanticNote: As of a point in time — 截至昨日 (as of yesterday), 截至目前 (as of now), 截至發稿前 (as of press time). Used to anchor a statistic or fact to a specific moment. Different from 截止 (deadline — when something ends) — 截至 sets a reference time for current data. Common in news writing: 截至今日，確診人數已達… (as of today, confirmed cases have reached…).

components.meaning: cut off; up to; as of

examples.chinese: 截至昨日下午，已有三萬人完成接種。
examples.pinyin: Jiézhì zuórì xiàwǔ, yǐ yǒu sān wàn rén wánchéng jiēzhòng.
examples.english: As of yesterday afternoon, 30,000 people had already completed vaccination.

examples.chinese: 截至發稿前，警方尚未公布嫌疑人身份。
examples.pinyin: Jiézhì fāgǎo qián, jǐngfāng shàngwèi gōngbù xiányírén shēnfèn.
examples.english: As of press time, police had not yet released the suspect's identity.

english: do one's utmost; spare no effort; give everything
semanticNote: Exert every last bit of strength — 竭盡全力去做 (do one's absolute best). 竭 means exhaust completely; 盡 = use up; 全力 = all one's strength. The most emphatic way to say you're giving everything. Used in earnest pledges and inspiring contexts. Similar to 全力以赴 (go all-out) — both are common in motivational and formal pledge language.

examples.chinese: 我們會竭盡全力，把這次比賽發揮到最好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huì jiéjìnquánlì, bǎ zhè cì bǐsài fāhuī dào zuì hǎo.
examples.english: We'll do our absolute best and give our all in this competition.

examples.chinese: 醫護人員竭盡全力救治傷患。
examples.pinyin: Yīhù rényuán jiéjìnquánlì jiùzhì shānghuàn.
examples.english: Medical staff did everything in their power to treat the injured.

semanticNote: To remove or lift a constraint — 解除封鎖 (lift a blockade), 解除合約 (terminate a contract), 解除警報 (all clear / lift an alert), 解除職務 (relieve of duties). Removes something that was holding, restricting, or causing a problem. Taiwan weather: 颱風警報已解除 (the typhoon warning has been lifted) — heard after every major typhoon.

examples.chinese: 颱風已過境，氣象局宣布解除警報。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng yǐ guòjìng, qìxiàngjú xuānbù jiěchú jǐngbào.
examples.english: The typhoon has passed — the Central Weather Bureau has announced the alert is lifted.

examples.chinese: 雙方同意解除合約，和平分手。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng tóngyì jiěchú héyuē, hépíng fēnshǒu.
examples.english: Both parties agreed to terminate the contract and part ways amicably.

semanticNote: Liberation — political, social, or personal freedom from oppression or constraint. 婦女解放 (women's liberation), 解放思想 (liberate thinking/emancipate the mind — a key PRC slogan). Historical: PRC's 解放軍 (People's Liberation Army). Also personal: 從壓力中解放出來 (freed from stress). The word carries strong revolutionary/political associations in mainland Chinese usage; Taiwan uses it more freely in various contexts.

examples.chinese: 女性解放運動爭取了許多重要的社會權利。
examples.pinyin: Nǚxìng jiěfàng yùndòng zhēngqǔle xǔduō zhòngyào de shèhuì quánlì.
examples.english: The women's liberation movement fought for many important social rights.

examples.chinese: 假期讓他從繁重的工作中解放出來。
examples.pinyin: Jiàqī ràng tā cóng fánzhòng de gōngzuò zhōng jiěfàng chūlái.
examples.english: The holiday freed him from the burden of his heavy workload.

english: dismiss; fire; lay off; terminate employment
semanticNote: To fire or dismiss an employee — 被解雇 (get fired), 解雇員工 (dismiss employees). The formal/legal term for terminating employment. More formal than 開除 (fire — can be more immediate/disciplinary) and 炒魷魚 (get fired — slang). In Taiwan labor law: 解雇 requires following specific procedures and often involves severance pay (資遣費).

examples.chinese: 公司因業績不佳，決定解雇部分員工。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yīn yèjī bùjiā, juédìng jiěgù bùfèn yuángōng.
examples.english: Due to poor performance, the company decided to lay off some employees.

examples.chinese: 他因違反公司規定而遭到解雇。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn wéifǎn gōngsī guīdìng ér zāodào jiěgù.
examples.english: He was dismissed for violating company regulations.

semanticNote: To dissect — literally (解剖青蛙 = dissect a frog, 解剖學 = anatomy) or figuratively (解剖社會現象 = dissect/analyze a social phenomenon). The figurative analytical sense is common in Chinese intellectual writing: 解剖一個問題 = cut a problem open and examine it thoroughly. 解剖刀 (scalpel — lit. dissection knife). Medical students study 解剖學 as a core subject.

examples.chinese: 醫學院學生必須學習人體解剖學。
examples.pinyin: Yīxuéyuàn xuéshēng bìxū xuéxí réntǐ jiěpōu xué.
examples.english: Medical school students must study human anatomy.

examples.chinese: 這篇文章深刻地解剖了當代青年的困境。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng shēnkè de jiěpōule dāngdài qīngnián de kùnjìng.
examples.english: This article incisively dissects the predicament of contemporary youth.

semanticNote: To disband or dissolve a group — 解散樂團 (disband a band), 解散議會 (dissolve parliament), 解散公司 (dissolve a company), 解散！(Dismissed! — military command). The group ceases to exist. Different from 分手 (break up — romantic) and 分離 (separate — general). 解散 is always about the formal ending of an organized group or institution. In Taiwan politics: 總統解散國會 (the president dissolves the legislature — constitutional power).

examples.chinese: 樂團在最後一場演唱會後宣告解散。
examples.pinyin: Yuètuán zài zuìhòu yī chǎng yǎnchànghuì hòu xuāngào jiěsàn.
examples.english: The band announced their disbandment after their final concert.

examples.chinese: 訓練結束後，教練宣布：「解散！」
examples.pinyin: Xùnliàn jiéshù hòu, jiàoliàn xuānbù: 「Jiěsàn!」
examples.english: After training ended, the coach announced: "Dismissed!"

english: disintegrate; fall apart; break up (of a state or system)
semanticNote: Disintegration — the complete breakdown of a structure, state, or system. 蘇聯解體 (the dissolution of the Soviet Union — a key historical event), 帝國解體 (the disintegration of an empire). More dramatic and total than 解散 (dissolve — which is an orderly ending) — 解體 implies fragmentation and collapse. Also used for physical disintegration: 結構解體 (structural disintegration).

examples.chinese: 一九九一年，蘇聯正式解體，冷戰宣告結束。
examples.pinyin: Yī jiǔ jiǔ yī nián, Sūlián zhèngshì jiětǐ, lěngzhàn xuāngào jiéshù.
examples.english: In 1991, the Soviet Union officially disintegrated and the Cold War was declared over.

examples.chinese: 如果缺乏信任，任何組織都可能走向解體。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ quēfá xìnrèn, rènhé zǔzhī dōu kěnéng zǒuxiàng jiětǐ.
examples.english: Without trust, any organization can fall apart.

english: be on guard; take precautions; alert
semanticNote: Being on alert and taking precautions — 嚴密戒備 (be on high alert), 戒備森嚴 (heavily guarded), 放下戒備 (lower one's guard). More active and defensive than 警惕 (be vigilant — which is more internal awareness). 戒備 implies concrete defensive measures. In security/military: 戒備狀態 (state of alert). Also emotional: 她對陌生人很戒備 (she's guarded with strangers).

examples.chinese: 活動期間，警方在場館周圍嚴密戒備。
examples.pinyin: Huódòng qījiān, jǐngfāng zài chǎnguǎn zhōuwéi yánmì jièbèi.
examples.english: During the event, police were on high alert around the venue.

examples.chinese: 她對初次見面的人總是很戒備。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì chūcì jiànmiàn de rén zǒng shì hěn jièbèi.
examples.english: She's always guarded with people she meets for the first time.

semanticNote: A boundary or dividing line — 劃清界限 (draw a clear line / set clear boundaries), 公私界限 (the line between public and private), 突破界限 (break through limits). Both literal borders and figurative boundaries (personal, ethical, conceptual). 劃清界限 is very common: with someone undesirable (cut ties clearly) or between concepts (draw a clear distinction). Different from 邊界 (border — geographic) and 限制 (restriction — imposed limit).

examples.chinese: 要與有問題的合作方劃清界限。
examples.pinyin: Yào yǔ yǒu wèntí de hézuò fāng huàqīng jièxiàn.
examples.english: You need to draw a clear line with problematic partners.

examples.chinese: 工作和私生活之間的界限越來越模糊了。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò hé sīshēnghuó zhījiān de jièxiàn yuè lái yuè móhu le.
examples.english: The line between work and private life is getting increasingly blurry.

english: draw lessons from; use as a reference; learn from
semanticNote: To use something as a reference or model to learn from — 借鑒他人的經驗 (draw on others' experience), 借鑒先進技術 (draw on advanced technology), 可以借鑒 (worth referencing/drawing lessons from). The 鑒 character (mirror/appraise) suggests using something as a mirror — seeing yourself reflected in it. Intellectual and formal register. Common in policy, academic, and business contexts.

components.meaning: mirror; appraise; take as a lesson

examples.chinese: 我們可以借鑒其他國家的成功經驗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ jièjiàn qítā guójiā de chénggōng jīngyàn.
examples.english: We can draw lessons from the successful experiences of other countries.

examples.chinese: 歷史是一面鏡子，值得我們深入借鑒。
examples.pinyin: Lìshǐ shì yī miàn jìngzi, zhídé wǒmen shēnrù jièjiàn.
examples.english: History is a mirror — well worth drawing deep lessons from.

english: with the help of; by means of; using
semanticNote: To use something as means or leverage — 借助科技 (with the help of technology), 借助他人的力量 (using the strength of others), 借助機會 (leveraging an opportunity). Always implies using an external resource or tool to accomplish something. More formal than 用 (use) and more specific about the enabling/leveraging function. Very common in formal writing: 借助…手段 (by means of…).

examples.chinese: 借助現代科技，遠距工作成為可能。
examples.pinyin: Jièzhù xiàndài kējì, yuǎnjù gōngzuò chéngwéi kěnéng.
examples.english: With the help of modern technology, remote work has become possible.

examples.chinese: 她借助獎學金完成了大學學業。
examples.pinyin: Tā jièzhù jiǎngxuéjīn wánchéngle dàxué xuéyè.
examples.english: She completed her university studies with the help of a scholarship.

semanticNote: Finance and banking as an industry — 金融市場 (financial market), 金融機構 (financial institution), 金融危機 (financial crisis), 金融科技 (fintech). The core term for the financial industry. 金融業 = the financial sector. Taiwan is a significant financial hub: 台北金融中心 (Taipei financial center). 金融風暴 (financial storm = financial crisis) — used dramatically in news.

examples.chinese: 二○○八年的全球金融危機影響了許多國家。
examples.pinyin: Èr líng líng bā nián de quánqiú jīnróng wēijī yǐngxiǎngle xǔduō guójiā.
examples.english: The 2008 global financial crisis affected many countries.

examples.chinese: 她在金融業工作了十五年，經驗豐富。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jīnróng yè gōngzuòle shíwǔ nián, jīngyàn fēngfù.
examples.english: She has worked in the financial industry for fifteen years with extensive experience.

english: with relish; eagerly; with great interest
semanticNote: Doing something with evident enjoyment and absorption — eating with gusto, reading with fascination. 津津有味地吃 (eat with relish), 津津有味地聽 (listen with rapt attention), 津津有味地讀 (read eagerly). 津津 suggests flowing/abundant (like saliva flowing at something delicious). Always positive — the person is genuinely engaged and enjoying themselves. Versatile: applies to food, conversation, reading, games.

examples.chinese: 爺爺津津有味地講著年輕時的故事。
examples.pinyin: Yéye jīnjīnyǒuwèi de jiǎngzhe niánqīng shí de gùshi.
examples.english: Grandpa told stories from his youth with obvious relish.

examples.chinese: 孩子們津津有味地吃著剛出爐的餅乾。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen jīnjīnyǒuwèi de chīzhe gāng chūlú de bǐnggān.
examples.english: The children ate the freshly baked cookies with great gusto.

semanticNote: Urgent and pressing — 緊迫的任務 (an urgent task), 時間緊迫 (time is pressing), 緊迫感 (sense of urgency). More immediate and pressuring than 緊急 (emergency — which describes actual emergencies). 緊迫 describes the feeling of pressure from a deadline or critical situation. 時間緊迫 is one of the most common expressions — 'time is tight/pressing.' Compare: 緊急會議 (emergency meeting) vs 緊迫的時程 (a pressing timeline).

examples.chinese: 時間緊迫，我們必須立刻做出決定。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān jǐnpò, wǒmen bìxū lìkè zuòchū juédìng.
examples.english: Time is pressing — we must make a decision immediately.

examples.chinese: 氣候危機帶來了緊迫的行動壓力。
examples.pinyin: Qìhòu wēijī dàiláile jǐnpò de xíngdòng yāli.
examples.english: The climate crisis has created urgent pressure to act.

english: add flowers to brocade; make something already excellent even better
semanticNote: Adding beauty to something already beautiful — making a good thing even better. Often contrasted with 雪中送炭 (deliver charcoal in snow = help someone truly in need): 錦上添花易，雪中送炭難 (it's easy to add to abundance, hard to give to those in need). Used to describe bonuses, extra praise, or complementary additions that enhance something already good. Sometimes used slightly cynically about people who only help the successful.

examples.chinese: 這首背景音樂為電影的高潮場景錦上添花。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu bèijǐng yīnyuè wèi diànyǐng de gāocháo chǎngjǐng jǐnshàng tiān huā.
examples.english: This background music added an extra touch of brilliance to the film's climactic scene.

examples.chinese: 他的演講已經很精彩，再加上這個故事真是錦上添花。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjiǎng yǐjīng hěn jīngcǎi, zài jiā shàng zhège gùshi zhēn shì jǐnshàng tiān huā.
examples.english: His speech was already excellent — adding this story made it even more brilliant.

english: and then; what follows next; proceeding to
semanticNote: Formal connective linking a first action to a subsequent one — stronger than 然後, implying logical progression. Common in written Mandarin and formal speech in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 他學好了中文，進而開始研究日文。
examples.pinyin: Tā xué hǎo le zhōngwén, jìn'ér kāishǐ yánjiū rìwén.
examples.english: He mastered Chinese and then began studying Japanese.

examples.chinese: 公司擴大規模，進而進軍國際市場。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī kuòdà guīmó, jìn'ér jìnjūn guójì shìchǎng.
examples.english: The company expanded its scale and then entered the international market.

english: attack; assault; go on the offensive
semanticNote: Military/sports term for launching an offensive. Contrasts with 防守 (defend). In Taiwan sports commentary, used as frequently in basketball and baseball contexts as military ones.

examples.chinese: 敵軍在夜間發動進攻。
examples.pinyin: Díjūn zài yèjiān fādòng jìngōng.
examples.english: The enemy forces launched an attack at night.

examples.chinese: 球隊在最後一節加強進攻，成功逆轉。
examples.pinyin: Qiúduì zài zuìhòu yī jié jiāqiáng jìngōng, chénggōng nìzhuǎn.
examples.english: The team intensified their offense in the final quarter and successfully turned the game around.

semanticNote: The standard scientific term for biological evolution (達爾文進化論). Distinct from 演化, which is also used in academic contexts. Taiwan biology curricula use both terms.

examples.chinese: 人類是從靈長類動物進化而來的。
examples.pinyin: Rénlèi shì cóng língzhǎng lèi dòngwù jìnhuà ér lái de.
examples.english: Humans evolved from primates.

examples.chinese: 物種的進化需要數百萬年。
examples.pinyin: Wùzhǒng de jìnhuà xūyào shù bǎiwàn nián.
examples.english: The evolution of a species takes millions of years.

semanticNote: Used to describe measurable forward movement in a project, negotiation, or situation. 有進展 (making progress) and 沒有進展 (no progress) are common patterns. More neutral than 突破 (breakthrough).

examples.chinese: 談判有了新的進展。
examples.pinyin: Tánpàn yǒu le xīn de jìnzhǎn.
examples.english: The negotiations have made new progress.

examples.chinese: 工程進展順利，預計提前完工。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchéng jìnzhǎn shùnlì, yùjì tíqián wán gōng.
examples.english: The project is progressing smoothly and is expected to finish ahead of schedule.

semanticNote: Refers to a recent, unspecified period of time — more vague than 最近. Common in written formal contexts and polite conversation: 近來還好嗎？(How have you been lately?). Slightly more formal register than 最近.

examples.chinese: 近來工作繁忙，沒有時間休息。
examples.pinyin: Jìnlái gōngzuò fánmáng, méiyǒu shíjiān xiūxi.
examples.english: Lately I've been swamped with work and haven't had time to rest.

examples.chinese: 近來天氣忽冷忽熱，要注意保暖。
examples.pinyin: Jìnlái tiānqì hū lěng hū rè, yào zhùyì bǎonuǎn.
examples.english: The weather has been erratic lately — take care to keep warm.

english: to be promoted to a higher position; promotion
semanticNote: Formal term for career promotion, typically within a hierarchy. More formal than 升職. Used in official announcements, HR contexts, and military rank changes. The 晉 character implies advancement through ranks.

examples.chinese: 他因表現優異而晉升為部門主管。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn biǎoxiàn yōuyì ér jìnshēng wéi bùmén zhǔguǎn.
examples.english: He was promoted to department head for his outstanding performance.

examples.chinese: 晉升後她承擔了更多的責任。
examples.pinyin: Jìnshēng hòu tā chéngdān le gèng duō de zérèn.
examples.english: After her promotion, she took on greater responsibilities.

english: to soak; to steep; to immerse
semanticNote: Describes prolonged immersion in liquid — soaking beans, marinating meat, steeping tea, or soaking feet. Common in cooking and home remedy contexts. Contrasts with 泡 (shorter/casual) — 浸泡 implies a deliberate, sustained process.

examples.chinese: 乾豆需要提前浸泡幾個小時。
examples.pinyin: Gān dòu xūyào tíqián jìnpào jǐ gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: Dried beans need to be soaked for several hours in advance.

examples.chinese: 她每晚用熱水浸泡雙腳以緩解疲勞。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi wǎn yòng rèshuǐ jìnpào shuāngjiǎo yǐ huǎnjiě píláo.
examples.english: She soaks her feet in hot water every night to relieve fatigue.

semanticNote: Botanical term for the stem or stalk of a plant. Used in biology, cooking, and gardening contexts. Taiwan biology textbooks use 莖 consistently. Note the traditional 莖 is more complex than the simplified 茎.

components.meaning: stem; stalk (grass radical 艹 + 巠)

examples.chinese: 玫瑰花的莖上長著刺。
examples.pinyin: Méiguì huā de jīng shàng zhǎng zhe cì.
examples.english: Rose stems have thorns on them.

examples.chinese: 竹子的莖非常堅硬。
examples.pinyin: Zhúzi de jīng fēicháng jiānyìng.
examples.english: The stem of bamboo is extremely hard.

semanticNote: Refers to allocated operational funds for institutions, programs, or government bodies — not personal expenses. 研究經費 (research funding), 教育經費 (education budget). More formal than 費用 or 錢.

examples.chinese: 這個研究計畫的經費不足。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yánjiū jìhuà de jīngfèi bùzú.
examples.english: This research project is underfunded.

examples.chinese: 政府增加了教育經費的撥款。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zēngjiā le jiàoyù jīngfèi de bōkuǎn.
examples.english: The government increased the allocation of education funds.

english: longitude and latitude; warp and woof; the ins and outs; main points
semanticNote: Literally 'longitude and latitude' (經度＋緯度), but metaphorically means 'the full picture' or 'all the details' of a complex matter. 說清楚事情的來龍去脈和經緯 means to lay out all the details of an event clearly.

examples.chinese: 他詳細說明了這件事的來龍去脈和經緯。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiángxì shuōmíng le zhè jiàn shì de láilóng-qùmài hé jīngwěi.
examples.english: He explained the full story and all the details of the matter.

examples.chinese: 地圖上標示了經緯座標。
examples.pinyin: Dìtú shàng biāoshì le jīngwěi zuòbiāo.
examples.english: The map shows longitude and latitude coordinates.

english: to alarm; to startle; to disturb; to alert
semanticNote: Implies unwanted disturbance or causing someone alarm, often used in polite apology: 驚動您了，真不好意思 (Sorry for the disturbance/trouble). Also used for alerting authorities or causing a commotion.

examples.chinese: 那聲巨響驚動了整棟樓的居民。
examples.pinyin: Nà shēng jùxiǎng jīngdòng le zhěng dòng lóu de jūmín.
examples.english: That loud noise startled all the residents in the building.

examples.chinese: 案子驚動了上級，引起高度關注。
examples.pinyin: Ànzi jīngdòng le shàngjí, yǐnqǐ gāodù guānzhù.
examples.english: The case alarmed upper management and drew high-level attention.

english: to be amazed; astonished; filled with wonder
semanticNote: Describes a sense of wonder at something unexpected or remarkable. Slightly more positive than 驚訝 (which can be neutral or negative surprise). 感到驚奇 (feel amazed) is a common pattern.

examples.chinese: 他對孩子的繪畫天分感到驚奇。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì háizi de huìhuà tiānfèn gǎndào jīngqí.
examples.english: He was amazed by the child's talent for drawing.

examples.chinese: 遊客對古廟的壯觀景象驚奇不已。
examples.pinyin: Yóukè duì gǔ miào de zhuàngguān jǐngxiàng jīngqí bù yǐ.
examples.english: Tourists were filled with wonder at the magnificent sight of the ancient temple.

semanticNote: The most neutral and common term for surprise/astonishment — can be positive or negative. Compare: 驚奇 (amazed with wonder), 震驚 (deeply shocked, often negative). 令人驚訝 (surprising, astonishing) is a frequent written pattern.

examples.chinese: 她聽到這個消息時非常驚訝。
examples.pinyin: Tā tīngdào zhège xiāoxi shí fēicháng jīngyà.
examples.english: She was very surprised when she heard the news.

examples.chinese: 他的進步速度令老師感到驚訝。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jìnbù sùdù lìng lǎoshī gǎndào jīngyà.
examples.english: His rate of improvement astonished his teachers.

english: cautious and conscientious; diligent and meticulous
semanticNote: Four-character idiom (成語) describing someone who works with great care and dedication, always alert and responsible. Commonly used to praise employees or officials. The reduplication of 兢兢 emphasizes the carefulness.

examples.chinese: 他兢兢業業地工作了三十年，從未出過差錯。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngjīng-yèyè de gōngzuò le sānshí nián, cóng wèi chūguò chācuò.
examples.english: He worked conscientiously for thirty years without ever making a mistake.

examples.chinese: 她兢兢業業的態度深受同事尊重。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngjīng-yèyè de tàidù shēn shòu tóngshì zūnzhòng.
examples.english: Her diligent and meticulous attitude earned deep respect from colleagues.

english: careful calculation; meticulous budgeting; penny-wise planning
semanticNote: Four-character idiom describing careful, detailed financial or resource planning. Not necessarily negative — can simply mean being thrifty and smart about resources. Common in business contexts and discussions of household budgeting.

examples.chinese: 這個家庭靠精打細算，存下了一筆積蓄。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiātíng kào jīng-dǎ-xì-suàn, cún xià le yī bǐ jīxù.
examples.english: Through careful budgeting, this family managed to save up a tidy sum.

examples.chinese: 創業初期要精打細算，控制每一筆開支。
examples.pinyin: Chuàngyè chūqī yào jīng-dǎ-xì-suàn, kòngzhì měi yī bǐ kāizhī.
examples.english: In the early stages of starting a business, you need meticulous planning and control over every expense.

english: essence; quintessence; the best part; cream of the crop
semanticNote: Refers to the most refined, valuable essence of something — a culture, a text, a technique. Common in formal praise: 文化精華 (cultural essence), 藝術精華 (the finest of art). Also used in cosmetics: 精華液 (serum/essence).

examples.chinese: 這本書匯集了中國古典哲學的精華。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū huìjí le zhōngguó gǔdiǎn zhéxué de jīnghuá.
examples.english: This book gathers the essence of classical Chinese philosophy.

examples.chinese: 博物館展出了該地區文化精華。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn zhǎnchū le gāi dìqū wénhuà jīnghuá.
examples.english: The museum displays the cultural quintessence of the region.

english: to simplify; to streamline; to cut down; concise
semanticNote: Used in organizational, administrative, and editorial contexts — streamlining staff (精簡人員), simplifying procedures (精簡程序), or cutting an essay down. Implies purposeful reduction to improve quality or efficiency.

examples.chinese: 公司決定精簡組織架構，提高效率。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng jīngjiǎn zǔzhī jiàgòu, tígāo xiàolǜ.
examples.english: The company decided to streamline its organizational structure to improve efficiency.

examples.chinese: 請將報告精簡至兩頁以內。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiāng bàogào jīngjiǎn zhì liǎng yè yǐnèi.
examples.english: Please condense the report to within two pages.

semanticNote: Used for instruments, manufacturing, and technical work requiring high accuracy. 精密儀器 (precision instruments), 精密工業 (precision industry) — a major sector in Taiwan's economy. Implies both accuracy and intricacy.

examples.chinese: 臺灣的精密機械工業享譽全球。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de jīngmì jīxiè gōngyè xiǎngyù quánqiú.
examples.english: Taiwan's precision machinery industry is renowned worldwide.

examples.chinese: 手術需要精密的設備和技術。
examples.pinyin: Shǒushù xūyào jīngmì de shèbèi hé jìshù.
examples.english: Surgery requires precise equipment and techniques.

semanticNote: Emphasizes exactness and correctness of measurement or expression. Slightly more formal than 準確. 精確度 (precision/accuracy) is a common compound. Used heavily in scientific, military, and technical writing.

examples.chinese: 數據必須精確才能得出正確的結論。
examples.pinyin: Shùjù bìxū jīngquè cái néng déchū zhèngquè de jiélùn.
examples.english: Data must be precise to reach correct conclusions.

examples.chinese: 她精確地計算出了所需的材料用量。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngquè de jìsuàn chū le suǒ xū de cáiliào yòngliàng.
examples.english: She calculated the required materials with precision.

english: to be proficient in; to have mastery of; expert command
semanticNote: Indicates deep, expert-level mastery — stronger than 熟悉 (familiar with) or 會 (can). 精通多國語言 (fluent in multiple languages), 精通武術 (master of martial arts). Sets a high bar — don't use loosely.

examples.chinese: 她精通英、日、法三國語言。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngtōng yīng, rì, fǎ sān guó yǔyán.
examples.english: She is proficient in English, Japanese, and French.

examples.chinese: 他精通古典音樂，尤其擅長鋼琴。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngtōng gǔdiǎn yīnyuè, yóuqí shàncháng gāngqín.
examples.english: He has mastery of classical music, especially the piano.

semanticNote: Describes actions done with careful, loving attention to detail — 精心準備 (carefully prepared), 精心設計 (meticulously designed). Implies effort and dedication, often with a positive connotation of craftsmanship or care.

examples.chinese: 她精心布置了婚禮現場。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngxīn bùzhì le hūnlǐ xiànchǎng.
examples.english: She meticulously decorated the wedding venue.

examples.chinese: 廚師精心烹製了這道菜。
examples.pinyin: Chúshī jīngxīn pēngzhì le zhè dào cài.
examples.english: The chef prepared this dish with great care.

english: constantly improving; striving for excellence; never satisfied with good enough
semanticNote: Four-character idiom meaning to seek even greater excellence from an already excellent state. Common in praise of craftsmen, artists, athletes, and companies. Captures the kaizen/continuous improvement philosophy popular in Taiwan's manufacturing culture.

examples.chinese: 這位工匠精益求精，幾十年如一日。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gōngjiàng jīng-yì-qiú-jīng, jǐ shí nián rú yī rì.
examples.english: This craftsman has been constantly striving for perfection for decades.

examples.chinese: 公司文化鼓勵員工精益求精，不斷創新。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī wénhuà gǔlì yuángōng jīng-yì-qiú-jīng, búduàn chuàngxīn.
examples.english: The company culture encourages employees to continually improve and innovate.

semanticNote: Describes objects of fine craftsmanship — jewelry, food presentation, architecture, gifts. Frequently used in Taiwan retail and tourism to describe quality goods. 精緻餐飲 (fine dining), 精緻伴手禮 (exquisite gifts). Note: in Taiwan, 緻 is preferred over simplified 致.

examples.chinese: 這套茶具做工精致，令人愛不釋手。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào chájù zuògōng jīngzhì, lìng rén ài bù shì shǒu.
examples.english: This tea set is exquisitely crafted — you can't put it down.

examples.chinese: 她的妝容精致，一絲不苟。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhuāngrōng jīngzhì, yī sī bù gǒu.
examples.english: Her makeup was flawless and meticulous.

semanticNote: The character 井 is also used as a shape descriptor (井字形, tic-tac-toe grid shape). In set phrases: 井井有條 (neat and orderly), 井水不犯河水 (mind your own business — lit. 'well water doesn't intrude on river water').

examples.chinese: 村裡的老井已經乾涸了。
examples.pinyin: Cūn lǐ de lǎo jǐng yǐjīng gānhé le.
examples.english: The old well in the village has dried up.

examples.chinese: 她把辦公室整理得井井有條。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ bàngōngshì zhěnglǐ de jǐngjǐng-yǒutiáo.
examples.english: She kept the office neat and orderly.

english: cervical vertebra; the cervical spine (neck vertebrae)
semanticNote: Medical/anatomical term for the seven cervical vertebrae in the neck. 頸椎病 (cervical spondylosis) is a common complaint associated with excessive phone/computer use — very frequently discussed in Taiwan health contexts.

examples.chinese: 長期低頭滑手機容易造成頸椎問題。
examples.pinyin: Chángqī dītóu huá shǒujī róngyì zàochéng jǐngzhuī wèntí.
examples.english: Frequently looking down at your phone can easily cause cervical spine problems.

examples.chinese: 她因頸椎不適去做了復健治療。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn jǐngzhuī bùshì qù zuò le fùjiàn zhìliáo.
examples.english: She went for rehabilitation treatment due to cervical spine discomfort.

english: to warn; to caution; a warning
semanticNote: A direct, official warning — stronger than 提醒 (remind). Used in legal, disciplinary, weather, and safety contexts. 黃色警告 (yellow warning), 最後警告 (final warning). Carries authority and formality.

examples.chinese: 氣象局發出颱風警告。
examples.pinyin: Qìxiàngjú fā chū táifēng jǐnggào.
examples.english: The meteorological bureau issued a typhoon warning.

examples.chinese: 他被公司正式警告，若再犯將予以解雇。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi gōngsī zhèngshì jǐnggào, ruò zài fàn jiāng yǔyǐ jiěgù.
examples.english: He received an official warning from the company that he would be fired if he violated again.

english: to be vigilant; alert; on guard; wary
semanticNote: Describes an active state of alertness against potential threats or risks. 提高警惕 (heighten vigilance) and 保持警惕 (remain on guard) are stock phrases in political speeches, safety briefings, and security contexts.

examples.chinese: 旅遊時要對扒竊保持警惕。
examples.pinyin: Lǚyóu shí yào duì páqiè bǎochí jǐngtì.
examples.english: When traveling, stay alert against pickpockets.

examples.chinese: 面對網路詐騙，民眾應提高警惕。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì wǎnglù zhàpiàn, mínzhòng yīng tígāo jǐngtì.
examples.english: The public should heighten their vigilance against online scams.

semanticNote: Formal term for organized competitions — academic (數學競賽), athletic (體育競賽), or professional. More formal and comprehensive than 比賽, which is used for a single game/match. 競賽 implies a series or official context.

examples.chinese: 她在全國數學競賽中獲得第一名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài quánguó shùxué jìngsài zhōng huòdé dì yī míng.
examples.english: She won first place in the national mathematics competition.

examples.chinese: 這場競賽吸引了來自各地的高手參與。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng jìngsài xīyǐn le láizì gè dì de gāoshǒu cānyù.
examples.english: This competition attracted top contenders from across the country.

english: to run for election; to campaign for office
semanticNote: The standard term for electoral campaigning in Taiwan's vibrant democratic context. 競選總統 (run for president), 競選活動 (campaign activities). Given Taiwan's active democracy, this is a word with high real-world frequency.

examples.chinese: 他宣布將競選市長。
examples.pinyin: Tā xuānbù jiāng jìngxuǎn shìzhǎng.
examples.english: He announced that he will run for mayor.

examples.chinese: 競選期間，候選人展開激烈辯論。
examples.pinyin: Jìngxuǎn qījiān, hòuxuǎnrén zhǎnkāi jīliè biànlùn.
examples.english: During the campaign, the candidates engaged in fierce debates.

english: to salute; to pay respects; best regards
semanticNote: In military/formal contexts, means to salute. At the end of formal letters, 敬禮 is a polite closing phrase meaning 'respectfully yours' or 'best regards' — equivalent to 謹上. Common in Taiwan formal correspondence.

examples.chinese: 士兵向長官敬禮。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīng xiàng zhǎngguān jìnglǐ.
examples.english: The soldier saluted the officer.

examples.chinese: 信末寫著「謹此敬禮」。
examples.pinyin: Xìn mò xiě zhe "jǐn cǐ jìnglǐ".
examples.english: The letter ended with 'respectfully yours.'

english: dedicated to one's work; work ethic; professionalism
semanticNote: Describes someone who takes their work seriously and gives it their full dedication. 敬業精神 (professional spirit/work ethic) is a key phrase in job evaluations and character references in Taiwan. Contrasts with 不負責任 (irresponsible).

examples.chinese: 她的敬業精神令所有同事佩服。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jìngyè jīngshén lìng suǒyǒu tóngshì pèifú.
examples.english: Her work ethic earns the admiration of all her colleagues.

examples.chinese: 他是位非常敬業的醫生，從不隨便對待病患。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wèi fēicháng jìngyè de yīshēng, cóng bù suíbiàn duìdài bìnghuàn.
examples.english: He is a very dedicated doctor who never takes his patients lightly.

semanticNote: Can refer to a physical boundary, but more commonly denotes a level or realm of achievement, consciousness, or artistry. 達到更高的境界 (reach a higher level). Used in philosophy, art criticism, and self-cultivation discussions in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 他的書法已達到爐火純青的境界。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shūfǎ yǐ dádào lúhuǒ-chúnqīng de jìngjiè.
examples.english: His calligraphy has reached a state of consummate mastery.

examples.chinese: 禪修幫助人達到內心平靜的境界。
examples.pinyin: Chánxiū bāngzhù rén dádào nèixīn píngjìng de jìngjiè.
examples.english: Zen meditation helps people attain a state of inner peace.

english: camera shot; camera lens; scene (in a film)
semanticNote: Dual meaning: the physical camera lens (鏡頭品質 = lens quality) and a film/TV scene or shot (特寫鏡頭 = close-up shot). Common in Taiwan's active film and media industries. 搶鏡頭 means to steal the spotlight.

examples.chinese: 導演喊停，重新拍攝這個鏡頭。
