semanticNote: The origin or source of something — news, funding, water, ideas. 消息來源 (news source), 資金來源 (source of funding), 追溯來源 (trace back to the source). Neutral and factual — simply identifies where something comes from. Common in journalism, research, and academic writing.

examples.chinese: 這條消息的來源不明，請謹慎對待。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiāoxi de láiyuán bùmíng, qǐng jǐnshèn duìdài.
examples.english: The source of this news is unclear — please treat it with caution.

examples.chinese: 政府正調查這筆資金的來源是否合法。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèng diàochá zhè bǐ zījīn de láiyuán shìfǒu héfǎ.
examples.english: The government is investigating whether the source of these funds is legitimate.

semanticNote: A recurring section or column in print media, or a program segment on TV/radio. 新聞欄目 (news segment), 專題欄目 (special feature column/segment), 體育欄目 (sports column). In digital contexts, also used for a navigation section or menu column on a website.

examples.chinese: 這份報紙有一個每週固定的財經欄目，很受讀者歡迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàozhǐ yǒu yī gè měizhōu gùdìng de cáijīng lánmù, hěn shòu dúzhě huānyíng.
examples.english: This newspaper has a fixed weekly financial column that is very popular with readers.

examples.chinese: 電視台新設了一個美食欄目，帶觀眾探訪全臺各地小吃。
examples.pinyin: Diànshìtái xīn shè le yī gè měishí lánmù, dài guānzhòng tànfǎng quán Tái gèdì xiǎochī.
examples.english: The TV station launched a new food segment, taking viewers to explore local street food across Taiwan.

semanticNote: Habitually unwilling to work or exert effort. 懶惰成性 (lazy by nature), 懶惰的人 (a lazy person). A character judgment — stronger than 懶 alone. The double-character form emphasizes laziness as a stable trait rather than momentary reluctance. Contrasts with 勤勞 (hardworking, industrious).

examples.chinese: 他因為懶惰，總是把事情拖到最後一刻才做。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi lǎnduò, zǒng shì bā shìqíng tuō dào zuìhòu yī kè cái zuò.
examples.english: Because he's lazy, he always puts things off until the very last moment.

examples.chinese: 父母擔心孩子在暑假期間變得懶惰，特別幫他安排了課外活動。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ dānxīn háizi zài shǔjià qījiān biàn de lǎnduò, tèbié bāng tā ānpái le kèwài huódòng.
examples.english: The parents worried their child would become lazy during summer break, so they arranged extracurricular activities for him.

english: in a difficult position or situation; in a tight corner; scoundrel! (derogatory)
semanticNote: In a sorry, embarrassed, or disheveled state. 狼狽不堪 (in a completely sorry state), 落得狼狽 (ended up in an embarrassing mess). Also appears in the idiom 狼狽為奸 (collude to do evil). The standalone adj sense — flustered, bedraggled, in a sorry state — is the most common everyday usage.

components.meaning: a legendary creature (helpless without the wolf); distressed

examples.chinese: 他在演講時忘詞，台上顯得相當狼狽。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yǎnjiǎng shí wàng cí, táishàng xiǎnde xiāngdāng lángbèi.
examples.english: He forgot his lines during the speech and looked quite flustered on stage.

examples.chinese: 颱風後，她渾身濕透，狼狽地跑進屋內。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng hòu, tā húnshēn shītòu, lángbèi de pǎo jìn wūnèi.
examples.english: After the typhoon, she was soaked to the bone and stumbled into the house in a sorry state.

english: wolf down one's food (idiom); gorge oneself
semanticNote: To eat ravenously and without manners — like a wolf swallowing and a tiger gulping. Used to describe someone eating as if starving. Vivid and slightly humorous. Register: informal/colloquial. Not used in formal contexts.

examples.chinese: 孩子跑回家後，狼吞虎咽地把整碗飯吃光了。
examples.pinyin: Háizi pǎo huí jiā hòu, lángtūn-hǔyàn de bǎ zhěng wǎn fàn chī guāng le.
examples.english: After running home, the child wolfed down the entire bowl of rice.

examples.chinese: 他連午餐都沒吃，回到家後便狼吞虎咽，一下子吃了兩個便當。
examples.pinyin: Tā lián wǔcān dōu méi chī, huí dào jiā hòu biàn lángtūn-hǔyàn, yīxiàzi chī le liǎng gè biàndāng.
examples.english: He hadn't even eaten lunch, so when he got home he wolfed down two lunch boxes in no time.

semanticNote: To scoop, fish, or dredge something up from liquid. 撈魚 (catch fish), 撈起 (fish up/retrieve). Extended meaning: exploit a situation for personal gain — 撈好處 (grab benefits), 撈一筆 (make a quick profit). Also: 撈不著 (fail to get anything — an idiom of futility).

components.meaning: dredge up; scoop; fish out (手 radical: hand action)

examples.chinese: 他用漁網在溪中撈起了幾條小魚。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng yúwǎng zài xī zhōng lāo qǐ le jǐ tiáo xiǎoyú.
examples.english: He scooped up a few small fish from the stream with a fishing net.

examples.chinese: 批評者認為他趁機大撈一筆，毫無廉恥之心。
examples.pinyin: Pīpíng zhě rènwéi tā chènjī dà lāo yī bǐ, háowú liánchǐ zhī xīn.
examples.english: Critics felt he seized the opportunity to make a quick profit without a shred of shame.

semanticNote: Solidly built or firmly established — not easy to break, loosen, or shake. 牢固的基礎 (a solid foundation), 連接牢固 (securely fastened). Applies to physical structures and abstract things like relationships, knowledge, and beliefs. Implies both strength and permanence.

examples.chinese: 施工隊確認橋梁的支柱非常牢固，才開放通車。
examples.pinyin: Shīgōng duì quèrèn qiáoliáng de zhīzhù fēicháng láogù, cái kāifàng tōngchē.
examples.english: The construction crew confirmed the bridge's supports were very solid before opening it to traffic.

examples.chinese: 從小培養的語言習慣往往比成年後學的更加牢固。
examples.pinyin: Cóng xiǎo péiyǎng de yǔyán xíguàn wǎngwǎng bǐ chéngnián hòu xué de gèngjiā láogù.
examples.english: Language habits formed from childhood tend to be more firmly ingrained than those learned in adulthood.

semanticNote: Petty, ongoing grumbles and grievances. 發牢騷 (to gripe/complain), 滿腹牢騷 (full of grievances). Implies the complaints may be valid but are expressed in a nagging, repetitive way. More colloquial than 抱怨 and carries a slightly dismissive connotation.

components.meaning: restless; disturb; agitated; 離騷 (lit. of Qu Yuan)

examples.chinese: 他對新政策滿腹牢騷，卻又不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì xīn zhèngcè mǎnfù láosāo, què yòu bù zhīdào gāi zěnme bàn.
examples.english: He was full of complaints about the new policy but had no idea what to do about it.

examples.chinese: 與其發牢騷，不如想辦法解決問題。
examples.pinyin: Yǔqí fā láosāo, bùrú xiǎng bànfǎ jiějué wèntí.
examples.english: Instead of grumbling, it's better to find a way to solve the problem.

english: be talkative (especially about trivial matters); be garrulous; prattle
semanticNote: To nag or ramble on repetitively about the same things. 媽媽很嘮叨 (Mom is always nagging). Implies repetition beyond necessity. More affectionate or resigned than hostile — the classic way to describe a nagging parent. Can also function as a noun: 那些嘮叨 (all that nagging).

examples.chinese: 媽媽每天嘮叨叫他早點睡，他卻置之不理。
examples.pinyin: Māma měitiān láodao jiào tā zǎo diǎn shuì, tā què zhì zhī bù lǐ.
examples.english: His mom nagged him every day to go to bed earlier, but he paid no attention.

examples.chinese: 他雖然嘮叨，但說的都是真心話，值得聽進去。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán láodao, dàn shuō de dōu shì zhēnxīnhuà, zhídé tīng jìnqù.
examples.english: Despite all the nagging, everything he said came from the heart and was worth listening to.

semanticNote: The pleasure or enjoyment derived from an activity — implies active engagement. 生活的樂趣 (the joys of life), 找到樂趣 (find enjoyment), 學習的樂趣 (the pleasure of learning). More specific and concrete than 快樂 (general happiness). Common in lifestyle, hobby, and education contexts.

examples.chinese: 攝影讓他找到了生活中的樂趣，每個週末都出去拍照。
examples.pinyin: Shèyǐng ràng tā zhǎodào le shēnghuó zhōng de lèqù, měi gè zhōumò dōu chūqù pāizhào.
examples.english: Photography gave him pleasure in life — he went out to shoot photos every weekend.

examples.chinese: 孩子們在沙灘上玩耍，盡情享受假期的樂趣。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng wánshuǎ, jìnqíng xiǎngshòu jiàqī de lèqù.
examples.english: The children played on the beach, enjoying every bit of the fun the holiday had to offer.

english: be happy/willing do something; content; satisfied
semanticNote: Willing and genuinely happy to do something — not grudging. 我很樂意幫你 (I'm happy to help you), 不樂意 (unwilling/unhappy about it). Contrasts with 願意 (willing, but neutral — doesn't imply happiness). More warm and positive in register.

examples.chinese: 他非常樂意為社區服務，從不計較報酬。
examples.pinyin: Tā fēicháng lèyì wèi shèqū fúwù, cóng bù jìjiào bàochou.
examples.english: He was genuinely happy to serve the community and never cared about compensation.

examples.chinese: 她說，只要對學生有幫助，她都樂意額外付出時間。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō, zhǐyào duì xuéshēng yǒu bāngzhù, tā dōu lèyì éwài fūchū shíjiān.
examples.english: She said that as long as it helps the students, she's happy to put in the extra time.

semanticNote: Radar — a phonetic loanword from English. 雷達偵測 (radar detection), 雷達系統 (radar system). Also used figuratively for sharp perception: 她的媽媽雷達很強 (her mom has a really sharp radar — is very perceptive). Common in military, aviation, and meteorology.

examples.chinese: 颱風來臨前，氣象局的雷達偵測到了強烈的風眼結構。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng láilín qián, qìxiàngjú de léidá zhēncè dào le qiángliè de fēngyǎn jiégòu.
examples.english: Before the typhoon arrived, the meteorological bureau's radar detected a strong eye structure.

examples.chinese: 這架戰機配備了最先進的雷達系統，能同時追蹤多個目標。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jià zhànjī pèibèi le zuì xiānjìn de léidá xìtǒng, néng tóngshí zhuīzōng duō gè mùbiāo.
examples.english: This fighter jet is equipped with the most advanced radar system, capable of tracking multiple targets simultaneously.

semanticNote: Similar to or resembling something in nature or structure. 類似的情況 (similar situation), 類似的案例 (analogous cases), 與…類似 (similar to…). More precise and analytical-sounding than 相似 — often used in legal, scientific, and comparative contexts.

examples.chinese: 法院指出，本案與去年的類似判例相符，因此適用同一原則。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn zhǐchū, běn àn yǔ qùnián de lèisì pànlì xiāngfú, yīncǐ shìyòng tóngyī yuánzé.
examples.english: The court noted that this case matched a similar precedent from last year and therefore applied the same principle.

examples.chinese: 他們兩人的個性類似，相處起來非常融洽。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎng rén de gèxìng lèisì, xiāngchǔ qǐlái fēicháng rónqià.
examples.english: The two of them have similar personalities and get along very well.

semanticNote: Cold-hearted and merciless — lacking empathy or warmth. 冷酷無情 (cold and merciless), 冷酷的現實 (the cold, hard reality). Stronger than 冷漠 (indifferent) — implies active harshness, not just passivity. Common in literary and journalistic contexts.

examples.chinese: 他雖然外表冷酷，但內心其實非常重視家人。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán wàibiǎo lěngkù, dàn nèixīn qíshí fēicháng zhòngshì jiārén.
examples.english: Despite his cold exterior, he actually cares deeply about his family.

examples.chinese: 資本主義的競爭有時顯得相當冷酷，弱者往往無從立足。
examples.pinyin: Zīběn zhǔyì de jìngzhēng yǒushí xiǎnde xiāngdāng lěngkù, ruòzhě wǎngwǎng wúcóng lìzú.
examples.english: Capitalist competition can sometimes seem quite ruthless — the weak often have no footing.

english: to treat somebody coldy; to snub; desolate; to give the cold shoulder
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) to give someone the cold shoulder, treat them coldly — 冷落朋友 (snub a friend); (2) (of a place) deserted, desolate — 門庭冷落 (a neglected doorstep). More intentional than 忽略 (overlook). Register: neutral to slightly literary.

components.meaning: fall; drop; left out; left behind

examples.chinese: 她在聚會上被朋友冷落，一個人坐在角落裡。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jùhuì shàng bèi péngyǒu lěngluò, yī gè rén zuò zài jiǎoluò lǐ.
examples.english: She was left out by her friends at the party and sat alone in the corner.

examples.chinese: 節慶過後，原本熱鬧的夜市漸漸冷落下來。
examples.pinyin: Jiéqìng guòhòu, yuánběn rènào de yèshì jiànjiàn lěngluò xiàlái.
examples.english: After the festival, the once-lively night market gradually became deserted.

semanticNote: To reduce temperature through cooling. 冷卻系統 (cooling system), 冷卻水 (cooling water). Extended: cool down enthusiasm, relations, or a heated situation — 熱情冷卻 (enthusiasm waned), 讓情緒冷卻 (let emotions cool down). Common in engineering, food science, and figurative contexts.

examples.chinese: 鋼鐵在高溫塑形後需要冷卻，才能定型。
examples.pinyin: Gāngtiě zài gāowēn sùxíng hòu xūyào lěngquè, cái néng dìngxíng.
examples.english: Steel must be cooled after being shaped at high temperature to set its form.

examples.chinese: 兩國關係因外交摩擦而逐漸冷卻。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó guānxi yīn wàijiāo mócā ér zhújiàn lěngquè.
examples.english: Relations between the two countries gradually cooled due to diplomatic friction.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) to be stunned or dazed — 愣住了 (froze; was stunned), 發愣 (space out; stare blankly); (2) spoken: reckless or blunt — 愣頭愣腦 (impetuous, reckless). The stupefied sense is most common. 愣了一下 (paused/froze for a moment) — very common in narrative fiction.

components.meaning: stunned; dazed; blunt; reckless (忄 heart radical)

examples.chinese: 聽到這個消息，她愣了一下，不知道該說什麼。
examples.pinyin: Tīng dào zhège xiāoxi, tā lèng le yīxià, bù zhīdào gāi shuō shénme.
examples.english: Hearing the news, she froze for a moment, not knowing what to say.

examples.chinese: 他站在門口發愣，不知道要進去還是離開。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài ménkǒu fā lèng, bù zhīdào yào jìnqù háishì líkāi.
examples.english: He stood at the door in a daze, unsure whether to go in or leave.

semanticNote: The moment of first light before sunrise. 黎明前的黑暗 (the darkness before dawn — a common metaphor for hardship preceding breakthrough). More literary and evocative than 早上 or 清晨. Common in poetry, political rhetoric, and literary prose.

examples.chinese: 他們趕在黎明前出發，穿越了整片森林。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gǎn zài límíng qián chūfā, chuānyuè le zhěng piàn sēnlín.
examples.english: They set off before dawn and crossed the entire forest.

examples.chinese: 革命的黎明終於到來，壓迫者的時代結束了。
examples.pinyin: Gémìng de límíng zhōngyú dào lái, yāpò zhě de shídài jiéshù le.
examples.english: The dawn of revolution finally arrived — the era of oppressors had ended.

semanticNote: Proper formal conduct and etiquette in social or ceremonial contexts. 注重禮節 (observe etiquette), 外交禮節 (diplomatic protocol). More formal and context-specific than 禮貌 (everyday politeness). Common in formal, diplomatic, and traditional settings.

examples.chinese: 外交場合講究禮節，每一個細節都代表著國家形象。
examples.pinyin: Wàijiāo chǎnghé jiǎngjiū lǐjié, měi yī gè xìjié dōu dàibiǎozhe guójiā xíngxiàng.
examples.english: Diplomatic occasions demand strict etiquette — every detail represents the country's image.

examples.chinese: 長輩來訪時，她總是格外注重禮節，讓對方感到受尊重。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎngbèi lái fǎng shí, tā zǒng shì géwài zhùzhòng lǐjié, ràng duìfāng gǎndào shòu zūnzhòng.
examples.english: When elders came to visit, she was always especially mindful of etiquette, making them feel respected.

semanticNote: Lit. 'propriety values going and coming' — courtesy is mutual. When others show you courtesy, you return it. Can be slightly ironic when used to justify returning a negative action. 禮尚往來 covers gift-giving, visits, and reciprocal favors.

examples.chinese: 他們年年互送年節禮品，可謂禮尚往來，感情深厚。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen niánnián hùsòng niánjié lǐpǐn, kě wèi lǐshàng-wǎnglái, gǎnqíng shēnhòu.
examples.english: They exchanged gifts every year during the holidays — a true example of reciprocal courtesy and deep friendship.

examples.chinese: 禮尚往來是人際交往的基本原則，懂得感恩與回報才能維繫關係。
examples.pinyin: Lǐshàng-wǎnglái shì rénjì jiāowǎng de jīběn yuánzé, dǒngde gǎn'ēn yǔ huíbào cái néng wéixì guānxi.
examples.english: Reciprocal courtesy is a basic principle of human relations — understanding gratitude and returning kindness is what sustains relationships.

semanticNote: Literally a road marker indicating distance traveled; figuratively any significant achievement or turning point. 歷史里程碑 (historical milestone), 具里程碑意義 (of milestone significance). The figurative use is far more common in modern usage.

examples.chinese: 這項科技突破被視為人類探索宇宙的重要里程碑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng kējì tūpò bèi shì wèi rénlèi tànsuǒ yǔzhòu de zhòngyào lǐchéngbēi.
examples.english: This technological breakthrough is seen as an important milestone in humanity's exploration of the universe.

examples.chinese: 臺灣在民主化進程中留下了許多具里程碑意義的時刻。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān zài mínzhǔ huà jìnchéng zhōng liú xià le xǔduō jù lǐchéngbēi yìyì de shíkè.
examples.english: Taiwan has left behind many milestone moments in its democratization process.

english: heed; pay attention to (usually used in the negative)
semanticNote: To take notice of or pay attention to someone — almost always used in negative constructions: 不理睬 (pay no attention to; ignore), 沒人理睬 (nobody paid attention). Used for interpersonal attention, not task attentiveness. Contrast: 重視 (take seriously).

components.meaning: manage; reason; care for; put in order
take notice of; pay heed to

examples.chinese: 她連發了幾封電子郵件，對方卻完全不理睬。
examples.pinyin: Tā lián fā le jǐ fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn, duìfāng què wánquán bù lǐcǎi.
examples.english: She sent several emails in a row, but the other party completely ignored them.

examples.chinese: 孩子哭著要糖吃，媽媽不理睬，繼續忙自己的事。
examples.pinyin: Háizi kū zhe yào táng chī, māma bù lǐcǎi, jìxù máng zìjǐ de shì.
examples.english: The child cried for candy, but the mom paid no attention and kept busy with her own things.

english: (idiom) it goes without saying; certainly; of course; be natural and right
semanticNote: Something so obviously right or natural it needs no justification. 理所當然地認為 (take it for granted that...). Often carries a critical edge when applied to someone who assumes too much. Common in spoken argument and written critique.

examples.chinese: 他理所當然地認為媽媽會幫他打掃房間，卻從不主動幫忙。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǐsuǒ-dāngrán de rènwéi māma huì bāng tā dǎsǎo fángjiān, què cóng bù zhǔdòng bāngmáng.
examples.english: He took it for granted that his mom would clean his room, but never once offered to help on his own.

examples.chinese: 付出努力就應該得到回報，這是理所當然的道理。
examples.pinyin: Fūchū nǔlì jiù yīnggāi dédào huíbào, zhè shì lǐsuǒ-dāngrán de dàolǐ.
examples.english: That hard work should be rewarded is simply a matter of course.

english: with justice on one's side, one is bold and assured; to have the courage of ones convictions; just and forceful
semanticNote: When you know you're in the right, you speak with confidence and without hesitation. 理直氣壯地反駁 (rebutted forcefully, knowing he was right). Sometimes used sarcastically when someone is overly aggressive despite being wrong.

examples.chinese: 他沒有犯錯，理直氣壯地向主管說明了整件事的經過。
examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu fàncuò, lǐzhí-qìzhuàng de xiàng zhǔguǎn shuōmíng le zhěng jiàn shì de jīngguò.
examples.english: Having done nothing wrong, he explained the whole situation to his supervisor with full confidence.

examples.chinese: 她理直氣壯地要求退款，商家只好照辦。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǐzhí-qìzhuàng de yāoqiú tuìkuǎn, shāngjia zhǐhǎo zhàobàn.
examples.english: She demanded a refund with complete confidence — the merchant had no choice but to comply.

semanticNote: Rational thinking and sound judgment — keeping a cool head. 保持理智 (keep one's composure), 失去理智 (lose one's reason), 理智上知道 (know rationally). Contrasts with 感情 (emotion). Key term in discussions of decision-making and emotional regulation.

examples.chinese: 在衝突中，她努力保持理智，沒有說出過激的話。
examples.pinyin: Zài chōngtū zhōng, tā nǔlì bǎochí lǐzhì, méiyǒu shuō chū guòjī de huà.
examples.english: In the conflict, she worked hard to keep her composure and didn't say anything extreme.

examples.chinese: 他知道這個決定在理智上是正確的，但感情上很難接受。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhīdào zhège juédìng zài lǐzhì shàng shì zhèngquè de, dàn gǎnqíng shàng hěn nán jiēshòu.
examples.english: He knew the decision was correct rationally, but emotionally it was hard to accept.

english: make every effort; do one's best
semanticNote: To strive hard to achieve something. 力求完美 (strive for perfection), 力求做到 (make every effort to accomplish). More emphatic than 盡力 (do one's best) — implies actively pushing hard toward a goal. Common in formal and written contexts.

examples.chinese: 設計師力求每個細節都完美，反覆修改了十幾次。
examples.pinyin: Shèjìshī lìqiú měi gè xìjié dōu wánměi, fǎnfù xiūgǎi le shíjǐ cì.
examples.english: The designer strove for perfection in every detail, revising the work over a dozen times.

examples.chinese: 政府力求在經濟成長與環境保護之間取得平衡。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ lìqiú zài jīngjì chéngzhǎng yǔ huánjìng bǎohù zhījiān qǔdé pínghéng.
examples.english: The government made every effort to strike a balance between economic growth and environmental protection.

english: within one's power; to the best of one's ability
semanticNote: Do everything that lies within one's capacity. 在力所能及的範圍內 (within the scope of what one can do). Often used modestly to offer limited but sincere help. Implies willingness bounded by actual ability — not a guarantee of outcome.

examples.chinese: 她表示，只要是力所能及的事，她一定全力幫忙。
examples.pinyin: Tā biǎoshì, zhǐyào shì lìsuǒ-néngjí de shì, tā yīdìng quánlì bāngmáng.
examples.english: She said that anything within her power, she would do her absolute best to help with.

examples.chinese: 志工們在力所能及的範圍內，盡力協助災區重建。
examples.pinyin: Zhìgōngmen zài lìsuǒ-néngjí de fànwéi nèi, jìnlì xiézhù zāiqū chóngjiàn.
examples.english: The volunteers did everything within their power to help with disaster-area reconstruction.

english: work hard; do all one can to; strive for/argue strongly
semanticNote: To fight hard for something or argue forcefully for one's position. 力爭上游 (strive to excel, lit. fight hard to go upstream), 據理力爭 (argue firmly on the basis of reason). More forceful than 爭取 (strive for). Common in labor, political, and debate contexts.

examples.chinese: 他在會議上據理力爭，終於說服了委員會接受新方案。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huìyì shàng jùlǐ lìzhēng, zhōngyú shuōfú le wěiyuánhuì jiēshòu xīn fāng'àn.
examples.english: He argued firmly on principle at the meeting and finally persuaded the committee to accept the new proposal.

examples.chinese: 勞工代表為爭取更好的工作條件不斷力爭，歷時數月才達成協議。
examples.pinyin: Láogōng dàibiǎo wèi zhēngqǔ gèng hǎo de gōngzuò tiáojiàn bùduàn lìzhēng, lìshí shù yuè cái dáchéng xiéyì.
examples.english: Labor representatives fought hard for better working conditions, and it took months of effort before an agreement was reached.

semanticNote: All previous dynasties or generations — 歷代帝王 (emperors throughout history), 歷代名作 (famous works through the ages), 歷代祖先 (ancestors through generations). More formal and literary than 古代 (ancient times). Common in historical, cultural, and heritage contexts.

components.meaning: generation; dynasty; era; replace; on behalf of

examples.chinese: 這座博物館珍藏著歷代帝王的書法真跡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò bówùguǎn zhēncáng zhe lìdài dìwáng de shūfǎ zhēnjī.
examples.english: This museum houses authentic calligraphy works by emperors throughout history.

examples.chinese: 歷代文人都為這片山水留下了膾炙人口的詩篇。
examples.pinyin: Lìdài wénrén dōu wèi zhè piàn shānshuǐ liú xià le kuàizhì-rénkǒu de shīpiān.
examples.english: Writers through the ages have left behind beloved poems about these mountains and waters.

semanticNote: From the beginning up to the present — referring to a consistent pattern or tradition. 歷來如此 (it has always been this way), 歷來最高 (the highest ever recorded). Implies continuity over time. More formal than 一直 (always, ongoing).

components.meaning: come; up to now; over time

examples.chinese: 這道菜的食譜歷來未變，保留了最傳統的做法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de shípǔ lìlái wèi biàn, bǎoliú le zuì chuántǒng de zuòfǎ.
examples.english: The recipe for this dish has never changed throughout history, preserving the most traditional method.

examples.chinese: 臺灣歷來重視教育，升學率居全球前列。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān lìlái zhòngshì jiàoyù, shēngxué lǜ jū quánqiú qiánliè.
examples.english: Taiwan has always placed great importance on education, with enrollment rates among the highest in the world.

semanticNote: One's stance or position on an issue. 堅定立場 (firm stance), 改變立場 (change one's position), 中立立場 (neutral stance). Implies a deliberate, principled position rather than a casual opinion. Essential vocabulary for politics, diplomacy, and debate.

examples.chinese: 在這個敏感議題上，政府明確表明了立場，不容曲解。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhège mǐngǎn yìtí shàng, zhèngfǔ míngquè biǎomíng le lìchǎng, bùróng qūjiě.
examples.english: On this sensitive issue, the government made its position clear and will not allow it to be misrepresented.

examples.chinese: 她的立場始終如一，從未因外界壓力而動搖。
examples.pinyin: Tā de lìchǎng shǐzhōng rúyī, cóng wèi yīn wàijiè yālì ér dòngyáo.
examples.english: Her position has remained consistent — she has never wavered under outside pressure.

semanticNote: A cube (3D shape) or a cubic unit of measurement. 立方公尺 (cubic meter), 立方公分 (cubic centimeter). Also the arithmetic operation of cubing: 2的立方是8 (2 cubed is 8). Used in geometry, physics, and engineering.

examples.chinese: 這個水箱的容量是兩立方公尺。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shuǐxiāng de róngliàng shì liǎng lìfāng gōngchǐ.
examples.english: This water tank has a capacity of two cubic meters.

examples.chinese: 老師解釋說，一個數的立方就是把它自乘三次。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiěshì shuō, yī gè shù de lìfāng jiù shì bǎ tā zì chéng sān cì.
examples.english: The teacher explained that the cube of a number is multiplying it by itself three times.

english: overpass; one road goes on top of another; cloverleaf intersection
semanticNote: A grade-separated road interchange — overpasses, underpasses, and cloverleaf intersections. Common in mainland urban planning vocabulary. In Taiwan, highway interchanges are typically called 交流道; overpasses 高架橋. The term 立交橋 is more common in mainland usage.

examples.chinese: 市區新建的立交橋大幅改善了交通壅塞問題。
examples.pinyin: Shìqū xīnjiàn de lìjiāoqiáo dàfú gǎishàn le jiāotōng yōngsāi wèntí.
examples.english: The newly built overpass in the urban area has significantly improved traffic congestion.

examples.chinese: 走這條路需要穿過幾個立交橋，第一次開車很容易迷路。
examples.pinyin: Zǒu zhè tiáo lù xūyào chuānguò jǐ gè lìjiāoqiáo, dì yī cì kāichē hěn róngyì mílù.
examples.english: Taking this road requires passing through several interchanges — it's easy to get lost the first time you drive it.

semanticNote: Three-dimensional — having length, width, and height. 立體圖形 (3D shape), 立體感 (sense of three-dimensionality/depth), 立體聲 (stereo sound, lit. 3D sound). Also figurative: 立體的描述 (a multi-dimensional, vivid description). Common in art, geometry, audio, and film.

examples.chinese: 這幅畫的立體感非常強，遠看像真正的實物一樣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà de lìtǐgǎn fēicháng qiáng, yuǎn kàn xiàng zhēnzhèng de shíwù yīyàng.
examples.english: This painting has a very strong sense of three-dimensionality — from a distance it looks like a real object.

examples.chinese: 新的電影院設備提供了立體音效，讓觀眾彷彿身臨其境。
examples.pinyin: Xīn de diànyǐngyuàn shèbèi tígōng le lìtǐ yīnxiào, ràng guānzhòng fǎngfú shēnlín qí jìng.
examples.english: The cinema's new equipment provides 3D surround sound, making the audience feel as if they're right there in the scene.

english: base oneself on; be established; have a footing
semanticNote: To have a footing or establish oneself. 立足點 (foothold; standpoint), 難以立足 (hard to get a foothold), 立足於事實 (based on facts). Both literal (physical footing) and figurative (establishing oneself in a field, market, or society). Common in business and career contexts.

examples.chinese: 這家新創公司努力在競爭激烈的市場中立足。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xīnchuàng gōngsī nǔlì zài jìngzhēng jīliè de shìchǎng zhōng lìzú.
examples.english: This startup is working hard to establish itself in the fiercely competitive market.

examples.chinese: 她以扎實的專業能力在業界立足，逐漸建立起口碑。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐ zhāshí de zhuānyè nénglì zài yèjiè lìzú, zhújiàn jiànlì qǐ kǒubēi.
examples.english: She established herself in the industry through solid professional skills and gradually built a reputation.

english: serious; formidable; devastating; (-hài: advantages and disadvantages)
semanticNote: Two readings: (1) lìhai — formidable, fierce, serious (often written 厲害 in modern usage); (2) lìhài — advantages and disadvantages: 利害關係 (vested interests; stakes), 權衡利害 (weigh the pros and cons). In formal writing, 利害 is the standard form for the pros-and-cons sense.

examples.chinese: 在做決定之前，應先仔細權衡利害關係。
examples.pinyin: Zài zuò juédìng zhīqián, yīng xiān zǐxì quánhéng lìhài guānxi.
examples.english: Before making a decision, one should carefully weigh the stakes and trade-offs involved.

examples.chinese: 他說話的口氣很利害，讓對方不敢輕易反駁。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà de kǒuqì hěn lìhai, ràng duìfāng bù gǎn qīngyì fǎnbó.
examples.english: His tone was so forceful that the other party didn't dare argue back.

semanticNote: An exception to a rule or general pattern. 無一例外 (without exception), 這次例外 (make an exception this time), 也不例外 (is no exception either). Fixed phrase: 毫無例外 (not a single exception). Used across all registers.

examples.chinese: 這項規定適用於所有人，沒有例外。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng guīdìng shìyòng yú suǒyǒu rén, méiyǒu lìwài.
examples.english: This regulation applies to everyone — there are no exceptions.

examples.chinese: 他平時很嚴格，但這次為了朋友破例，算是例外。
examples.pinyin: Tā píngshí hěn yángé, dàn zhè cì wèile péngyǒu pòlì, suànshì lìwài.
examples.english: He's normally very strict, but this time he made an exception for a friend.

english: a grain; granule; (mw for grain-like things)
semanticNote: A grain or granule; also a measure word for small, round or grain-like objects — 一粒米 (a grain of rice), 一粒藥 (one pill/tablet), 一粒珍珠 (a pearl). As a noun: 粒子 (particle — physics), 顆粒 (granule). Very common as a measure word in everyday speech.

examples.chinese: 她小心翼翼地把每一粒珍珠串成了一條項鍊。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoxīn yìyì de bǎ měi yī lì zhēnzhū chuàn chéng le yī tiáo xiàngliàn.
examples.english: She carefully strung each pearl one by one into a necklace.

examples.chinese: 醫生叮囑他每天要按時服用兩粒藥。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng dīngzhǔ tā měitiān yào ànshí fúyòng liǎng lì yào.
examples.english: The doctor instructed him to take two pills on time every day.

english: successive years; over many years; once again this year
semanticNote: Year after year; for many consecutive years. 連年虧損 (losses year after year), 連年豐收 (bumper harvests year after year), 連年戰爭 (years of continuous war). Emphasizes persistence or continuity over multiple years. Slightly formal — common in news and historical writing.

examples.chinese: 這個地區連年乾旱，農作物收成嚴重受損。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū liánnián gānhàn, nóngzuòwù shōuchéng yánzhòng shòusǔn.
examples.english: This region has suffered drought year after year, causing severe damage to crop yields.

examples.chinese: 公司連年盈利，董事會決定擴大投資規模。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī liánnián yínglì, dǒngshìhuì juédìng kuòdà tóuzī guīmó.
examples.english: The company has been profitable year after year, so the board decided to expand its investment scale.

semanticNote: A chain — both literal (interlocking links) and figurative: 連鎖反應 (chain reaction), 連鎖店 (chain store), 連鎖效應 (knock-on effect). Common in business (franchise/chain operations) and scientific contexts. Convenience store chains (便利商店連鎖) are ubiquitous in Taiwan's economy.

examples.chinese: 這家餐廳發展成全臺最大的連鎖品牌，門市超過三百家。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng fāzhǎn chéng quán Tái zuì dà de liánsuǒ pǐnpái, ménshì chāoguò sānbǎi jiā.
examples.english: This restaurant has grown into Taiwan's largest chain brand, with over three hundred locations.

examples.chinese: 一家銀行倒閉引發了連鎖反應，導致多家金融機構相繼陷入危機。
examples.pinyin: Yī jiā yínháng dǎobì yǐnfā le liánsuǒ fǎnyìng, dǎozhì duō jiā jīnróng jīgòu xiāngjì xiàn rù wēijī.
examples.english: The collapse of one bank triggered a chain reaction, leading several other financial institutions into crisis one after another.

semanticNote: Together with; along with — used to include something additional in a bundled action. 連同附件一起發送 (send along with the attachment). More formal than 和 (and), emphasizing inclusive bundling. Common in formal writing and legal documents.

examples.chinese: 請連同申請表一起繳交相關證明文件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng liántóng shēnqǐng biǎo yīqǐ jiǎojiāo xiāngguān zhèngmíng wénjiàn.
examples.english: Please submit the relevant supporting documents together with the application form.

examples.chinese: 他把自己的積蓄，連同父母的遺產，全部捐給了慈善機構。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zìjǐ de jīxù, liántóng fùmǔ de yíchǎn, quánbù juān gěi le císhàn jīgòu.
examples.english: He donated all his savings, together with his parents' inheritance, to a charitable organization.

semanticNote: A celebratory gathering or get-together. 聯歡晚會 (gala evening; celebration party), 聯歡會 (social gathering). Often refers to organized group celebrations — school year-end parties, company banquets, New Year's galas. More festive and organized than 聚會 (casual gathering).

examples.chinese: 學校每年年底都會舉辦聯歡晚會，全體師生共同慶祝。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào měinián niándǐ dōu huì jǔbàn liánhuān wǎnhuì, quántǐ shīshēng gòngtóng qìngzhù.
examples.english: The school holds a year-end gala every year for all teachers and students to celebrate together.

examples.chinese: 公司舉辦了一場跨部門的聯歡活動，增進了同事之間的感情。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī jǔbàn le yī chǎng kuà bùmén de liánhuān huódòng, zēngjìn le tóngshì zhījiān de gǎnqíng.
examples.english: The company organized a cross-departmental get-together that strengthened bonds between colleagues.

semanticNote: To contact or communicate with someone. 保持聯絡 (keep in touch), 聯絡方式 (contact information), 失去聯絡 (lose contact), 聯絡人 (contact person; liaison). Both a verb and a noun. Very common across everyday and formal contexts.

examples.chinese: 搬家後，她努力與老朋友保持聯絡。
examples.pinyin: Bānjiā hòu, tā nǔlì yǔ lǎo péngyǒu bǎochí liánluò.
examples.english: After moving, she made every effort to stay in touch with old friends.

examples.chinese: 請在表格上填寫您的聯絡方式，以便我們後續通知您。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài biǎogé shàng tiánxiě nín de liánluò fāngshì, yǐbiàn wǒmen hòuxù tōngzhī nín.
examples.english: Please fill in your contact information on the form so we can notify you later.

semanticNote: A formal alliance, union, or coalition — between nations, parties, or organizations. 歐盟 (EU — short for 歐洲聯盟), 軍事聯盟 (military alliance), 政治聯盟 (political coalition). More institutionalized than 聯合 (joint/combined). Common in international relations and political discourse.

examples.chinese: 這幾個小國結成聯盟，共同抵禦外來威脅。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ gè xiǎo guó jiéchéng liánméng, gòngtóng dǐyù wàilái wēixié.
examples.english: These small nations formed an alliance to jointly resist external threats.

examples.chinese: 多個環保團體組成聯盟，向政府施壓要求制定更嚴格的排放標準。
examples.pinyin: Duō gè huánbǎo tuántǐ zǔchéng liánméng, xiàng zhèngfǔ shīyā yāoqiú zhìdìng gèng yángé de páifàng biāozhǔn.
examples.english: Several environmental groups formed a coalition to pressure the government to adopt stricter emission standards.

english: to associate (cognitively); to make an associative connection; mental association; word prediction and auto-complete functions of input method editing programs; abbr. for 联想集团 Lenovo Group (PRC computer firm)
semanticNote: To make a mental association — 引發聯想 (trigger associations), 由此聯想到 (this brings to mind…). Also the brand name 聯想集團 (Lenovo Group). In language learning: 聯想記憶法 (mnemonic association method). Versatile — used in cognitive, creative, and everyday contexts.

examples.chinese: 看到這首歌，她自然聯想起了第一次見面的情景。
examples.pinyin: Kàn dào zhè shǒu gē, tā zìrán liánxiǎng qǐ le dì yī cì jiànmiàn de qíngjǐng.
examples.english: Seeing this song, she naturally associated it with the scene of their first meeting.

examples.chinese: 孩子們天生擅長聯想，常常把雲朵聯想成各種動物。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen tiānshēng shàncháng liánxiǎng, chángcháng bǎ yúnduǒ liánxiǎng chéng gè zhǒng dòngwù.
examples.english: Children are naturally good at making associations, often imagining clouds as all sorts of animals.

semanticNote: Clean-handed and incorruptible — free from corruption and bribery. 廉潔自律 (self-disciplined and incorruptible), 廉潔奉公 (serve the public with integrity), 廉政 (clean government; anti-corruption). A key term in political and administrative discourse. Contrasts with 貪腐 (corrupt).

examples.chinese: 這位官員以廉潔著稱，從未接受過任何賄賂。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi guānyuán yǐ liánjié zhùchēng, cóng wèi jiēshòu guò rènhé huìlù.
examples.english: This official is known for his integrity and has never accepted any bribe.

examples.chinese: 政府推動廉政改革，要求公務員廉潔自律，杜絕貪腐。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ tuīdòng liánzhèng gǎigé, yāoqiú gōngwùyuán liánjié zìlǜ, dùjué tānfǔ.
examples.english: The government is promoting clean-governance reforms, demanding that civil servants maintain integrity to root out corruption.

semanticNote: Conscience — one's inner moral sense of right and wrong. 憑良心說 (in all conscience; to be honest), 昧著良心 (against one's conscience), 良心上過不去 (can't live with it). 黑心商人 (unscrupulous merchants) contrasts directly with 良心. A core moral vocabulary word.

examples.chinese: 他憑良心說，這件事確實是他的錯，不應該推諉他人。
examples.pinyin: Tā píng liángxīn shuō, zhè jiàn shì quèshí shì tā de cuò, bù yīnggāi tuīwěi tārén.
examples.english: In all conscience, he admitted this was indeed his fault and he shouldn't shift the blame to others.

examples.chinese: 她賣假藥賺錢，完全沒有良心。
examples.pinyin: Tā mài jiǎyào zhuànqián, wánquán méiyǒu liángxīn.
examples.english: She sold fake medicine for profit — she has absolutely no conscience.

english: understanding; make an allowance for; forgive
semanticNote: To understand and make allowances for someone's situation; to forgive in light of circumstances. 請多諒解 (please understand/forgive), 相互諒解 (mutual understanding), 尋求諒解 (seek understanding). More formal than 原諒 (forgive) — implies understanding the circumstances, not just pardoning.

examples.chinese: 他向同事解釋了遲到的原因，希望大家能諒解。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng tóngshì jiěshì le chídào de yuányīn, xīwàng dàjiā néng liàngjiě.
examples.english: He explained his reason for being late to his colleagues, hoping they would understand.

examples.chinese: 兩國經過多輪談判，終於達成了相互諒解，化解了外交危機。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó jīngguò duō lún tánpàn, zhōngyú dáchéng le xiānghù liàngjiě, huàjiě le wàijiāo wēijī.
examples.english: After multiple rounds of talks, the two countries finally reached mutual understanding, defusing the diplomatic crisis.

english: dry in the air/sun; (colloquial) snub or ignore
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) to air-dry or hang out to dry — 晾衣服 (hang laundry to dry), 晾乾 (air-dry); (2) colloquial: to leave someone hanging or ignore them — 把他晾在那裡 (left him standing there, ignored). The laundry sense is primary; the snubbing sense is informal/spoken.

components.meaning: dry in the air; hang out to dry (日 sun radical)

examples.chinese: 她把洗好的衣服拿到陽臺上晾乾。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xǐhǎo de yīfú ná dào yángtái shàng liàng gān.
examples.english: She took the freshly washed clothes out to the balcony to dry.

examples.chinese: 客人等了半小時，主人才出現，把大家晾了好一會兒。
examples.pinyin: Kèrén děng le bàn xiǎoshí, zhǔrén cái chūxiàn, bǎ dàjiā liàng le hǎo yīhuìr.
examples.english: The guests waited half an hour before the host appeared — leaving everyone hanging for quite a while.

semanticNote: Vast in area; wide and expansive. 遼闊的草原 (vast grasslands), 遼闊的海洋 (the boundless ocean). More evocative and poetic than 廣大 (broad and large) — often conveys grandeur and scale. Common in literary description and geographic writing.

examples.chinese: 站在山頂，眼前是一片遼闊的草原，令人心曠神怡。
examples.pinyin: Zhàn zài shāndǐng, yǎnqián shì yī piàn liáokuò de cǎoyuán, lìng rén xīnkuàng-shényí.
examples.english: Standing at the mountaintop, a vast grassland stretched out before the eyes, filling one with a sense of peace and joy.

examples.chinese: 這片遼闊的大海讓她忘卻了所有的煩惱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piàn liáokuò de dàhǎi ràng tā wàngquè le suǒyǒu de fánnǎo.
examples.english: The boundless sea made her forget all her worries.

semanticNote: To enumerate or list items one by one. 列舉事實 (cite facts), 列舉例子 (give examples), 列舉如下 (as enumerated below). More formal and systematic than 舉例 (give an example — just one). Common in academic writing, legal documents, and formal presentations.

components.meaning: row; line up; arrange in order; list; column

examples.chinese: 老師要求學生列舉五個支持論點的具體例子。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yāoqiú xuéshēng lièjǔ wǔ gè zhīchí lùndiǎn de jùtǐ lìzi.
examples.english: The teacher asked students to enumerate five specific examples supporting their argument.

examples.chinese: 報告中列舉了多項造成空氣污染的主要原因。
examples.pinyin: Bàogào zhōng lièjǔ le duō xiàng zàochéng kōngqì wūrǎn de zhǔyào yuányīn.
examples.english: The report enumerated several major causes of air pollution.

semanticNote: Clinical — relating to direct patient care as opposed to theoretical or lab-based medicine. 臨床試驗 (clinical trial), 臨床醫學 (clinical medicine), 臨床經驗 (clinical experience). Literally 'at the bedside' (臨 = approach; 床 = bed). Essential in medicine and pharmaceutical research.

components.meaning: approach; face; be at; overlook; copy (calligraphy)

examples.chinese: 這種新藥已通過臨床試驗，即將正式上市。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng xīnyào yǐ tōngguò línchuáng shìyàn, jíjiāng zhèngshì shàngshì.
examples.english: This new drug has passed clinical trials and will soon officially come to market.

examples.chinese: 他有豐富的臨床經驗，能快速判斷病情並做出處置。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu fēngfù de línchuáng jīngyàn, néng kuàisù pànduàn bìngqíng bìng zuòchū chǔzhì.
examples.english: He has extensive clinical experience and can quickly assess a patient's condition and respond.

semanticNote: To drench or pour liquid over something; to be caught in the rain. 淋雨 (get drenched in the rain), 淋濕 (soaked through), 淋浴 (shower — lit. drench-bathe). Also appears in 淋漓盡致 (give full and vivid expression to). Very common in daily speech.

components.meaning: drench; pour over; drip; soak (氵 water radical)

examples.chinese: 她忘了帶傘，被突如其來的大雨淋得全身濕透。
examples.pinyin: Tā wàng le dài sǎn, bèi tūrú qí lái de dàyǔ lín de quánshēn shītòu.
examples.english: She forgot her umbrella and was drenched from head to toe by a sudden downpour.

examples.chinese: 澆花時要小心，不要把葉子淋得太濕，容易腐爛。
examples.pinyin: Jiāohuā shí yào xiǎoxīn, bùyào bǎ yèzi lín de tài shī, róngyì fǔlàn.
examples.english: When watering flowers, be careful not to soak the leaves too much — they can easily rot.

semanticNote: Stingy and unwilling to spend or share. 吝嗇鬼 (miser; skinflint), 對人吝嗇 (stingy toward others). Stronger than 小氣 (petty/cheap) — more of a stable character fault. Common in everyday speech and literary description of misers. Antonym: 慷慨 (generous).

examples.chinese: 他雖然有錢，卻極為吝嗇，連請朋友吃頓飯都捨不得。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán yǒuqián, què jíwéi lìnsè, lián qǐng péngyǒu chī dùn fàn dōu shě bude.
examples.english: Despite being wealthy, he was extremely stingy — he even begrudged treating friends to a meal.

examples.chinese: 在金錢上吝嗇或許能積累財富，但在感情上吝嗇卻會失去朋友。
examples.pinyin: Zài jīnqián shàng lìnsè huòxǔ néng jīlěi cáifù, dàn zài gǎnqíng shàng lìnsè què huì shīqù péngyǒu.
examples.english: Being stingy with money may accumulate wealth, but being stingy with affection will lose you friends.

semanticNote: Quick-witted, clever, and lively. 口齒伶俐 (quick-tongued; articulate), 伶俐的孩子 (a sharp child). Implies both cognitive sharpness and a lively, communicative manner — not just book-smart. More colloquial and affectionate than 聰明. Often used to describe children or quick-witted speakers.

examples.chinese: 這孩子口齒伶俐，才七歲就能對答如流。
examples.pinyin: Zhè háizi kǒuchǐ línglì, cái qī suì jiù néng duìdá rúliú.
examples.english: This child is so articulate that at just seven years old, she can already answer questions fluently.

examples.chinese: 她應對得相當伶俐，讓面試官印象深刻。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìngduì de xiāngdāng línglì, ràng miànshìguān yìnxiàng shēnkè.
examples.english: She handled the questions with great sharpness, leaving a deep impression on the interviewer.

english: inspiration; insight; a burst of creativity in scientific or artistic endeavor
semanticNote: Creative inspiration — a sudden burst of ideas or insight in artistic or scientific work. 靈感來了 (inspiration struck), 從…獲得靈感 (draw inspiration from…), 缺乏靈感 (lacking inspiration). Implies something that arrives unexpectedly rather than through deliberate effort. Common in art, music, literature, and innovation.

examples.chinese: 他看著窗外的落葉，突然靈感一來，便提筆寫下了這首詩。
examples.pinyin: Tā kànzhe chuāng wài de luòyè, tūrán línggǎn yī lái, biàn tí bǐ xiě xià le zhè shǒu shī.
examples.english: Watching the falling leaves outside the window, inspiration suddenly struck and he took up his brush to write this poem.

examples.chinese: 設計師表示，這件作品的靈感來源於臺灣的原住民族圖紋。
examples.pinyin: Shèjìshī biǎoshì, zhè jiàn zuòpǐn de línggǎn láiyuán yú Táiwān de yuánzhùmínzú túwén.
examples.english: The designer said the inspiration for this work came from the indigenous patterns of Taiwan.

semanticNote: The soul or spirit of a person — religious (the soul that leaves after death) and figurative (the essence or core of something). 靈魂人物 (the soul/key driving force of a group), 音樂的靈魂 (the soul of music). Common in philosophy, religion, and figurative expression.

components.meaning: soul; spirit (the ethereal soul, contrasted with 魄 pò the corporeal)

examples.chinese: 她是這個樂團的靈魂人物，少了她整個表演就失去了光彩。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhège yuètuán de línghún rénwù, shǎo le tā zhěng gè biǎoyǎn jiù shīqù le guāngcǎi.
examples.english: She is the soul of this band — without her, the whole performance loses its brilliance.

examples.chinese: 他認為，文化是一個民族的靈魂，不可失去。
examples.pinyin: Tā rènwéi, wénhuà shì yī gè mínzú de línghún, bùkě shīqù.
examples.english: He believes that culture is the soul of a people and must not be lost.

semanticNote: Quick and sensitive in perception or response — of senses, instruments, or reflexes. 嗅覺靈敏 (keen sense of smell), 反應靈敏 (quick reflexes), 靈敏的儀器 (sensitive instrument). More specific than 敏感 (sensitive broadly) — 靈敏 emphasizes functional quickness and acuity. Common in science, military, and animal behavior contexts.

examples.chinese: 警犬的嗅覺非常靈敏，能在幾百公尺外察覺到氣味。
examples.pinyin: Jǐng quǎn de xiùjué fēicháng língmǐn, néng zài jǐ bǎi gōngchǐ wài chájué dào qìwèi.
examples.english: Police dogs have extremely keen noses, able to detect scents from hundreds of meters away.

examples.chinese: 這款感測器靈敏度極高，能偵測到極微小的震動。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn gǎncèqì língmǐndù jí gāo, néng zhēncè dào jí wēixiǎo de zhèndòng.
examples.english: This sensor has extremely high sensitivity and can detect the most minute vibrations.

semanticNote: The early hours of the morning — typically midnight to around 5am, before dawn. 凌晨三點 (3am), 凌晨時分 (in the wee hours). More specific than 清晨 (early morning, closer to dawn) or 早上 (morning generally). Common in news reporting and everyday conversation.

examples.chinese: 地震發生在凌晨兩點，許多人在睡夢中被震醒。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn fāshēng zài língchén liǎng diǎn, xǔduō rén zài shuìmèng zhōng bèi zhèn xǐng.
examples.english: The earthquake struck at 2am, waking many people from their sleep.

examples.chinese: 她熬夜工作，直到凌晨才終於完成了報告。
examples.pinyin: Tā áoyè gōngzuò, zhídào língchén cái zhōngyú wánchéng le bàogào.
examples.english: She worked through the night and finished the report only in the early hours of the morning.

semanticNote: Scattered and sporadic — occurring in small amounts here and there, not systematically. 零星小雨 (scattered light rain), 零星的資訊 (fragmentary information), 零星攻擊 (sporadic attacks). Implies incompleteness and irregularity. Common in weather reports, news, and descriptions of patchy data.

examples.chinese: 今天臺灣北部有零星陣雨，出門請攜帶雨具。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān Táiwān běibù yǒu língxīng zhènyǔ, chūmén qǐng xiédài yǔjù.
examples.english: There will be scattered showers in northern Taiwan today — please bring rain gear when going out.

examples.chinese: 他的筆記本上只有零星的幾條記錄，根本無法拼湊出完整的情況。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bǐjìběn shàng zhǐ yǒu língxīng de jǐ tiáo jìlù, gēnběn wúfǎ pīncòu chū wánzhěng de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: His notebook had only a few scattered notes — it was impossible to piece together a complete picture.

semanticNote: To understand and grasp the meaning, intent, or spirit of something — a deeper, fuller comprehension. 領會精神 (grasp the spirit/intent), 領會意思 (understand the meaning). Implies more complete understanding than 理解 (understand logically). Common in formal and written contexts.

components.meaning: understand; meet; be able to; will; converge

examples.chinese: 他讀了好幾遍才真正領會了這段話的深層含義。
examples.pinyin: Tā dú le hǎo jǐ biàn cái zhēnzhèng lǐnghuì le zhè duàn huà de shēncéng hányì.
examples.english: He read it several times before truly grasping the deeper meaning of this passage.

examples.chinese: 主管希望員工能領會公司政策的精神，而不只是照章辦事。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔguǎn xīwàng yuángōng néng lǐnghuì gōngsī zhèngcè de jīngshén, ér bùzhǐ shì zhàozhāng bànshì.
examples.english: The manager hopes employees will grasp the spirit of company policies, not just follow the rules mechanically.

semanticNote: A consulate — a government office in a foreign city providing visas, citizen assistance, and notary services. Smaller than an embassy (大使館). In Taiwan, most countries maintain a 辦事處 (representative office) rather than a 領事館 due to One China complications; the US equivalent is the American Institute in Taiwan (美國在臺協會).

examples.chinese: 她前往法國領事館辦理簽證，卻發現需要預約。
examples.pinyin: Tā qiánwǎng Fǎguó lǐngshìguǎn bànlǐ qiānzhèng, què fāxiàn xūyào yùyuē.
examples.english: She went to the French consulate to apply for a visa, only to find that an appointment was required.

examples.chinese: 海外發生緊急事故時，公民應立即聯絡當地的領事館尋求協助。
examples.pinyin: Hǎiwài fāshēng jǐnjí shìgù shí, gōngmín yīng lìjí liánluò dāngdì de lǐngshìguǎn xúnqiú xiézhù.
examples.english: When an emergency occurs abroad, citizens should immediately contact the local consulate for assistance.

semanticNote: The territory of a nation — land over which a government has sovereignty. 領土主權 (territorial sovereignty), 領土爭端 (territorial dispute), 侵犯領土 (encroach on territory). A key term in international law and geopolitics. Highly relevant in Taiwan's cross-strait and South China Sea context.

examples.chinese: 兩國因一座小島的歸屬問題，引發了嚴重的領土爭端。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó yīn yī zuò xiǎodǎo de guīshǔ wèntí, yǐnfā le yánzhòng de lǐngtǔ zhēngduān.
examples.english: A serious territorial dispute broke out between the two countries over the ownership of a small island.

examples.chinese: 捍衛國家領土完整，是每一個公民的責任。
examples.pinyin: Hànwèi guójiā lǐngtǔ wánzhěng, shì měi yī gè gōngmín de zérèn.
examples.english: Defending the territorial integrity of the nation is the responsibility of every citizen.

semanticNote: To arrive at a deeper understanding through reflection — often suddenly, like a realization or insight. 領悟人生道理 (grasp the truths of life), 終於領悟了 (finally understood/realized). More experiential and insightful than 理解 (understand rationally). Common in philosophical, literary, and reflective contexts.

examples.chinese: 經歷了這場挫折，他終於領悟了堅持的重要性。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglì le zhè chǎng cuòzhé, tā zhōngyú lǐngwù le jiānchí de zhòngyàoxìng.
examples.english: After going through this setback, he finally came to understand the importance of perseverance.

examples.chinese: 她花了多年才領悟到，真正的幸福來自內心的平靜。
examples.pinyin: Tā huā le duō nián cái lǐngwù dào, zhēnzhèng de xìngfú láizì nèixīn de píngjìng.
examples.english: It took her many years to realize that true happiness comes from inner peace.

english: leadership; to lead; be in front
semanticNote: To be in the lead or ahead of others — in a race, competition, or ranking. 領先一步 (be one step ahead), 大幅領先 (lead by a large margin), 科技領先 (technological lead). Used as an adjective: 領先的國家 (leading nations). Common in sports, business, and technology contexts.

examples.chinese: 臺灣在半導體製造領域長期領先全球。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān zài bàndǎotǐ zhìzào lǐngyù chángqī lǐngxiān quánqiú.
examples.english: Taiwan has long led the world in semiconductor manufacturing.

examples.chinese: 比賽進行到最後一圈，她依然領先，最終奪得冠軍。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jìnxíng dào zuìhòu yī quān, tā yīrán lǐngxiān, zuìzhōng duódé guànjūn.
examples.english: In the final lap of the race, she was still in the lead and ultimately took the championship.

semanticNote: A leader — of a nation, movement, party, or organization. 政治領袖 (political leader), 精神領袖 (spiritual leader), 領袖風範 (the bearing/charisma of a leader). More elevated and formal than 領導人 or 頭目. Carries connotations of charisma, vision, and commanding authority.

components.meaning: sleeve; (historically: one who leads — collar leads, sleeve follows)

examples.chinese: 他以沉穩的風格贏得了黨內外的尊重，逐漸成為公認的政治領袖。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐ chéngwěn de fēnggé yíngdé le dǎng nèiwài de zūnzhòng, zhújiàn chéngwéi gōngrèn de zhèngzhì lǐngxiù.
examples.english: With his composed style, he earned respect both within and outside the party, gradually becoming a recognized political leader.

examples.chinese: 在危機時刻，一個國家最需要的是一位有遠見的領袖。
examples.pinyin: Zài wēijī shíkè, yī gè guójiā zuì xūyào de shì yī wèi yǒu yuǎnjiàn de lǐngxiù.
examples.english: In times of crisis, what a nation needs most is a leader with vision.

english: slip away; to skate; to glide
semanticNote: To slip or glide smoothly; also to sneak away. 溜走 (slip away; sneak off), 溜冰 (ice-skate / roller-skate), 溜出去 (sneak out). The sneak-away sense is very colloquial. Also appears in 阿諛逢迎/溜鬚拍馬 (to flatter and fawn).

components.meaning: slip; slide; glide; sneak away (氵 water radical)

examples.chinese: 開會開到一半，他趁人不注意悄悄地溜走了。
examples.pinyin: Kāihuì kāi dào yī bàn, tā chèn rén bù zhùyì qiāoqiāo de liūzǒu le.
examples.english: Halfway through the meeting, he quietly slipped away when no one was paying attention.

examples.chinese: 冬天一到，孩子們就喜歡到公園溜冰。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān yī dào, háizimen jiù xǐhuān dào gōngyuán liū bīng.
examples.english: As soon as winter arrives, the children love to go skating at the park.

semanticNote: To be reluctant to leave a place or situation because of fond attachment. 留戀故鄉 (reluctant to leave one's hometown), 依依留戀 (fondly unwilling to depart), 留戀往事 (cling fondly to the past). More literary and emotional than 捨不得 (can't bear to part with).

components.meaning: love; be attached to; yearn for; romance

examples.chinese: 旅行結束時，她對這座城市充滿留戀，遲遲不想離去。
examples.pinyin: Lǚxíng jiéshù shí, tā duì zhè zuò chéngshì chōngmǎn liúliàn, chíchí bù xiǎng líqù.
examples.english: At the end of the trip, she was filled with reluctance to leave this city and lingered, unwilling to go.

examples.chinese: 他雖然退休了，仍對昔日的工作環境留戀不已。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán tuìxiū le, réng duì xīrì de gōngzuò huánjìng liúliàn bùyǐ.
examples.english: Even after retiring, he couldn't stop longing fondly for his former work environment.

semanticNote: To keep something as a memory or souvenir; to do something in remembrance. 合照留念 (take a group photo as a memento), 留念品 (souvenir; keepsake), 留作留念 (keep as a keepsake). Often used in formal parting contexts. More literary than 紀念 (commemorate).

components.meaning: read; think of; miss; remember; thought

examples.chinese: 畢業典禮後，同學們一起拍了張大合照留念。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè diǎnlǐ hòu, tóngxuémen yīqǐ pāi le zhāng dà hézhào liúniàn.
examples.english: After the graduation ceremony, the classmates took a large group photo together as a keepsake.

examples.chinese: 她把這張舊車票保存了下來，留念第一次出國旅行的回憶。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhè zhāng jiù chēpiào bǎocún le xiàlái, liúniàn dì yī cì chūguó lǚxíng de huíyì.
examples.english: She kept the old ticket as a memento of her first trip abroad.

english: (idiom) take care to ...; be careful of ...
semanticNote: To pay careful attention; to watch out. 留神安全 (watch out for safety), 留神點兒 (be careful — spoken). More colloquial and immediate than 注意 (pay attention). Often used as a direct warning: 走路留神 (watch your step). Slightly more literary than 小心 (be careful).

examples.chinese: 下雨天地板溼滑，走路要留神，小心跌倒。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ tiān dìbǎn shī huá, zǒulù yào liú shén, xiǎoxīn diēdǎo.
examples.english: The floor is slippery in the rain — watch your step and be careful not to fall.

examples.chinese: 他叮囑孩子出門後要留神周圍的環境，不要和陌生人說話。
examples.pinyin: Tā dīngzhǔ háizi chūmén hòu yào liú shén zhōuwéi de huánjìng, bùyào hé mòshēng rén shuōhuà.
examples.english: He reminded the child to stay alert to the surroundings when outside and not to talk to strangers.

semanticNote: To drift about with no fixed home or purpose — like a vagabond or stray. 流浪漢 (vagrant; drifter), 流浪狗 (stray dog), 流浪生活 (life of wandering). Can be neutral-to-romantic (the wandering artist) or pitiful (homeless). 流浪狗 is a significant animal welfare issue in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 這隻流浪狗在街上徘徊了好幾天，最後被善心人士收養。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī liúlàng gǒu zài jiēshàng páihuái le hǎo jǐ tiān, zuìhòu bèi shànxīn rénshì shōuyǎng.
examples.english: This stray dog wandered the streets for several days before finally being adopted by a kind-hearted person.

examples.chinese: 大學畢業後，他選擇了流浪生活，騎著腳踏車環遊世界。
examples.pinyin: Dàxué bìyè hòu, tā xuǎnzé le liúlàng shēnghuó, qízhe jiǎotàchē huányóu shìjiè.
examples.english: After graduating from university, he chose a life of wandering, cycling around the world.

semanticNote: To unintentionally reveal or let emotions/thoughts show. 流露出感情 (let feelings show), 眼神中流露出擔憂 (worry showing in the eyes). The subject is typically an emotion or thought. More literary and subtle than 表現 (express/show) — implies the leaking of inner states.

examples.chinese: 她雖然努力掩飾，但眼神中還是流露出了一絲擔憂。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán nǔlì yǎnshì, dàn yǎnshén zhōng háishì liúlù chū le yī sī dānyōu.
examples.english: Despite her efforts to hide it, a hint of worry still showed in her eyes.

examples.chinese: 他在演講中不經意地流露出對現任政策的不滿。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yǎnjiǎng zhōng bù jīngyì de liúlù chū duì xiànrèn zhèngcè de bùmǎn.
examples.english: In his speech, he inadvertently let slip his dissatisfaction with current policies.

semanticNote: A rogue, hooligan, or person of loose morals. 流氓行為 (hooligan/indecent behavior), 流氓罪 (crime of hooliganism — a former PRC legal term), 耍流氓 (behave like a hooligan; act indecently). Can mean a street thug or someone who behaves lewdly. Register: informal, pejorative.

examples.chinese: 她走在路上被幾名流氓騷擾，幸好路人及時報警。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒu zài lù shàng bèi jǐ míng liúmáng sāorǎo, xìnghǎo lùrén jíshí bàojǐng.
examples.english: She was harassed by several hooligans while walking down the street — fortunately, a passerby called the police in time.

examples.chinese: 他在網路上的言論相當粗鄙，被網友直接罵成「網路流氓」。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǎnglù shàng de yánlùn xiāngdāng cūbǐ, bèi wǎngyǒu zhíjiē mà chéng "wǎnglù liúmáng".
examples.english: His language online was extremely crude — netizens directly called him an "internet troll/hooligan."

semanticNote: To circulate or flow freely — of money, goods, air, or information. 貨幣流通 (currency circulation), 商品流通 (circulation of goods), 流通量 (volume of circulation), 空氣流通 (air circulation). In economics, 流通 refers to the distribution and exchange phase. Common in financial, logistical, and physical contexts.

examples.chinese: 銀行控制貨幣流通量，以穩定市場物價。
examples.pinyin: Yínháng kòngzhì huòbì liútōng liàng, yǐ wěndìng shìchǎng wùjià.
examples.english: Banks control the volume of currency in circulation to stabilize market prices.

examples.chinese: 這間房間的空氣不流通，待久了容易頭暈。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān fángjiān de kōngqì bù liútōng, dāi jiǔ le róngyì tóuyūn.
examples.english: The air in this room doesn't circulate well — staying too long will easily make you dizzy.

semanticNote: Deaf-mute — being both deaf and unable to speak. 聾啞人 (deaf-mute person), 聾啞學校 (school for the deaf-mute). An older term — modern Taiwan prefers 聾人 (Deaf person) or 聽語障礙 (hearing and speech impairment). 聾 alone = deaf; 啞 alone = mute/dumb.

components.meaning: mute; dumb; hoarse; unable to speak

examples.chinese: 這所學校專門為聾啞學生提供手語教育。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào zhuānmén wèi lóngyǎ xuéshēng tígōng shǒuyǔ jiàoyù.
examples.english: This school provides sign language education specifically for deaf-mute students.

examples.chinese: 他從小失去聽覺與說話能力，但靠著手語與外界溝通，生活並不孤立。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo shīqù tīngjué yǔ shuōhuà nénglì, dàn kào zhe shǒuyǔ yǔ wàijiè gōutōng, shēnghuó bìng bù gūlì.
examples.english: He lost his hearing and speech from a young age, but communicates with the outside world through sign language and lives far from isolated.

semanticNote: Grand, solemn, and ceremonious — used for important formal occasions. 隆重的典禮 (grand ceremony), 隆重登場 (make a grand entrance), 隆重推出 (launch with great fanfare). Implies pomp and significance. More formal than 盛大 (grand/magnificent). Common in official, diplomatic, and celebratory contexts.

examples.chinese: 畢業典禮在學校大禮堂隆重舉行，場面十分莊嚴。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè diǎnlǐ zài xuéxiào dà lǐtáng lóngzhòng jǔxíng, chǎngmiàn shífēn zhuāngyán.
examples.english: The graduation ceremony was held grandly in the school auditorium — the scene was very solemn.

examples.chinese: 新任總統隆重宣誓就職，全國矚目。
examples.pinyin: Xīnrèn zǒngtǒng lóngzhòng xuānshì jiùzhí, quánguó zhǔmù.
examples.english: The newly elected president was solemnly sworn in, drawing the attention of the whole nation.

semanticNote: To monopolize or hold a monopoly over a market or resource. 壟斷市場 (monopolize the market), 打破壟斷 (break up a monopoly), 國家壟斷 (state monopoly). A key economics and antitrust term. Common in business news and competition law discourse.

components.meaning: cut off; sever; decide; monopolize; stop

examples.chinese: 政府推動反壟斷法規，防止少數企業壟斷市場。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ tuīdòng fǎn lǒngduàn fǎguī, fángzhǐ shǎoshù qǐyè lǒngduàn shìchǎng.
examples.english: The government is promoting anti-monopoly regulations to prevent a few companies from monopolizing the market.

examples.chinese: 這家科技公司被指控壟斷搜尋引擎市場，面臨鉅額罰款。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kējì gōngsī bèi zhǐkòng lǒngduàn sōuxún yǐnqíng shìchǎng, miànlín jùé fákuǎn.
examples.english: This tech company is accused of monopolizing the search engine market and faces a massive fine.

english: envelop; to shroud; be masked by
semanticNote: To envelop or cover completely — like a mist, shadow, or atmosphere hanging over something. 籠罩在迷霧中 (shrouded in mist), 籠罩在恐懼中 (enveloped in fear). The subject is usually something pervasive — fog, darkness, fear, grief. Typically evocative and slightly literary.

components.meaning: cover; hood; shade; drape over; screen

examples.chinese: 清晨的山谷被濃霧籠罩，看不清遠方的輪廓。
examples.pinyin: Qīngchén de shāngǔ bèi nóngwù lǒngzhào, kàn bù qīng yuǎnfāng de lúnkuò.
examples.english: The valley in the early morning was shrouded in thick mist, the distant outlines invisible.

examples.chinese: 消息傳出後，整個社區都籠罩在一片悲傷之中。
examples.pinyin: Xiāoxi chuán chū hòu, zhěng gè shèqū dōu lǒngzhào zài yī piàn bēishāng zhī zhōng.
examples.english: After the news broke, the entire community was enveloped in a wave of grief.

semanticNote: To hold or embrace someone with one's arms. 摟住 (hold/embrace tightly), 摟著孩子 (hold the child in one's arms), 摟抱 (hug). Implies warmth and physical closeness. More specific than 抱 (hug/hold) — often implies wrapping an arm sideways around someone. Very common in affectionate and parental contexts.

components.meaning: hug; hold close; embrace; clasp (扌 hand radical)

examples.chinese: 她見到多年未見的老友，立刻上前緊緊地摟住她。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiàn dào duō nián wèi jiàn de lǎoyǒu, lìkè shàngqián jǐnjǐn de lǒu zhù tā.
examples.english: When she saw her old friend she hadn't seen for many years, she immediately stepped forward and held her tightly.

examples.chinese: 爸爸把孩子摟在懷裡，輕聲安慰他不要害怕。
examples.pinyin: Bàba bǎ háizi lǒu zài huái lǐ, qīngshēng ānwèi tā bùyào hàipà.
examples.english: Dad held the child in his arms and gently reassured him not to be afraid.

english: kitchen range; cooking range; stovetop range
semanticNote: A kitchen stove or cooking range. In Taiwan, gas stoves (瓦斯爐) are dominant; 爐灶 is a slightly general or old-fashioned term for the cooking range setup. Key figurative use: 另起爐灶 (start from scratch; set up a new operation — lit. 'build a new stove').

components.meaning: kitchen stove; cooking range; kitchen god shrine

examples.chinese: 奶奶在舊式的磚砌爐灶上燒著柴火，煮出一鍋熱騰騰的稀飯。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zài jiùshì de zhuān qì lúzào shàng shāo zhe cháihuǒ, zhǔ chū yī guō rè téng téng de xīfàn.
examples.english: Grandma cooked over a wood-burning brick stove, producing a pot of steaming hot rice porridge.

examples.chinese: 他決定離開原本的公司，另起爐灶，自己創業。
examples.pinyin: Tā juédìng líkāi yuánběn de gōngsī, lìng qǐ lúzào, zìjǐ chuàngyè.
examples.english: He decided to leave his former company and start fresh, founding his own business.

semanticNote: Repeatedly and on multiple occasions. 屢次警告 (warned repeatedly), 屢次失敗 (fail time and again), 屢見不鮮 (seen repeatedly; nothing new — idiom). More formal and slightly literary than 一再 (again and again) or 多次 (multiple times). Emphasizes persistent or habitual action.

components.meaning: repeatedly; time after time; again and again
time; occasion; order; sequence; second (in quality)

examples.chinese: 他屢次違反規定，最終被公司辭退。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǚcì wéifǎn guīdìng, zuìzhōng bèi gōngsī cítuì.
examples.english: He repeatedly violated regulations and was ultimately dismissed by the company.

examples.chinese: 這個問題屢次被提出，卻始終沒有得到妥善解決。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí lǚcì bèi tíchū, què shǐzhōng méiyǒu dédào tuǒshàn jiějué.
examples.english: This issue has been raised time and again, yet it has never been properly resolved.

semanticNote: To fulfill or carry out obligations, duties, or promises. 履行義務 (fulfill one's obligations), 履行合約 (execute a contract), 履行職責 (carry out one's duties). Formal — common in legal, administrative, and diplomatic contexts. Stronger than 完成 (complete) — implies adherence to a formal commitment.

components.meaning: shoe; tread; walk; carry out; step through
walk; carry out; perform; OK; conduct

examples.chinese: 簽約後，雙方都必須嚴格履行合約中的各項條款。
examples.pinyin: Qiānyuē hòu, shuāngfāng dōu bìxū yángé lǚxíng héyuē zhōng de gè xiàng tiáokuǎn.
examples.english: After signing the contract, both parties must strictly fulfill all of its terms.

examples.chinese: 政治人物應兌現競選承諾，切實履行對選民的責任。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngzhì rénwù yīng duìxiàn jìngxuǎn chéngnuò, qièshí lǚxíng duì xuǎnmín de zérèn.
examples.english: Politicians should honor their campaign promises and genuinely fulfill their responsibilities to voters.

semanticNote: To plunder or rob by force — seizing resources, territory, or wealth. 掠奪資源 (plunder resources), 殖民掠奪 (colonial plunder). A strong, formal word with historical and political connotations. More literary than 搶奪 (snatch/grab). Common in historical, political, and environmental discourse.

components.meaning: seize; snatch; wrest; deprive; contend for

examples.chinese: 殖民統治期間，大量天然資源遭到掠奪，當地人民深受其苦。
examples.pinyin: Zhímín tǒngzhì qījiān, dàliàng tiānrán zīyuán zāodào lüèduó, dāngdì rénmín shēn shòu qí kǔ.
examples.english: During the colonial period, vast natural resources were plundered and the local people suffered greatly.

examples.chinese: 戰爭期間，士兵大肆掠奪民間財物，留下一片廢墟。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng qījiān, shìbīng dàsì lüèduó mínjiān cáiwù, liú xià yī piàn fèixū.
examples.english: During the war, soldiers plundered civilian property on a large scale, leaving behind ruins.

semanticNote: A steamship or large motor-powered vessel. 乘輪船 (take a ship), 輪船公司 (shipping company). 輪 refers to the wheel/propeller. In modern Taiwan, 輪船 is used broadly for large passenger and cargo ships; 渡輪 is specifically for ferries (like the Kinmen-Xiamen route or river crossings).

components.meaning: wheel; rim; propeller; take turns; round

examples.chinese: 在飛機普及之前，人們乘坐輪船橫渡大西洋需要一週以上。
examples.pinyin: Zài fēijī pǔjí zhīqián, rénmen chéngzuò lúnchuán héngdù Dàxīyáng xūyào yī zhōu yǐshàng.
examples.english: Before air travel became widespread, crossing the Atlantic by ship took over a week.

examples.chinese: 那艘輪船在暴風雨中失去了動力，發出求救信號。
examples.pinyin: Nà sōu lúnchuán zài bàofēngyǔ zhōng shīqù le dònglì, fāchū qiújiù xìnhào.
examples.english: The ship lost power in the storm and sent out a distress signal.

semanticNote: The outline, silhouette, or contour of something. 臉部輪廓 (facial contour), 大致輪廓 (general outline/overview), 初具輪廓 (has taken shape). Both literal (visual outline) and figurative (rough overview of a plan or idea).

examples.chinese: 霧中隱約可見山脈的輪廓，令人感到神秘。
examples.pinyin: Wù zhōng yǐnyuē kějiàn shānmài de lúnkuò, lìng rén gǎndào shénmì.
examples.english: Through the mist, the outline of the mountain range was faintly visible, giving it a mysterious quality.

examples.chinese: 計畫的大致輪廓已經確定，接下來是細節的落實。
examples.pinyin: Jìhuà de dàzhì lúnkuò yǐjīng quèdìng, jiē xià lái shì xìjié de luòshí.
examples.english: The general outline of the plan has been determined — next comes the implementation of the details.

semanticNote: A tire — the rubber ring around a wheel. 爆胎 (blowout; flat tire), 換輪胎 (change a tire), 輪胎氣壓 (tire pressure). In Taiwan, 爆胎 on the highway is a common road safety topic. 備胎 (spare tire).

components.meaning: fetus; embryo; the rubber layer of a tire

examples.chinese: 他開車途中突然爆胎，緊急靠邊停車換備胎。
examples.pinyin: Tā kāichē túzhōng tūrán bàotāi, jǐnjí kào biān tíngchē huàn bèitāi.
examples.english: While driving, he suddenly had a blowout and pulled over urgently to change the spare tire.

examples.chinese: 出發前記得檢查輪胎氣壓，確保行車安全。
examples.pinyin: Chūfā qián jìde jiǎnchá lúntāi qìyā, quèbǎo xíngchē ānquán.
examples.english: Before setting off, remember to check the tire pressure to ensure safe driving.

semanticNote: A forum — for public debate, academic discussion, or online exchange. 學術論壇 (academic forum), 網路論壇 (internet forum/message board), 國際論壇 (international forum). In Taiwan, PTT (批踢踢) is the most well-known online 論壇.

examples.chinese: 他在國際論壇上發表了一篇關於氣候變遷的演講，獲得廣泛迴響。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guójì lùntán shàng fābiǎo le yī piān guānyú qìhòu biànqiān de yǎnjiǎng, huòdé guǎngfàn huíxiǎng.
examples.english: He delivered a speech on climate change at an international forum and received wide response.

examples.chinese: 這個網路論壇聚集了許多熱愛語言學習的使用者，資訊交流非常活躍。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wǎnglù lùntán jùjí le xǔduō rè'ài yǔyán xuéxí de shǐyòngzhě, zīxùn jiāoliú fēicháng huóyuè.
examples.english: This online forum has gathered many users passionate about language learning, and information exchange is very active.

english: prove a point; expound on; argumentation
semanticNote: To establish a point through argument and evidence; also the process of argumentation itself. 充分論證 (fully argue/prove), 論證過程 (argumentation process), 無法論證 (cannot be proven). More structured than 討論 (discuss) — implies building a logical case. Common in academic, legal, and philosophical contexts.

examples.chinese: 他在論文中詳細論證了這項理論的可行性。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài lùnwén zhōng xiángxì lùnzhèng le zhè xiàng lǐlùn de kěxíngxìng.
examples.english: In his thesis, he argued the feasibility of this theory in detail.

examples.chinese: 辯論隊員必須用事實和邏輯來論證自己的立場，不能只憑感覺。
examples.pinyin: Biànlùn duìyuán bìxū yòng shìshí hé luójí lái lùnzhèng zìjǐ de lìchǎng, bùnéng zhǐ píng gǎnjué.
examples.english: Debate team members must use facts and logic to prove their position — they can't rely on feelings alone.

semanticNote: Long-winded, nagging, or unnecessarily complicated. 說話囉唆 (speak in a long-winded way), 別囉唆了 (stop your nagging/rambling). Similar to 嘮叨 (nag) but 囉唆 can also describe a situation as troublesome or fussy. Very common in spoken Mandarin.

examples.chinese: 他說話囉唆，講一件小事也要花半小時。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà luōsuo, jiǎng yī jiàn xiǎoshì yě yào huā bàn xiǎoshí.
examples.english: He's so long-winded — even a minor thing takes him half an hour to explain.

examples.chinese: 「好了，別囉唆了，直接說重點。」
examples.pinyin: "Hǎo le, bié luōsuo le, zhíjiē shuō zhòngdiǎn."
examples.english: "Alright, stop rambling — just get to the point."

semanticNote: An unceasing, continuous stream — of visitors, vehicles, tourists, or goods. 遊客絡繹不絕 (tourists come in an endless stream). Used to describe bustling activity. Positive or neutral in tone. Common in descriptions of busy tourist spots, markets, and events.

examples.chinese: 每逢假日，這條老街的遊客絡繹不絕，熱鬧非凡。
examples.pinyin: Měi féng jiàrì, zhè tiáo lǎojiē de yóukè luòyì-bùjué, rènào fēifán.
examples.english: On every holiday, tourists stream endlessly through this old street, making it extraordinarily lively.

examples.chinese: 開幕當天，前來參觀的民眾絡繹不絕，現場人聲鼎沸。
examples.pinyin: Kāimù dàngtiān, qián lái cānguān de mínzhòng luòyì-bùjué, xiànchǎng rénshēng-dǐngfèi.
examples.english: On opening day, visitors came in an endless stream and the venue was filled with the buzz of the crowd.

semanticNote: A building or structure has been completed and is ready for use. 大樓落成 (the building is completed), 落成典禮 (completion/inauguration ceremony). Applies only to buildings and construction projects — not used for other types of completion.

examples.chinese: 新的國立圖書館歷時五年終於落成，預計下個月對外開放。
examples.pinyin: Xīn de guólì túshūguǎn lìshí wǔ nián zhōngyú luòchéng, yùjì xià gè yuè duìwài kāifàng.
examples.english: The new national library took five years to complete and is expected to open to the public next month.

examples.chinese: 社區活動中心落成當天，居民們特地舉行了慶祝典禮。
examples.pinyin: Shèqū huódòng zhōngxīn luòchéng dàngtiān, jūmínmen tèdì jǔxíng le qìngzhù diǎnlǐ.
examples.english: On the day the community center was completed, residents held a special celebration ceremony.

semanticNote: To put something into concrete practice; to implement. 落實政策 (implement policy), 落實計畫 (carry out a plan). The opposite of talking without acting. A key governance and management term — implies translating words or plans into tangible results.

examples.chinese: 政策制定後，關鍵在於如何有效落實到基層。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngcè zhìdìng hòu, guānjiàn zàiyú rúhé yǒuxiào luòshí dào jīcéng.
examples.english: Once policy is formulated, the key is how to effectively implement it at the grassroots level.

examples.chinese: 他承諾會改善工作環境，但半年過去了，什麼都沒有落實。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngnuò huì gǎishàn gōngzuò huánjìng, dàn bànnián guò qù le, shénme dōu méiyǒu luòshí.
examples.english: He promised to improve the work environment, but half a year has passed without anything being put into practice.

semanticNote: Three senses: (1) physical paralysis or numbness — 下肢麻痺 (lower limb paralysis); (2) having lost sensitivity — become numb to; (3) cause someone to let down their guard — 麻痺敵人 (lull the enemy into complacency). The strategic 'drop one's guard' sense is a common political/military usage.

examples.chinese: 他中風後導致右半身麻痺，需要長期復健治療。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhòngfēng hòu dǎozhì yòu bàn shēn mábì, xūyào chángqī fùjiàn zhìliáo.
examples.english: After his stroke, he suffered paralysis on his right side and requires long-term rehabilitation.

examples.chinese: 長期的和平讓人們對潛在危機產生了麻痺感，失去了應有的警惕。
examples.pinyin: Chángqī de hépíng ràng rénmen duì qiánzài wēijī chǎnshēng le mábì gǎn, shīqù le yīngyǒu de jǐngtì.
examples.english: A long period of peace caused people to become numb to potential crises, losing the vigilance they should have maintained.

semanticNote: Physically numb (like a limb that has 'fallen asleep') or emotionally numb/unresponsive. 手腳麻木 (hands and feet are numb), 麻木不仁 (callously indifferent — a fixed phrase). The emotional sense — unable to feel or react — is very common.

examples.chinese: 長時間跪著之後，她的雙腿開始麻木，站都站不起來。
examples.pinyin: Cháng shíjiān guì zhe zhīhòu, tā de shuāng tuǐ kāishǐ mámù, zhàn dōu zhàn bù qǐlái.
examples.english: After kneeling for a long time, her legs became numb and she couldn't even stand up.

examples.chinese: 他對周遭的苦難麻木不仁，讓周圍的人感到寒心。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhōuzào de kǔnàn mámù bùrén, ràng zhōuwéi de rén gǎndào hánxīn.
examples.english: His callous indifference to the suffering around him chilled everyone near him.

semanticNote: Anesthesia — rendering insensible for surgery. 全身麻醉 (general anesthesia), 局部麻醉 (local anesthesia), 麻醉劑 (anesthetic). Also figurative: 用娛樂麻醉自己 (numb oneself with entertainment to escape reality). Common in medical and figurative contexts.

examples.chinese: 手術前，醫生為病患進行了全身麻醉，以確保手術順利進行。
examples.pinyin: Shǒushù qián, yīshēng wèi bìnghuàn jìnxíng le quánshēn mázuì, yǐ quèbǎo shǒushù shùnlì jìnxíng.
examples.english: Before the operation, the doctor administered general anesthesia to ensure the surgery proceeded smoothly.

examples.chinese: 他沉迷於電玩，彷彿用遊戲麻醉自己，逃避現實的壓力。
examples.pinyin: Tā chénmí yú diànwán, fǎngfú yòng yóuxì mázuì zìjǐ, táobì xiànshí de yālì.
examples.english: He was addicted to video games, as if numbing himself with play to escape real-world pressure.

semanticNote: A dock, wharf, or pier where ships load and unload. 輪渡碼頭 (ferry dock), 漁船碼頭 (fishing pier). In Taiwan: 基隆港碼頭 and 高雄港碼頭 are major cargo and passenger docks. Also used in informal/gangster contexts: 碼頭老大 (syndicate boss; dock boss).

examples.chinese: 漁民們清晨就趕到碼頭，準備出海捕魚。
examples.pinyin: Yúmínmen qīngchén jiù gǎn dào mǎtou, zhǔnbèi chūhǎi bǔyú.
examples.english: The fishermen rushed to the dock at dawn, preparing to head out to sea to fish.

examples.chinese: 基隆港碼頭是臺灣重要的貨物進出口樞紐。
examples.pinyin: Jīlóng gǎng mǎtou shì Táiwān zhòngyào de huòwù jìn chūkǒu shūniǔ.
examples.english: Keelung Port's docks are an important hub for Taiwan's import and export of goods.

semanticNote: An ant. 螞蟻搬家 (ants moving house — folk sign of coming rain; also: a slow, piecemeal operation). Figurative: 螞蟻雄兵 (army of ants — a large, united force of small people). Common in everyday and figurative speech about collective effort.

components.meaning: ant (蟲 insect radical + 馬 phonetic)

examples.chinese: 院子裡出現了一排螞蟻搬運食物，井然有序地回到蟻穴。
examples.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ chūxiàn le yī pái mǎyǐ bānyùn shíwù, jǐngrán yǒuxù de huí dào yǐxué.
examples.english: A line of ants appeared in the yard carrying food, returning to their nest in an orderly fashion.

examples.chinese: 每隻螞蟻體型微小，卻能搬動超過自身體重數十倍的重物。
examples.pinyin: Měi zhī mǎyǐ tǐxíng wēixiǎo, què néng bāndòng chāoguò zìshēn tǐzhòng shùshí bèi de zhòngwù.
examples.english: Each ant is tiny, yet it can carry objects dozens of times its own body weight.

english: (used to persuade somebody to do something); (particle indicating obviousness) | (colloqial) what?
semanticNote: Sentence-final particle with two main functions: (1) indicating something is obvious or self-evident — 就是這樣嘛 (it's obviously just like that); (2) softening a request or coaxing — 你幫我一下嘛 (come on, just help me). More affectionate and coaxing in register. Very common in spoken Mandarin and Taiwan Chinese.

components.meaning: sentence-final obviousness/coaxing particle (口 mouth + 麻 phonetic)

examples.chinese: 「你不是說要早點回家嘛，怎麼還在這裡？」
examples.pinyin: "Nǐ bùshì shuō yào zǎo diǎn huí jiā ma, zěnme hái zài zhèlǐ?"
examples.english: "Didn't you say you'd come home early? Why are you still here?"

examples.chinese: 「幫我一個忙嘛，就這一次，好不好？」
examples.pinyin: "Bāng wǒ yī gè máng ma, jiù zhè yī cì, hǎo bù hǎo?"
examples.english: "Do me a favor, just this once, okay?"

semanticNote: To lie in ambush; an ambush. 設埋伏 (set an ambush), 中了埋伏 (walked into an ambush), 埋伏圈 (the ambush zone). Military and thriller contexts primarily. Also used colloquially for any hidden trap or surprise waiting to be sprung.

components.meaning: lie down; ambush; hide; subdue; submit

examples.chinese: 士兵們提前埋伏在山谷兩側，等待敵軍通過。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīngmen tíqián máifu zài shāngǔ liǎng cè, děngdài díjūn tōngguò.
examples.english: The soldiers lay in ambush on both sides of the valley, waiting for the enemy troops to pass through.

examples.chinese: 警方事先掌握情報，在嫌犯必經路口設下埋伏，將其一舉逮捕。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng shìxiān zhǎngwò qínggào, zài xiánfàn bì jīng lùkǒu shè xià máifu, jiāng qí yījǔ dàibǔ.
examples.english: The police obtained intelligence in advance and set an ambush at an intersection the suspect had to pass, capturing him in one move.

semanticNote: To bury under or cause to disappear; to neglect or waste potential. 埋沒人才 (waste/overlook talent), 被埋沒的英雄 (unsung hero). Physical burial exists but the figurative sense — talent going unrecognized — is far more common in everyday usage.

examples.chinese: 他的才華長期被埋沒，直到一位伯樂出現才讓他大放異彩。
examples.pinyin: Tā de cáihuá chángqī bèi máimò, zhídào yī wèi bólè chūxiàn cái ràng tā dàfàng yìcǎi.
examples.english: His talent was buried for a long time — it wasn't until a perceptive mentor appeared that he was able to shine.

examples.chinese: 這位詩人生前默默無聞，死後作品才被發現，終未被歷史埋沒。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi shīrén shēng qián mòmò wúwén, sǐ hòu zuòpǐn cái bèi fāxiàn, zhōng wèi bèi lìshǐ máimò.
examples.english: This poet was obscure during his lifetime — his works were only discovered after his death, but he was not ultimately forgotten by history.

semanticNote: To bury a body; to inter. Also figurative: 埋葬舊制度 (bury the old system — completely done away with), 埋葬過去 (bury the past). Stronger and more final than 安葬 (lay to rest, which implies reverence). Used in both literal and powerful figurative contexts.
