examples.chinese: 許多遊客前往中正紀念堂瞻仰歷史文物。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō yóukè qiánwǎng Zhōngzhèng Jìniàntáng zhānyǎng lìshǐ wénwù.
examples.english: Many tourists visit the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall to reverently view historical artifacts.

english: to chop the nail and slice the iron (idiom); resolute and decisive; definitely
semanticNote: Chengyu meaning 'resolute and decisive; speaking firmly without hesitation' — literally 'chopping through nails and cutting through iron,' used to describe someone speaking or acting with absolute certainty and firmness, leaving no room for doubt (斬釘截鐵地拒絕, decisively/firmly refuse). Common when praising or describing someone's decisive, unwavering manner of speech, especially in negotiations or firm refusals.

examples.chinese: 面對誘惑,他斬釘截鐵地拒絕了對方的提議。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì yòuhuò, tā zhǎndīngjiétiě de jùjuéle duìfāng de tíyì.
examples.english: Facing temptation, he firmly and decisively refused the other party's proposal.

examples.chinese: 她斬釘截鐵地表示,這件事絕對沒有商量的餘地。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǎndīngjiétiě de biǎoshì, zhè jiàn shì juéduì méiyǒu shāngliáng de yúdì.
examples.english: She stated firmly and decisively that there was absolutely no room for negotiation on this matter.

semanticNote: 'To display; to exhibit; to showcase' — used for presenting something openly for others to see, whether physical objects (展示新產品, showcase new products) or abstract qualities (展示才華, display one's talent). Common in retail, exhibition, and presentation contexts, implying an intentional act of showing something to an audience.

examples.chinese: 這場車展展示了各大廠牌最新的車款。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng chēzhǎn zhǎnshìle gèdà chǎngpái zuìxīn de chēkuǎn.
examples.english: This auto show displayed the latest models from major manufacturers.

examples.chinese: 選手們在舞台上展示了精湛的舞技。
examples.pinyin: Xuǎnshǒumen zài wǔtái shàng zhǎnshìle jīngzhàn de wǔjì.
examples.english: The competitors showcased their exquisite dance skills on stage.

english: outlook; prospect; to look ahead; look forward to
semanticNote: 'To look ahead; outlook; prospect (for the future)' — used for forward-looking assessment of future possibilities, common in business, economic, and personal planning contexts (未來展望, future outlook; 展望明年, look ahead to next year). Positive and forward-thinking in tone, common in year-end reviews and strategic planning documents.

examples.chinese: 分析師對明年的經濟展望持樂觀態度。
examples.pinyin: Fēnxīshī duì míngnián de jīngjì zhǎnwàng chí lèguān tàidù.
examples.english: Analysts hold an optimistic attitude toward next year's economic outlook.

examples.chinese: 展望未來,公司計畫開拓海外市場。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎnwàng wèilái, gōngsī jìhuà kāità hǎiwài shìchǎng.
examples.english: Looking ahead, the company plans to expand into overseas markets.

semanticNote: 'To reveal; to manifest; to unfold (before one's eyes)' — used for something gradually or vividly coming into view or being expressed, whether visually (展現在眼前, unfold before one's eyes) or as a quality being demonstrated (展現實力, demonstrate/reveal one's ability). Similar to 展示 but 展現 leans slightly more toward something naturally emerging or being revealed, rather than being deliberately put on display.

examples.chinese: 登上山頂那一刻,壯麗的美景展現在眼前。
examples.pinyin: Dēngshàng shāndǐng nà yíkè, zhuànglì de měijǐng zhǎnxiàn zài yǎnqián.
examples.english: The moment he reached the summit, a magnificent view unfolded before his eyes.

examples.chinese: 這位新人在比賽中展現了驚人的實力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi xīnrén zài bǐsài zhōng zhǎnxiànle jīngrén de shílì.
examples.english: This newcomer revealed astonishing ability in the competition.

semanticNote: 'Brand new; entirely fresh (with a sense of newness/renewal)' — a stronger, more evocative version of 新 (new), often emphasizing a fresh start or significant change (嶄新的開始, a brand-new start; 嶄新的面貌, an entirely new/transformed appearance). Common in motivational and transformational contexts describing renewal or a fresh chapter, rather than simply describing a newly purchased item.

examples.chinese: 搬到新城市後,他展開了嶄新的人生篇章。
examples.pinyin: Bāndào xīn chéngshì hòu, tā zhǎnkāile zhǎnxīn de rénshēng piānzhāng.
examples.english: After moving to a new city, he began an entirely new chapter of his life.

examples.chinese: 經過整修,這間老屋煥然一新,呈現出嶄新的樣貌。
examples.pinyin: Jīngguò zhěngxiū, zhè jiān lǎowū huànrányīxīn, chéngxiàn chū zhǎnxīn de yàngmào.
examples.english: After renovation, this old house was completely transformed, presenting a brand-new appearance.

semanticNote: 'To occupy; to take up (space, position, or time)' — used for taking possession of space, a position, or a share of something (占據市場, occupy/dominate a market; 占據重要地位, occupy an important position). Neutral-to-assertive in tone, common in business, geography, and abstract discussions of dominance or share.

examples.chinese: 這家公司在市場中占據了主導地位。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zài shìchǎng zhōng zhànjùle zhǔdǎo dìwèi.
examples.english: This company occupies a dominant position in the market.

examples.chinese: 手機占據了現代人生活中極大一部分的時間。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī zhànjùle xiàndàirén shēnghuó zhōng jídà yíbùfèn de shíjiān.
examples.english: Cell phones occupy a very large portion of modern people's daily time.

semanticNote: 'To occupy (militarily); to capture territory' — a strong, specifically military/political term for taking control of a location by force (占領城市, occupy a city; 軍隊占領, military occupation). More forceful and specifically territorial than 占據 (occupy space/position, can be neutral/business) — 占領 implies conquest or forceful control, common in history and current-events discussions of conflict.

examples.chinese: 這座城市在戰爭期間曾被敵軍占領。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì zài zhànzhēng qíjiān céng bèi díjūn zhànlǐng.
examples.english: This city was once occupied by enemy forces during the war.

examples.chinese: 軍隊迅速占領了敵方的重要據點。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì xùnsù zhànlǐngle dífāng de zhòngyào jùdiǎn.
examples.english: The army swiftly captured the enemy's important strategic position.

english: to fight; to battle; to struggle
semanticNote: 'To fight; to battle; a battle/combat' — the standard military term for armed combat (激烈的戰鬥, intense fighting/battle), also extended figuratively for a fierce struggle or competitive effort (為理想而戰鬥, fight for one's ideals). Distinct from 戰爭 (war, the overall conflict) — 戰鬥 refers to a specific engagement or fight, whether military or metaphorical.

examples.chinese: 士兵們在前線與敵軍展開激烈戰鬥。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīngmen zài qiánxiàn yǔ díjūn zhǎnkāi jīliè zhàndòu.
examples.english: The soldiers engaged in intense combat with enemy forces at the front lines.

examples.chinese: 他把每一次考試都當作一場戰鬥來全力以赴。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ měi yí cì kǎoshì dōu dàngzuò yì chǎng zhàndòu lái quánlìyǐfù.
examples.english: He treats every exam as a battle and gives it his all.

semanticNote: 'Strategy (broad, long-term)' — refers to overarching, long-term planning toward a major goal, whether military (軍事戰略, military strategy) or business (企業戰略, corporate strategy). Distinct from 戰術 (tactics, the specific short-term methods used to execute the strategy) — 戰略 is the big-picture plan, 戰術 is the specific execution, a distinction commonly discussed in both military history and business management contexts.

examples.chinese: 公司調整了長期發展戰略,轉向數位化服務。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī tiáozhěngle chángqí fāzhǎn zhànlüè, zhuǎnxiàng shùwèihuà fúwù.
examples.english: The company adjusted its long-term development strategy, shifting toward digital services.

examples.chinese: 這場戰爭的勝負,取決於雙方的戰略布局。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng zhànzhēng de shèngfù, qǔjué yú shuāngfāng de zhànlüè bùjú.
examples.english: The outcome of this war depends on both sides' strategic positioning.

semanticNote: 'Tactics (specific, short-term methods)' — refers to the concrete methods used to achieve a goal within a broader strategy, common in military, sports, and business contexts (球隊戰術, team's game tactics; 銷售戰術, sales tactics). Paired conceptually with 戰略 (strategy, the big-picture plan) — 戰術 is the on-the-ground execution, common in sports commentary discussing a team's in-game approach.

examples.chinese: 教練在中場休息時調整了球隊的進攻戰術。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zài zhōngchǎng xiūxi shí tiáozhěngle qiúduì de jìngōng zhànshù.
examples.english: The coach adjusted the team's offensive tactics during halftime.

examples.chinese: 這家公司採取了低價競爭的戰術來搶占市場。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī cǎiqǔle dījià jìngzhēng de zhànshù lái qiǎngzhàn shìchǎng.
examples.english: This company adopted low-price competition tactics to seize market share.

semanticNote: 'Military campaign; battle (a defined engagement within a larger war)' — a formal military history term for a specific, named engagement (諾曼第戰役, the Normandy campaign), also used figuratively for a major, defined effort or struggle (行銷戰役, a marketing campaign — a common business metaphor). Distinct from 戰爭 (the overall war) and 戰鬥 (a fight/combat generally) — 戰役 specifically refers to a bounded, often historically named engagement.

examples.chinese: 這場戰役被視為二戰的轉捩點。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng zhànyì bèi shìwéi Èrzhàn de zhuǎnlìdiǎn.
examples.english: This battle is regarded as the turning point of World War II.

examples.chinese: 公司將這次的產品發表會視為一場重要的行銷戰役。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī jiāng zhè cì de chǎnpǐn fābiǎohuì shìwéi yì chǎng zhòngyào de xíngxiāo zhànyì.
examples.english: The company treats this product launch as an important marketing campaign.

english: written rules; statute; regulations; charter of a corporation
semanticNote: 'Charter; bylaws; written statutes (of an organization)' — a formal legal/organizational document outlining an institution's rules and governance structure (公司章程, company bylaws/articles of incorporation; 協會章程, association charter). Standard vocabulary in business, nonprofit, and legal contexts where organizational governance documents are discussed.

examples.chinese: 公司章程明訂董事會的組成與職權。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zhāngchéng míngdìng dǒngshìhuì de zǔchéng yǔ zhíquán.
examples.english: The company's bylaws clearly stipulate the board of directors' composition and authority.

examples.chinese: 修改協會章程需經全體會員表決通過。
examples.pinyin: Xiūgǎi xiéhuì zhāngchéng xū jīng quántǐ huìyuán biǎojué tōngguò.
examples.english: Amending the association's charter requires a vote passed by all members.

semanticNote: 'Tent' — standard outdoor/camping vocabulary (搭帳篷, pitch a tent; 露營帳篷, camping tent). Common in the context of Taiwan's popular camping culture (露營), as well as in disaster-relief contexts (臨時帳篷, temporary tent shelters set up after earthquakes or typhoons).

examples.chinese: 他們花了將近半小時才把帳篷搭好。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen huāle jiāngjìn bàn xiǎoshí cái bǎ zhàngpeng dāhǎo.
examples.english: It took them nearly half an hour to finish pitching the tent.

examples.chinese: 地震發生後,災民暫時住在臨時搭建的帳篷裡。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn fāshēng hòu, zāimín zhànshí zhù zài línshí dājiàn de zhàngpeng lǐ.
examples.english: After the earthquake, disaster victims temporarily lived in makeshift tents.

semanticNote: 'Barrier; obstacle; impediment' — used for both physical obstacles (交通障礙, traffic obstruction) and abstract ones blocking progress (語言障礙, language barrier; 心理障礙, psychological barrier/hang-up). Standard, versatile vocabulary common across discussions of accessibility, communication, and personal or organizational challenges.

examples.chinese: 剛到國外時,語言障礙讓他吃了不少苦頭。
examples.pinyin: Gāng dào guówài shí, yǔyán zhàng'ài ràng tā chīle bùshǎo kǔtóu.
examples.english: When he first went abroad, the language barrier gave him a lot of trouble.

examples.chinese: 這座建築設有無障礙坡道,方便輪椅使用者進出。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiànzhú shèyǒu wúzhàng'ài pōdào, fāngbiàn lúnyǐ shǐyòngzhě jìnchū.
examples.english: This building has a barrier-free ramp, making it convenient for wheelchair users to enter and exit.

semanticNote: 'To invite bids; to put out to tender' — a formal business/government procurement term for soliciting competitive bids from contractors or suppliers (公開招標, open/public tender; 招標案, a tender/bidding case). Common in government contracting and construction industry news in Taiwan, where public infrastructure projects must legally go through formal 招標 processes.

examples.chinese: 政府針對這項公共工程進行公開招標。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhēnduì zhè xiàng gōnggòng gōngchéng jìnxíng gōngkāi zhāobiāo.
examples.english: The government conducted an open tender for this public infrastructure project.

examples.chinese: 這家營造公司順利標得了招標案。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yíngzào gōngsī shùnlì biāo déle zhāobiāo'àn.
examples.english: This construction company successfully won the bid for the tender.

semanticNote: 'To recruit; to enroll; to take in (new members/students/employees)' — used for formally admitting new participants into an institution, program, or organization (招收新生, enroll new students; 招收員工, recruit employees). Standard vocabulary in education and HR contexts, common in admissions and hiring announcements.

examples.chinese: 這所大學今年首次招收國際學生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ dàxué jīnnián shǒucì zhāoshōu guójì xuéshēng.
examples.english: This university is recruiting international students for the first time this year.

examples.chinese: 公司正在招收具有相關經驗的新進工程師。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèngzài zhāoshōu jùyǒu xiāngguān jīngyàn de xīnjìn gōngchéngshī.
examples.english: The company is currently recruiting new engineers with relevant experience.

english: full of youthful energy (idiom); full of vigour and vitality; energetic; spirited; a bright spark
semanticNote: Chengyu meaning 'full of youthful vigor and vitality; energetic and spirited' — describes a person or group radiating fresh energy and enthusiasm, often associated with youth or a fresh start (朝氣蓬勃的年輕人, youthful, energetic young people). Positive, upbeat description common in contexts praising a vibrant atmosphere, whether describing individuals, teams, or a lively environment like a school or startup.

examples.chinese: 校園裡到處是朝氣蓬勃的學生,充滿活力。
examples.pinyin: Xiàoyuán lǐ dàochù shì zhāoqìpéngbó de xuéshēng, chōngmǎn huólì.
examples.english: The campus is full of youthful, energetic students bursting with vitality.

examples.chinese: 這間新創公司的團隊個個朝氣蓬勃,充滿幹勁。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān xīnchuàng gōngsī de tuánduì gège zhāoqìpéngbó, chōngmǎn gànjìn.
examples.english: This startup's team is full of youthful energy, every member bursting with drive.

semanticNote: 'To be fascinated; to become captivated/obsessed with' — describes being drawn deeply into something enjoyable to the point of preoccupation (對電玩著迷, be fascinated/hooked on video games). Similar to 沉迷 but 著迷 is generally milder and more neutral-to-positive, describing genuine enthrallment rather than the more negative 'addiction' connotation that 沉迷 can carry.

examples.chinese: 他從小就對天文學十分著迷。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù duì tiānwénxué shífēn zháomí.
examples.english: He has been deeply fascinated by astronomy since he was young.

examples.chinese: 這部小說情節精彩,讓讀者看得十分著迷。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō qíngjié jīngcǎi, ràng dúzhě kàn de shífēn zháomí.
examples.english: This novel's plot is so exciting that it thoroughly captivates readers.

semanticNote: 'Marsh; swamp; wetland' — the standard geographic/ecological term for waterlogged land (沼澤地, marshland; 濕地生態, wetland ecology, a related environmental term). Common in discussions of environmental conservation and geography, including Taiwan's own wetland reserves important for migratory bird habitats.

examples.chinese: 這片沼澤地是候鳥度冬的重要棲地。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piàn zhǎozédì shì hòuniǎo dùdōng de zhòngyào qīdì.
examples.english: This marshland is an important habitat for migratory birds wintering here.

examples.chinese: 探險隊小心翼翼地穿越危險的沼澤地帶。
examples.pinyin: Tànxiǎnduì xiǎoxīn yìyì de chuānyuè wéixiǎn de zhǎozé dìdài.
examples.english: The expedition team carefully made their way through the dangerous swamp area.

semanticNote: 'As before; just the same; still (despite circumstances)' — used to indicate that something continues unchanged despite an expected reason for it to change (雖然生病,他照樣去上班, although he's sick, he still went to work as usual). Common in everyday speech to express that a habit or state persisted despite some obstacle or change in circumstance.

examples.chinese: 雖然下著大雨,他照樣準時出門上班。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán xiàzhe dàyǔ, tā zhàoyàng zhǔnshí chūmén shàngbān.
examples.english: Even though it was pouring rain, he still left for work on time as usual.

examples.chinese: 就算被拒絕了好幾次,他照樣不放棄追求夢想。
examples.pinyin: Jiùsuàn bèi jùjuéle hǎojǐ cì, tā zhàoyàng bú fàngqì zhuīqiú mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: Even after being rejected several times, he still didn't give up pursuing his dream.

semanticNote: 'To shine (upon); to illuminate brightly' — used for light, especially sunlight, shining brightly over a wide area (陽光照耀大地, sunlight shines upon the land). More vivid and literary than the plain 照 (shine/light) — 照耀 conveys a broad, radiant illumination, common in descriptive and poetic writing about natural light.

examples.chinese: 溫暖的陽光照耀著整片稻田。
examples.pinyin: Wēnnuǎn de yángguāng zhàoyàozhe zhěng piàn dàotián.
examples.english: The warm sunlight shines upon the entire rice field.

examples.chinese: 月光照耀下的湖面,顯得格外寧靜美麗。
examples.pinyin: Yuèguāng zhàoyào xià de húmiàn, xiǎnde géwài níngjìng měilì.
examples.english: The lake's surface, illuminated by moonlight, appeared exceptionally tranquil and beautiful.

english: toss from side to side (e.g. sleeplessly); do something over and over again; cause suffering; play crazy; screw around
semanticNote: 'To toss and turn; to fuss over repeatedly; to put someone through the wringer' — a colloquial term for repetitive, exhausting activity or being subjected to a troublesome, drawn-out process (折騰了一整晚, tossed and turned all night; 別再折騰了, stop messing around/causing trouble). Common in casual complaints about exhausting bureaucratic processes, sleepless nights, or someone causing unnecessary hassle.

examples.chinese: 寶寶昨晚生病,折騰了媽媽一整夜沒睡。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobǎo zuówǎn shēngbìng, zhēteng le māma yì zhěngyè méi shuì.
examples.english: The baby was sick last night and kept his mom up the whole night.

examples.chinese: 為了辦這個證件,他被折騰得跑了好幾趟公家機關。
examples.pinyin: Wèile bàn zhè ge zhèngjiàn, tā bèi zhēteng de pǎole hǎojǐ tàng gōngjiā jīguān.
examples.english: In order to process this document, he was put through the wringer, having to run to government offices several times.

semanticNote: 'To block; to shield from; to obstruct (view or light)' — describes physically blocking something from passing through, whether sunlight, wind, or a line of sight (遮擋陽光, block/shield from sunlight; 視線遭到遮擋, one's view is obstructed). Common in practical, everyday descriptions of physical obstruction, distinct from 掩蓋 (cover up facts) — 遮擋 is purely physical/visual blocking.

examples.chinese: 他撐傘遮擋刺眼的陽光。
examples.pinyin: Tā chēngsǎn zhēdǎng cìyǎn de yángguāng.
examples.english: He held up an umbrella to block the glaring sunlight.

examples.chinese: 路邊的大樹遮擋了店家的招牌,不容易被看見。
examples.pinyin: Lùbiān de dàshù zhēdǎngle diànjiā de zhāopái, bù róngyì bèi kànjiàn.
examples.english: The large tree by the roadside blocks the shop's sign, making it hard to see.

english: to break; to fracture; convert into; to fold
semanticNote: 'To break; to fold; to convert (into a discount/percentage)' — used for physical breaking/folding (骨折, bone fracture; 對折, fold in half) and, very commonly in Taiwan retail, for discounts expressed as tenths (打八折, 20% off — literally 'strike an 8-fold discount,' meaning pay 80% of the price). Understanding the 折 discount system is essential practical shopping vocabulary in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 他不小心摔倒,造成手臂骨折。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn shuāidǎo, zàochéng shǒubì gǔzhé.
examples.english: He accidentally fell and fractured his arm.

examples.chinese: 這件外套現在打七折,原價的百分之七十。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn wàitào xiànzài dǎ qī zhé, yuánjià de bǎifēnzhī qīshí.
examples.english: This jacket is now 30% off, meaning 70% of the original price.

semanticNote: 'To torment; to torture (physically or emotionally); torment' — describes prolonged, severe suffering, whether physical (病痛的折磨, the torment of illness/pain) or psychological (精神折磨, mental/emotional torment). Strong, serious vocabulary implying deep, sustained anguish, common in discussions of chronic illness, grief, and emotional hardship.

examples.chinese: 長期失眠的折磨讓他身心俱疲。
examples.pinyin: Chángqí shīmián de zhémo ràng tā shēnxīn jùpí.
examples.english: The prolonged torment of insomnia has left him exhausted physically and mentally.

examples.chinese: 失去至親的悲痛,折磨了她好長一段時間。
examples.pinyin: Shīqù zhìqīn de bēitòng, zhémole tā hǎo cháng yíduàn shíjiān.
examples.english: The grief of losing a close family member tormented her for a long time.

semanticNote: 'Detective' — refers to someone who investigates crimes or mysteries, whether professionally (私家偵探, private detective) or as a fictional genre archetype (偵探小說, detective fiction, a popular literary and film genre). Standard vocabulary for discussing mystery/crime genre entertainment and, less commonly in Taiwan (where private investigation has legal restrictions), real investigative professionals.

examples.chinese: 他從小就很喜歡看福爾摩斯這類的偵探小說。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù hěn xǐhuan kàn Fú'ěrmósī zhè lèi de zhēntàn xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: He's loved reading detective novels like Sherlock Holmes since he was a child.

examples.chinese: 劇中的偵探憑著細微的線索破解了謎案。
examples.pinyin: Jù zhōng de zhēntàn píngzhe xìwēi de xiànsuǒ pòjiěle mí'àn.
examples.english: The detective in the drama solved the mystery case relying on subtle clues.

semanticNote: 'Precious; valuable (often sentimentally or historically)' — describes something of great value, whether material (珍貴的文物, precious artifacts) or emotional/relational (珍貴的回憶, precious memories; 珍貴的友誼, a precious friendship). Broader than 昂貴 (expensive, purely monetary) — 珍貴 emphasizes worth that may not be purely financial, often sentimental or irreplaceable.

examples.chinese: 這些老照片是他最珍貴的回憶。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē lǎo zhàopiàn shì tā zuì zhēnguì de huíyì.
examples.english: These old photos are his most precious memories.

examples.chinese: 博物館收藏了許多珍貴的歷史文物。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn shōucángle xǔduō zhēnguì de lìshǐ wénwù.
examples.english: The museum has collected many precious historical artifacts.

semanticNote: 'Rare and precious (especially of endangered species or scarce resources)' — commonly used in conservation and biology contexts to describe endangered or scarce plants/animals (珍稀動物, rare/endangered animal; 珍稀植物, rare plant species). More specific to biological/natural rarity than the broader 珍貴 (precious, can apply to anything valuable) — 珍稀 emphasizes scarcity in nature specifically.

examples.chinese: 台灣黑熊是台灣特有的珍稀保育動物。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān hēixióng shì Táiwān tèyǒu de zhēnxī bǎoyù dòngwù.
examples.english: The Formosan black bear is a rare, protected animal unique to Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 這座森林保護區是許多珍稀植物的棲息地。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò sēnlín bǎohùqū shì xǔduō zhēnxī zhíwù de qīxīdì.
examples.english: This forest reserve is a habitat for many rare plant species.

semanticNote: 'Pearl' — the standard term for pearls used in jewelry and, notably, as the namesake ingredient in 珍珠奶茶 (bubble/pearl milk tea), one of Taiwan's most famous culinary exports, where 珍珠 refers to the chewy tapioca balls resembling pearls. Both the literal gemstone sense and the food-culture sense are essential vocabulary in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 她戴著一條珍珠項鍊出席晚宴。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàizhe yì tiáo zhēnzhū xiàngliàn chūxí wǎnyàn.
examples.english: She wore a pearl necklace to attend the evening banquet.

examples.chinese: 珍珠奶茶是台灣最具代表性的飲料之一。
examples.pinyin: Zhēnzhū nǎichá shì Táiwān zuì jù dàibiǎoxìng de yǐnliào zhī yī.
examples.english: Bubble milk tea (pearl milk tea) is one of Taiwan's most representative beverages.

semanticNote: 'Truth (universal/philosophical, not just a fact)' — refers to a fundamental, universally valid truth, often in philosophical, scientific, or religious contexts (追求真理, pursue truth; 真理是不變的, truth is unchanging). More elevated and abstract than 事實 (fact, a specific concrete piece of information) — 真理 implies a deep, often timeless principle rather than a single verifiable fact.

examples.chinese: 科學家窮盡一生追求自然界的真理。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā qióngjìn yìshēng zhuīqiú zìránjiè de zhēnlǐ.
examples.english: The scientist devoted his entire life to pursuing the truths of the natural world.

examples.chinese: 有些哲學家認為,真理是不會隨時間改變的。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē zhéxuéjiā rènwéi, zhēnlǐ shì búhuì suí shíjiān gǎibiàn de.
examples.english: Some philosophers believe that truth doesn't change with time.

semanticNote: 'The truth; the actual facts (of a specific situation, especially one that was hidden or unclear)' — refers to the real facts behind a specific event or mystery, often after confusion, deception, or investigation (真相大白, the truth comes to light; 事情的真相, the truth of the matter). Distinct from the more abstract/philosophical 真理 (universal truth) — 真相 is concrete and situational, common in news about scandals, crimes, and mysteries being resolved.

examples.chinese: 經過警方調查,案件的真相終於水落石出。
examples.pinyin: Jīngguò jǐngfāng diàochá, ànjiàn de zhēnxiàng zhōngyú shuǐluòshíchū.
examples.english: After police investigation, the truth of the case finally came to light.

examples.chinese: 他決定站出來揭露事件的真相。
examples.pinyin: Tā juédìng zhàn chūlái jiēlù shìjiàn de zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: He decided to come forward and expose the truth behind the incident.

semanticNote: 'Sincere; genuine (of feelings, especially affection or friendship)' — describes deeply heartfelt, unpretentious emotion, particularly in relationships (真摯的友誼, sincere friendship; 真摯的感情, genuine affection). More elevated and literary than the everyday 真心 — 真摯 often appears in formal speeches, tributes, and written expressions of heartfelt sentiment.

examples.chinese: 他們兩人之間有著真摯而深厚的友誼。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎng rén zhījiān yǒuzhe zhēnzhì ér shēnhòu de yǒuyì.
examples.english: There is a sincere and deep friendship between the two of them.

examples.chinese: 他在信中表達了對老師真摯的感激之情。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài xìn zhōng biǎodále duì lǎoshī zhēnzhì de gǎnjī zhī qíng.
examples.english: In the letter, he expressed his sincere gratitude toward his teacher.

semanticNote: 'To deliberate; to carefully consider (weighing options before deciding, especially on wording)' — used for the careful, considered process of choosing words or making a decision, often implying a nuanced judgment call rather than a simple choice (斟酌用詞, carefully weigh one's word choice; 仔細斟酌, deliberate carefully). Common in professional writing, editing, and formal decision-making contexts.

examples.chinese: 撰寫正式信函時,用詞需要仔細斟酌。
examples.pinyin: Zhuànxiě zhèngshì xìnhán shí, yòngcí xūyào xìjí zhēnzhuó.
examples.english: When writing a formal letter, word choice needs to be carefully considered.

examples.chinese: 面對這項重大決定,他花了好幾天時間反覆斟酌。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì zhè xiàng zhòngdà juédìng, tā huāle hǎojǐ tiān shíjiān fǎnfù zhēnzhuó.
examples.english: Facing this major decision, he spent several days deliberating over it repeatedly.

semanticNote: 'Pillow' — basic everyday household vocabulary (枕頭套, pillowcase; 抱枕, throw/hug pillow). No significant register variation; standard vocabulary across all contexts involving bedding and sleep.

examples.chinese: 這個枕頭太軟了,讓他的脖子有些不舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zhěntou tài ruǎn le, ràng tā de bózi yǒuxiē bù shūfu.
examples.english: This pillow is too soft, and it's making his neck a bit uncomfortable.

examples.chinese: 她抱著抱枕坐在沙發上看電視。
examples.pinyin: Tā bàozhe bàozhěn zuò zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì.
examples.english: She sat on the sofa hugging a throw pillow, watching TV.

semanticNote: '(Military) position; battlefront' — a formal military term for a defended location or front line (防守陣地, defensive position; 堅守陣地, hold one's position). Also extended figuratively for a stronghold or key position in a non-military struggle (輿論陣地, a position/stronghold in public opinion discourse). Common in military history and, figuratively, in describing strategic footholds in competitive contexts.

examples.chinese: 士兵們奮力堅守自己的陣地。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīngmen fènlì jiānshǒu zìjǐ de zhèndì.
examples.english: The soldiers fought hard to hold their position.

examples.chinese: 這家媒體長期占據著輿論的重要陣地。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā méitǐ chángqí zhànjùzhe yúlùn de zhòngyào zhèndì.
examples.english: This media outlet has long occupied an important position in shaping public opinion.

semanticNote: 'Lineup; formation (of a team, cast, or group)' — refers to the composition and arrangement of members in a group, especially in sports (球隊陣容, team lineup) and entertainment (演員陣容, cast lineup). Common in sports commentary and entertainment news discussing who makes up a team or production.

examples.chinese: 這部電影集結了眾多明星,陣容十分堅強。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jíjiéle zhòngduō míngxīng, zhènróng shífēn jiānqiáng.
examples.english: This movie brings together many stars — the lineup/cast is very strong.

examples.chinese: 教練調整了球隊的先發陣容。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoliàn tiáozhěngle qiúduì de xiānfā zhènróng.
examples.english: The coach adjusted the team's starting lineup.

english: stir oneself up; raise one's spirits; inspire
semanticNote: 'To be invigorated; to stir up excitement/spirit; uplifted' — describes a surge of positive energy or morale, often in response to good news or inspiring events (振奮人心, uplifting/inspiring — a common set phrase describing news or events that boost morale). Positive, energizing vocabulary common in describing collective reactions to good news or motivational moments.

examples.chinese: 選手奪冠的消息振奮了全國人心。
examples.pinyin: Xuǎnshǒu duóguàn de xiāoxi zhènfènle quánguó rénxīn.
examples.english: The news of the athlete winning the championship uplifted the spirits of the entire nation.

examples.chinese: 聽了這場演講,他感到十分振奮,充滿了幹勁。
examples.pinyin: Tīngle zhè chǎng yǎnjiǎng, tā gǎndào shífēn zhènfèn, chōngmǎnle gànjìn.
examples.english: After hearing this speech, he felt greatly invigorated and full of drive.

english: develop vigorously; promote; revive; revitalize; invigorate; re-energize
semanticNote: 'To revitalize; to reinvigorate; to promote vigorous development (of an economy, industry, or culture)' — used for actively bringing renewed vitality to something in decline, especially at a national or industry level (振興經濟, revitalize the economy; 振興觀光, boost/revitalize tourism — a common government policy term in Taiwan, e.g. 振興券, stimulus/revitalization vouchers). Common in economic policy discussions.

examples.chinese: 政府推出振興券,希望帶動國內消費。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ tuīchū zhènxīngquàn, xīwàng dàidòng guónèi xiāofèi.
examples.english: The government launched stimulus vouchers, hoping to boost domestic spending.

examples.chinese: 地方政府努力振興傳統產業,創造更多就業機會。
examples.pinyin: Dìfāng zhèngfǔ nǔlì zhènxīng chuántǒng chǎnyè, chuàngzào gèng duō jiùyè jīhuì.
examples.english: The local government is working hard to revitalize traditional industries and create more job opportunities.

semanticNote: 'To shake profoundly; shocking/stunning (emotionally powerful impact)' — describes an intense emotional or sensory impact, stronger than surprise, often evoked by something dramatic, tragic, or awe-inspiring (震撼人心, deeply moving/shocking; 視覺震撼, visually stunning/powerful). Common in describing reactions to disasters, powerful art, or dramatic news, emphasizing the profound emotional weight of the impact.

examples.chinese: 這部紀錄片呈現的畫面令觀眾深感震撼。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù jìlùpiàn chéngxiàn de huàmiàn lìng guānzhòng shēngǎn zhènhàn.
examples.english: The scenes presented in this documentary left the audience deeply shaken.

examples.chinese: 地震發生的瞬間,整棟大樓都感受到強烈的震撼。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn fāshēng de shùnjiān, zhěng dòng dàlóu dōu gǎnshòu dào qiángliè de zhènhàn.
examples.english: The moment the earthquake struck, the entire building felt an intense shaking.

semanticNote: 'To shock; to astonish; astonished' — describes an intense reaction of surprise, usually to unexpected and often distressing news (震驚社會, shock society; 感到十分震驚, feel utterly shocked). Common in news headlines about crimes, scandals, and unexpected events, describing widespread public reaction of disbelief or alarm.

examples.chinese: 這起殺人事件震驚了整個社會。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ shārén shìjiàn zhènjīngle zhěnggè shèhuì.
examples.english: This murder incident shocked all of society.

examples.chinese: 聽到自己被解雇的消息,他感到十分震驚。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zìjǐ bèi jiěgù de xiāoxi, tā gǎndào shífēn zhènjīng.
examples.english: Upon hearing the news that he had been fired, he felt utterly shocked.

semanticNote: 'Calm; composed; unperturbed (especially under pressure)' — describes maintaining a steady, cool-headed demeanor in a stressful or dangerous situation (保持鎮定, stay calm/composed). Common in emergency and crisis contexts praising someone's composure, similar to 冷靜 but 鎮定 leans slightly more toward physical/outward steadiness under acute pressure.

examples.chinese: 面對突發火警,他保持鎮定,冷靜地引導大家疏散。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì tūfā huǒjǐng, tā bǎochí zhèndìng, lěngjìng de yǐndǎo dàjiā shūsàn.
examples.english: Facing the sudden fire alarm, he stayed calm and composedly guided everyone to evacuate.

examples.chinese: 即使飛機劇烈搖晃,空服員依然表現得十分鎮定。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ fēijī jùliè yáohuàng, kōngfúyuán yīrán biǎoxiàn de shífēn zhèndìng.
examples.english: Even as the plane shook violently, the flight attendant remained very composed.

semanticNote: 'Calm; tranquil; composed' — largely synonymous with 鎮定 (calm under pressure), though 鎮靜 also appears in the medical term 鎮靜劑 (sedative/tranquilizer). Interchangeable with 鎮定 in most everyday usage for describing composure, with the medical/pharmacological sense being a distinguishing additional usage.

examples.chinese: 醫生開了鎮靜劑,幫助病患緩解焦慮情緒。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng kāile zhènjìngjì, bāngzhù bìnghuàn huǎnjiě jiāolǜ qíngxù.
examples.english: The doctor prescribed a sedative to help the patient relieve their anxiety.

examples.chinese: 遇到危險時,保持鎮靜才能做出正確的判斷。
examples.pinyin: Yùdào wéixiǎn shí, bǎochí zhènjìng cái néng zuòchū zhèngquè de pànduàn.
examples.english: When facing danger, only by staying calm can one make the right judgment.

english: the first month of the lunar calendar
semanticNote: 'The first month of the lunar calendar' — refers specifically to the first lunar month, encompassing Lunar New Year and its associated festivities through the Lantern Festival (正月初一, the first day of the lunar new year; 正月十五, the 15th day, i.e. Lantern Festival). Essential vocabulary for discussing Taiwan's traditional lunar calendar and holiday timing, distinct from the Gregorian calendar's January (一月).

components.meaning: first (lunar month, special reading); correct/upright (elsewhere zhèng)

examples.chinese: 正月初一是農曆新年的第一天。
examples.pinyin: Zhēngyuè chū yī shì nónglì xīnnián de dì yī tiān.
examples.english: The first day of the first lunar month is the first day of the Lunar New Year.

examples.chinese: 許多傳統習俗都集中在正月期間舉行。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō chuántǒng xísú dōu jízhōng zài zhēngyuè qíjiān jǔxíng.
examples.english: Many traditional customs are concentrated during the first lunar month.

semanticNote: 'Dispute; conflict; a point of contention' — a formal term for a disagreement or conflict, especially between nations, organizations, or parties in a formal dispute (領土爭端, territorial dispute; 貿易爭端, trade dispute). Common in international relations, legal, and political news discussing formal conflicts between parties.

examples.chinese: 兩國之間長期存在領土爭端。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhījiān chángqí cúnzài lǐngtǔ zhēngduān.
examples.english: There has long been a territorial dispute between the two countries.

examples.chinese: 這起貿易爭端最終透過國際仲裁解決。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ màoyì zhēngduān zuìzhōng tòuguò guójì zhòngcái jiějué.
examples.english: This trade dispute was ultimately resolved through international arbitration.

semanticNote: 'To fight over; to contend for; to compete fiercely for' — describes intense competition to obtain something limited and desirable, whether territory, resources, or honors (爭奪冠軍, fight/compete for the championship; 爭奪市場, compete for market share). Stronger and more combative than 競爭 (compete, general) — 爭奪 implies a fierce, sometimes zero-sum contest.

components.meaning: seize; take by force; compete for

examples.chinese: 兩支隊伍將在決賽中爭奪冠軍寶座。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhī duìwǔ jiāng zài juésài zhōng zhēngduó guànjūn bǎozuò.
examples.english: The two teams will compete for the championship title in the final.

examples.chinese: 各大廠商激烈爭奪這塊龐大的市場。
examples.pinyin: Gèdà chǎngshāng jīliè zhēngduó zhè kuài pángdà de shìchǎng.
examples.english: Major manufacturers are fiercely competing for this huge market.

english: work hard for sth.; determined not to fall short
semanticNote: 'To work hard to prove oneself; to strive not to disappoint (especially to redeem family/group honor)' — describes making a determined effort to achieve success, particularly to live up to expectations or avoid embarrassment for oneself or one's family (爭一口氣, prove oneself/save face through achievement; 你要爭氣點, you need to shape up and make us proud). Common in parenting and motivational contexts, carrying an emotional weight tied to family honor or personal pride.

examples.chinese: 他發憤圖強,努力爭氣,不讓父母失望。
examples.pinyin: Tā fāfèntúqiáng, nǔlì zhēngqì, bú ràng fùmǔ shīwàng.
examples.english: He worked hard with determination, striving to make his parents proud rather than disappointing them.

examples.chinese: 這次終於考上了理想的學校,總算為自己爭了一口氣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì zhōngyú kǎoshàngle lǐxiǎng de xuéxiào, zǒngsuàn wèi zìjǐ zhēngle yì kǒu qì.
examples.english: This time he finally got into his dream school, finally proving himself/redeeming his pride.

english: striving to be first; compete with each other
semanticNote: Chengyu meaning 'striving to be first, afraid of being left behind; competing eagerly with one another' — describes a scene of many people rushing or competing simultaneously to be first, often chaotic (爭先恐後地擠上車, scrambling eagerly to squeeze onto the vehicle). Vividly captures a chaotic, competitive rush, common in describing crowded transit boarding, sales rushes, or eager participation.

examples.chinese: 捷運門一開,乘客們爭先恐後地擠上車。
examples.pinyin: Jiéyùn mén yì kāi, chéngkèmen zhēngxiānkǒnghòu de jǐ shàng chē.
examples.english: As soon as the MRT doors opened, passengers scrambled eagerly to squeeze onto the train.

examples.chinese: 限量商品一上架,顧客們就爭先恐後地搶購。
examples.pinyin: Xiànliàng shāngpǐn yí shàngjià, gùkèmen jiù zhēngxiānkǒnghòu de qiǎnggòu.
examples.english: As soon as the limited-edition item was stocked, customers rushed eagerly to buy it before others.

semanticNote: 'Controversy; dispute; contention' — the standard term for a matter over which people disagree publicly, often on a significant scale (引發爭議, spark controversy; 具爭議性, controversial). Common in news, politics, and public discourse discussing contentious topics where opinions are sharply divided.

examples.chinese: 這項政策一公布,立刻引發社會廣泛爭議。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè yì gōngbù, lìkè yǐnfā shèhuì guǎngfàn zhēngyì.
examples.english: As soon as this policy was announced, it immediately sparked widespread controversy in society.

examples.chinese: 這起判決結果具有高度爭議性。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ pànjué jiéguǒ jùyǒu gāodù zhēngyìxìng.
examples.english: The result of this ruling is highly controversial.

semanticNote: 'To conquer; to subdue (militarily or figuratively)' — used both literally for military conquest of territory (征服他國, conquer another nation) and figuratively for overcoming a challenge or captivating an audience (征服觀眾, win over/captivate the audience; 征服高峰, conquer a mountain peak). The figurative sense is common in describing impressive achievements that overcome significant obstacles or win widespread admiration.

examples.chinese: 歷史上,許多帝國曾試圖征服鄰近的國家。
examples.pinyin: Lìshǐ shàng, xǔduō dìguó céng shìtú zhēngfú línjìn de guójiā.
examples.english: Throughout history, many empires attempted to conquer neighboring countries.

examples.chinese: 她精湛的演技征服了在場所有的觀眾。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngzhàn de yǎnjì zhēngfúle zàichǎng suǒyǒu de guānzhòng.
examples.english: Her superb acting won over every member of the audience present.

semanticNote: 'To levy; to collect (a tax, fee, or fine) as a governing authority' — a formal administrative/legal term for the government collecting mandatory payments from citizens or businesses (徵收稅款, levy taxes; 徵收土地, expropriate/requisition land — a significant term in property and urban development law). Common in tax, legal, and government policy discussions.

examples.chinese: 政府依法向企業徵收營業稅。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ yīfǎ xiàng qǐyè zhēngshōu yíngyèshuì.
examples.english: The government levies business tax on companies in accordance with the law.

examples.chinese: 為了興建道路,政府決定徵收這塊私有土地。
examples.pinyin: Wèile xīngjiàn dàolù, zhèngfǔ juédìng zhēngshōu zhè kuài sīyǒu tǔdì.
examples.english: In order to build the road, the government decided to expropriate this private land.

semanticNote: 'To struggle (physically or against difficult circumstances)' — used both literally (在水中掙扎, struggle in the water) and figuratively for enduring hardship or internal conflict (在生死邊緣掙扎, struggle at the edge of life and death; 內心掙扎, an inner struggle). Common in describing both physical peril and emotional/moral dilemmas, often conveying prolonged, difficult effort against adversity.

examples.chinese: 溺水者在水中拚命掙扎,幸好被及時救起。
examples.pinyin: Nìshuǐzhě zài shuǐ zhōng pīnmìng zhēngzhá, xìnghǎo bèi jíshí jiùqǐ.
examples.english: The drowning person struggled desperately in the water and was fortunately rescued in time.

examples.chinese: 面對要不要轉職的抉擇,他內心十分掙扎。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì yào bú yào zhuǎnzhí de juézé, tā nèixīn shífēn zhēngzhá.
examples.english: Facing the choice of whether to change careers, he struggled greatly inside.

semanticNote: 'To evaporate; evaporation' — the standard scientific term for the physical process of liquid turning to vapor (水分蒸發, moisture evaporation). Also used figuratively and colloquially for something disappearing suddenly and completely, especially money or a person (資產瞬間蒸發, assets vanish in an instant; 人間蒸發, disappear without a trace — a common idiom-like phrase for someone who vanishes completely).

examples.chinese: 太陽出來後,地面上的水漬很快就蒸發了。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng chūlái hòu, dìmiàn shàng de shuǐzì hěn kuài jiù zhēngfā le.
examples.english: After the sun came out, the water stains on the ground quickly evaporated.

examples.chinese: 股市崩盤讓他多年的積蓄一夕之間蒸發。
examples.pinyin: Gǔshì bēngpán ràng tā duōnián de jīxù yìxī zhījiān zhēngfā.
examples.english: The stock market crash caused his years of savings to vanish overnight.

semanticNote: 'To reorganize; to consolidate; to rectify (a disorganized or problematic situation)' — used for systematically fixing and reordering something that has become messy, corrupt, or inefficient (整頓紀律, tighten up discipline; 整頓市場秩序, restore order to market practices). Common in government and organizational contexts describing top-down reform or cleanup efforts.

examples.chinese: 政府展開行動,整頓夜市攤販的衛生問題。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhǎnkāi xíngdòng, zhěngdùn yèshì tānfàn de wèishēng wèntí.
examples.english: The government launched an operation to rectify the hygiene issues among night market vendors.

examples.chinese: 新上任的主管決定先整頓部門內部的管理制度。
examples.pinyin: Xīn shàngrèn de zhǔguǎn juédìng xiān zhěngdùn bùmén nèibù de guǎnlǐ zhìdù.
examples.english: The newly appointed supervisor decided to first reorganize the department's internal management system.

semanticNote: 'Legitimate; proper; justified (of a claim or action)' — describes an action or right that is fair and legally/morally justified (正當防衛, justifiable/legitimate self-defense — a real legal concept; 正當理由, legitimate reason). Note: the skeleton also lists a temporal reading (zhèng dāng, 'just at the moment when...'), a formal literary usage for describing timing (正當此時, just at this moment); the adjective sense (zhèngdàng, proper/legitimate) is far more common in everyday Taiwan usage.

examples.chinese: 他辯稱自己的行為屬於正當防衛。
examples.pinyin: Tā biànchēng zìjǐ de xíngwéi shǔyú zhèngdàng fángwèi.
examples.english: He argued that his actions constituted legitimate self-defense.

examples.chinese: 公司必須以正當的手段來獲取利潤。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī bìxū yǐ zhèngdàng de shǒuduàn lái huòqǔ lìrùn.
examples.english: Companies must obtain profit through proper and legitimate means.

semanticNote: 'Positive and negative; plus-minus' — a mathematical/scientific term used for indicating a range or margin (正負三度, plus or minus three degrees; 正負電荷, positive and negative electric charge). Common in weather forecasts, scientific measurements, and statistics for expressing margins of error or ranges.

examples.chinese: 今天的氣溫預計是攝氏二十度,正負一度。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de qìwēn yùjì shì shèshì èrshí dù, zhèngfù yí dù.
examples.english: Today's temperature is expected to be twenty degrees Celsius, plus or minus one degree.

examples.chinese: 電池上標示了正負極,安裝時要特別注意。
examples.pinyin: Diànchí shàng biāoshìle zhèngfùjí, ānzhuāng shí yào tèbié zhùyì.
examples.english: The positive and negative terminals are marked on the battery — pay special attention when installing it.

semanticNote: 'Formal; regular; standardized (following official/proper procedures)' — describes something that follows established, official standards or channels, as opposed to informal or unofficial alternatives (正規教育, formal education; 正規管道, proper/official channels). Common when distinguishing legitimate, standard processes from shortcuts or unofficial workarounds.

examples.chinese: 他沒有接受過正規的醫學訓練,卻自稱是醫生。
examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu jiēshòuguò zhèngguī de yīxué xùnliàn, què zìchēng shì yīshēng.
examples.english: He never received formal medical training, yet he claims to be a doctor.

examples.chinese: 申請簽證應透過正規管道,避免上當受騙。
examples.pinyin: Shēnqǐng qiānzhèng yīng tòuguò zhèngguī guǎndào, bìmiǎn shàngdàng shòupiàn.
examples.english: Visa applications should go through official channels to avoid being scammed.

semanticNote: 'Decent; proper; serious (not frivolous or improper)' — describes someone or something respectable and appropriately serious, common in both praise (正經的工作, a decent/respectable job) and in gentle scolding for not being serious enough (正經一點, be more serious/behave properly). Also used colloquially as an intensifier meaning 'really/genuinely' (正經八百, seriously/no joking, an emphatic colloquial expression).

examples.chinese: 他終於找到一份正經的工作,家人都很欣慰。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú zhǎodào yí fèn zhèngjing de gōngzuò, jiārén dōu hěn xīnwèi.
examples.english: He finally found a decent, respectable job, and his family is relieved.

examples.chinese: 上課時請正經一點,不要一直開玩笑。
examples.pinyin: Shàngkè shí qǐng zhèngjing yìdiǎn, bú yào yìzhí kāi wánxiào.
examples.english: Please be more serious during class and don't keep joking around.

semanticNote: 'Righteous spirit; upright moral integrity; a healthy, honest atmosphere' — refers to moral uprightness and integrity, whether in a person's character (一身正氣, full of righteous integrity) or in a collective environment (社會正氣, a righteous/healthy social atmosphere). Carries a somewhat elevated, moralistic tone, common in discussions of ethics, integrity, and combating corruption or dishonesty.

examples.chinese: 這位法官一身正氣,不畏權貴,秉公審理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi fǎguān yìshēn zhèngqì, búwèi quánguì, bǐnggōng shěnlǐ.
examples.english: This judge, full of righteous integrity, doesn't fear the powerful and adjudicates impartially.

examples.chinese: 教育的目的之一,是培養社會的正氣。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoyù de mùdì zhīyī, shì péiyǎng shèhuì de zhèngqì.
examples.english: One purpose of education is to cultivate a righteous, healthy atmosphere in society.

semanticNote: 'Justice; righteous; just' — a formal, weighty term for moral rightness and fairness, especially in legal and social contexts (伸張正義, uphold justice; 社會正義, social justice — a common term in discussions of equity and fairness). More formal and philosophical than 公平 (fair, everyday) — 正義 implies a broader moral principle beyond simple fairness in one transaction.

examples.chinese: 檢察官誓言要為受害者伸張正義。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎncháguān shìyán yào wèi shòuhàizhě shēnzhāng zhèngyì.
examples.english: The prosecutor vowed to uphold justice for the victim.

examples.chinese: 追求社會正義,是許多社運人士的共同信念。
examples.pinyin: Zhuīqiú shèhuì zhèngyì, shì xǔduō shèyùn rénshì de gòngtóng xìnniàn.
examples.english: Pursuing social justice is a shared belief among many social activists.

semanticNote: 'Authentic; orthodox; the genuine original (style/tradition)' — describes something that faithfully follows an original, authoritative tradition, especially common in food culture (正宗台灣味, authentic Taiwanese flavor; 正宗川菜, authentic Sichuan cuisine). Widely used in Taiwan restaurant marketing and everyday food talk to distinguish genuine traditional preparation from imitations or fusion adaptations.

examples.chinese: 這家小吃店賣的是正宗的台南擔仔麵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xiǎochīdiàn mài de shì zhèngzōng de Táinán dànzǎimiàn.
examples.english: This eatery sells authentic Tainan-style danzai noodles.

examples.chinese: 他堅持使用傳統工法,做出最正宗的味道。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiānchí shǐyòng chuántǒng gōngfǎ, zuò chū zuì zhèngzōng de wèidào.
examples.english: He insists on using traditional methods to create the most authentic flavor.

semanticNote: 'To confirm; to verify as true (a suspicion, claim, or hypothesis)' — used when evidence or investigation proves that something previously uncertain is indeed true (證實傳聞, confirm a rumor; 有待證實, yet to be confirmed/unverified). Common in news reporting and scientific writing to indicate that a claim has moved from speculation to confirmed fact.

examples.chinese: 官方尚未證實這項傳聞的真實性。
examples.pinyin: Guānfāng shàngwèi zhèngshí zhè xiàng chuánwén de zhēnshíxìng.
examples.english: The authorities have not yet confirmed the truth of this rumor.

examples.chinese: 檢驗結果證實了他罹患的是流感,而非新冠肺炎。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎnyàn jiéguǒ zhèngshíle tā líhuàn de shì liúgǎn, ér fēi xīnguān fèiyán.
examples.english: The test results confirmed that he had the flu, not COVID-19.

semanticNote: 'Certificate; credential (official document proving qualification)' — a standard term for a formal document certifying an achievement, qualification, or status (畢業證書, diploma; 專業證書, professional certificate). Common in education, employment, and licensing contexts across Taiwan's professional and academic life.

examples.chinese: 他花了半年的時間考取了這張專業證書。
examples.pinyin: Tā huāle bàn nián de shíjiān kǎoqǔle zhè zhāng zhuānyè zhèngshū.
examples.english: He spent half a year obtaining this professional certificate.

examples.chinese: 畢業典禮上,校長親自頒發證書給每位畢業生。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè diǎnlǐ shàng, xiàozhǎng qīnzì bānfā zhèngshū gěi měi wèi bìyèshēng.
examples.english: At the graduation ceremony, the principal personally handed out diplomas to each graduate.

semanticNote: 'Solemn; serious and formal (in manner or statement)' — describes a deliberate, weighty formality applied to a statement, promise, or action (鄭重聲明, a formal/solemn statement/declaration; 鄭重道歉, formally and sincerely apologize). Implies the speaker wants their words to be taken with full seriousness, common in official statements, apologies, and important promises.

examples.chinese: 公司發表鄭重聲明,否認一切不實指控。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī fābiǎo zhèngzhòng shēngmíng, fǒurèn yíqiè bùshí zhǐkòng.
examples.english: The company issued a formal statement denying all false accusations.

examples.chinese: 他鄭重地向對方道歉,並承諾不再犯同樣的錯誤。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzhòng de xiàng duìfāng dàoqiàn, bìng chéngnuò bú zài fàn tóngyàng de cuòwù.
examples.english: He solemnly apologized to the other party and promised not to make the same mistake again.

semanticNote: 'Policy (government or institutional)' — the standard term for official, formalized courses of action taken by governments, institutions, or organizations (經濟政策, economic policy; 移民政策, immigration policy). Fundamental civics and business vocabulary appearing constantly in Taiwan news coverage of government decisions and institutional planning.

examples.chinese: 政府推出新的能源政策,鼓勵民眾使用綠能。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ tuīchū xīn de néngyuán zhèngcè, gǔlì mínzhòng shǐyòng lǜnéng.
examples.english: The government launched a new energy policy encouraging the public to use green energy.

examples.chinese: 這項教育政策引發了家長們的熱烈討論。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng jiàoyù zhèngcè yǐnfāle jiāzhǎngmen de rèliè tǎolùn.
examples.english: This education policy sparked heated discussion among parents.

semanticNote: 'Political power; a regime; the ruling authority' — refers to the ruling government or governing authority of a nation, especially in discussions of political change or power struggles (奪取政權, seize political power; 政權轉移, transfer of power/regime change). Common in historical and political discussions, particularly relevant to discussions of governance and political legitimacy.

examples.chinese: 這場革命最終推翻了原本的政權。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng gémìng zuìzhōng tuīfānle yuánběn de zhèngquán.
examples.english: This revolution ultimately overthrew the original regime.

examples.chinese: 台灣經歷過多次和平的政權轉移。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān jīnglìguò duō cì hépíng de zhèngquán zhuǎnyí.
examples.english: Taiwan has experienced multiple peaceful transfers of political power.

semanticNote: 'Symptom (of an illness)' — the standard medical term for observable signs of a disease or condition (發燒是感冒常見的症狀, fever is a common symptom of a cold). Essential health and medical vocabulary used in doctor visits, health education, and everyday discussions of illness.

examples.chinese: 如果出現咳嗽、發燒等症狀,請盡快就醫。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ chūxiàn késòu, fāshāo děng zhèngzhuàng, qǐng jìnkuài jiùyī.
examples.english: If symptoms such as coughing or fever appear, please seek medical attention as soon as possible.

examples.chinese: 醫生根據他描述的症狀,初步判斷是腸胃炎。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng gēnjù tā miáoshù de zhèngzhuàng, chūbù pànduàn shì chángwèiyán.
examples.english: Based on the symptoms he described, the doctor's preliminary judgment was gastroenteritis.

english: during; at the time of; the time when something happens
semanticNote: 'At the time of; on the occasion of; just when (formal)' — a literary connective used to mark a significant moment or occasion, common in formal speeches and ceremonial contexts (在此新春之際, on this occasion of the new spring/Lunar New Year; 值此畢業之際, at this moment of graduation). Elevated and formal register, appropriate for speeches, greeting cards, and ceremonial writing rather than casual conversation.

examples.chinese: 值此新年之際,祝福大家平安健康。
examples.pinyin: Zhí cǐ xīnnián zhījì, zhùfú dàjiā píng'ān jiànkāng.
examples.english: On this occasion of the New Year, I wish everyone peace and health.

examples.chinese: 在公司成立十週年之際,舉辦了一場盛大的慶祝活動。
examples.pinyin: Zài gōngsī chénglì shí zhōunián zhījì, jǔbànle yì chǎng shèngdà de qìngzhù huódòng.
examples.english: On the occasion of the company's tenth anniversary, a grand celebration was held.

semanticNote: 'To support; to prop up (physically or figuratively); support/backing' — used both for literal structural support (支撐屋頂的柱子, pillars supporting the roof) and figurative support keeping something going, like resolve or finances (精神支撐, spiritual/emotional support; 支撐一個家, support a family financially). Common across construction, emotional resilience, and financial-responsibility contexts.

examples.chinese: 這幾根鋼柱負責支撐整座橋樑的重量。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ gēn gāngzhù fùzé zhīchēng zhěng zuò qiáoliáng de zhòngliàng.
examples.english: These steel columns are responsible for supporting the entire bridge's weight.

examples.chinese: 對家人的責任感,是他咬牙撐下去的支撐力量。
examples.pinyin: Duì jiārén de zérèngǎn, shì tā yǎoyá chēng xiàqù de zhīchēng lìliàng.
examples.english: His sense of responsibility toward his family is the supporting force that keeps him pushing through.

semanticNote: 'To spend; expenditure; expenses (paid out)' — the standard financial term for money paid out, paired conceptually with 收入 (income). Used in personal finance, business accounting, and government budgeting (家庭支出, household expenses; 政府支出, government spending). Basic financial vocabulary appearing constantly in budget and accounting discussions.

examples.chinese: 每個月的房租是家庭最大的一筆支出。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge yuè de fángzū shì jiātíng zuìdà de yì bǐ zhīchū.
examples.english: Monthly rent is the family's largest single expense.

examples.chinese: 他仔細記錄每一筆收入與支出。
examples.pinyin: Tā xìjí jìlù měi yì bǐ shōurù yǔ zhīchū.
examples.english: He carefully records every item of income and expenditure.

semanticNote: 'Tributary (of a river); a minor branch/offshoot' — the standard geographic term for a smaller river feeding into a main river (河流的支流, a river's tributary). Also used figuratively for a minor, secondary aspect of a larger issue or movement (只是主流文化的一個支流, just a minor offshoot of mainstream culture). Common in both geography and abstract discussions of trends and movements.

examples.chinese: 這條小溪是濁水溪眾多支流之一。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiǎoxī shì Zhuóshuǐxī zhòngduō zhīliú zhī yī.
examples.english: This small stream is one of the many tributaries of the Zhuoshui River.

examples.chinese: 這種次文化只是主流音樂中的一個支流。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cì wénhuà zhǐshì zhǔliú yīnyuè zhōng de yí ge zhīliú.
examples.english: This subculture is just a minor offshoot within mainstream music.

semanticNote: 'To control; to dominate; to dictate (the use or direction of something)' — used for having decisive control over resources, time, or behavior (支配時間, control/manage one's time; 受人支配, be controlled/dominated by someone). Can imply either neutral management (支配資源) or a more critical power imbalance (被他人支配, being dominated by another), context-dependent in tone.

examples.chinese: 他很懂得支配自己的時間,工作與休息兼顧。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn dǒngde zhīpèi zìjǐ de shíjiān, gōngzuò yǔ xiūxi jiāngù.
examples.english: He's very skilled at managing his own time, balancing work and rest.

examples.chinese: 在那段婚姻裡,她的生活完全受丈夫支配。
examples.pinyin: Zài nà duàn hūnyīn lǐ, tā de shēnghuó wánquán shòu zhàngfū zhīpèi.
examples.english: In that marriage, her life was completely controlled by her husband.

semanticNote: 'To support; to reinforce; aid/assistance (often organizational or emergency)' — describes providing help, resources, or reinforcement to someone in need, common in disaster relief, military, and workplace contexts (支援災區, provide support to disaster areas; 人力支援, staffing support/reinforcement). Distinct from 幫助 (help, general) — 支援 often implies a more organized, resource-based form of assistance from one group to another.

examples.chinese: 各縣市消防隊紛紛派遣人力支援災區救援工作。
examples.pinyin: Gè xiànshì xiāofángduì fēnfēn pàiqiǎn rénlì zhīyuán zāiqū jiùyuán gōngzuò.
examples.english: Fire departments from various counties and cities dispatched personnel to support the disaster area's rescue work.

examples.chinese: 業務量暴增,公司緊急從其他部門調人支援。
examples.pinyin: Yèwùliàng bàozēng, gōngsī jǐnjí cóng qítā bùmén diàorén zhīyuán.
examples.english: As the workload surged, the company urgently transferred staff from other departments to help out.

semanticNote: 'Pillar; mainstay; backbone (of support, literal or figurative)' — used literally for a physical support structure (建築支柱, a building's support pillar) and, very commonly, figuratively for the primary source of support in an economy, family, or system (經濟支柱, economic pillar/mainstay; 家庭支柱, the family's main breadwinner/pillar of support). The figurative sense is extremely common in describing key sectors of an economy or a family's primary provider.

examples.chinese: 半導體產業是台灣經濟的重要支柱。
examples.pinyin: Bàndǎotǐ chǎnyè shì Táiwān jīngjì de zhòngyào zhīzhù.
examples.english: The semiconductor industry is an important pillar of Taiwan's economy.

examples.chinese: 自從父親過世後,他成了家中的經濟支柱。
examples.pinyin: Zìcóng fùqīn guòshì hòu, tā chéngle jiāzhōng de jīngjì zhīzhù.
examples.english: Ever since his father passed away, he has become the family's economic pillar.

english: branch; twig; (mw for sticks, rods, pencils)
semanticNote: 'Branch; twig' (noun), or a measure word for long, thin objects like sticks, pens, and pencils (一枝筆, one pen; 一枝花, one flower stem). The measure-word usage is common and practical everyday vocabulary, distinct from 支 which is also used as a measure word for similar objects — the two are often interchangeable in practice, though 枝 has a stronger botanical/plant-stem association.

components.meaning: branch; twig; measure word for slender objects

examples.chinese: 強風吹斷了樹上的好幾根枝條。
examples.pinyin: Qiángfēng chuīduànle shùshàng de hǎojǐ gēn zhītiáo.
examples.english: The strong wind broke off several branches from the tree.

examples.chinese: 他從筆筒裡拿出一枝鉛筆開始寫字。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng bǐtǒng lǐ náchū yì zhī qiānbǐ kāishǐ xiězì.
examples.english: He took a pencil out of the pen holder and began writing.

semanticNote: 'Perception; consciousness; sensation' — refers to sensory awareness and the state of consciousness, especially in medical contexts (失去知覺, lose consciousness; 恢復知覺, regain consciousness). Also used more broadly for perceptual awareness (視覺、聽覺等知覺, perceptions like sight and hearing). Common in medical and psychological discussions of consciousness and sensory experience.

examples.chinese: 他從高處摔落後,一度失去知覺。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng gāochù shuāiluò hòu, yídù shīqù zhījué.
examples.english: After falling from a height, he lost consciousness for a while.

examples.chinese: 手術結束後幾小時,病人才逐漸恢復知覺。
examples.pinyin: Shǒushù jiéshù hòu jǐ xiǎoshí, bìngrén cái zhújiàn huīfù zhījué.
examples.english: Several hours after the surgery ended, the patient gradually regained consciousness.

semanticNote: Chengyu meaning 'to be content with what one has brings lasting happiness' — a philosophical, often Daoist/Buddhist-flavored piece of life wisdom advocating contentment over constant striving for more (知足常樂,不貪求太多, be content and you'll always be happy — don't be greedy for more). Common in reflective conversations about happiness, materialism, and life philosophy, often quoted as advice for a peaceful mindset.

examples.chinese: 奶奶常說,知足常樂,人生就會過得比較輕鬆。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai cháng shuō, zhīzúchánglè, rénshēng jiù huì guò de bǐjiào qīngsōng.
examples.english: Grandma often says that being content brings lasting happiness, and life will feel much easier.

examples.chinese: 他雖然收入不高,但秉持知足常樂的心態,活得很快樂。
examples.pinyin: Tā suīrán shōurù bù gāo, dàn bǐngchí zhīzúchánglè de xīntài, huó de hěn kuàilè.
examples.english: Although his income isn't high, he lives happily by holding onto a contented, 'enough is enough' mindset.

semanticNote: '(Body) fat' — the standard biological/nutritional term for fat, used in health, fitness, and dietary discussions (體脂肪, body fat percentage; 脂肪肝, fatty liver — a real and common health condition discussed in Taiwan health checkups). Common vocabulary for discussing diet, exercise, and health metrics.

components.meaning: fat (body fat, always paired with 脂)

examples.chinese: 健檢報告顯示他的體脂肪比例偏高。
examples.pinyin: Jiànjiǎn bàogào xiǎnshì tā de tǐzhīfáng bǐlì piāngāo.
examples.english: The health checkup report showed his body fat percentage was on the high side.

examples.chinese: 醫生建議他減少攝取高脂肪食物。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā jiǎnshǎo shèqǔ gāo zhīfáng shíwù.
examples.english: The doctor recommended he reduce his intake of high-fat foods.

semanticNote: 'To execute; to carry out; to implement (a plan, order, or law)' — the standard term for putting a decision or plan into concrete action (執行任務, carry out a mission/task; 執行長, CEO — literally 'chief executor,' a common corporate title). Essential vocabulary across business, government, and organizational contexts for describing action following planning or decision-making.

examples.chinese: 團隊已擬定計畫,接下來就是全力執行。
examples.pinyin: Tuánduì yǐ nǐdìng jìhuà, jiēxiàlái jiùshì quánlì zhíxíng.
examples.english: The team has already drafted the plan; next is to carry it out with full effort.

examples.chinese: 軍人必須無條件服從並執行上級的命令。
examples.pinyin: Jūnrén bìxū wútiáojiàn fúcóng bìng zhíxíng shàngjí de mìnglìng.
examples.english: Soldiers must unconditionally obey and carry out their superiors' orders.

english: to refuse to change one's viewpoint
semanticNote: 'Persistent; deeply committed; to hold onto (an idea or goal) stubbornly' — describes unwavering dedication to a goal or belief, which can be admirable (執著追求夢想, persistently pursue one's dream) or, depending on context, seen as stubborn rigidity (太過執著, too stubbornly attached). Context and tone determine whether it reads as praise for determination or mild criticism of inflexibility.

examples.chinese: 他對音樂的執著,讓他堅持了二十年從未放棄。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì yīnyuè de zhízhuó, ràng tā jiānchíle èrshí nián cóng wèi fàngqì.
examples.english: His persistent devotion to music made him stick with it for twenty years without ever giving up.

examples.chinese: 有時候太執著於一個想法,反而會錯過更好的機會。
examples.pinyin: Yǒushíhou tài zhízhuó yú yí ge xiǎngfǎ, fǎn'ér huì cuòguò gèng hǎo de jīhuì.
examples.english: Sometimes being too stubbornly attached to one idea can actually cause you to miss better opportunities.

semanticNote: 'Live broadcast; to livestream' — the standard term for real-time, unrecorded broadcasting, essential vocabulary in the modern social media era (直播主, livestreamer/streamer; 開直播, start a livestream). Extremely common in describing social media content, sports broadcasts, and news coverage across Taiwan's active livestreaming culture.

examples.chinese: 這位網紅每晚都會在社群平台上直播。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi wǎnghóng měi wǎn dōuhuì zài shèqún píngtái shàng zhíbō.
examples.english: This internet celebrity livestreams on social media every night.

examples.chinese: 電視台將全程直播這場總統就職典禮。
examples.pinyin: Diànshìtái jiāng quánchéng zhíbō zhè chǎng zǒngtǒng jiùzhí diǎnlǐ.
examples.english: The TV station will broadcast this presidential inauguration ceremony live in its entirety.

semanticNote: 'Diameter' — the standard mathematical/geometric term for the distance across a circle through its center (圓的直徑, a circle's diameter). Common in math education and technical/measurement contexts describing round objects.

examples.chinese: 這個圓形餐桌的直徑大約是一百二十公分。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge yuánxíng cānzhuō de zhíjìng dàyuē shì yìbǎi èrshí gōngfēn.
examples.english: This round dining table's diameter is approximately 120 centimeters.

examples.chinese: 老師教學生如何計算圓的直徑與周長。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiāo xuéshēng rúhé jìsuàn yuán de zhíjìng yǔ zhōucháng.
examples.english: The teacher taught students how to calculate a circle's diameter and circumference.

semanticNote: 'Nephew (brother's son)' — a formal kinship term specifically for a brother's son, part of Taiwan's detailed traditional family-relations vocabulary that distinguishes paternal-side from maternal-side relatives (a sister's son would be 外甥, a different term). Learners should note this precision, as English 'nephew' doesn't distinguish which side of the family.

examples.chinese: 叔叔特地買了生日禮物送給他的侄子。
examples.pinyin: Shūshu tèdì mǎile shēngrì lǐwù sòng gěi tā de zhízi.
examples.english: The uncle specially bought a birthday gift for his nephew.

examples.chinese: 這個週末,他要帶侄子去動物園玩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zhōumò, tā yào dài zhízi qù dòngwùyuán wán.
examples.english: This weekend, he's going to take his nephew to the zoo.

english: be on duty; work a shift
semanticNote: 'To be on duty; to work a shift (especially overnight or during off-hours)' — a common workplace term for being scheduled to work during a designated shift, especially one requiring continuous coverage (值夜班, work the night shift; 今天輪到我值班, today it's my turn to be on duty). Common in hospital, security, customer service, and other shift-based work contexts.

examples.chinese: 今晚輪到他在急診室值班。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn lúndào tā zài jízhěnshì zhíbān.
examples.english: Tonight it's his turn to be on duty in the emergency room.

examples.chinese: 保全人員二十四小時輪流值班,確保社區安全。
examples.pinyin: Bǎoquán rényuán èrshísì xiǎoshí lúnliú zhíbān, quèbǎo shèqū ānquán.
examples.english: Security personnel work rotating 24-hour shifts to ensure the community's safety.

semanticNote: 'Function; role (of an institution or department, formal)' — a formal organizational term for the designated purpose or role of an entity (部門職能, a department's function; 政府職能, the functions of government). More formal and institutional than 功能 (function, general/everyday, can apply to devices too) — 職能 specifically describes the designated role of an organization, position, or department within a system.

examples.chinese: 這次組織改造重新界定了各部門的職能。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì zǔzhī gǎizào chóngxīn jièdìngle gè bùmén de zhínéng.
examples.english: This organizational restructuring redefined the functions of each department.

examples.chinese: 地方政府的職能包括教育、交通與環保等事務。
examples.pinyin: Dìfāng zhèngfǔ de zhínéng bāokuò jiàoyù, jiāotōng yǔ huánbǎo děng shìwù.
examples.english: Local government functions include matters such as education, transportation, and environmental protection.

semanticNote: '(Professional) position; job title' — refers to a specific job role or rank within an organization (應徵職位, apply for a position; 職位晉升, position promotion). Standard HR and career vocabulary, commonly used in job postings and discussions of career advancement.

examples.chinese: 這個職位需要具備至少三年的相關經驗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zhíwèi xūyào jùbèi zhìshǎo sān nián de xiāngguān jīngyàn.
examples.english: This position requires at least three years of relevant experience.

examples.chinese: 他經過多年努力,終於獲得升遷,擔任更高的職位。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngguò duōnián nǔlì, zhōngyú huòdé shēngqiān, dānrèn gèng gāo de zhíwèi.
examples.english: After years of hard work, he finally got promoted to a higher position.

semanticNote: 'Post; official duties/responsibilities (of a position)' — refers to the specific duties and responsibilities attached to a job, sometimes overlapping with 職位 (the title/rank itself) but 職務 emphasizes the actual work/responsibilities carried out (履行職務, fulfill one's duties; 職務調動, job/duty transfer). Common in formal HR and administrative contexts discussing role responsibilities.

examples.chinese: 他因表現優異,被調任更重要的職務。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn biǎoxiàn yōuyì, bèi diàorèn gèng zhòngyào de zhíwù.
examples.english: Due to his outstanding performance, he was transferred to a more important post.

examples.chinese: 公務員必須嚴格遵守相關法規,履行職務。
examples.pinyin: Gōngwùyuán bìxū yángé zūnshǒu xiāngguān fǎguī, lǚxíng zhíwù.
examples.english: Civil servants must strictly comply with relevant regulations in fulfilling their duties.

semanticNote: 'Colony' — the standard historical/political term for a territory controlled by a foreign power (殖民地時期, the colonial period). Historically significant vocabulary for Taiwan, which itself was a Japanese colony (日本殖民地) from 1895-1945 — an important term in Taiwan's own historical self-understanding and in discussions of colonialism's lasting cultural and infrastructural effects.

examples.chinese: 台灣曾在日治時期作為日本的殖民地長達五十年。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān céng zài Rìzhì shíqí zuòwéi Rìběn de zhímíndì chángdá wǔshí nián.
examples.english: Taiwan was a Japanese colony during the Japanese colonial period for as long as fifty years.

examples.chinese: 許多非洲國家在二十世紀中葉才擺脫殖民地的身分獨立。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō Fēizhōu guójiā zài èrshí shìjì zhōngyè cái bǎituō zhímíndì de shēnfèn dúlì.
examples.english: Many African countries only shed their status as colonies and gained independence in the mid-20th century.

semanticNote: 'Indicator; index; benchmark target' — a formal term for a quantifiable measure used to evaluate performance or set a goal (經濟指標, economic indicator; 業績指標, performance target). Standard vocabulary in business, economics, and statistics for discussing measurable benchmarks or goals.

examples.chinese: 失業率是衡量經濟狀況的重要指標之一。
examples.pinyin: Shīyèlǜ shì héngliáng jīngjì zhuàngkuàng de zhòngyào zhǐbiāo zhī yī.
examples.english: The unemployment rate is one of the important indicators for measuring economic conditions.

examples.chinese: 公司為每位員工設定了明確的業績指標。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī wèi měi wèi yuángōng shèdìngle míngquè de yèjì zhǐbiāo.
examples.english: The company set clear performance targets for each employee.

semanticNote: 'To appoint; to designate; to specify (a particular person/place/thing)' — used for officially selecting a specific person, location, or item from among options (指定接班人, designate a successor; 指定地點, a designated location). Standard formal vocabulary in official appointments, event logistics, and legal designations.

examples.chinese: 董事長在退休前指定了自己的接班人。
examples.pinyin: Dǒngshìzhǎng zài tuìxiū qián zhǐdìngle zìjǐ de jiēbānrén.
examples.english: The chairman designated his successor before retiring.

examples.chinese: 請大家在指定的時間與地點集合。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā zài zhǐdìng de shíjiān yǔ dìdiǎn jíhé.
examples.english: Please everyone gather at the designated time and location.

semanticNote: 'Fingernail; nail (of fingers or toes)' — basic everyday body-part vocabulary (剪指甲, cut/trim one's nails; 指甲油, nail polish). No significant register variation; standard vocabulary for personal grooming and hygiene discussions.

examples.chinese: 媽媽提醒他要定期修剪指甲,保持衛生。
examples.pinyin: Māma tíxǐng tā yào dìngqí xiūjiǎn zhǐjia, bǎochí wèishēng.
examples.english: Mom reminded him to regularly trim his nails to maintain hygiene.

examples.chinese: 她今天特地去美甲店塗了亮麗的指甲油。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān tèdì qù měijiǎdiàn túle liànglì de zhǐjiayóu.
examples.english: She specially went to a nail salon today to have vibrant nail polish applied.

semanticNote: 'Instruction; command; directive' — a formal term for an authoritative order to be followed, used in military/organizational contexts (下達指令, issue a command) and technical contexts (電腦指令, computer command/instruction). More formal and authoritative than 命令 in some contexts, or interchangeable with it — common in both human chain-of-command and computer programming contexts.

examples.chinese: 指揮官向部隊下達了撤退的指令。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐhuīguān xiàng bùduì xiàdále chètuì de zhǐlìng.
examples.english: The commander issued the order to retreat to the troops.

examples.chinese: 工程師輸入了正確的指令,系統才順利運作。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī shūrùle zhèngquè de zhǐlìng, xìtǒng cái shùnlì yùnzuò.
examples.english: The engineer entered the correct command, and only then did the system run smoothly.

semanticNote: 'Compass (navigational instrument)' — the standard term for a magnetic direction-finding tool (指南針指向北方, a compass points north). Used both literally in navigation/hiking contexts and occasionally figuratively for guiding principles (人生的指南針, a compass for life). Common practical vocabulary for outdoor activities and historical discussions (the compass is one of China's celebrated 'Four Great Inventions,' 四大發明).

examples.chinese: 登山客隨身攜帶指南針,以防迷路。
examples.pinyin: Dēngshānkè suíshēn xiédài zhǐnánzhēn, yǐfáng mílù.
examples.english: Hikers carry a compass with them to avoid getting lost.

examples.chinese: 指南針是中國古代的四大發明之一。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐnánzhēn shì Zhōngguó gǔdài de sì dà fāmíng zhī yī.
examples.english: The compass is one of ancient China's Four Great Inventions.

semanticNote: 'To instruct; to indicate; instructions/directive' — used both for giving formal directions/orders (上級指示, instructions from a superior) and for something pointing/indicating information (儀表板指示燈, dashboard indicator light). Common in both workplace hierarchy contexts (following a boss's instructions) and technical contexts (indicator signals on devices).

examples.chinese: 員工必須依照主管的指示完成工作。
examples.pinyin: Yuángōng bìxū yīzhào zhǔguǎn de zhǐshì wánchéng gōngzuò.
examples.english: Employees must complete their work according to their supervisor's instructions.

examples.chinese: 儀表板上的指示燈亮起,代表油量不足。
examples.pinyin: Yíbiǎobǎn shàng de zhǐshìdēng liàngqǐ, dàibiǎo yóuliàng bùzú.
examples.english: The indicator light on the dashboard lit up, indicating the fuel is running low.

semanticNote: 'To hope for; to count on; hope/expectation' — describes relying on or hoping for a particular outcome, often with an implied risk of disappointment (別指望他會幫忙, don't count on him to help; 唯一的指望, the only hope). More colloquial than 期望 (expect/hope, more formal), common in everyday speech about relying on uncertain future outcomes.

examples.chinese: 別老是指望別人,自己也要努力。
examples.pinyin: Bié lǎoshì zhǐwàng biérén, zìjǐ yě yào nǔlì.
examples.english: Don't always count on others — you need to work hard yourself too.

examples.chinese: 這筆退休金是他晚年唯一的指望。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ tuìxiūjīn shì tā wǎnnián wéiyī de zhǐwàng.
examples.english: This pension is his only hope for his later years.

english: to censure; criticize; find fault with
semanticNote: 'To censure; to criticize; to accuse (of wrongdoing)' — a formal, serious term for pointing out and condemning someone's fault or wrongdoing (遭到指責, be subjected to criticism/censure; 互相指責, mutually blame each other). Stronger and more formal than 責怪 (blame, milder/interpersonal) — 指責 often appears in public, political, or serious interpersonal contexts involving accountability.

examples.chinese: 官員因處理不當而遭到民眾嚴厲指責。
examples.pinyin: Guānyuán yīn chǔlǐ búdàng ér zāodào mínzhòng yánlì zhǐzé.
examples.english: The official was severely censured by the public for mishandling the matter.

examples.chinese: 雙方為了這起糾紛互相指責,誰也不肯讓步。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng wèile zhè qǐ jiūfēn hùxiāng zhǐzé, shéi yě bùkěn ràngbù.
examples.english: Both sides blamed each other over this dispute, and neither was willing to back down.

semanticNote: 'Ambition; resolve; backbone/drive' — describes a person's inner determination and aspiration to achieve something meaningful, often used encouragingly (要爭氣、有志氣, be determined and have ambition/resolve). Positive, motivational vocabulary common in encouraging young people to have drive and self-respect, distinct from 野心 (ambition, which carries a negative overreaching connotation) — 志氣 is wholly positive.

examples.chinese: 父母常鼓勵孩子要有志氣,不要輕易向困難低頭。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ cháng gǔlì háizi yào yǒu zhìqì, bú yào qīngyì xiàng kùnnán dītóu.
examples.english: Parents often encourage their children to have ambition and not easily bow to difficulties.

examples.chinese: 他憑著一股志氣,從零開始白手起家。
examples.pinyin: Tā píngzhe yì gǔ zhìqì, cóng líng kāishǐ báishǒuqǐjiā.
examples.english: Relying on sheer determination, he built himself up from nothing.

semanticNote: 'To sanction; to punish (formally, especially internationally); sanctions' — a formal legal/political term for punitive measures imposed by an authority, especially economic sanctions between nations (經濟制裁, economic sanctions) or legal punishment for wrongdoing (法律制裁, legal punishment). Common in international relations news and legal discourse about accountability for wrongdoing.

examples.chinese: 國際社會對該國實施了嚴厲的經濟制裁。
examples.pinyin: Guójì shèhuì duì gāi guó shíshīle yánlì de jīngjì zhìcái.
examples.english: The international community imposed severe economic sanctions on that country.

examples.chinese: 犯下罪行的人終將受到法律的制裁。
examples.pinyin: Fànxià zuìxíng de rén zhōngjiāng shòudào fǎlǜ de zhìcái.
examples.english: Those who commit crimes will ultimately face legal punishment.

english: uniform; to subdue; to bring under control
semanticNote: 'Uniform' (noun, e.g. school or work uniform) or 'to subdue; to bring under control' (verb, a distinct meaning sharing the same characters). As a noun, standard everyday vocabulary (校服/制服, school uniform; 警察制服, police uniform). As a verb, more formal, used for physically overpowering someone (制服嫌犯, subdue a suspect) — the two meanings are unrelated in usage despite identical characters, distinguishable entirely by context.

examples.chinese: 這所學校的制服是藍白相間的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào de zhìfú shì lánbái xiāngjiàn de.
examples.english: This school's uniform is blue and white.

examples.chinese: 警方合力將暴力抗拒的嫌犯制服。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng hélì jiāng bàolì kàngjù de xiánfàn zhìfú.
examples.english: Police worked together to subdue the violently resisting suspect.
